policy_statement: Bahrain will implement net metering to enable consumers to generate on-site grid-connected renewable energy such as rooftop solar.
source_quote: Net metering: This will enable consumers to generate on-site, grid-connected, renewable energy, for example via the installation of solar panels on roofs; Feed-in tariffs: This is a tender-based mechanism to support renewable energy characterized by long-term power purchase agreements;
extraction_rationale: This is a specific policy instrument under NREAP. It is explicit and operational, with a clear renewable energy intervention.

parent_statement: National Renewable Energy Action Plan (NREAP)
policy_statement: Bahrain will use feed-in tariffs through tender-based long-term power purchase agreements to support renewable energy.
source_quote: Feed-in tariffs: This is a tender-based mechanism to support renewable energy characterized by long-term power purchase agreements; and Mandates: This refers to renewable energy mandates for new buildings.
extraction_rationale: This is a classic economic support mechanism for renewable energy and therefore a financial instrument. It is explicitly listed as a policy under NREAP.

parent_statement: National Renewable Energy Action Plan (NREAP)
policy_statement: Bahrain will apply renewable energy mandates for new buildings.
source_quote: Feed-in tariffs: This is a tender-based mechanism to support renewable energy characterized by long-term power purchase agreements; and Mandates: This refers to renewable energy mandates for new buildings.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding-style regulatory mechanism for new buildings under NREAP. It is a specific intervention with direct mitigation relevance.

policy_statement: The National Energy Efficiency Action Plan targets a 6% reduction in final energy consumption by 2025, equivalent to about 6,000 GWh, through 22 initiatives.
source_quote: After extensive consultations with stakeholders, the SEU established the target of a 6% reduction (about 6,000 GWh) in final energy consumption by 2025. It is estimated that this would lead to a cumulative reduction in greenhouse gas emissions of 3.4 million tonnes of CO2 by 2025.
extraction_rationale: This is a named national plan with quantified target and explicit emissions outcome. It is a parent because multiple initiatives are listed beneath it.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Bahrain will integrate energy efficiency objectives into building regulations governing design, construction, and maintenance of structures.
source_quote: Building codes: This involves the integration of energy efficiency objectives into regulations governing the design, construction, and maintenance of structures. The new Bahrain International Airport, currently under construction, will be NEEAP-compliant;
extraction_rationale: This is a specific regulatory intervention under NEEAP. It directly targets energy efficiency and therefore qualifies as policy.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Bahrain will introduce new minimum demand-side efficiency standards for lighting, appliances, motor vehicles, and street lighting.
source_quote: Demand-side efficiency standards: This involves new minimum standards for lighting, appliances, motor vehicles, and street lighting; Supply-side efficiency standards: This focuses on electricity generation, including efficiency enhancements for the transmission and distribution of electricity, and the installation of smart meters;
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete standards-based policy under NEEAP. It is regulatory and directly linked to energy savings.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Bahrain will improve supply-side electricity efficiency through transmission and distribution enhancements and smart meter installation.
source_quote: Supply-side efficiency standards: This focuses on electricity generation, including efficiency enhancements for the transmission and distribution of electricity, and the installation of smart meters; District cooling: This involves the introduction of highly efficient, industrial-grade equipment to produce space cooling for buildings through an insulated underground piping network;
extraction_rationale: This is a specific operational and standards-based intervention under NEEAP. It directly targets energy system efficiency.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Bahrain will introduce district cooling systems using highly efficient industrial-grade equipment and insulated underground piping networks.
source_quote: District cooling: This involves the introduction of highly efficient, industrial-grade equipment to produce space cooling for buildings through an insulated underground piping network; and Green building initiatives: This involves retrofitting of government buildings; and other initiatives; and
extraction_rationale: This is a named technology intervention under NEEAP. It is a specific efficiency measure with direct climate relevance.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Bahrain will pursue green building initiatives including retrofitting government buildings.
source_quote: Green building initiatives: This involves retrofitting of government buildings; and other initiatives; and Subsidy reform: This involves reforms to both power subsidies and those that affect transport to offset perverse incentives for wasteful consumption.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific intervention under NEEAP with a named action. It is operational rather than financial.

parent_statement: National Energy Efficiency Action Plan (NEEAP)
policy_statement: Bahrain will reform power and transport subsidies to remove incentives for wasteful consumption.
source_quote: Subsidy reform: This involves reforms to both power subsidies and those that affect transport to offset perverse incentives for wasteful consumption.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific economic policy instrument under NEEAP. It changes price signals and therefore qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Bahrain's climate change policy includes project-level greenhouse gas mitigation initiatives and education-based initiatives.
source_quote: While NREAP and NEEAP are the flagship components of Bahrain's energy policy, they also represent an important pillar of Bahrain's climate change policy. Other pillars include project-based initiatives for greenhouse gas mitigation and public awareness raising about climate change, as outlined below.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella statement introducing listed climate policy pillars. It is a parent because sub-initiatives follow.

parent_statement: Other pillars of Bahrain's climate change policy
policy_statement: Bahrain launched BAPCO's carbon recovery plan to find industrial applications for waste CO2 from oil extraction activities.
source_quote: Project-level initiatives: Two projects have been launched. The first is BAPCO's carbon recovery plan, which finds industrial applications for the waste CO2 associated with its oil extraction activities.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific named mitigation project under climate policy. It directly targets CO2 recovery.

parent_statement: Other pillars of Bahrain's climate change policy
policy_statement: Bahrain launched GPIC's carbon dioxide recovery unit in 2009 for petrochemical operations.
source_quote: The other is a carbon dioxide recovery unit launched by Gulf Petrochemicals Industries Company (GPIC) in 2009, a first for a petrochemicals company in the Middle East.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete project-level mitigation intervention with a named technology and launch year.

parent_statement: Other pillars of Bahrain's climate change policy
policy_statement: Bahrain will improve climate change education and awareness by introducing changes in primary school curricula and proposing educational reforms to the Ministry of Education.
source_quote: Education-based initiatives: This involves improving education and awareness on climate change primarily by introducing changes in educational curricula in primary schools. In addition, specific proposals for educational reforms were delivered to the Ministry of Education on the basis of studies of how other countries have introduced climate change into educational curricula.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific government-backed intervention on climate education. It is climate-relevant but peripheral to direct emissions or resilience outcomes.

policy_statement: Tubli Bay was declared a protected area in 1995 and designated a natural reserve under Law 53/2006.
source_quote: In response, Tubli Bay was declared nationally as a protected area in 1995 and Law 53/2006 designated Tubli Bay as a natural reserve. In 1997, it was designated internationally as a RAMSAR Site.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding legal conservation measure protecting mangrove habitat. It supports climate resilience through ecosystem protection, though the original motivation is broader conservation.

policy_statement: Bahrain is considering a set of adaptation strategies to build resilience against climate change risks to Tubli Bay mangroves.
source_quote: There are several adaptation strategies that are under consideration to build resilience against climate change risks Tubli Bay mangrove, as outlined below:
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella adaptation package with listed sub-actions. It qualifies as a parent because specific strategies follow.

parent_statement: Adaptation strategies under consideration to build resilience against climate change risks to Tubli Bay mangrove
policy_statement: Bahrain aims to establish a Tubli Bay observatory to strengthen observation systems for mangrove ecological services through monitoring, species mapping, documentation, and information dissemination.
source_quote: Tubli Bay observatory: This aims to strengthen existing observation systems to better understand the ecological services provided by mangrove habitats in Tubli Bay. Activities include monitoring, species mapping, systematic documentation, and dissemination of collected information to policymakers.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific named adaptation-support intervention under the mangrove strategy. It is concrete though still planning-oriented.

parent_statement: Adaptation strategies under consideration to build resilience against climate change risks to Tubli Bay mangrove
policy_statement: Bahrain aims to introduce ecosystem services valuation for Tubli Bay mangroves to account for market and non-market services in financial planning frameworks.
source_quote: Ecosystem services valuation: This aims introduce economic valuation as a basis to account for the value of the market (i.e., tourism) and non-market (i.e., regulating, provisioning, supporting) services that, Tubli Bay mangrove habitats provide. It will leverage information developed by the Tubli Bay observatory and apply state-of-the art ecological valuation methods to in support of financial planning frameworks.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific planned intervention supporting mangrove adaptation planning. It is not itself a financial instrument, but informs planning and valuation.

parent_statement: Adaptation strategies under consideration to build resilience against climate change risks to Tubli Bay mangrove
policy_statement: Bahrain aims to develop a blue carbon inventory for Tubli Bay to estimate and document carbon pools and fluxes consistent with international guidance.
source_quote: Blue carbon inventory: This aims to augment Bahrain's existing GHG emission tracking system to estimate and document carbon pools/fluxes in Tubli Bay consistent with international methodological guidance. This will involve data sharing across institutions, database development, information management, documentation, and dissemination of the levels and rates of carbon pool storage.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete named intervention with explicit carbon accounting and mangrove ecosystem focus. It has both ecosystem and mitigation dimensions explicitly stated.

policy_statement: Bahrain's 2009 building codes require the ground floor of new buildings to be 1.5 meters above pavement level.
source_quote: Some adaptation measures have already taken place in certain sectors. For example, while not explicitly in reference to sea level rise, Bahrain's building codes enacted in 2009 call for the height of the ground floor of a new building being 1.5 meters above the level of the pavement surface (KoB, 2009).
extraction_rationale: This is a binding code requirement with a clear physical resilience implication for flooding and sea level rise. Climate relevance is indirect because the text notes it was not explicitly enacted for sea level rise.

policy_statement: Bahrain should organize systematic adaptation planning for sea level rise using strategies for protection, accommodation, retreat, and avoidance.
source_quote: Going forward, it is recommended that systematic adaptation planning efforts be organized within an adaptation framework that address strategies for protection, accommodation, retreat, and avoidance. In the near-term, the focus should be on the following elements, with the aim of increasing institutional capacity to incorporate sea level rise risks within development planning:
extraction_rationale: Although framed as recommendation, it specifies an adaptation framework with listed tools and clear planning purpose. It is extracted as a parent because sub-tools are enumerated.

parent_statement: Adaptation framework for sea level rise
policy_statement: Bahrain should use planning tools including coastal hazard assessment, coastal risk modeling and management, and emergency preparedness strategies to mitigate sea level rise effects.
source_quote: Planning tools: Planning tools include activities of setting an overall policy to mitigate the effect of sea level rise. At minimum, it should incorporate assessment of coastal hazards, coastal risk modeling/management, and development of emergency preparedness strategies.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation planning intervention under the sea-level-rise framework. It is concrete enough to qualify despite being forward-looking.

parent_statement: Adaptation framework for sea level rise
policy_statement: Bahrain should enact regulatory tools such as coastal zoning offsets, revised building codes, and sea-level-rise considerations in real estate permits including no-build zones.
source_quote: Regulatory tools: These include tools such as enacting land use regulations (e.g., zoning offsets from the coastline), adjusting building codes (e.g., increasing the distance from pavement to ground floor) and accounting for sea level rise in real estate development permits (e.g., identification of no-build zones).
extraction_rationale: This is a specific set of regulatory adaptation measures. It qualifies because it names concrete regulatory mechanisms.

parent_statement: Adaptation framework for sea level rise
policy_statement: Bahrain should apply land-use tools including land acquisition, reclamation restrictions, rezoning vulnerable land, and subdivision conservation requirements.
source_quote: Land use tools: These refer to tools in support of strategic adaptation and include such as land acquisition (i.e., purchase/transfer of development rights), reclamation (e.g., adding more restrictions on top of basic zoning requirements for certain high-risk areas), zoning (i.e., reclassifying highly vulnerable land for low risk uses) and subdivision regulation (e.g., minimum conservation requirements)
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete package of land-use adaptation measures. It is not financial overall because it is primarily planning/regulatory, despite mentioning acquisition.

parent_statement: Adaptation framework for sea level rise
policy_statement: Bahrain should assess hard and soft structural coastal protection measures including dikes, breakwaters, mangrove plantations, and beach nourishment.
source_quote: Hard and soft structural tools: Structural tools include assessment frameworks by which to assess the optimality of coastal protection with either hard measures (e.g., dikes, breakwaters) or soft measures (e.g., mangrove plantations, beach nourishment).
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation intervention set. Because mangrove plantations are explicitly named as soft measures, a nature-based secondary category is warranted.

policy_statement: Bahrain established a National Water Resources Council in 2016 to reactivate the High Water Council as the organizational framework for sustainable water resource management.
source_quote: In 2016, Bahrain moved one step in this direction by establishing a National Water Resources Council (Royal Decree No. 36/2009) to reactivate the previously formed High Water Council in 1982, seen as the most suitable organizational framework to ensure sustainable water resource management.
extraction_rationale: This is an institutional reform established by decree with a clear governance role in water adaptation. It directly supports climate resilience in water management.

policy_statement: Bahrain should formulate a clear, comprehensive, and integrated national water resources policy and strategy based on IWRM principles.
source_quote: The results of the assessment make clear that significant water demand reductions are possible and therefore it is imperative for Bahrain to formulate a clear comprehensive national water policy and strategy based on integrated water resource management (IWRM) principles.
extraction_rationale: This is framed as imperative policy direction with a named management framework. It is adaptation-focused because it responds to climate-driven water stress.

policy_statement: Bahrain's first water adaptation initiative aims to reduce per capita municipal water demand by 33% by 2035, from 183 to 122 cubic meters per person per year.
source_quote: The first initiative aims to achieve a 33% reduction in per capita municipal water demand, from the current level of 183 to 122 m3 per person per year by 2035. The second initiative aims to reduce leakage in the water distribution network to achieve reductions of 22% of annual water production by 2035 relative to water production in that year under business-as-usual conditions.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified adaptation initiative with a deadline and measurable target. It is adaptation-primary because it is part of climate resilience planning for water supply-demand equilibrium.

policy_statement: Bahrain's second water adaptation initiative aims to reduce leakage in the water distribution network by 22% of annual water production by 2035 relative to business-as-usual.
source_quote: The second initiative aims to reduce leakage in the water distribution network to achieve reductions of 22% of annual water production by 2035 relative to water production in that year under business-as-usual conditions.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified adaptation initiative with a clear target and timeframe. It is adaptation-primary because it is explicitly part of climate resilience planning.

policy_statement: Bahrain is pursuing a policy of expanding treated wastewater reuse in irrigation to protect groundwater and meet irrigation and landscaping demand.
source_quote: At present, Bahrain is pursuing a policy of expansion in the re-use of treated wastewater in irrigation. The primary objectives are to protect groundwater from further lowering of the groundwater table, deterioration in water quality, and satisfying demands for irrigation and landscaping.
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit policy statement with clear objectives and intervention. It is adaptation-focused because it addresses water scarcity and groundwater deterioration under climate stress.

policy_statement: Bahrain incentivizes farmers to use treated wastewater instead of groundwater by providing free delivery of treated wastewater to farms.
source_quote: The policy incentivizes farmers to use treated wastewater instead of groundwater by providing free delivery of treated wastewater to the farmer lands. Currently, an average of 154 thousand m3/d of treated wastewater is delivered to 547 farms with a total area of 3,100 hectares.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete incentive-based policy with a specific delivery mechanism and implementation scale. Because it provides a subsidized service, it qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Bahrain strengthened water tariffs for commercial, industrial, touristic, and other non-household users under a new block tariff schedule.
source_quote: Effective 1 March 2016, water tariffs for commercial, industrial, touristic, and other non-household users are being gradually strengthened in accordance with the new tariff schedule established by EWA. The block water tariff structure is shown in Figure 3-25.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear price-based policy instrument with implementation date and target user groups. It is a financial instrument and supports water efficiency.

policy_statement: Bahrain should establish a cooperation mechanism with Saudi Arabia for development and management of transboundary groundwater resources including artificial recharge using surplus tertiary treated wastewater.
source_quote: Further deterioration of groundwater resources should be addressed by establishing a cooperation mechanism between Bahrain and Saudi Arabia in the development and management of transboundary groundwater resources, including groundwater artificial recharge/storage enhancement using surplus tertiary treated wastewater.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation recommendation with named institutional cooperation and intervention. It directly addresses climate-vulnerable groundwater resources.

policy_statement: Bahrain's INDC committed to measures for reducing the future growth of greenhouse gases in the country.
source_quote: In 2015, Bahrain submitted its Intended Nationally Determined Contribution (INDC) toward confronting the challenge of climate change. The INDC committed to a set of measures for reducing the future growth of GHGs in the country.
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit national climate commitment under the UNFCCC process. The quote is broad and does not specify measures, but it clearly states a commitment.

policy_statement: Cabinet endorsed the National Energy Efficiency Action Plan through Cabinet Resolution No 2392-1.
source_quote: The NEEAP was prepared in consultation with a wide range of stakeholder groups, including the National Oil and Gas Authority; all line ministries, the Supreme Council for the Environment; the Bahrain Defense Force; large industry groups; and academia (SEU, 2017a). It has been officially endorsed through Cabinet Resolution No 2392-1.
extraction_rationale: This is a formal government endorsement of a named plan, giving it policy standing. The substantive target is captured separately, so this entry reflects the binding mechanism.

policy_statement: NEEAP establishes 22 initiatives to reduce energy use by 6% by 2025 relative to average 2009-2013 energy use, equal to 5,792 GWh primary energy savings.
source_quote: In all, 22 initiatives have been established that together will contribute to a reduction in energy use of 6% by 2025 relative to average energy use over the period 2009-2013. On a primary energy equivalent basis, this amounts to savings of 5,792 GWh (or 498 kTOE) by 2025.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified national target with a named plan and implementation package. It directly qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Cabinet endorsed the National Renewable Energy Action Plan through Cabinet Resolution No 2392-1.
source_quote: The Plan was also prepared by the SEU and relied extensively upon a similarly wide range of stakeholder groups. It has been officially endorsed through Cabinet Resolution No 2392-1.
extraction_rationale: This is a formal endorsement mechanism for a named renewable energy plan. The substantive targets are captured separately.

policy_statement: NREAP establishes three policies to achieve renewable energy targets of 5% of peak capacity by 2025 and 10% by 2035.
source_quote: In all, 3 policies have been established that together will contribute to a national renewable energy target of 5% of peak capacity by 2025 and 10% by 2035, relative to the projected peak capacities in those years. On an electric generation basis, this amounts to 478 GWh and 1,456 GWh of renewable electricity by 2025 and 2035, respectively.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified renewable energy target with explicit implementation policies. It is a direct mitigation policy.

policy_statement: The SEC was established by Royal Decree 22/2019 as an independent centre reporting directly to Cabinet via the Minister of Electricity and Water Affairs.
source_quote: The Plan was prepared by the Sustainable Energy Unit which has recently been transformed by Royal Decree 22/2019 which established the Sustainable Energy Center (SEC). The SEC is an independent centre, which reports directly to Cabinet via the Minister of Electricity and Water Affairs.
extraction_rationale: This is a formal institutional policy change by royal decree. It supports climate governance directly through energy transition implementation.

policy_statement: Bahrain developed a climate change awareness plan specifying activities, target groups, input requirements, and institutional roles.
source_quote: Other major findings include the need to make better use of social media to build awareness, as well as print and televised media, including the use of slogans. Based on these findings, a climate change awareness plan was developed that specified activities, target groups, input requirements, and institutional roles.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete plan with specified implementation components. It is climate-specific but peripheral to direct mitigation or adaptation outcomes.

policy_statement: Bahrain's public awareness programme on climate change includes workshops, updated awareness content, social media outreach, and establishment of an association.
source_quote: Based on these findings, a climate change awareness plan was developed, as outlined in Table 5-1.
extraction_rationale: The table presents a structured programme with multiple planned activities, so it functions as a parent initiative. The quote is brief because the table itself contains the sub-actions.

parent_statement: Public awareness programme on climate change
policy_statement: Bahrain will hold three workshops to raise climate awareness among media organizations, parliamentarians, civil society organizations, and educators.
source_quote: Three workshops to raise awareness | ü Media organizations ü Shura Council and Members of Parliament ü Civil Society Organizations ü Educators | Holding training workshops for: ü Ministry of Information Affairs ü Shura Council and members of Parliament ü Civil society Associations ü Education sector in the Ministry of Education (Training of trainers)
extraction_rationale: This is a specific planned activity with target groups and implementation detail from Table 5-1. It is climate-specific but peripheral.

parent_statement: Public awareness programme on climate change
policy_statement: Bahrain will update awareness workshop content to include GHG inventory results, all greenhouse gases, climate impacts, Paris Agreement, NDCs, SDGs, and climate policies.
source_quote: Preparation of a new training material in the upcoming training workshops containing the following topics: ü Results of the emissions inventory for the third National Communication Report (abbreviated) ü All GHGs gases causing climate change and demonstrating their impact over time, � raising awareness of the impacts of climate change on various sectors in the Kingdom of Bahrain. ü Explain the Paris 2015 agreement, Nationally determined contributions (NDCs), the Sustainable development agenda (SDGs 2030) and its intersection with climate change, especially Goal 13 .
extraction_rationale: This is a specific planned intervention with detailed content requirements. It is climate-specific but peripheral to direct climate outcomes.

parent_statement: Public awareness programme on climate change
policy_statement: Bahrain will use social media to raise awareness about climate change through awareness messages, logo design, and scientific materials.
source_quote: Use of social media to raise awareness about climate change | Population of Bahrain | ü Set up a mental map (mind map) for awareness messages ü Logo Design (proposal of five logos required for approval by the Supreme Council for Environment) ü Preparation of scientific material for awareness messages
extraction_rationale: This is a specific planned outreach activity from Table 5-1. It is climate-specific but peripheral.

parent_statement: Public awareness programme on climate change
policy_statement: Bahrain will establish an association to raise awareness of climate change and its impacts on Bahrain.
source_quote: NGOs/CSOs | Population of Bahrain | Establishing an association to raise awareness of climate change and its impacts on Bahrain
extraction_rationale: This is a specific institutional awareness action from Table 5-1. It is climate-specific but peripheral.

policy_statement: Bahrain proposes curriculum reform, teacher awareness raising, and climate-based teaching activities to remedy weak climate change coverage in elementary education.
source_quote: The degree to which climate change is part of early grade education was evaluated through a series of studies. To remedy this situation, several recommendations have been proposed focusing on curriculum reform, teacher awareness raising, and introducing climate-based activities as teaching aides.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete reform package with named interventions, though framed as recommendations. It is climate-specific but peripheral to direct climate outcomes.

policy_statement: Bahrain developed educational materials on climate change for fourth and fifth graders through six instructional units and teacher training.
source_quote: This involved the development of educational materials for building climate change awareness aimed at fourth and fifth graders. Educational activities were divided into six units, as briefly described below.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific educational intervention with defined target groups and structured content. It is climate-specific but peripheral.

policy_statement: Bahrain recommends introducing climate change education into grades four to six, building staff awareness, reviewing higher-grade curricula, and integrating climate activities into other subjects.
source_quote: Going forward, several recommendations are offered based on the research undertaken the Educational Team: Introduce the climate change educational in the curriculum for fourth, fifth and sixth grade throughout Bahrain; Build awareness of climate change topics among all elementary school staff;
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete package of proposed education reforms with named actions. It is climate-specific but peripheral.

policy_statement: Bahrain should provide an enabling environment for technology transfer in renewable energy technologies based on technology needs assessment findings.
source_quote: Provision of an enabling environment for technology transfer in renewable energy technologies in light of the findings of a previously conducted technology needs assessment;
extraction_rationale: This is a specific policy recommendation for renewable energy technology transfer. It directly supports mitigation through clean technology deployment.

policy_statement: Bahrain should enforce intellectual property rights to provide confidence to prospective private sector investors in climate-related technology transfer.
source_quote: Enforcing intellectual property rights to provide confidence to prospective private sector investors;
extraction_rationale: This is a specific enabling policy for technology transfer. Climate relevance is indirect because it supports investment conditions rather than directly reducing emissions.

policy_statement: Bahrain should improve knowledge management processes and platforms for climate technology knowledge sharing.
source_quote: Improving knowledge management processes and platforms for knowledge sharing;
extraction_rationale: This is a specific enabling action for technology transfer. It is climate-related but indirect in causal effect.

policy_statement: Bahrain should enhance funding for R&D in green and climate technologies for small and medium-sized enterprises.
source_quote: Enhancing funding for R&D in green technology and climate technologies for small- and medium-sized enterprises;
extraction_rationale: This is a resource allocation commitment area focused on climate technologies, so it qualifies as a financial instrument. It directly supports mitigation innovation.

policy_statement: Bahrain should develop technology transfer policies and integrate them within technology action plans.
source_quote: Developing technology transfer policies and integrating them within technology actions plans; and
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit policy development commitment related to climate technology transfer. It is direct but enabling rather than operational.

policy_statement: Bahrain should enhance human capacity to support science-policy dialogue, public awareness, and technology information management for climate technologies.
source_quote: Enhancing human capacity to support science-policy dialogues, build public awareness, and manage technology information.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific capacity-building action tied to climate technology transfer. It is climate-specific but indirect in effect.

policy_statement: Bahrain prioritizes introduction of solar thermal and advanced natural gas combined-cycle technologies for the power sector.
source_quote: Introduction of solar thermal technologies (i.e., concentrated solar power), and advanced natural gas technologies for the power sector (i.e., combined cycle);
extraction_rationale: This is a specific technology transfer priority with named technologies. It directly supports mitigation.

policy_statement: Bahrain prioritizes introduction of energy-efficient technologies in aluminum smelting including efficient motors, pumps, and waste heat recovery.
source_quote: Introduction of energy efficient technologies in the aluminum smelting industry (e.g., efficient motors, pumps, waste heat recovery).
extraction_rationale: This is a specific industrial efficiency technology priority. It directly supports mitigation through efficiency.

policy_statement: Bahrain prioritizes development of incentive regimes to facilitate investments in clean energy technologies, sustainable practices, and innovative research.
source_quote: Development of incentive regimes to facilitate investments in clean energy technologies, sustainable practices, and innovative research.
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit incentive-based policy direction and therefore a financial instrument. It directly supports climate technology deployment.

policy_statement: Bahrain prioritizes encouraging niche energy service markets through regulatory reform and new incentive regimes.
source_quote: Encouragement of emerging niche markets for energy services through regulatory reform and new incentive regimes.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific policy direction combining regulatory reform and incentives. It directly supports mitigation-enabling markets.

policy_statement: Bahrain prioritizes regional cooperation on renewable energy through network development, harmonized standards, shared technical research, and improved GCC grid interconnection.
source_quote: Support of regional cooperation on renewable energy through network development, harmonization of standards, sharing of technical research, and improving the GCC interconnection grid.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific regional policy priority with named interventions. It directly supports renewable energy deployment.

policy_statement: Bahrain prioritizes integrating green development strategies into economic diversification and using international cooperation opportunities such as the clean development mechanism.
source_quote: Integration of green development strategies within the ongoing economic diversification strategy and tapping into international cooperation opportunities like the clean development mechanism.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific strategic policy direction linking green development and international climate cooperation. It directly supports mitigation.

policy_statement: Lebanon will establish a transparency framework to improve institutional arrangements, data availability, monitoring, and evaluation of mitigation and adaptation projects.
source_quote: Clarity and effectiveness of action can only be guaranteed through a robust monitoring and transparency framework, tackling climate and sustainable development action, as well as support. In order to enhance the impacts of policymaking, and to successfully participate in tracking the global progress of the climate fight, a transparency framework will be established to improve institutional arrangements, data availability and periodicity, as well as monitoring and evaluation of mitigation and adaptation projects.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete institutional commitment to establish a named framework with specified functions. It qualifies as a policy because it commits to a specific intervention rather than stating a general aspiration.

policy_statement: Lebanon will revise its policymaking process to include gender institutions, youth groups, and vulnerable communities in climate action.
source_quote: Integrated solutions to the climate crisis, as well as economic recovery, cannot be performed without the effective inclusion of gender institutions, youth groups and vulnerable communities. Lebanon plans to revise its policymaking process to include these groups which are key to the success of the NDC and are the most impacted by climate impacts.
extraction_rationale: This is a governance reform commitment with a specific action—revising policymaking processes to include named groups. It is climate-relevant because it is explicitly tied to NDC success, though it is more enabling than sectoral.

policy_statement: Lebanon will stimulate research and development for low-carbon and sustainable technologies and support public investment, academic partnerships, and innovation labs.
source_quote: Lebanon aims to reduce the carbon intensity of its economy through stimulating Research and Development for low carbon and sustainable technologies. It is therefore important to foster an innovative environment by sustainably enhancing the capabilities of the private sector, driving large public investments for research and piloting, partnering with academic bodies to provide the needed readiness for transformational change, and encouraging innovation labs.
section_header: CAE4: Innovative Research and Development Encouraged
extraction_rationale: This qualifies as a policy because it identifies a specific intervention area—R&D for low-carbon technologies—and names implementation mechanisms. The commitment is somewhat broad, but still concrete enough to count as a policy enabler.

policy_statement: Lebanon will scale up partnerships with non-state actors to increase their involvement in mitigation, adaptation, and climate advocacy.
source_quote: The role of Non-State Actors (NSAs), including the private sector and Civil Society Organizations is primordial to implement climate action. It is therefore important to scale-up the existing partnerships with NSAs to enable their increased involvement in mitigation and adaptation actions, as well as climate advocacy.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific enabling commitment to expand partnerships with identified actors for climate implementation. It is not merely descriptive because it states an intended action to scale up partnerships.

policy_statement: Lebanon will use fiscal incentives and disincentives to operationalize the Polluter Pays Principle across emitting sectors and climate-proof investments.
source_quote: Additionally, fiscal incentives and disincentives are necessary to operationalize the 'Polluter Pays Principle' across all relevant emitting sectors to fast-track the shift to greener options. Finally, climate-proofing public and private investments and projects is necessary to avoid climate-negative projects.
section_header: CAE2: Incentivized Action and Fiscal Reform
extraction_rationale: This qualifies as a policy because it commits to a broad fiscal reform approach and climate-proofing of investments. The statement is somewhat umbrella-like but still contains specific mechanisms: incentives, disincentives, and climate-proofing.

policy_statement: Lebanon will prioritize climate governance and build institutional capacities to plan, coordinate, regulate, and mainstream climate and sustainable development action.
source_quote: Lebanon prioritizes climate governance as the enabling of institutions to plan, prepare and react to climate change. Building the needed institutional capacities to reform, analyze, coordinate and regulate climate and sustainable development action is essential.
section_header: CAE1: Improved Governance and Institutional Capacities
extraction_rationale: This is a policy because it commits to strengthening governance and institutional capacity for climate action. It is broad and enabling, but still a deliberate governmental intervention with clear climate purpose.

policy_statement: Lebanon's updated mitigation contribution includes economy-wide 2030 targets for GHG reduction, renewable energy deployment, and energy-efficiency improvements.
source_quote: This NDC represents a progression beyond Lebanon's 2015 NDC by unconditionally increasing its Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emission target relative to the Business-As-Usual (BAU) scenario from 15% to 20%, and conditionally increasing its GHG emission target relative to the BAU scenario from 30% to 31%. Moreover, Lebanon commits to unconditionally generate 18% of the power demand (i.e. electricity demand) and 11% of its heat demand (in the building sector) from renewable energy sources in 2030, compared to a combined 15% in 2015.
extraction_rationale: This is a parent policy because the section presents a named umbrella mitigation contribution followed by three distinct numbered target commitments. The umbrella commitment organizes the sub-actions and is itself a valid policy package.

parent_statement: Lebanon's updated mitigation contribution includes economy-wide 2030 targets for GHG reduction, renewable energy deployment, and energy-efficiency improvements.

CO2eq.) and to conditionally reduce its greenhouse gas emissions by 31% below its Business-As-Usual (BAU) scenario in 2030 (amounting to 12,075 Gg. CO2eq.)

policy_statement: Lebanon's adaptation priorities set sectoral actions to build resilience across agriculture, ecosystems, water, biodiversity, coasts, health, and disaster risk management.
source_quote: Below are guiding principles and sectoral adaptation priorities which, together, aim to preserve and restore the natural capital and enhance and protect the built capital, as well as livelihoods, to ensure sustainable growth and resilience to climate change. Therefore, the below priorities constitute part of Lebanon's Adaptation Communication in accordance with paragraph 10 of Article 7 of the Paris Agreement and Law 115/2019.
extraction_rationale: This is a parent policy because it introduces a structured set of numbered adaptation priorities that function as sub-actions. The umbrella adaptation priorities are explicitly framed as part of Lebanon's adaptation communication.

parent_statement: Lebanon's adaptation priorities set sectoral actions to build resilience across agriculture, ecosystems, water, biodiversity, coasts, health, and disaster risk management.
policy_statement: Lebanon will strengthen the agricultural sector's resilience to enhance agricultural output in a climate-smart manner.
source_quote: Adaptation priority 1 Strengthen the agricultural sector's resilience to enhance Lebanon's agricultural output in a climate-smart manner. Key activities • Restore the livelihoods and productive capacity of farmers and producers; • Increase agricultural production and productivity; • Enhance efficiency and competitiveness of agri-food value chains including fisheries.
extraction_rationale: This is a named adaptation priority with a clear sectoral objective and listed implementation activities. It qualifies as a sub-policy under the adaptation priorities framework.

parent_statement: Lebanon's adaptation priorities set sectoral actions to build resilience across agriculture, ecosystems, water, biodiversity, coasts, health, and disaster risk management.
policy_statement: Lebanon will promote sustainable use of natural resources, restore degraded landscapes, and increase forest cover through sustainable forest management.
source_quote: Adaptation priority 2 Promote the sustainable use of natural resources, restore degraded landscapes, and increase Lebanon's forest cover while meeting the ecological, social and economic needs of sustainable forest management. Key activities • Achieve the goals listed in the Brummana Declaration for the Role of Mediterranean Forests to Fulfil the NDCs; • Adapt forest systems to climate change by halting land degradation, controlling erosion of topsoil, improving water quality and soil productivity.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation priority with named interventions in forests and landscapes. It also explicitly references forest cover and restoration, making it a clear sub-policy.

parent_statement: Lebanon's adaptation priorities set sectoral actions to build resilience across agriculture, ecosystems, water, biodiversity, coasts, health, and disaster risk management.
policy_statement: Lebanon will structure and develop sustainable water services, including irrigation, to improve living conditions.
source_quote: Adaptation priority 3 Structure and develop sustainable water services, including irrigation, in order to improve people's living conditions. Key activities • Implement the Beirut Water Declaration; • Enhance the efficient use of irrigation water and expand the supply of surface water sources for irrigation; • Encourage and support the use of renewable energy in agricultural irrigation and in drinking water supply.
extraction_rationale: This is a sectoral adaptation commitment with specific activities on irrigation efficiency, water supply, and renewable-powered services. It is a sub-policy under the adaptation priorities list.

parent_statement: Lebanon's adaptation priorities set sectoral actions to build resilience across agriculture, ecosystems, water, biodiversity, coasts, health, and disaster risk management.
policy_statement: Lebanon will sustainably manage terrestrial and marine biodiversity to preserve ecosystems, habitats, and species and maintain access to ecosystem goods and services.
source_quote: Adaptation priority 4 Value and sustainably manage Lebanon's terrestrial and marine biodiversity for the preservation and conservation of its ecosystems and habitats and the species they harbour in order to adequately respond to anthropogenic and natural pressures and to ensure Lebanese citizens equal access to ecosystem goods and services. Key activities • Identify the status of 75% of known flora and fauna species and implement conservation actions on 50% of threatened species; • Protect at least 20% of natural terrestrial and marine ecosystems and represent all types of ecosystems in the protected areas network.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified biodiversity and ecosystem management commitment with explicit percentages and conservation actions. It clearly qualifies as a policy and is a sub-item under adaptation priorities.

parent_statement: Lebanon's adaptation priorities set sectoral actions to build resilience across agriculture, ecosystems, water, biodiversity, coasts, health, and disaster risk management.
policy_statement: Lebanon will reduce vulnerability to climate change impacts on coastal zones, especially in cities.
source_quote: Adaptation priority 5 Reduce the vulnerability of climate change impacts on coastal zones, especially in cities. Key activities • Assess the sea-water intrusion in the major coastal aquifers; • Enhance the Artificial Recharge of some selected aquifers; • Increase the protective capacity of coasts against storm surges and sea-level rise.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear adaptation policy because it targets named climate hazards in coastal zones and lists specific interventions. It is a sub-policy within the adaptation priorities structure.

parent_statement: Lebanon's adaptation priorities set sectoral actions to build resilience across agriculture, ecosystems, water, biodiversity, coasts, health, and disaster risk management.
policy_statement: Lebanon will ensure public health and safety through climate-resilient health systems.
source_quote: Adaptation priority 6 Ensure overall public health and safety through climate-resilient health systems. Key activities • Assess the vulnerability of public health sector to climate change, identifying the current and future health effects and establishing early warning systems • Upgrade epidemiological surveillance to incorporate new health outcomes in the Epidemiological Surveillance Unit; • Develop a mechanism to incorporate climate data in the national health information system.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation commitment focused on health-system resilience, surveillance, and early warning. It is a sub-policy because it is one numbered adaptation priority.

parent_statement: Lebanon's adaptation priorities set sectoral actions to build resilience across agriculture, ecosystems, water, biodiversity, coasts, health, and disaster risk management.
policy_statement: Lebanon will reduce disaster risk and minimize damages from climate-related natural hazards and extreme weather.
source_quote: Adaptation priority 7 Reduce disaster risk and minimize damages by mitigating and adapting to climate-related natural hazards and extreme weather. Key activities • Conduct a multi-hazard risk assessment; • Update/revisit flood, fire and drought risk maps; • Upgrade and develop an early warning platform for multi-hazards.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation and disaster-risk policy with named actions on risk assessment, hazard mapping, and early warning. It is a sub-policy under the adaptation priorities framework.

policy_statement: Lebanon will establish the Lebanon Green Investment Facility to provide accessible climate and green finance instruments and technical assistance for bankable projects.
source_quote: Therefore, Lebanon is working towards the establishment of the Lebanon Green Investment Facility (LGIF) as stipulated in the Government's Financial Recovery Plan, to provide climate and green finance through accessible and affordable finance instruments for both the public and private sectors, as well as to provide needed technical assistance to various entities to create bankable projects. The LGIF is foreseen to substantially contribute to the implementation of the NDC by increasing investments to climate-friendly projects, through strong donor and investor coordination mechanism and capitalization strategy.
section_header: 6. Support Needed for NDC Implementation and Achievement
extraction_rationale: This is a clear financial policy instrument because it establishes a named facility with a financing function and technical assistance role. It is one of the strongest policy commitments in the support section.

policy_statement: Lebanon will develop a climate-proofing methodology to assess and reduce the impacts of climate-negative projects and guide investment evaluation through a climate lens.
source_quote: Moreover, Lebanon is currently developing a climate-proofing methodology which aims to assess and reduce the impacts of climate-negative projects, as well as potentially guide the evaluation of investments, through a climate-lens. Ultimately, Lebanon intends to explore the possibility of greening foreign investments including Official Development Assistance (ODA) to accelerate the achievement of the NDC and avoid locking in carbon emissions on the long-term.
section_header: 6. Support Needed for NDC Implementation and Achievement
extraction_rationale: This qualifies as a policy because it commits to a specific methodological tool for screening investments and projects. The second sentence adds a related but more tentative investment-greening intention; the methodology itself is the firmer commitment.

policy_statement: Lebanon will clarify support needs through the Green Climate Fund country programme to guide investors and donors on NDC priorities.
source_quote: Lebanon plans to make its support needs clear, starting with the Green Climate Fund (GCF)'s country programme for Lebanon. The programme plans to provide guidance for investors and donors on NDC priorities, which will be in line with the planned investments for economic recovery.
section_header: 6. Support Needed for NDC Implementation and Achievement
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete planning commitment tied to a named programme and a defined output—guidance for investors and donors. It is climate-relevant but more implementation-support oriented than a direct emissions or resilience measure.

policy_statement: Adopt a citywide climate target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 55% by 2030 and achieving carbon neutrality by 2050, while strengthening resilience to climate change.
source_quote: The Climate Plan defines ambitious quantified targets for the City of Brussels that will enable it to at least meet the commitments set out in the Majority Agreement, the Climate Emergency Declaration and the regional and European targets for the various topics. It therefore aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 55% by 2030, achieve carbon neutrality by 2050 and strengthen the region's resilience to climate change. In addition, the objective of energy carbon neutrality for public buildings has been brought back to 2040.
extraction_rationale: This is a core policy because it sets quantified, time-bound climate targets for mitigation and resilience at city scale.

policy_statement: Consume water sustainably as a precious resource.
source_quote:
1. Water, a precious resource to be consumed sustainably
2.  Reduce our consumption of mains water by 40% in the use of buildings and in the maintenance of outdoor areas
-  Equip the municipality with a rainwater storage capacity.
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella initiative with multiple water-demand and storage sub-actions.

parent_statement: Water, a precious resource to be consumed sustainably
policy_statement: Reduce mains water consumption by 40% in buildings and outdoor maintenance by identifying and treating every leak and equipping public buildings with water storage where technically possible.
source_quote:
2.  Reduce our consumption of mains water by 40% in the use of buildings and in the maintenance of outdoor areas: The City Council has set itself the target of identifying and treating every leak in all of its buildings, as well as equipping all public buildings, where technically possible, with a water storage capacity equivalent to their needs for watering plants, sanitary facilities, road cleaning, vehicles or vegetable gardens
(rainwater tank, water from lowering the water table, swimming pools, canal, grey water).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified water-efficiency target with explicit implementation measures. Climate hazards are explicitly discussed in the section context.

parent_statement: Water, a precious resource to be consumed sustainably
policy_statement: Equip the municipality with rainwater storage capacity covering the equivalent of 20 days' use for watering green spaces and cleaning.
source_quote: -  Equip the municipality with a rainwater storage capacity. Together, these installations will cover the equivalent of 20 days' use (watering green spaces and cleaning).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified infrastructure target for water resilience and conservation.

parent_statement: Water, a precious resource to be consumed sustainably
policy_statement: During renovation, equip public buildings with rainwater storage capacity equivalent to 20 days' use where conditions allow.

extraction_rationale: This is a specific building-retrofit requirement tied to water resilience.

parent_statement: Water, a precious resource to be consumed sustainably

source_quote: -  Increase access to drinking water: Public drinking fountains will be easily accessible in densely built-up areas and in the immediate vicinity of every sports ground and children's play area.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete public infrastructure commitment related to heat resilience and water access.

policy_statement: Combat the growing risk of flooding.
source_quote:
## 2. Combatting the growing risk of flooding

-  Generalise Integrated Stormwater Management (ISWM) during public works in priority areas and upstream of them
-  The City Council is committed to permeabilising or disconnecting from the sewers at least 250,000m² of impermeable surfaces
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella initiative with multiple flood-risk reduction sub-actions.

parent_statement: Combatting the growing risk of flooding
policy_statement: Ensure 100% of roadworks in priority intervention zones and upstream of flood-prone areas incorporate integrated rainwater management.

extraction_rationale: This is a quantified adaptation requirement for public works.

parent_statement: Combatting the growing risk of flooding
policy_statement: Permeabilise or disconnect from sewers at least 250,000 m² of impermeable surfaces in the priority intervention zone of the Molenbeek catchment area.
source_quote: -  The City Council is committed to permeabilising or disconnecting from the sewers at least 250,000m² of impermeable surfaces in the priority intervention zone of the Molenbeek catchment area. This objective can be achieved with a strategy that gives priority to action on the Heysel plateau, and includes action by the City Council and local interested parties.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified flood-risk reduction target using permeabilisation as the mechanism.

parent_statement: Combatting the growing risk of flooding

parent_statement: Combatting the growing risk of flooding
policy_statement: Carry out at least 50 voluntary integrated rainwater management system projects by local interested parties in priority intervention zones through awareness campaigns and grants.

-  The City Council undertakes to do its utmost, in cooperation with the Regional Council and the municipalities in the same catchment area, to reduce the discharge of sewage into the canal and the Seine river.

parent_statement: A city that meets the demand for sustainable, accessible food

policy_statement: Protect and develop local and urban biodiversity.

- o 100% of the city's green spaces to be labelled Réseau Nature by 2030.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete ecological management policy with a quantified coverage target.

parent_statement: Protecting and developing local and urban biodiversity
policy_statement: Map and develop the city's green network by 2030 to complement the regional network, including new green spaces, greening with trees, shrubs, climbing plants and green roofs, and identifying priority migration corridors.
source_quote:
-  Develop the City of Brussels' green network - connected to the regional green network, integrating flora and fauna. Creation of a green network will be carried out in conjunction with local operators, while respecting third party rights:

Priority migration corridors will have been identified, giving rise to new measures to promote biodiversity and species migration.
extraction_rationale: This is a detailed, time-bound ecological infrastructure policy.

parent_statement: Protecting and developing local and urban biodiversity

extraction_rationale: This is a spatial accessibility target for urban green infrastructure.

parent_statement: Protecting and developing local and urban biodiversity
policy_statement: Develop two pilot projects to protect nocturnal biodiversity while guaranteeing a sense of security.

extraction_rationale: This is a quantified pilot-project commitment for biodiversity protection.

parent_statement: Protecting and developing local and urban biodiversity
policy_statement: Continue the Neder-Over-Hembeek Urban Forest project to create an extensive biodiversity conservatory.

parent_statement: Protecting and developing local and urban biodiversity
policy_statement: Adopt and ensure compliance with a tree charter for local operators to guide species selection, planting and tree management.
source_quote: -  Adopt and ensure compliance with a tree charter aimed at all local operators, so that the right species can be planted in the right places and in the right way, and these trees can be managed with respect. Integrate these principles as early as possible in the project and throughout the life of the trees to maximise all the possible benefits of the plantations.
extraction_rationale: This is a governance and standards-based policy for urban tree planting and management.

policy_statement: Preserve biodiversity on a global scale.

Linked to the regional Citizens' Climate Assembly, the Local Climate Assembly ensures transparent monitoring and sharing of the actions carried out in the area, by identifying the CO2 emissions produced by all the players in the area, as well as the actions aimed at better adapting the area to climate change.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete governance mechanism with explicit mitigation and adaptation monitoring functions.
