policy_statement: Budapest will reduce its emissions by 40% by 2030 compared to the 2015 base year.
source_quote:
Accordingly, the Municipality of Budapest has set the target to reduce its emissions by 40% by 2030 compared to the base year of 2015.

Chart 2: The decarbonisation target of Budapest
section_header: 4.1.   REDUCTION OF THE EMISSION OF GREENHOUSE GASES (MITIGATION)
extraction_rationale: This is a clear quantified emissions-reduction target with a deadline and baseline, so it qualifies as a standalone climate policy target.

policy_statement: Budapest commits to a long-term target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by at least 80% by 2050 compared to 1990 and/or below 2 metric tons per capita annually.
source_quote: In addition to the foregoing, the Municipality of Budapest has also assumed a long-term commitment by joining the Under 2 Coalition. By joining the Coalition, the parties undertake to reduce their emission of greenhouse gases by 80% as a minimum by 2050 compared to the values in 1990 and/or reduce their annual per capita emission below 2 metric tons.
section_header: 4.1.   REDUCTION OF THE EMISSION OF GREENHOUSE GASES (MITIGATION)
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified long-term mitigation commitment tied to coalition membership. It is a policy target even though it references an external initiative.

policy_statement: Improve the energy efficiency of buildings, industrial production and tertiary-sector facilities while increasing the share of renewables.
source_quote:
## Má -1 Improving the energy efficiency of buildings, industrial production and service provider facilities and increasing the ratio of renewables

The energy consumption of buildings is primarily responsible for the CO2 emission of Budapest. The majority of the energy used is generated from fossil resources, whereas the ratio of renewables still remains low.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella mitigation objective with multiple named sub-measures M1-M7 listed beneath it, so it should be extracted as a parent policy.

parent_statement: Má -1 Improving the energy efficiency of buildings, industrial production and service provider facilities and increasing the ratio of renewables
policy_statement: Refurbish and operate municipal buildings and public-service-provider facilities in an energy-conscious way, targeting 12,156 MWh/year energy savings and 2,460 tCO2/year by 2030.
source_quote:
The Municipality of Budapest maintains numerous institutions and companies, thus operates a large number of buildings and facilities (social institutions, theatres, educational institutions, public utility companies, etc.), and may directly influence their energy consumption and energy efficient renovation and operation.

Target year value: 12,156 MWh/annum 2,460 tCO2 /annum
extraction_rationale: M1 is a specific named intervention with quantified target outcomes and implementation responsibility. It is clearly a sub-action under objective Má-1.

parent_statement: Má -1 Improving the energy efficiency of buildings, industrial production and service provider facilities and increasing the ratio of renewables
policy_statement: Upgrade public lighting by replacing obsolete luminaires with LEDs, targeting 18,242 MWh/year savings and 4,200 tCO2/year by 2027.
source_quote:
According to the data of BDK, of the 183 thousand luminaries used in Budapest for public lighting, about 110 thousand are worn-out and technically outdated and of high energy consumption and operating cost and will need to be replaced in the next 5 years. The effect of the total upgrading project has been estimated by assuming that they would be replaced by LED luminaries.

Target year value: 18,242 MWh/annum 4,200 tCO 2 /annum
extraction_rationale: M2 is a concrete infrastructure upgrade with a named technology and quantified savings target, making it a clear policy measure.

parent_statement: Má -1 Improving the energy efficiency of buildings, industrial production and service provider facilities and increasing the ratio of renewables
policy_statement: Refurbish one third of Budapest's residential buildings through insulation, heating modernization, and renewable technologies by 2030.
source_quote:
One of the most effective ways to mitigate GHG emissions in Budapest is to reduce the energy demand of residential buildings, resulting in the mitigation of the consumption of electricity, natural gas and other energy sources. The measure comprises the following elements: thermal insulation of external walls; modernisation of the heating system; installation of renewable energy technologies.

The renovation of one third of the residential buildings in Budapest has a saving potential of 4,809,105 MWh energy and 981,977 t CO2 per annum.
extraction_rationale: M3 is a specific building retrofit program with explicit interventions and quantified mitigation potential. It is a core sub-policy under Má-1.

parent_statement: Má -1 Improving the energy efficiency of buildings, industrial production and service provider facilities and increasing the ratio of renewables
policy_statement: Promote solar photovoltaic development to reach about 1,500 MW installed capacity in Budapest by 2030.
source_quote:
According to the data available, the portion of the buildings and roofs in Budapest which are suitable for the installation of solar panels and the areas suitable for being used for this purpose are sufficient for the installation of solar panels of a total installed capacity of 1500 MW (1750 MWp). This would require a (roof) area of ca. 10 million m2.

Target year value: 2,031,409 MWh/annum 467,224 t CO 2 /annum
extraction_rationale: M4 is a named renewable-energy deployment measure with quantified capacity and emissions outcomes. It is a clear mitigation policy.

parent_statement: Má -1 Improving the energy efficiency of buildings, industrial production and service provider facilities and increasing the ratio of renewables
policy_statement: Develop and reconstruct the district heating system to increase efficiency and renewable/waste heat use, targeting 719,066 MWh/year savings and 176,135 tCO2/year by 2030.
source_quote:
The purpose of the district heating development program is to refurbish and develop the district heating system (own heat generators, pipelines, heat centres), and to increase the ratio of renewable energy resources as well as to realize 'efficient district heating and cooling' in terms of Article 2, Section 41 of Directive 2012/27/EU.

Target year value: 719,066 MWh/annum 176,135 tCO 2 /annum
extraction_rationale: M5 is a concrete infrastructure and energy-system modernization measure with quantified targets and explicit renewable-energy criteria.

parent_statement: Má -1 Improving the energy efficiency of buildings, industrial production and service provider facilities and increasing the ratio of renewables
policy_statement: Conduct surveys and research on renewable-energy application, sustainable energy management, and circular economy feasibility by 2022.
source_quote:
Appropriate planning, emission reduction and increasing the ratio of renewables substantially necessitate a more precise presentation of the possibilities for the residential and non-residential application of renewable energy resources in Budapest (solar panel and geothermal potentials primarily). As part of this, it is important to survey and model the existing buildings in detail, to create a database.

Timeframe 2022
extraction_rationale: M6 is more preparatory than operational, but it still qualifies because it is a specific named intervention with a timeframe and budget. Slightly weaker as a policy because direct outcomes are not quantified.

parent_statement: Má -1 Improving the energy efficiency of buildings, industrial production and service provider facilities and increasing the ratio of renewables
policy_statement: Support industrial and tertiary-sector decarbonisation by informing businesses about advanced technologies and financing options, targeting 390,000 MWh/year savings and 78,780 tCO2/year by 2030.
source_quote:
The municipality plays a role in this respect primarily in providing information to businesses, making them acquainted with state-of-the-art technologies and providing assistance in finding the necessary financing for applying those technologies. 

Target year value: 390,000 MWh/annum 78,780 tCO 2 /annum
extraction_rationale: M7 is a named decarbonisation support measure with quantified target outcomes, though the mechanism is softer and information-based rather than regulatory.

policy_statement: Improve transport energy efficiency and support environmentally friendly transport modes.
source_quote:
## Má -2  Improving  the  energy  efficiency  of  transport  infrastructures  and  supporting  and developing environmentally friendly forms of transport

The energy consumption of transport is responsible for ca. 28% of all greenhouse gas emissions in Budapest.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella transport mitigation objective with sub-measures M8-M12 beneath it, so it should be treated as a parent policy.

parent_statement: Má -2 Improving the energy efficiency of transport infrastructures and supporting and developing environmentally friendly forms of transport
policy_statement: Develop public transport vehicles, services, and infrastructure to raise public transport's modal share to 50% by 2030.
source_quote:
According to the Budapest Mobility Plan (BMP), the share of public transport shall be increased to 50% by 2030 with consideration to the distances covered. (The recommended target values determined for other means of transport, again based on passenger km-s, are 15% for walking, 5% for cycling and 30% for passenger cars.)

Target year value: 1,908,791 MWh/annum 496,286 tCO 2 /annum
extraction_rationale: M8 is a concrete transport policy with a quantified modal-share target and quantified energy/emissions impacts.

parent_statement: Má -2 Improving the energy efficiency of transport infrastructures and supporting and developing environmentally friendly forms of transport
policy_statement: Expand cycling and pedestrian infrastructure to raise cycling's share to 5% and walking's share to 15% by 2030.
source_quote:
By means of the preferred development of cycling traffic, the share of cycling should be increased to 5% by 2030 based on the distances covered. 

The goal is to continue constructing the central areas of the external parts of the city with preference to pedestrians and to integrate the pedestrian and cyclist friendly public spaces of the inner parts of the city in a uniform network, a liveable city functioning as an organism.
extraction_rationale: M9 is a specific infrastructure measure with explicit modal-share targets and quantified savings in the indicator table.

parent_statement: Má -2 Improving the energy efficiency of transport infrastructures and supporting and developing environmentally friendly forms of transport
policy_statement: Facilitate electric and low-emission vehicle uptake, targeting 30% of vehicles in environmental class 5 by 2030.
source_quote:
Despite the continuously growing demand, the number of electric or low emission cars is still low in Budapest (in 2019, there were 8,205 cars registered in Budapest with green licence plate), therefore the development of e-mobility is a particularly important task.

Target year value: 30% (225,000 pcs) 19,843 MWh/annum; 8,733 tCO 2 /annum
extraction_rationale: M10 is a named transport electrification measure with a quantified adoption target and supporting interventions such as charging stations and parking incentives.

parent_statement: Má -2 Improving the energy efficiency of transport infrastructures and supporting and developing environmentally friendly forms of transport
policy_statement: Promote car-sharing and car-pooling systems, targeting 1,200 car-sharing vehicles by 2030.
source_quote:
The objective of the integrated transport organisation entity of Budapest is to establish the rules of a uniform, transparent, universally accessible and, last but not least, environmentally friendly, integrated community system of car rental or car sharing. 

Target year value: 1,200 pcs 433 MWh/annum; 191 tCO 2 /annum
extraction_rationale: M11 is a specific mobility-system intervention with a target indicator. It is somewhat softer than infrastructure mandates but still qualifies as a named policy measure.

parent_statement: Má -2 Improving the energy efficiency of transport infrastructures and supporting and developing environmentally friendly forms of transport
policy_statement: Use traffic control, low-emission zones, congestion charging, and P+R infrastructure to reduce car use and expand P+R capacity to 22,000 spaces by 2030.
source_quote:
The designation of climate protection zones may be the 'ante-room' to the banning of combustion engines in the farther future. The introduction of an emission-proportionate congestion charge may be an effective tool to achieving the traffic policy goals of the city, provided that it is realized as a result of proper legal, economic and infrastructural preparation.

Target year value: 22,000 pcs 117,280 MWh/annum 32,877 tCO 2 /annum
extraction_rationale: M12 contains multiple concrete regulatory and infrastructure interventions, including tolls and low-emission zones, plus a quantified P+R target. Because the measure itself is broad and named, it is extracted as one sub-policy.

policy_statement: Increase the size and quality of green areas to enhance carbon absorption capacity.
source_quote:
## Má -3  Increasing  the  size  of  green  areas  and  improving  their  quality  to  enhance  their  carbon  absorption capacity

The ratio of green areas is quite low in Budapest, therefore their carbon absorption capacity is weak as well, although green areas would have an important role in the absorption of CO2.
section_header: 4.1.   REDUCTION OF THE EMISSION OF GREENHOUSE GASES (MITIGATION)
extraction_rationale: This is a mitigation objective, but the document explicitly redirects implementation to adaptation section Aá-1 rather than listing separate sub-items here. Extracted as an individual objective to preserve the mitigation commitment without duplicating A1-A7 as children here.

policy_statement: Carry out local climate modelling, runoff modelling, and detailed vulnerability assessment for Budapest by 2022.
source_quote:
As part of this measure, forecasts need to be generated on a local level (cells of 1-5 km), based on a scientifically substantiated climate model. 

It is also necessary to conduct a detailed vulnerability examination for the territory of Budapest based on these models, based on which we can determine and parameterise the necessary adaptation measures.
extraction_rationale: Aá0 is a standalone preparatory adaptation measure with a timeframe and budget. It is not just background analysis because it commits to producing specific models and assessments.

policy_statement: Develop Budapest's green-blue infrastructure.
source_quote:
## Aá -1 Development of the green -blue infrastructure

The climate of the city is influenced by the ratio of inactive, paved surfaces and biologically active, green areas and water surfaces to a large extent.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear umbrella adaptation objective with sub-actions A1-A7 listed beneath it, so it should be extracted as a parent policy.

parent_statement: Aá -1 Development of the green -blue infrastructure
policy_statement: Increase and improve green areas and water surfaces, raising Budapest's cumulative green area intensity from 52.5% to 57% by 2030.
source_quote:
The primary task is to increase the quantity and improve the quality of the areas owned and managed by the Municipality of Budapest by the implementation of programs and projects suited to the priority objectives determined in the Green Infrastructure Development and Maintenance Action Plan.

Target year value: 57%
extraction_rationale: A1 is a specific green-blue infrastructure measure with a quantified target indicator. It explicitly serves both adaptation and carbon absorption.

parent_statement: Aá -1 Development of the green -blue infrastructure
policy_statement: Improve green-area and forest provision, increasing per-capita green area from 6 to 7 m2/person by 2030 and to 9 m2/person by 2050.
source_quote:
Currently, the per capita size of green area (public garden, public park) is only 6 m2, in contrast to the internationally recommended (WHO) target value of 9 m2/person. 

By realizing the planned increase in the per capita green area supply by 1 m2 by 2030, CO2 absorption could be increased by 140 t CO2/annum.
extraction_rationale: A2 is a concrete greening and afforestation measure with explicit quantitative targets and explicit carbon absorption benefits.

parent_statement: Aá -1 Development of the green -blue infrastructure
policy_statement: Revitalize small watercourses and blue infrastructure, targeting 10 km of revitalized sections by 2026.
source_quote:
The purpose of the measure is to implement complex revitalisation programs which facilitate the environmental, ecological, functional (surface drainage, water habitat, recreation) and landscape architectural integration and improve the characteristics of small water courses.

Target year value: 10km
extraction_rationale: A3 is a specific ecosystem-based adaptation measure with a quantified implementation target and named pilot projects.

parent_statement: Aá -1 Development of the green -blue infrastructure
policy_statement: Prepare and implement a 10-year public-space tree planting plan, increasing municipally managed public-space trees from 107,000 to 130,000 by 2030.
source_quote:
It is necessary to elaborate a 10 years' plan for planting trees in public spaces, then to continue rolling planning, specifying an annual timetable including not only the venues and the numbers, but also data relevant to quality development.

Target year value: 130,000 pcs;
extraction_rationale: A4 is a concrete planning and implementation commitment with a quantified tree target and explicit climate-adaptive species selection criteria.

parent_statement: Aá -1 Development of the green -blue infrastructure
policy_statement: Amend higher-level and municipal legal rules to strengthen tree protection, planting standards, and construction-site tree safeguards.
source_quote:
It is necessary to initiate the amendment of higher-level legal rules to ensure the more effective protection of trees. Gov. Decree 346/2008 (XII.30.) on the protection of woody plants shall be supplemented with the provision that the Chief Clark may only make a decision in the proceeding for the felling and replacement of trees by involving an expert.

The relevant regulation of the Municipality of Budapest (Regulation No. 10/2005. (III. 8.) of the General Assembly) requires some update to include provisions concerning the planting and protection of avenues and individual trees.
extraction_rationale: A5 clearly qualifies because it proposes specific legal amendments and standards. It is regulatory rather than aspirational.

parent_statement: Aá -1 Development of the green -blue infrastructure
policy_statement: Establish and operate a uniform, up-to-date green space cadastre for all of Budapest by 2024.
source_quote:
It is necessary to create an up-to-date green space cadastre encompassing the entire public administrative area of Budapest based on a uniform methodology in cooperation with the district municipalities and organisations concerned, which shall take stock not only of trees, but of parks, forests, semi-natural areas and gardens as well.

Timeframe 2024
extraction_rationale: A6 is a specific administrative and monitoring intervention with a timeframe and budget. It supports climate adaptation planning and management.

parent_statement: Aá -1 Development of the green -blue infrastructure
policy_statement: Promote brownfield revitalisation and prioritize green-area uses and temporary greening over new greenfield development through planning instruments and support schemes.
source_quote:
In the interest of increasing the green area intensity to offset emissions, urban planning instruments should be modified in the future by giving priority to the use of land as green areas, especially in the regions less supplied with green areas (public parks and public gardens) and forest areas. In addition, the developments should be diverted to brown-field areas instead of making greenfield investments.

Accordingly, it is advisable not to designate any new areas to be built up in the Settlement Structure Plan, unless it is justified.
extraction_rationale: A7 is a planning and land-use policy with explicit intervention logic and a climate-related objective. The target indicator is vague, but the intervention is concrete enough to qualify.

policy_statement: Mitigate the heat island effect in the built environment.
source_quote:
## Aá -2 Mitigation of the heat island effect in the built environment

Due to the characteristics of Budapest, the intensity of the heat island effect is high in the city, with special regard to the downtown area and the Pest side.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella adaptation objective with sub-actions A8-A9 beneath it.

parent_statement: Aá -2 Mitigation of the heat island effect in the built environment
policy_statement: Protect ventilation corridors and maintain sufficient street airspace ratios through planning controls, reducing build-up in key ventilation areas by 2030.
source_quote:
The Municipality of Budapest can provide for the ventilation corridors of significance for the settlement structure in its Settlement Structure Plan (TSZT) and the Rules of Urban Planning (FRSZ). In these areas, the designation of new areas to be built up or the raising of the permitted building height may not be supported.

Target year value: it should be reduced
extraction_rationale: A8 is a regulatory urban-planning measure aimed explicitly at reducing heat-island impacts. The target is directional rather than numeric, but the mechanism is concrete.

parent_statement: Aá -2 Mitigation of the heat island effect in the built environment
policy_statement: Promote climate-friendly construction materials and technologies in procurement, tenders, and municipal investments, including permeable and high-albedo surfaces, green roofs, and green facades.
source_quote:
Climate protection has to be a priority criterion in the public procurement processes and the tender-based support schemes of the Municipality of Budapest. 

Instead of traditional asphalt, 'cooler' and, if possible, permeable surfaces of higher albedo should be applied. In addition, the energy consumption of the individual buildings may be reduced considerably by the application of green roofs and green façades as well.
extraction_rationale: A9 is a concrete procurement and design standard measure. It explicitly names adaptation-oriented materials and technologies and also mentions energy savings.

policy_statement: Develop the flood control system.
source_quote:
## Aá -3 Development of the flood control system

Because of increased flood hazard, there are large areas in the capital city at risk.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella adaptation objective with one listed sub-action A10.

parent_statement: Aá -3 Development of the flood control system
policy_statement: Construct and upgrade flood control structures so that flood protection lines meeting DFE + 1.3m safety level increase from 33.73 km to 69 km by 2030.
source_quote:
Due to climate effects seen on the entire catchment area of the Danube, flood waves reaching or even exceeding a water level of 8 m by far may arise in the subsequent period as well just like in recent year, therefore the flood protection line needs to be developed urgently. The development and further construction of existing flood control structures can provide for the regulated propagation of flood waves and the prevention of various kinds of flood damage.

Target year value: 69 km
extraction_rationale: A10 is a classic adaptation infrastructure policy with a quantified target and clear implementation scope.

policy_statement: Implement adaptive rainwater management.
source_quote:
## Aá -4 Adaptive rainwater management

Besides flood hazard, short-term but high-intensity incidents of a large volume of precipitation and flash floods have also been causing more and more severe problems.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella adaptation objective with sub-actions A11-A12.

parent_statement: Aá -4 Adaptive rainwater management
policy_statement: Create a hybrid rainwater drainage and runoff-regulation system for Budapest, including modelling, infrastructure review, and phased drainage upgrades.
source_quote:
In the case of Budapest, we could aim at the creation of a hybrid system, so that the regulation and drainage of rainwater could be the most effective and most economical in the individual subareas, in accordance with the given circumstances.

The complete mid- and long-term rainwater drainage concept for Budapest is to be created with regard to all of these factors.
extraction_rationale: A11 is a substantial adaptation infrastructure and planning measure with a defined intervention package and budget, though no single numeric outcome indicator is given.

parent_statement: Aá -4 Adaptive rainwater management
policy_statement: Support on-site rainwater retention, infiltration, delayed runoff, and greywater use through planning, regulation, and support schemes.
source_quote:
Rainwater management should be realized in an adaptive manner, as close as possible to the catchment area, in line with the National Water Strategy (Jenő Kvassay Plan). 

In order to promote the application and spread of such systems, they need to be integrated in the planning of municipal or governmental investment projects and, for private investments, the appropriate regulatory instruments and the related support system should be elaborated.
extraction_rationale: A12 is a concrete adaptation measure with explicit interventions and governance tools. It is somewhat broad but clearly policy-like.

policy_statement: Prepare for extreme weather conditions and the health impacts of climate change.
source_quote:
## Aá -5 Preparation for extreme weather conditions and the health impacts of climate change

Extreme heat, strong UV radiation, gusts of wind, extreme precipitation events and other extreme weather conditions and the ensuing floods, flash floods, inundations and drought periods jeopardize human health, involve the risk of accidents and may cause material damage.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella adaptation objective with sub-actions A13-A16.

parent_statement: Aá -5 Preparation for extreme weather conditions and the health impacts of climate change
policy_statement: Adapt transport systems and public utility networks to extreme weather through resilient design standards, materials, and emergency scenarios.
source_quote:
Transport systems and public utility networks should be designed with consideration to the prognostications that temperatures can be expected to increase and heatwaves, storms and flash floods will occur more frequently. 

It is recommended to elaborate an emergency scenario for the resolution of operating disruptions caused by extreme weather conditions.
extraction_rationale: A13 is a specific adaptation planning and design measure for transport infrastructure. It is concrete despite lacking a numeric target.

parent_statement: Aá -5 Preparation for extreme weather conditions and the health impacts of climate change
policy_statement: Maintain and update hazard control, flood protection, evacuation, and emergency information systems to address climate-related extreme events.
source_quote:
It is necessary to examine and ensure that emergency plans manage extreme events which may occur due to climate change (drought, flood, flash flood, damage to critical infrastructure, etc.), and to review the publication prepared to inform the citizens.

In connection with the activity of the Municipality of Budapest related to flood and inland water protection, it is necessary to maintain and review flood control structures and equipment.
extraction_rationale: A14 is a concrete emergency-management and hazard-control commitment tied to climate hazards. It is operational and institutional rather than infrastructural.

parent_statement: Aá -5 Preparation for extreme weather conditions and the health impacts of climate change
policy_statement: Assess climate vulnerability of water bases and drinking water supply and upgrade water production wells and operations accordingly by 2022.
source_quote:
Due to climate change affecting the catchment area of the Danube as well, extreme weather conditions are becoming more and more frequent: based on the weather trends experienced and evaluated in recent years, there is a justified demand for elaborating operational changes for periods hit by extreme drought.

Budapest Waterworks has started the development of 60 water production wells as part of a project.
extraction_rationale: A15 is a specific adaptation measure with a timeframe, budget, and concrete operational/infrastructure response to drought and low-water risks.

parent_statement: Aá -5 Preparation for extreme weather conditions and the health impacts of climate change
policy_statement: In preserving and renovating municipal buildings, prioritize design against windstorms, floods, flash floods, and inundation.
source_quote:
The foreseeable increase in the frequency of windstorms means a source of physical hazard for the building stock of the Municipality of Budapest, affecting primarily the structural boundaries of buildings, i.e. structures on the façades and roofs. Floods, flash floods and inundations also have a significant effect on the building stock.

For all these reasons, the Municipality has to pay priority attention concerning its own building stock to the proper sizing of support structures, basements, windows, sun shades and waterproofing sheets.
extraction_rationale: A16 is a concrete adaptation design standard for municipal buildings. It lacks quantified targets but clearly commits to a specific intervention approach.

policy_statement: Mitigate the vulnerability of natural and landscape values.
source_quote:
## Aá -6 Mitigation of the vulnerability of natural and landscape values

Natural elements are also exposed to high risk due to the effects of climate change.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella adaptation objective with sub-actions A17-A19.

parent_statement: Aá -6 Mitigation of the vulnerability of natural and landscape values
policy_statement: Prepare a detailed climate change risk and vulnerability assessment for natural values by 2023.
source_quote:
Effective nature conservation and the confining of invasive animal and plant species requires the examination of the sensitivity of natural values to climate change as part of regular status assessment, based on the forecasts of a precise climate model and the assessment and monitoring of risks and vulnerabilities.

Timeframe 2023
extraction_rationale: A17 is a specific assessment commitment with a timeframe. It is preparatory but still a concrete adaptation policy action.

parent_statement: Aá -6 Mitigation of the vulnerability of natural and landscape values
policy_statement: Expand protected natural sites of local importance from 861 ha to 1,200 ha by 2026.
source_quote:
The primary objective is to protect the botanical, zoological, geological and landscape values of protected areas, to preserve biodiversity, to reduce conflicts concerning nature and the achieve that new areas are declared to be protected sites on an estimated area of 800 ha based on preliminary surveys.

Target year value: 1200 ha
extraction_rationale: A18 is a clear land-protection policy with a quantified target area and deadline.

parent_statement: Aá -6 Mitigation of the vulnerability of natural and landscape values
policy_statement: Manage protected natural areas and confine invasive plant and animal species, reducing invasive plant coverage in protected local sites by 2030.
source_quote:
One of the most important tasks of this management is to confine invasive species in the areas concerned, but nature conservation aspects need to be enforced not only in protected natural sites, but in the 'urban ecosystem' as well. In the urban ecosystem, special emphasis must be laid on the confinement of plant species causing allergy as well.

Target year value: it should be reduced
extraction_rationale: A19 is a concrete ecosystem management measure with a directional target indicator. It is adaptation-focused through biodiversity resilience.

policy_statement: Promote climate-conscious city management that leads by example in climate protection.
source_quote:
## SZ-1  Climate  conscious  city  management:  cooperative  city  management  taking  the  lead  in  climate protection

It is of priority importance to realize some kind of internal awareness-raising, i.e. to improve climate consciousness in the operation of the Mayor's Office and the public service providers as well.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella awareness/governance objective with sub-actions SZ1-SZ4.

parent_statement: SZ-1 Climate conscious city management: cooperative city management taking the lead in climate protection
policy_statement: Support climate-conscious operation of the Mayor's Office and municipal companies, including staff training reaching 1,500 participants by 2030.
source_quote:
The goal of the measure is to support and encourage initiatives promoting the climateconscious operation of the Mayor's Office and its companies and to introduce climate protection measures.

Target year value: 1,500 persons
extraction_rationale: SZ1 is a concrete internal capacity-building measure with a target indicator and annual budget. Climate effects are indirect because it changes organizational behavior.

parent_statement: SZ-1 Climate conscious city management: cooperative city management taking the lead in climate protection
policy_statement: Integrate horizontal climate protection principles into urban development, sectoral planning, legal rules, tenders, and major investments.
source_quote: This measure is intended to integrate climate protection measures and/or horizontal climate protection principles during the preparation and review of urban development and thematic sectoral strategies, thus establish correlation of the documents with the Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plan. It is also necessary to integrate climate-related aspects in the due diligence and detailed planning of major investments from the point of view of climate protection.
extraction_rationale: SZ2 is a governance mainstreaming policy with explicit institutional application across planning and legal instruments. It is broad but concrete enough to qualify.

parent_statement: SZ-1 Climate conscious city management: cooperative city management taking the lead in climate protection
policy_statement: Operate the Budapest Climate Change Platform and online best-practice platform, targeting 20 sessions and 30,000 visitors by 2030.
source_quote:
The purpose of the measure is to establish long-term cooperation with stakeholders playing a strategic role in the promotion of climate consciousness and the sharing of best practices. The platform facilitates continuous communication with target groups on a wide scale, the collection and sharing of target group specific and thematic contents and best practices.

Target year value: 20 sessions, 30,000 visitors
extraction_rationale: SZ3 is a specific institutional cooperation and information-sharing measure with quantified activity targets.

parent_statement: SZ-1 Climate conscious city management: cooperative city management taking the lead in climate protection
policy_statement: Establish cooperation with companies, chambers, and associations to support and help finance Budapest's mitigation, adaptation, and awareness measures.
source_quote:
The purpose of the measure is to establish cooperation between the Municipality of Budapest and companies and to involve companies in the implementation and financing of the mitigation, adaptation and awareness-raising measure of Budapest, e.g. in the field of the expansion and development of green areas, solar panel investments and communication campaigns.

In order to reduce climate risks and reinforce climate consciousness in the corporate sector, it is necessary to establish cooperation and enter into thematic agreements with the interest groups and professional organisations of the corporate sector.
extraction_rationale: SZ4 is a concrete partnership-building measure with explicit climate implementation and financing roles. The target is only directional ('growth'), so specificity is moderate.

policy_statement: Strengthen environmental culture and responsibility among citizens and economic actors.
source_quote:
## SZ-2 Climate conscious citizens: strengthening the environmental awareness and responsibility among the population and economic actors

In addition to the influencing of the lifestyle, the consumption habits, the activities and the way of thinking of the population and the strengthening of responsibility and climate consciousness among citizens, it is the attitude and the decisions of the businesses in the capital city which will fundamentally determine the success of the climate strategy.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella awareness objective with sub-actions SZ5-SZ7.

parent_statement: SZ-2 Climate conscious citizens: strengthening the environmental awareness and responsibility among the population and economic actors
policy_statement: Run thematic awareness campaigns and information activities focused especially on reducing household energy consumption, targeting 432,496 MWh and 85,744 tCO2 annual savings by 2030.
source_quote:
Priority issues include the reduction of the energy consumption of households, the support of the building energy investments of the citizens, the promotion of public transport and cycling as opposed to the use of cars, the preparation of corporate mobility plans, the reduction of waste generation and the creation of conscious consumption and waste collection habits.

Target year value: 432,496 MWh; 85,744 tCO 2 /annum
extraction_rationale: SZ5 is a concrete awareness-raising program with quantified mitigation outcomes, making it stronger than a generic outreach statement.

parent_statement: SZ-2 Climate conscious citizens: strengthening the environmental awareness and responsibility among the population and economic actors
policy_statement: Develop public adaptation knowledge and capacity on heat waves, rainwater management, property protection, and green infrastructure, reaching 100,000 people by 2030.
source_quote:
The population must be made aware of the adverse effects of heatwaves on human health and the necessary and possible ways of protecting against them, with special regard to vulnerable groups of the society (the elderly). 

Target year value: 100 000
extraction_rationale: SZ6 is a specific adaptation-awareness measure with a quantified outreach target and named hazard topics.

parent_statement: SZ-2 Climate conscious citizens: strengthening the environmental awareness and responsibility among the population and economic actors
policy_statement: Create a sustainable, green, and innovative public procurement strategy that embeds climate protection in public services and procurement processes by 2022.
source_quote:
The purpose of the objective is to enforce climate protection aspects in the public procurement practice of the Mayor's Office and the companies owned by the capital city. 

For this reason, the Municipality of Budapest wishes to create its sustainable, green and innovative procurement strategy as soon as possible.
extraction_rationale: SZ7 is a concrete governance and procurement reform commitment with a timeframe. It is cross-cutting and climate-relevant through procurement criteria.

policy_statement: Reduce California greenhouse gas emissions to 1990 levels by 2020.
source_quote: On September 27, 2006, Governor Schwarzenegger signed Assembly Bill 32, the Global Warming Solutions Act of 2006 (Núñez, Chapter 488, Statutes of 2006).  The event marked a watershed moment in California's history.  By requiring in law a reduction of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions to 1990 levels by 2020, California set the stage for its transition to a sustainable, clean energy future.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding statutory statewide emissions target with a clear deadline, so it qualifies as a policy. It is broad but concrete and repeatedly framed as the core legal commitment.

policy_statement: Reduce greenhouse gas emissions to 80 percent below 1990 levels by 2050 under Executive Order S-3-05.
source_quote: According to climate scientists, California and the rest of the developed world will have to cut emissions by 80 percent from today's levels to stabilize the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere and prevent the most severe effects of global climate change.  This long range goal is reflected in California Executive Order S-3-05 that requires an 80 percent reduction of greenhouse gases from 1990 levels by 2050.
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit long-term emissions reduction requirement established by executive order, with a quantified target and date. It is a standalone statewide policy target.

policy_statement: Key elements of California's recommendations for reducing greenhouse gas emissions to 1990 levels by 2020.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella list introducing multiple concrete measures that follow as bullets. Under the hierarchy rules, the introductory initiative should be extracted as a parent because it clearly governs listed sub-actions.

extraction_rationale: This bullet names a specific intervention area and is part of the formal recommended measures. It is concrete enough to qualify even though detailed implementation appears later.

extraction_rationale: This is a quantified statewide target for renewable energy share, making it a clear policy commitment. It is later elaborated as the Renewables Portfolio Standard.

extraction_rationale: This is a named market-based regulatory program and a central commitment of the plan. It is specific and later detailed in its own section.

extraction_rationale: This bullet commits to a defined planning and target-setting intervention for regional transport emissions. It is concrete and later supported by SB 375 implementation details.

extraction_rationale: This is a bundled commitment to implement named measures. It is somewhat umbrella-like, but still qualifies because it references specific existing legal mechanisms and interventions.

parent_statement: Key elements of California's recommendations for reducing greenhouse gas emissions to 1990 levels by 2020.
policy_statement: Create targeted fees including a public goods charge on water use, fees on high global warming potential gases, and a fee to fund AB 32 administration.
source_quote:
- Creating targeted fees, including a public goods charge on water use, fees on high global warming potential gases, and a fee to fund the administrative costs of the State's long term commitment to AB 32 implementation.

After Board approval of this plan, the measures in it will be developed and adopted through the normal rulemaking process, with public input.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear commitment to deploy fee-based instruments. Because the policy itself is the creation of fees, it qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Provide a margin of safety through additional greenhouse gas reduction strategies for uncapped sectors to ensure the 2020 target is met.
source_quote: Provides a 'margin of safety' by recommending additional greenhouse gas emissions reduction strategies to account for measures in uncapped sectors that do not achieve the greenhouse gas emissions reductions estimated in the Proposed Scoping Plan.  Along with the certainty provided by the cap, this will ensure that the 2020 target is met.
section_header: A. Summary of Changes from the Draft Scoping Plan / 1.  General
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete program design commitment to add extra reductions as a safeguard. It is not quantified in tons here, but it is a specific implementation mechanism tied to meeting the statutory target.

policy_statement: Recommend a local government greenhouse gas reduction target of 15 percent below current levels by 2020 for municipal and community-wide emissions.
source_quote: - In recognition of the importance of local governments in the successful implementation of AB 32, adds a section describing this role and recommends a greenhouse gas emissions reduction target for local government municipal and community-wide emissions of a 15 percent reduction from current levels by 2020 to parallel the State's target.
section_header: A. Summary of Changes from the Draft Scoping Plan / 2.  Proposed Measures
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified target with a deadline for local governments. Although framed as a recommendation rather than a mandate, it is specific enough to count as a policy commitment in the scoping plan.

policy_statement: Add four industrial source measures to regulate fugitive emissions from oil and gas recovery and transmission, reduce refinery flaring, and remove the methane exemption for refineries.
source_quote: - Adds four measures to address emissions from industrial sources.  These proposed measures would regulate fugitive emissions from oil and gas recovery and gas transmission activities, reduce refinery flaring, and remove the methane exemption for refineries.  These proposed measures are anticipated to provide 1.5 MMTCO2E of greenhouse gas reductions in 2020.
section_header: A. Summary of Changes from the Draft Scoping Plan / 2.  Proposed Measures
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete package of named regulatory interventions with an estimated emissions impact. It qualifies despite being summarized at a high level because the interventions are specific.

policy_statement: Recommend measures to move the recycling and waste sector toward high recycling and zero waste.
source_quote: - In consultation with the California Integrated Waste Management Board, reassesses potential measures in the Recycling and Waste sector.  As a result of this assessment, ARB increased the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions that can ultimately be anticipated from the Recycling and Waste Sector from 1 to 10 MMTCO2E, recommending measures to move toward high recycling and zerowaste.  Research to help quantify these greenhouse gas emissions is continuing, so only 1 MMTCO2E of these reductions is currently counted towards the AB 32 goal in this plan.
section_header: A. Summary of Changes from the Draft Scoping Plan / 2.  Proposed Measures
extraction_rationale: This is a specific sectoral intervention with an estimated reduction range and named strategy. Some uncertainty remains in quantification, but the policy direction itself is concrete.

policy_statement: Add a High Global Warming Potential mitigation fee to reflect climate impacts in prices and encourage reduced use, lower end-of-life losses, and alternatives.
source_quote: - Adds a High Global Warming Potential (GWP) Mitigation Fee measure to ensure that the climate impact of these gases is reflected in their price to encourage reduced use and end-of-life losses, as well as the development of alternatives.
section_header: A. Summary of Changes from the Draft Scoping Plan / 2.  Proposed Measures
extraction_rationale: This is a clearly defined fee-based instrument with an explicit climate objective and behavioral mechanism. It squarely qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Create greenhouse gas performance standards for new long-term financial investments in base-load electricity generation serving California customers.
source_quote: In 2006, SB 1368 (Perata, Chapter 598, Statutes of 2006) created greenhouse gas performance standards for new long-term financial investments in base-load electricity generation serving California customers.  This law is designed to help spur the transition toward cleaner energy in California by placing restrictions on the ability of utilities to build new carbon-intensive plants or enter into new contracts with high carbon sources of electricity.
section_header: B. Background / 1.  Climate Change Policy in California
extraction_rationale: This is a binding statutory standard affecting electricity procurement and investment. It is a clear regulatory climate policy with a direct mitigation purpose.

source_quote:
AB 32 includes a number of specific requirements for ARB:

- Identify the statewide level of greenhouse gas emissions in 1990 to serve as the emissions limit to be achieved by 2020 (Health and Safety Code (HSC) §38550). In December 2007, the Board approved the 2020 emission limit of 427 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (MMTCO2E) of greenhouse gases.

extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella list of statutory implementation duties with multiple concrete sub-items. Under the hierarchy rules, the introductory list should be treated as a parent.

The reporting regulation serves as a solid foundation to determine greenhouse gas emissions and track future changes in emission levels.
section_header: B. Background / 2.  Assembly Bill 32:  The Global Warming Solutions Act

The Board identified nine Discrete Early Action measures including potential regulations affecting landfills, motor vehicle fuels, refrigerants in cars, port operations and other sources in 2007.  The Board has already approved two Discrete Early Action measures (ship electrification at ports and reduction of high GWP gases in consumer products).
section_header: B. Background / 2.  Assembly Bill 32:  The Global Warming Solutions Act

ARB, along with California's local air districts and the California Climate Action Registry, is working to implement this program.
section_header: B. Background / 2.  Assembly Bill 32:  The Global Warming Solutions Act
extraction_rationale: This is a formal policy commitment with an approved procedure for crediting early action. It is concrete enough to qualify, though details are procedural.

policy_statement: Create a statewide plan to reduce State government greenhouse gas emissions by a minimum of 30 percent by 2020.
source_quote: The State Operations Subgroup has been created to work with State agencies to create a statewide plan to reduce State government's greenhouse gas emissions by a minimum of 30 percent by 2020.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified target for state operations with a deadline. It is a concrete policy commitment even though the detailed plan is to be developed.

policy_statement: Implement most Scoping Plan measures through rulemaking, with regulations adopted by January 1, 2011 and effective at the beginning of 2012, except Discrete Early Actions by January 1, 2010.
source_quote: Most of the measures in this Proposed Scoping Plan will be implemented through the full rulemaking processes at ARB or other agencies.  These processes will provide opportunity for public input as the measures are developed and analyzed in more detail.  With the exception of Discrete Early Actions, which will be in place by January 1, 2010, other regulations are expected to be adopted by January 1, 2011 and take effect at the beginning of 2012.

source_quote: California will not be implementing the measures in this Plan in a vacuum. policy_statement: Establish a State government target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by at least 30 percent below business-as-usual by 2020, about 15 percent below current levels.
source_quote: Therefore, California State government has established a target of reducing its greenhouse gas emissions by a minimum of 30 percent below its estimated business-as-usual emissions by 2020 - approximately a 15 percent reduction from current levels.
section_header: A. The Role of State Government:  Setting an Example
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified target with a deadline for state operations. It is a clear policy commitment.

policy_statement: Require amended CEQA guidelines addressing greenhouse gases to be adopted by January 1, 2010.
source_quote: The Governor's Office of Planning and Research and the Resources Agency are developing proposed amendments to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines to provide guidance on how to address greenhouse gases in CEQA documents.  As required by SB 97 (Chapter 185, Statutes of 2007), the amended CEQA guidelines will be adopted by January 1, 2010.
section_header: A. The Role of State Government:  Setting an Example
extraction_rationale: This is a binding regulatory guidance commitment with a deadline. It qualifies as a policy because it changes planning and permitting treatment of greenhouse gases.

policy_statement: Retain state ownership of quantifiable and marketable greenhouse gas emission reductions associated with state-funded projects.
source_quote: The State expends funds to provide services to California residents - from preserving our natural resources to building and maintaining infrastructure like roads, bridges and dams. California residents should reap all of the benefits of these projects, including any associated quantifiable and marketable reductions in greenhouse gas emissions.  Because of this, California should retain ownership of these greenhouse gas emissions reductions and use them to promote the goals of AB 32 and other goals of the state.
section_header: A. The Role of State Government:  Setting an Example
extraction_rationale: This is a specific policy on ownership and use of emissions reductions from public projects. It is concrete though not a classic emissions-control measure.

policy_statement: Encourage local governments to use the Local Government Operations Protocol to track reductions from municipal operations.
source_quote: To provide local governments guidance on how to inventory and report greenhouse gas emissions from government buildings, facilities, vehicles, wastewater and potable water treatment facilities, landfill and composting facilities, and other government operations, ARB recently adopted the Local Government Operations Protocol.  ARB encourages local governments to use this protocol to track their progress in achieving reductions from municipal operations.
section_header: B. The Role of Local Government: Essential Partners
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adopted protocol and implementation encouragement for local governments. It is somewhat softer than a mandate, but still a concrete policy tool.

policy_statement: Develop a community emissions protocol covering emissions from the community as a whole beyond municipal operations.
source_quote: ARB is also developing an additional protocol for community emissions.  This protocol will go beyond just municipal operations and include emissions from the community as a whole, including residential and commercial activity.
section_header: B. The Role of Local Government: Essential Partners
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete commitment to develop a specific accounting protocol. It is a planning and implementation policy instrument.

policy_statement: Encourage local governments to adopt a municipal operations emissions reduction goal and move toward community emissions goals paralleling a 15 percent reduction from current levels by 2020.
source_quote: In addition to tracking emissions using these protocols, ARB encourages local governments to adopt a reduction goal for municipal operations emissions and move toward establishing similar goals for community emissions that parallel the State commitment to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by approximately 15 percent from current levels by 2020.
section_header: B. The Role of Local Government: Essential Partners
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified target recommendation for local governments. It is not mandatory, but it is specific and policy-like enough to extract.

policy_statement: Implement a broad-based California cap-and-trade program linked with Western Climate Initiative partner programs.
source_quote: Implement a broad-based California cap-and-trade program to provide a firm limit on emissions.  Link the California cap-and-trade program with other Western Climate Initiative Partner programs to create a regional market system to achieve greater environmental and economic benefits for California.  Ensure California's program meets all applicable AB 32 requirements for market-based mechanisms.
section_header: 1.  California Cap-and-Trade Program Linked to Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions
extraction_rationale: This is a named flagship policy with a clear regulatory mechanism and explicit climate objective. It is one of the central commitments of the plan.

policy_statement: Develop cap-and-trade regulations by January 1, 2011 with the program beginning in 2012.
source_quote: Based on the requirements of AB 32, regulations to implement the cap-and-trade program need to be developed by January 1, 2011, with the program beginning in 2012.  This rule development schedule will be coordinated with the WCI timeline for developing a regional cap-and-trade program.
section_header: 1.  California Cap-and-Trade Program Linked to Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete implementation deadline for a major regulatory program. It qualifies as a policy commitment because it sets the adoption schedule.

policy_statement: Phase cap-and-trade coverage to include electricity generation and large industrial facilities in 2012, then upstream fuel combustion and transportation fuels in 2015.
source_quote:
The proposed cap-and-trade measure phases in the following sectors:

Starting in the first compliance period (2012):
- Electricity generation, including imports not covered by a WCI Partner jurisdiction
- Large industrial facilities that emit over 25,000 metric tons CO2E per year.

Starting in the second compliance period (2015):
- Upstream treatment of industrial fuel combustion at facilities with emissions at or below 25,000 metric tons CO2E, and all commercial and residential fuel combustion regulated where the fuel enters into commerce
- Transportation fuel combustion regulated where the fuel enters into commerce.
section_header: 1.  California Cap-and-Trade Program Linked to Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions / California Cap-and-Trade Program
extraction_rationale: This is a detailed phased coverage design with dates and thresholds. It is a concrete regulatory commitment.

policy_statement: Set a preliminary 2020 cap-and-trade emissions limit of 365 MMTCO2E covering about 85 percent of California emissions.
source_quote: As shown in Table 5, the preliminary estimate of the cap on greenhouse gas emissions for sectors covered by the cap-and-trade program is 365 MMTCO2E in 2020, which covers about 85 percent of California's total greenhouse gas emissions.  Greenhouse gas emissions from most of the sectors covered by a cap-and-trade program will also be governed by other measures, including performance standards, efficiency programs, and direct regulations.
section_header: 1.  California Cap-and-Trade Program Linked to Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions / California Cap-and-Trade Program
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified cap level and coverage commitment. Although preliminary pending rulemaking, it is specific enough to qualify.

policy_statement: Phase in regionally coordinated auctions of allowances with at least 10 percent auctioned initially and 25 percent by 2020, with aspiration toward higher shares.
source_quote: The WCI Partner jurisdictions have agreed to phase in regionally coordinated auctions of allowances, with a minimum percentage of allowances auctioned in each period starting with 10 percent in the first compliance period and increasing to 25 percent in 2020.  WCI partners aspire to reach higher auction percentages over time, possibly to 100 percent.
section_header: 1.  California Cap-and-Trade Program Linked to Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions / Linkage with the Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete allowance distribution design with quantified auction shares and dates. Because it concerns auctioning allowances, it is a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Use an allowance reserve price for the first 5 percent of auctioned allowances in the regional cap-and-trade program.
source_quote: The WCI Partner jurisdictions are also proposing the use of an allowance reserve price for the first 5 percent of the auctioned allowances in the regional cap.  A reserve price will help to ensure that the cap is set at a level that will motivate real emissions reductions and may provide an opportunity for the regional cap-and-trade program to provide reductions that exceed the regional target.
section_header: 1.  California Cap-and-Trade Program Linked to Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions / Linkage with the Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions
extraction_rationale: This is a specific market design feature affecting allowance auctions. It qualifies as a financial instrument because it directly structures auction pricing.

policy_statement: Set aside allowances to reward early actions, incentivize local government and efficiency strategies, and target projects in low-income or disadvantaged communities.
source_quote: One approach would be to dedicate a portion of the allowances for such purposes as rewarding early actions to reduce emissions, providing incentives for local governments and others to promote energy efficiency, better land use planning, and other reduction strategies, and targeting projects to reduce emissions in low-income or disadvantaged communities.  This type of dedicated use of allowances is typically referred to as an allowance 'set-aside.'
section_header: 1.  California Cap-and-Trade Program Linked to Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions / Allowances and Revenues
extraction_rationale: This is a specific proposed use of allowance value within the cap-and-trade system. It is a financial instrument because it allocates economic value for targeted purposes, though final design is pending.

policy_statement: Pursue a transition to 100 percent auction of allowances as a goal for distributing cap-and-trade allowances.
source_quote: ARB agrees that a transition to a 100 percent auction is a worthwhile goal for distributing allowances. However a broad set of factors must be considered in evaluating the potential timing of a transition to a full auction including competiveness, potential for emissions leakage, the effect on regulated vs. unregulated industrial sectors, the overall impact on consumers, and the strategic use of auction revenues.
section_header: 1.  California Cap-and-Trade Program Linked to Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions / Allowances and Revenues
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit policy direction on allowance distribution. It is not yet final, but it is a concrete design goal and clearly financial in nature.

policy_statement: Limit the use of offsets and allowances from other systems to no more than 49 percent of required emissions reductions.
source_quote: Consequently, the use of offsets and allowances from other systems are limited to no more than 49 percent of the required reduction of emissions.  This quantitative limit will help provide balance between the need to achieve meaningful emissions reductions from capped sources with the need to provide sources within capped sectors the opportunity for low-cost reduction opportunities that offsets can provide.
section_header: 1.  California Cap-and-Trade Program Linked to Western Climate Initiative Partner Jurisdictions / Offsets
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified compliance rule for offset use. It is a concrete regulatory design feature of the cap-and-trade program.

policy_statement: Implement adopted Pavley standards and a planned second phase, while aligning zero-emission vehicle, alternative fuel, and vehicle technology programs with long-term climate goals.
source_quote: Implement adopted Pavley standards and planned second phase of the program. Align zero-emission vehicle, alternative and renewable fuel and vehicle technology programs with long-term climate change goals.
section_header: 2.  California Light-Duty Vehicle Greenhouse Gas Standards
extraction_rationale: This is the section's headline commitment and names the core vehicle standards policy. It is a concrete regulatory program.

policy_statement: Adopt a second, more stringent phase of the Pavley regulations for light-duty vehicles.
source_quote: The Pavley regulations incorporate both performance standards and market-based compliance mechanisms.  To obtain additional reductions from the light duty fleet, ARB plans to adopt a second, more stringent, phase of the Pavley regulations.
section_header: 2.  California Light-Duty Vehicle Greenhouse Gas Standards / Pavley Greenhouse Gas Vehicle Standards
extraction_rationale: This is a specific planned regulatory tightening of an existing vehicle standard. It is concrete and climate-focused.

policy_statement: Evaluate and potentially implement a feebate program as a backstop or supplement to Pavley standards to achieve equivalent or greater reductions.
source_quote: ARB is currently evaluating the use of a feebate program as the mechanism to secure these reductions.  A feebate regulation would combine a rebate program for low-emitting vehicles with a fee program for high-emitting vehicles.  This program would be designed in a way to generate equivalent or greater cumulative reductions of greenhouse gas emissions compared to what would have been achieved under the Pavley regulations.
section_header: 2.  California Light-Duty Vehicle Greenhouse Gas Standards / Pavley Greenhouse Gas Vehicle Standards
extraction_rationale: This is a specific proposed fee-and-rebate instrument with an explicit emissions objective. It is not yet adopted, but it is concrete enough to qualify as a proposed policy.

policy_statement: Require placement of increasing numbers of zero-emission and near-zero-emission vehicles through the ZEV program and redesign it in 2009 to support 2020 and 2050 targets.
source_quote: Through 2012, the program requires placement of hundreds of ZEVs (including hydrogen fuel cell and battery electric vehicles) and thousands of near-zero emission vehicles (plug-in hybrids, conventional hybrids, compressed natural gas vehicles).  In the mid-term (2012-2015), the program will require placement of increasing numbers of ZEVs and near-zero emission vehicles in California.  In 2009, the Board will consider a proposal that is currently being developed to ensure that the ZEV program is optimally designed to help the State meet its 2020 target and put us on the path to meeting our 2050 target of an 80 percent reduction in greenhouse gas emissions.
section_header: 2.  California Light-Duty Vehicle Greenhouse Gas Standards / Zero-Emission Vehicle Program
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete regulatory deployment requirement with specified vehicle categories and timeframes. It clearly qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Administer the Air Quality Improvement Program to provide about $50 million per year in grants for clean vehicle and equipment projects and alternative fuel research.
source_quote: Under AB 118 (Núñez, Chapter 750, Statutes of 2007), ARB is administering the Air Quality Improvement Program, which provides approximately $50 million per year for grants to fund clean vehicle/equipment projects and research on the air quality impacts of alternative fuels and advanced technology vehicles.
section_header: 2.  California Light-Duty Vehicle Greenhouse Gas Standards / Air Quality Improvement Program/Alternative and Renewable Fuel and Vehicle Technology Program
extraction_rationale: This is a clear funding commitment with an annual amount and defined eligible uses. It qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Fund the Alternative and Renewable Fuel and Vehicle Technology Program at up to $120 million per year from 2008 to 2015 to develop, demonstrate, and deploy innovative fuel and vehicle technologies.
source_quote: AB 118 also created the Alternative and Renewable Fuel and Vehicle Technology Program and authorized CEC to spend up to $120 million per year for over seven years (from 2008-2015) to develop, demonstrate, and deploy innovative technologies to transform California's fuel and vehicle types.  This program creates the opportunities for investment in technologies and fuels that will help meet the Low Carbon Fuel Standard, the AB 1007 (Pavley, Chapter 371, Statutes of 2005) goal of increasing alternative fuels, the AB 32 goal of reducing greenhouse gas emissions to 1990 levels by 2020, and the State's overall goal of reducing greenhouse gas emissions 80 percent below 1990 levels by 2050.
section_header: 2.  California Light-Duty Vehicle Greenhouse Gas Standards / Air Quality Improvement Program/Alternative and Renewable Fuel and Vehicle Technology Program
extraction_rationale: This is a specific multi-year funding authorization with a clear climate technology purpose. It is a financial instrument.

These targets represent a higher goal than existing efficiency targets established by CPUC for the investor-owned utilities due to the inclusion of innovative strategies above traditional utility programs.

Achieve 33 percent renewable energy mix statewide.

CEC estimates that about 12 percent of California's retail electric load is currently met with renewable resources.
extraction_rationale: This is the section's headline target and a quantified statewide renewable energy commitment. It clearly qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Develop and adopt a Low Carbon Fuel Standard reducing the carbon intensity of transportation fuels by at least 10 percent by 2020.
source_quote: To reduce the carbon intensity of transportation fuels, ARB is developing a Low Carbon Fuel Standard (LCFS), which would reduce the carbon intensity of California's transportation fuels by at least ten percent by 2020 as called for by Governor Schwarzenegger in Executive Order S-01-07.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified fuel standard with a deadline and explicit climate objective. It is a clear regulatory policy.

policy_statement: Develop regional passenger vehicle greenhouse gas reduction targets for 2020 and 2035 by September 30, 2010 under SB 375.
source_quote: SB 375 requires ARB to develop, in consultation with metropolitan planning organizations (MPOs), passenger vehicle greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets for 2020 and 2035 by September 30, 2010.  It sets forth a collaborative process to establish these targets, including the appointment by ARB of a Regional Targets Advisory Committee to recommend factors to be considered and methodologies for setting greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets.
section_header: 6.  Regional Transportation-Related Greenhouse Gas Targets / Establishment of Regional Targets
extraction_rationale: This is a statutory target-setting requirement with dates and process. It is a concrete climate planning policy.

policy_statement: Require metropolitan planning organizations to prepare a sustainable communities strategy to meet regional greenhouse gas targets, or an alternative planning strategy if the target is not met.
source_quote: SB 375 requires MPOs to prepare a sustainable communities strategy to reach the regional target provided by ARB.  MPOs would use the sustainable communities strategy for the land use pattern underlying the region's transportation plan.  If the strategy does not meet the target, the MPO must document the impediments and show how the target could be met with an alternative planning strategy.
section_header: 6.  Regional Transportation-Related Greenhouse Gas Targets / Reaching the Targets
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete planning requirement under SB 375. It is a clear policy mechanism for reducing transport emissions.

policy_statement: Provide CEQA relief for development projects consistent with sustainable communities strategies or alternative planning strategies that meet regional targets.

The California Integrated Waste Management Board (CIWMB) with various partners continues to conduct a public awareness campaign to promote sustainable tire practices.  ARB is pursuing a regulation to ensure that tires are properly inflated when vehicles are serviced.  In addition, CEC in consultation with CIWMB is developing an efficient tire program focusing first on data gathering and outreach, then on potential adoption of minimum fuel-efficient tire standards, and lastly on the development of consumer information requirements for replacing tires.
extraction_rationale: This is a package of specific interventions, including a regulation and standards development. It qualifies as policy despite being a bundle.

ARB is proposing to develop and implement additional measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions due to goods movement from trucks, ports and other related facilities.
extraction_rationale: This combines an adopted regulation and a commitment to additional measures for goods movement. It is a concrete policy package.

extraction_rationale: This is a quantified capacity target under a named program. It is a clear policy commitment.

In addition, hybridization of medium- and heavy-duty vehicles would also reduce greenhouse gas emissions through increased fuel efficiency.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific package of vehicle efficiency interventions. It is concrete enough to qualify as policy.

The audit would include an assessment of the impacts of replacing or upgrading older, less efficient units such as boilers and heaters, or replacing the units with combined heat and power (CHP) units.
