policy_statement: Develop measures for oil and gas producers and pipeline operators to reduce methane emissions through leak detection, process modifications, retrofits, new equipment, and best management practices.
source_quote: Two measures would be developed to reduce methane emissions in the oil and gas production and gas transmission processes from leaks and incomplete combustion of methane (used as fuel).  These measures would include improved leak detection, process modifications, equipment retrofits, installation of new equipment, and best management practices.
section_header: 11.  Industrial Emissions / Oil and Gas Recovery Operations and Transmission/Refineries
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete package of regulatory interventions for methane control. It qualifies as policy despite future rulemaking details remaining open.

parent_statement: Industrial emissions measures.
policy_statement: Develop refinery measures to limit greenhouse gas emissions from flares and remove the fugitive methane exemption in refinery VOC regulations.
source_quote: Two measures would be developed for oil refineries.  The first would limit the greenhouse gas emissions from refinery flares while preserving flaring as needed for safety reasons.  The second would remove the current fugitive methane exemption in most refinery Volatile Organic Compounds (VOC) regulations.
section_header: 11.  Industrial Emissions / Oil and Gas Recovery Operations and Transmission/Refineries
extraction_rationale: This is a specific pair of refinery regulatory measures. It clearly qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Support implementation of a high speed rail system between northern and southern California.
source_quote:
Support implementation of a high speed rail system.

A high speed rail (HSR) system is part of the statewide strategy to provide more mobility choice and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.  This measure supports implementation of plans to construct and operate a HSR system between northern and southern California.
extraction_rationale: This is a named infrastructure policy with a clear climate rationale. It is somewhat contingent on voter approval, but still a concrete policy commitment in the plan.

policy_statement: Expand green building practices to reduce the carbon footprint of new and existing buildings.
source_quote:
Expand the use of green building practices to reduce the carbon footprint of California's new and existing inventory of buildings.

Collectively, energy use and related activities by buildings are the second largest contributor to California's greenhouse gas emissions.
extraction_rationale: This is the section's headline commitment and a named strategy. It is broad but clearly policy-oriented and later supported by specific actions.

policy_statement: Include Zero Net Energy goals for new and existing homes and commercial buildings in the Green Building Strategy.
source_quote: The Green Building Strategy includes Zero Net Energy (ZNE) goals for new and existing homes and commercial buildings consistent with the recently-adopted California Long Term Energy Efficiency Strategic Plan.  ARB encourages local governments to raise the bar by adopting 'beyond-code' green building requirements.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific target-setting element within the green building strategy. It qualifies as policy even though exact percentages are not given here.

policy_statement: Establish a 2011 target for commercial buildings so that one quarter of all new buildings reduce energy and water consumption by at least 25 percent beyond code.
source_quote: For commercial buildings, a 2011 target should be established such that a quarter of all new buildings reduce energy and water consumption by at least 25 percent beyond code.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified target with a date and explicit performance level. It clearly qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Establish an environmental performance rating system for homes and commercial buildings and adopt mechanisms to encourage and require retrofits for buildings below minimum standards.
source_quote: This Proposed Scoping Plan recommends the establishment of an environmental performance rating system for homes and commercial buildings and further recommends that California adopt mechanisms to encourage and require retrofits for buildings that do not meet minimum standards of performance.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific policy package involving ratings and retrofit requirements. It is concrete enough to qualify.

policy_statement: Require all new State buildings to exceed existing Green Building Initiative energy goals and achieve LEED-NC Gold, and retrofit existing State buildings to LEED-EB Silver equivalent.
source_quote: The State of California will set an example by requiring all new State buildings to exceed existing Green Building Initiative energy goals and achieve nationally-recognized building sustainability standards such as Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design - New Construction (LEED-NC) 'Gold' certification.  Existing State buildings would also be retrofitted to achieve higher standards equivalent to LEED-EB for existing buildings (EB) 'Silver.'
extraction_rationale: This is a clear requirement for state buildings with named certification standards. It is a concrete policy commitment.

policy_statement: Require all new schools and existing schools seeking modernization funds to meet CHPS 2009 criteria.
source_quote: All new schools should be required to meet the Collaborative for High Performance Schools (CHPS) 2009 criteria.  Existing schools applying for modernization funds should also be required to meet CHPS 2009 criteria.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific requirement tied to school construction and modernization. It is concrete and policy-like, though phrased as a recommendation.

policy_statement: Adopt measures to reduce high global warming potential gases through direct regulations and mitigation fees.
source_quote: High GWP gases are released primarily in two ways.  The first is through leaking systems, and the second is during the disposal process.  Once high GWP materials are released, they persist in the atmosphere for tens or even hundreds of years.  Recommended measures to address this growing problem take the form of direct regulations and use of mitigation fees.
extraction_rationale: This is the section's overarching commitment and names the policy mechanisms. It is a concrete policy package.

policy_statement: Establish an upstream mitigation fee on high global warming potential gases so their climate impact is reflected in product cost.
source_quote: ARB is also proposing to establish an upstream mitigation fee on the use of high GWP gases.  Even with the reductions from the specific high GWP measures described above, this sector's emissions are still projected to more than double from current levels by 2020.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific fee-based instrument with an explicit climate pricing rationale. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Reduce methane emissions at landfills and increase waste diversion, composting, and commercial recycling to move toward zero waste.
source_quote: Reduce methane emissions at landfills.  Increase waste diversion, composting, and commercial recycling.  Move toward zero-waste.
extraction_rationale: This is the section's headline commitment and names several specific interventions. It is a concrete policy package.

policy_statement: Develop a Discrete Early Action measure for landfill methane control.
source_quote: Capturing landfill methane results in greenhouse gas benefits, as well as reductions in other air pollutants such as volatile organic compounds.  ARB is working closely with the California Integrated Waste Management Board (CIWMB) to develop a Discrete Early Action measure for landfill methane control that will be presented to ARB in January.
section_header: 15.  Recycling and Waste / Reduction in Landfill Methane
extraction_rationale: This is a specific regulatory development commitment for landfill methane. It qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Increase commercial recycling through voluntary or mandatory programs, protocols, partnerships with local governments, and financial incentives.
source_quote: As noted by ETAAC, recycling in the commercial sector could be substantially increased.  This could be implemented, for example, through voluntary or mandatory programs, including protocols, enhanced partnerships with local governments, and provision of appropriate financial incentives.  ARB will work with CIWMB to develop and implement these types of programs.
section_header: 15.  Recycling and Waste / High Recycling / Zero Waste
extraction_rationale: This is a specific implementation commitment with named mechanisms. It qualifies as policy, though some details remain open.

policy_statement: Provide direct incentives for the use of compost in agriculture and landscaping and explore incentives for commercial recycling and food scrap collection for composting and anaerobic digestion.
source_quote: ARB will also work with CIWMB, the California Department of Food and Agriculture, the Department of Transportation, and others to provide direct incentives for the use of compost in agriculture and landscaping.  Further, CIWMB will explore the use of incentives for all Recycling and Waste Management measures, including for commercial recycling and for local jurisdictions to encourage the collection of residentially and commercially-generated food scraps for composting and in-vessel anaerobic digestion.
section_header: 15.  Recycling and Waste / High Recycling / Zero Waste
extraction_rationale: This is a specific incentive-based policy package with named applications. It qualifies as a financial instrument because incentives are central.

policy_statement: Preserve forest sequestration and encourage the use of forest biomass for sustainable energy generation.
source_quote:
Preserve forest sequestration and encourage the use of forest biomass for sustainable energy generation.

The 2020 Proposed Scoping Plan target for California's forest sector is to maintain the current 5 MMTCO2E of sequestration through sustainable management practices, including reducing the risk of catastrophic wildfire, and the avoidance or mitigation of land-use changes that reduce carbon storage.
extraction_rationale: This is the section's headline commitment and includes a quantified sequestration target. It is a concrete policy.

policy_statement: Maintain the current 5 MMTCO2E of forest sequestration through sustainable management, wildfire risk reduction, and avoiding or mitigating land-use changes that reduce carbon storage.
source_quote: The 2020 Proposed Scoping Plan target for California's forest sector is to maintain the current 5 MMTCO2E of sequestration through sustainable management practices, including reducing the risk of catastrophic wildfire, and the avoidance or mitigation of land-use changes that reduce carbon storage.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified sequestration target with named implementation mechanisms. Because wildfire risk reduction is explicitly named, an adaptation secondary category is warranted.

policy_statement: Develop a forest carbon monitoring program and determine actions needed to meet the 2020 forest target.
source_quote: Monitoring carbon sequestered on forest lands will be necessary to implement the target.  The Board of Forestry and Fire Protection, working with the Resources Agency, the Department of Forestry and Fire Protection and ARB would be tasked with developing a monitoring program, improving greenhouse gas inventories, and determining what actions are needed to meet the 2020 target for the Forest sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete implementation and monitoring commitment tied to the forest target. It qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Continue water efficiency programs and use cleaner energy sources to move and treat water.
source_quote:
Continue efficiency programs and use cleaner energy sources to move and treat water.

Water use requires significant amounts of energy.
extraction_rationale: This is the section's headline commitment and a named policy direction. It is broad but concrete enough given the detailed measures that follow.

policy_statement: Recommend a public goods charge on water bills to fund water management actions that improve water and energy efficiency and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
source_quote: ARB recommends a public goods charge for funding investments in water management actions that improve water and energy efficiency and reduce GHG emissions.  As noted by the Economic and Technology Advancements Advisory Committee, a public goods charge on water can be collected on water bills and then used to fund end-use water efficiency improvements, system-wide efficiency projects, water recycling, and other actions that improve water and energy efficiency and reduce GHG emissions.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific fee-based funding mechanism with defined uses. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Encourage investment in manure digesters in the near term and reassess at the five-year Scoping Plan update whether the program should become mandatory for large dairies by 2020.
source_quote:
In the near-term, encourage investment in manure digesters and at the five-year Scoping Plan update determine if the program should be made mandatory by 2020.

Encouraging the capture of methane through use of manure digester systems at dairies can provide emission reductions on a voluntary basis.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific agricultural methane policy pathway with a future decision point on mandatory regulation. It qualifies despite the initial voluntary approach.

policy_statement: Explore opportunities to reduce nitrous oxide emissions from fertilizer use after completing research on variables affecting fertilizer emissions.
source_quote: Nitrogen fertilizer, which produces N2O emissions, is the other significant source of greenhouse gases in the Agricultural sector.  ARB has begun a research program to better understand the variables affecting fertilizer N2O emissions (Phase 1), and based on the findings, will explore opportunities for emission reductions (Phase 2).
extraction_rationale: This is borderline because it is partly research-oriented, but it includes a stated commitment to pursue emission reduction opportunities based on findings. It is extracted as a policy with some vagueness noted.

policy_statement: Provide appropriate credit for voluntary early greenhouse gas reductions through allowance set-asides, allocation rules, and recognition in other regulations.
source_quote: ARB will provide appropriate credit for voluntary early reductions that can be adequately quantified and verified through three primary means.  First, within the cap-and-trade program, ARB would set aside a certain number of allowances from the first compliance period to use to reward voluntary reductions that occur before 2012.  In addition, ARB will assure that the allocation process in the first compliance period does not disadvantage facilities that have made reductions after AB 32 went into effect at the start of 2007 and before 2012.
section_header: D. Voluntary Early Actions and Reductions / 1.  Voluntary Early Action
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete policy for recognizing early action using specific mechanisms. Because it uses allowance set-asides, it has a financial instrument component.

policy_statement: Adopt methodologies for quantifying voluntary reductions and offsets.
source_quote: ARB will adopt methodologies for quantifying voluntary reductions. (HSC §38571) The Board adopted a methodology for forest projects in October 2007, and for local government operations, urban forestry, and manure digesters in September 2008.
section_header: D. Voluntary Early Actions and Reductions / 2.  Voluntary Reductions
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete methodological policy commitment under statute. It qualifies as a policy instrument for voluntary reductions.

policy_statement: Use allowance set-asides to reward voluntary early action both for capped entities and for emissions-reducing projects outside the cap.
source_quote: Allowance set-asides, in addition to being used to potentially reward voluntary early actions by facilities that will be included in the cap-and-trade program, could also be used to reward voluntary early action at other facilities not covered by the cap.  An early action allowance set-aside could be utilized both by entities that are covered by the cap, and by those who develop emissions reducing projects outside of the cap, or purchase the reductions associated with those projects, and have not sold or used them.
section_header: D. Voluntary Early Actions and Reductions / 2.  Voluntary Reductions
extraction_rationale: This is a specific allowance allocation mechanism to reward voluntary action. It qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Possible uses of allowances and revenues under the AB 32 program.
source_quote:
Possible uses of allowances and of the revenue generated under the program include:

- Reducing costs of emissions reductions or achieving additional reductions Funding energy efficiency and renewable resource development could lower overall costs to consumers and companies, and provide the opportunity to achieve greater emissions reductions than would otherwise be possible.
section_header: E. Use of Allowances and Revenues
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella list of proposed revenue uses. Under the hierarchy rules it should be treated as a parent because multiple sub-items follow.

parent_statement: Possible uses of allowances and revenues under the AB 32 program.
policy_statement: Use revenues to fund energy efficiency and renewable resource development to lower costs and achieve additional emissions reductions.
source_quote: - Reducing costs of emissions reductions or achieving additional reductions Funding energy efficiency and renewable resource development could lower overall costs to consumers and companies, and provide the opportunity to achieve greater emissions reductions than would otherwise be possible.  Program revenues could be used to fund programs directly, or create financial incentives for others.
section_header: E. Use of Allowances and Revenues
extraction_rationale: This is a specific proposed use of program revenues. It is a financial instrument by definition.

parent_statement: Possible uses of allowances and revenues under the AB 32 program.
policy_statement: Use revenues to achieve environmental co-benefits by enhancing greenhouse gas reductions that also reduce air and other pollutants affecting public health.
source_quote: - Achieving environmental co-benefits Criteria and toxic air pollutants create health risks, and some communities bear a disproportionate burden from air pollution. Revenues could be used to enhance greenhouse gas emission reductions that also provide reductions in air and other pollutants that affect public health.
section_header: E. Use of Allowances and Revenues
extraction_rationale: This is a specific proposed revenue use. It is a financial instrument and explicitly tied to climate and pollution co-benefits.

parent_statement: Possible uses of allowances and revenues under the AB 32 program.
policy_statement: Provide funding or incentives to local governments for land-use planning, infrastructure, recycling, composting, and renewable energy from anaerobic digestion.
source_quote: - Incentives to local governments Funding or other incentives to local governments for well-designed land-use planning and infrastructure projects could lead to shorter commutes and encourage walking, bicycling and the use of public transit.  Funding of other incentives for local governments could also be used to increase recycling, composting, and to generating renewable energy from anaerobic digestion.
section_header: E. Use of Allowances and Revenues
extraction_rationale: This is a specific proposed incentive use of revenues. It is a financial instrument and names concrete intervention areas.

parent_statement: Possible uses of allowances and revenues under the AB 32 program.
policy_statement: Use revenues for consumer rebates to offset costs and encourage greater energy efficiency.
source_quote: - Consumer rebates Utilities and other businesses could use revenues to support and increase rebate programs to customers to offset some of the cost associated with increased investments in renewable resources and to encourage increased energy efficiency.
section_header: E. Use of Allowances and Revenues
extraction_rationale: This is a specific rebate-based revenue use. It is clearly a financial instrument.

parent_statement: Possible uses of allowances and revenues under the AB 32 program.
policy_statement: Recycle revenue directly back to consumers through per capita dividends, earned income tax credits, or other mechanisms.
source_quote: - Direct refund to consumers Revenue from the program could be recycled directly back to consumers in a variety of forms including per capita dividends, earned income tax credits, or other mechanisms.
section_header: E. Use of Allowances and Revenues
extraction_rationale: This is a specific proposed fiscal recycling mechanism. It is a financial instrument, though climate effects are more indirect.

parent_statement: Possible uses of allowances and revenues under the AB 32 program.
policy_statement: Use program revenues for climate change adaptation programs to help the state adapt to climate impacts.
source_quote: - Climate change adaptation programs Climate change will impact natural and human environments.  Program revenues could be used to help the state adapt to the effects of climate change which will be detailed in the State's Climate Adaptation Strategy being prepared by the Resources Agency to be completed in early 2009.
section_header: E. Use of Allowances and Revenues
extraction_rationale: This is a specific proposed revenue use for adaptation. It is a financial instrument with a direct adaptation objective.

parent_statement: Possible uses of allowances and revenues under the AB 32 program.
policy_statement: Use revenues as subsidies to reduce immediate cost impacts for covered industries making substantial upfront capital investments to reduce emissions.
source_quote: - Subsidies Revenues could be used to reduce immediate cost impacts to covered industries required to make substantial upfront capital investments to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
section_header: E. Use of Allowances and Revenues
extraction_rationale: This is a specific subsidy proposal. It is clearly a financial instrument.

parent_statement: Possible uses of allowances and revenues under the AB 32 program.
policy_statement: Use revenues to support research, development, and deployment of green technologies.
source_quote: - RD&D funding Revenues could be used to support research, development, and deployment of green technologies.
section_header: E. Use of Allowances and Revenues
extraction_rationale: This is a specific funding use for climate-related technology development. It is a financial instrument.

parent_statement: Possible uses of allowances and revenues under the AB 32 program.
policy_statement: Use revenues for worker transition assistance and training programs to support the labor force in new green industries.
source_quote: - Worker transition assistance Regulating greenhouse gas emissions will probably shift economic growth to some sectors and green technologies and away from higher carbon intensity industries.  Worker training programs could help the California labor force be competitive in these new industries.
section_header: E. Use of Allowances and Revenues
extraction_rationale: This is a specific proposed revenue use for workforce transition. It is a financial instrument, though climate relevance is indirect.

parent_statement: Possible uses of allowances and revenues under the AB 32 program.
policy_statement: Use a portion of revenues to underwrite the State's AB 32 programs and operating costs.
source_quote: - Administration of a greenhouse gas program A portion of revenues could be used to underwrite the State's AB 32 programs and operating costs.
section_header: E. Use of Allowances and Revenues
extraction_rationale: This is a specific proposed administrative funding use. It is a financial instrument.

parent_statement: Possible uses of allowances and revenues under the AB 32 program.
policy_statement: Use revenues to purchase and retire greenhouse gas reductions, including projects such as afforestation and reforestation.
source_quote: - Direct emission reductions Revenues could be used to purchase greenhouse gas reductions for the sole purpose of retirement, providing direct additional greenhouse gas emission reductions.  Potential projects, such as afforestation and reforestation, would both sequester CO2 and provide other environmental benefits.
section_header: E. Use of Allowances and Revenues
extraction_rationale: This is a specific revenue use for direct emissions reduction purchases. It is a financial instrument and explicitly mentions biological sequestration.

policy_statement: Recommend a de minimis threshold of 0.1 MMTCO2E annual emissions per source category for Scoping Plan regulation applicability.
source_quote: After this review and considering the level of emissions needed to meet the 1990 target established by AB 32, ARB recommends a de minimis level 0.1 MMTCO2E annual emissions per source category.  Source categories whose total aggregated emissions are below this level are not proposed for emission reduction requirements in the Proposed Scoping Plan but may contribute toward the target via other means.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified regulatory applicability threshold. It is a concrete policy design choice.

policy_statement: Develop climate change education components for the State's K-12 model school curriculum by 2010.
source_quote: By 2010, California will develop climate change education components to the State's new K-12 model school curriculum as part of the Education and the Environment Initiative (AB 1548, Pavley, Chapter 665, Statutes of 2003).  Expanding the knowledge and opportunities of young people to participate in promoting their own and their communities' environmental health will be an important theme for all these efforts.
section_header: B. Public Outreach and Education / 2.  Education and Workforce Development
extraction_rationale: This is a dated curriculum development commitment. It is climate-related but more peripheral to direct emissions outcomes.

policy_statement: Develop an online small business toolkit with carbon calculators, inventory protocols, best practices, financing resources, peer networking, and awards.
source_quote: With our State partners, we are developing an on-line small business 'toolkit' designed for small and medium-sized businesses that will provide a one-stop shop for technical and financial resources.  Toolkit components will include a business-specific calculator to assess a company's carbon footprint; a voluntary greenhouse gas inventory protocol for measuring greenhouse gas emissions; recommended best practices for energy, transportation, building, purchasing, and recycling; case studies demonstrating how small and medium California businesses have reduced greenhouse gas emissions; program financing resources; peernetworking opportunities; and an awards program to recognize reductions of greenhouse gas emissions among California businesses.
section_header: B. Public Outreach and Education / 3.  Small Businesses
extraction_rationale: This is a specific outreach and technical assistance program with defined components. It is climate-related but indirect rather than a direct emissions control policy.

policy_statement: Update the Scoping Plan at least once every five years.
source_quote: ARB will update the plan at least once every five years (HSC §38561(h)).  These updates will allow ARB to evaluate the progress made toward the State's greenhouse gas emission reduction goals and correct the Plan's course where necessary.
extraction_rationale: This is a statutory planning and review requirement with a defined interval. It is a concrete governance policy.

policy_statement: Require every State agency to prepare an annual greenhouse gas Report Card and outside audits every three years as funds are available.
source_quote: SB 85 (Budget Committee, Chapter 178, Statutes of 2007) requires every State agency to prepare an annual 'Report Card,' detailing measures the agency has adopted and taken to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, including the actual emissions reduced as a result of those actions.  Agencies are also required, as funds are available, to have an outside audit of greenhouse gas-related actions completed every three years to verify actual and projected reductions.
section_header: D. Tracking and Measuring Progress / 1.  Report Card
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete reporting and audit requirement with specified frequency. It qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Create a statewide approach to meet the State government commitment to reduce emissions by at least 30 percent below business-as-usual by 2020.
source_quote: The CAT recently established a State Government Subgroup to work with State agencies to create a statewide approach to meet the Scoping Plan's commitment to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by a minimum of 30 percent by 2020 below the State's estimated business-as-usual emissions - approximately a 15 percent reduction from current levels.
section_header: D. Tracking and Measuring Progress / 3.  Progress Toward the State Government Target
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete implementation commitment for the state operations target. It qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Require annual greenhouse gas reporting from the largest facilities in the state under the mandatory reporting regulation, with third-party verification beginning in 2010.
source_quote: The regulation requires annual reporting from the largest facilities in the state, accounting for 94 percent of greenhouse gas emissions from industrial and commercial stationary sources in California.  Affected facilities will begin tracking their greenhouse gas emissions in 2008, to be reported beginning in 2009 with a phase-in process to allow facilities to develop reporting systems and train personnel in data collection.  Beginning in 2010, emissions reports will be more rigorous and will be subject to third-party verification.
section_header: D. Tracking and Measuring Progress / 4.  Mandatory Reporting Regulation
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete regulatory reporting requirement with coverage and timing details. It clearly qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Develop a comprehensive enforcement plan for the cap-and-trade program covering market monitoring, prosecution, and penalty setting.
source_quote: These working group meetings are ongoing and will culminate in a comprehensive enforcement plan to accompany the proposed cap-and-trade program when the Board considers regulatory requirements.  This enforcement plan would describe the administrative structures needed for market monitoring, prosecution, and penalty setting.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete commitment to create an enforcement framework for cap-and-trade. It qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Formalize enforcement agreements with Western Climate Initiative partner jurisdictions for emissions verification, offset certification, and non-compliance enforcement.
source_quote: This plan recommends that California implement a cap-and-trade program that links with other Western Climate Initiative partner programs to create a regional market system.  This system would require California to formalize enforcement agreements with its WCI partner jurisdictions for all phases of cap-and-trade program operations, including verification of emissions, certification of offsets based on common protocols, and detection of and punishment for non-compliance.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific interjurisdictional enforcement commitment tied to the regional cap-and-trade system. It qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Initiate a fee rulemaking to fund AB 32 administration, implementation, and enforcement, aiming to collect fees in fiscal year 2009-2010.
source_quote: AB 32 authorizes ARB to collect fees to fund implementation of the statute.  This fall ARB will initiate a rulemaking for a fee program to fund administration of the program.  ARB is moving on an expedited schedule to develop a fee regulation and expects to take a regulation to the Board in early 2009, with the aim of beginning to collect fees in the 2009-2010 fiscal year.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete fee-based funding commitment with a timeline. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Chicago commits to reduce citywide GHG emissions by at least 62% by 2040 from 2017 levels.
source_quote: The 2022 CAP aims to chart an equitable path to reduce Chicago's GHG emissions by a minimum of 62% by 2040. Following the principles defined in this plan, this pathway prioritizes improving the lives of all Chicagoans by promoting environmental justice, generating household savings, improving community health, transitioning away from fossil-fuel dependency, and ensuring that all Chicago communities are prepared for the undeniable impacts of climate change, by 2040.
extraction_rationale: This is a core quantified emissions-reduction target with a deadline, clearly qualifying as a climate policy.

policy_statement: Chicago will not count carbon offsets toward achieving its 62% GHG reduction goal and will prioritize reducing its own emissions first.
source_quote: Chicago will not count offset credits toward its 62% GHG reduction goal achievement. Furthermore, the City will reduce its own emissions before taking action beyond its borders.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear policy constraint governing how the emissions target will be met. It is not a target itself but a binding implementation rule.

policy_statement: The City will assess options to remove and store carbon within city limits, including urban forestry and soil management.
source_quote: As the City's energy agenda evolves, carbon offsets may be considered for their potential role to reach net-zero. In parallel, the City will assess options to remove and store carbon within City limits, including urban forestry and soil management.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific named intervention on carbon removal, though somewhat exploratory because it is framed as an assessment rather than implementation.

policy_statement: The City will establish community-led climate advisory boards and forums for regular community participation in CAP implementation and reporting.
source_quote: The City will also establish community-led climate advisory boards and forums for regular community participation in implementing, reporting, and achieving the actions related to the 2022 CAP. The City also practices accountability by reporting progress on carbon-reduction strategies and other climate goals to national and global institutions.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete governance commitment with a named institutional mechanism, relevant to climate implementation and accountability.

policy_statement: The City will develop more resolutions and ordinances to bolster the actions of the 2022 CAP.
source_quote: This resolution has kickstarted initiatives like the Request for Proposals for renewable energy supply to all City operations. The City will develop more resolutions and ordinances to bolster the actions of the 2022 CAP.
extraction_rationale: This is a formal commitment to future regulatory action, but it is broad and lacks specificity on which ordinances; included as a governance policy edge case.

policy_statement: Chicago has committed $188 million for climate resiliency and mitigation as part of the Chicago Recovery Plan.
source_quote: In October 2021, Chicago's City Council approved $188 million for climate resiliency and mitigation, as part of Mayor Lori Lightfoot's $2.5 billion Chicago Recovery Plan. This historic level of investment toward climate action will provide funding for resilient infrastructure and green workforce development opportunities.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear budget appropriation for climate action and therefore a financial instrument.

source_quote: Chicago Recovery Plan funding overlap with Chicago's 2022 Climate Action Plan (total climate funding of $188M).
section_header: Chicago Recovery Plan funding overlap with Chicago's 2022 Climate Action Plan

extraction_rationale: This is a funded retrofit and decarbonization program with quantified units and budget.

The project will decrease the energy burden on organizations and provide critical services to underserved communities. This program aims to develop a network of resiliency hubs throughout Chicago and provide energy education services and shelter during extreme weather.

policy_statement: Allocate $5 million to retrofit up to 10 Chicago Public Libraries and install solar panels.
source_quote: Library Power Project | $5 million | Enable retrofits and install solar panels at up to 10 Chicago Public Libraries, minimizing utility costs and ensuring that we sustain our library assets for the long term.

policy_statement: Develop in 2020 and begin implementing in 2021 a Strategy for Capacity Development and Climate Empowerment to strengthen capacities for national mitigation and adaptation targets.

source_quote:
a) Setting EDTTCC's institutionality and governance

- By 2020, Chile will have established a governance and institutional  framework for the implementation of the EDTTCC and will support the national contribution in mitigation and adaptation, as well as the global long-term response to climate change. ·

- By 2030, Chile will have evaluated and updated its EDTTCC, from the evaluation and monitoring done during the implementation in climate change. ·

b) Implementing and operating mechanisms and instruments for the analysis of needs and for the implementation of technological action plans in specific areas.

(2)  All ministers must, where relevant, review and revise key performance indicators and job descriptions for civil servants within their ministry with the aim of ensuring that civil servants are increasingly equipped with relevant specialist skills to support the implementation of this Act.

policy_statement: The Minister responsible for finance may grant incentives for mitigation, adaptation, resilience and accredited climate training, and must set non-discretionary rules for such incentives by regulation.
source_quote:
88. -(1)	 The	Minister	responsible	for	finance	may,	in	accordance	with	the	Financial Management Act 2004, grant to persons that-
- (a) encourage and put in place measures for the mitigation of climate change including reduction of greenhouse emissions, use of renewable energy and energy	efficiency;
- (b) put  in  place  measures  to  adapt  and  improve  Fiji's  resilience  to  climate change; or
- (c) are involved in the conduct of accredited training in programmes that are aimed at mitigating and adapting to climate change,

such incentives as may be necessary for the advancement of such measures and activities designed for the mitigation of and adaptation to climate change.
section_header: Incentives for the promotion of climate change initiatives
extraction_rationale: This is a clear financial incentive instrument for climate action across mitigation and adaptation.

policy_statement: The Minister responsible for finance may establish guidelines for the use of climate finance by accredited state entities or private organisations.
source_quote: (3)	 The	Minister	responsible	for	finance	may,	with	the	support	of	the	Director,	establish guidelines	for	the	use	of	climate	finance,	to	be	applied	by	the	State	entities	or	private organisations in subsection (1), in order to ensure strategic and complementary use of the	funds	that	will	be	allocated	for	climate	finance.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific climate finance governance instrument for fund use.

policy_statement: The Minister responsible for finance may institute financial instruments and mechanisms to implement the Act and climate mitigation and adaptation actions.
source_quote: 90. The	Minister	responsible	for	finance,	 subject	 to	 and	 in	 accordance	 with	 all written	laws,	may	institute	financial	instruments	and	mechanisms	with	the	purpose	of implementing this Act and climate change mitigation and adaptation actions pursuant to the objectives and principles of this Act.
extraction_rationale: This is a broad but explicit authorization to create climate finance instruments.

policy_statement: The Minister responsible for finance, in consultation with the Reserve Bank, must develop and review national climate finance strategies, frameworks and approaches every 5 years.
source_quote:
91. -(1)	 The	Minister	responsible	for	finance,	in	consultation	with	the	Reserve	Bank,	must	develop	national	climate	finance	strategies,	frameworks	and	approaches	to	support and	coordinate	Fiji's	ongoing	access	to	climate	finance.

(3)  The Minister, in consultation with the Reserve Bank, must review the national climate	finance	strategies	and	frameworks	every	5	years.
extraction_rationale: This is a mandatory climate finance strategy instrument with a recurring review cycle.

policy_statement: The Minister may establish a private sector advisory committee to support implementation of the Act and climate-aligned public-private partnerships.

(2)  In developing such guidance materials, the Minister must have regard to industry best practice including the recommendations of the Financial Stability Board's Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures.

policy_statement: Helsinki will become carbon-neutral by 2035 by reducing greenhouse gas emissions 80% from 1990 levels and compensating the remaining 20% outside the city.
source_quote: According to the Strategy, Helsinki will be carbon-neutral by 2035. This goal will be achieved by reducing the greenhouse gas emissions in Helsinki by 80 per cent. The remaining 20 per cent will be compensated for by Helsinki taking care of implementing emissions reductions outside the city.
extraction_rationale: This is a core quantified climate commitment with a target year and explicit mechanism (80% reduction plus compensation), so it clearly qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Helsinki will reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 60% from 1990 levels by 2030 as an intermediate target.
source_quote: The City Strategy also includes an intermediate goal for 2030: greenhouse gas emissions will be reduced by 60 per cent during 1990-2030.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified interim emissions target with a deadline, meeting the extraction criteria.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will strive to achieve carbon neutrality before 2050.
source_quote: The community in general expects Hong Kong to go further in deep decarbonisation… The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region will strive to achieve carbon neutrality before 2050. To this end, the Government will set out more proactive strategies and measures to reduce carbon emissions.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear government commitment with a defined long-term target year. It qualifies as a policy because it sets a formal climate outcome target, even though the specific measures are elaborated elsewhere.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will reduce total carbon emissions by half from the 2005 level before 2035.
source_quote:
Adopting the prevailing technologies that are relatively mature and cost-effective, we aim to reduce the total carbon emissions by half before 2035 from the 2005 level, i.e. from about 40 million tonnes in 2005 to nearly 20 million tonnes in 2035.

In the meantime, we need to prepare for the development and trials of various technologies and solutions that may be suitable for Hong Kong in future, with a view to achieving carbon neutrality before 2050 through the adoption of mature, reliable and cost-effective solutions in a timely manner.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified medium-term emissions target with a baseline and deadline, which clearly qualifies as a policy commitment.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will pursue net-zero electricity generation before 2050 by increasing zero-carbon electricity supply and exploring new energy and regional cooperation.
source_quote: At present, fossil fuels, including natural gas and coal, account for over 70% of Hong Kong's fuel mix for electricity generation. Under the overall strategy of achieving carbon neutrality, we must progressively increase the use of zero-carbon energy for electricity generation before 2050. In searching for suitable zero-carbon energy, four important factors should be taken into account : safety, reliability, affordability and environmental performance.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella initiative with multiple specific actions listed beneath it, including coal phase-out, renewable energy expansion, and regional cooperation. It therefore qualifies as a parent policy.

parent_statement: Net-zero Electricity Generation
policy_statement: Hong Kong will increase the share of renewable energy in the fuel mix for electricity generation to 15% before 2050.
source_quote: On RE development, we can increase RE supply through government-developed facilities, investment by power companies and encouraging public participation. Our goal is to increase the share of RE in the fuel mix for electricity generation from the existing less than 1% to 15% before 2050. Specifically, the Government can strive to develop more advanced waste-to-energy facilities to turn waste into electricity.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified renewable energy target nested under the broader net-zero electricity strategy. It is a specific mitigation commitment with a deadline.

parent_statement: Net-zero Electricity Generation
policy_statement: Hong Kong will continue replacing coal with natural gas and zero-carbon energy in the medium term and explore regional zero-carbon energy projects.
source_quote: Apart from developing RE as far as possible, we will continue to increase the use of natural gas with lower carbon emissions and zero-carbon energy to replace coal for electricity generation in the medium term. We will also explore the supply of new zero-carbon energy by collaborating with neighbouring regions to participate in and operate zero-carbon energy projects near Hong Kong through joint ventures and joint development, etc.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete intervention under the electricity strategy: fuel switching and regional project participation. It is specific enough to qualify despite not giving a numeric target in this paragraph.

parent_statement: Net-zero Electricity Generation
policy_statement: Hong Kong will explore and trial hydrogen and other zero-carbon energy technologies for local electricity generation.
source_quote: Therefore, we must, at the same time, explore and try out other types of zero-carbon energy (e.g. hydrogen energy) for electricity generation in Hong Kong, and progressively increase their application. The Government and the power companies are actively studying the development and application of new energy such as hydrogen, including importing hydrogen or other forms of new energy for use as fuels, so that they may be adopted for trial and application in Hong Kong when the technologies become relatively mature.
extraction_rationale: This is a named intervention involving trials and application of hydrogen and other zero-carbon energy. It qualifies as a policy because it commits the government and utilities to active study and trial deployment.

policy_statement: By 2035, Hong Kong will cease using coal for daily electricity generation and retain coal only for backup support.
source_quote: Coal, accounting for around a quarter in the current fuel mix for electricity generation, emits the highest level of carbon emissions. Hong Kong has ceased to build coal-fired generation units since 1997 and has been gradually phasing out the existing units. By 2035, we will cease using coal for daily electricity generation and will only keep it for providing backup support.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is a clear phase-out commitment with a deadline and operational condition. It is a standalone policy target even though it also sits within the broader electricity strategy.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will increase the share of renewable energy in electricity generation to 7.5% to 10% by 2035.
source_quote:
To expedite transformation to low-carbon energy, we are committed to increasing the share of RE in the fuel mix for electricity generation from less than 1% at present to 7.5% to 10% by 2035.

To achieve this target, we will strive to develop more advanced waste-to-energy facilities, including the infrastructure for recycling of food waste and construction of another large-scale integrated waste management facility.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified renewable energy target with a deadline and supporting interventions. It clearly qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will expand waste-to-energy facilities so they can meet around 3% to 4% of electricity demand by 2035.
source_quote: To achieve this target, we will strive to develop more advanced waste-to-energy facilities, including the infrastructure for recycling of food waste and construction of another large-scale integrated waste management facility. It is estimated that around 3% to 4% of Hong Kong's electricity demand would be met by the electricity generated by such facilities by 2035.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is a specific infrastructure commitment with an estimated quantified contribution to electricity demand by a target year. It qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will pursue offshore wind development to supply around 3.5% to 4% of electricity demand by 2035.
source_quote: The Government and the two power companies are reviewing proposals to develop offshore wind farms. The two power companies expect that improvement in the design of wind farms and the adoption of new technologies can increase the amount of electricity generated and the economic benefits. Our preliminary estimate shows that by 2035, the wind energy generated would be able to meet around 3.5% to 4% of Hong Kong's electricity demand.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete renewable energy development commitment with a quantified expected contribution by 2035.

policy_statement: Hong Kong expects solar energy to meet around 1% to 2% of electricity demand by 2035.
source_quote: The Government has introduced with the power companies the FiT Scheme in recent years to encourage the community to develop distributed RE, such as solar energy. The Government has also developed a wide range of RE projects in various premises, such as reservoirs, restored landfills, government buildings and other suitable facilities. With the continuous technological advancement and the active participation of the community, we expect that solar energy would be able to meet around 1% to 2% of Hong Kong's electricity demand by 2035, and the total share of RE in Hong Kong's fuel mix would reach 7.5% to 10%.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified deployment expectation tied to government-supported solar policy instruments and projects. It qualifies as a policy target.

policy_statement: The Government will require renewable energy technologies in all capital works projects and raise rooftop renewable energy requirements in new government buildings from 10% to 25% of available roof space.
source_quote: The Government will continue to take the lead in developing RE and strive to incorporate RE technologies in all capital works projects. We will update the Government circular on Green Government Buildings and raise the requirements of applying RE technologies in new government buildings. For instance, the proportion of available roof space for installing RE systems will be increased from the current 10% to 25%.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete government-building requirement with a quantified design standard. It qualifies as a policy because it changes implementation requirements for public projects.

policy_statement: The Water Supplies Department will install larger floating solar systems at reservoirs and study a more than 100 MW floating solar project at Plover Cove Reservoir.
source_quote: Building on the success of the pilot projects of floating solar energy generation systems at Shek Pik Reservoir and Plover Cove Reservoir, the Water Supplies Department (WSD) plans to install larger floating solar energy generation systems with a generating capacity of 5-10 megawatts (MW) each at various reservoirs, including Plover Cove Reservoir, Shek Pik Reservoir and Tai Lam Chung Reservoir. In addition, WSD has embarked on a study on installing a floating solar energy generation system with a generating capacity of over 100 MW at Plover Cove Reservoir.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is a specific infrastructure deployment and study commitment with named sites and capacities, making it a clear policy action.

policy_statement: The Government will pilot solar energy generation at the South East New Territories Landfill and expand renewable energy use at restored landfills.
source_quote: We will also make use of landfills to generate RE. Apart from utilising landfill gas for electricity generation, we are actively exploring the installation of solar energy generation systems at restored landfills. For instance, EPD will launch a pilot scheme on solar energy generation at the South East New Territories Landfill in Tseung Kwan O.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is a named pilot scheme and broader intervention to deploy renewable energy on landfill sites. It qualifies as a policy due to the specific intervention and implementing agency.

policy_statement: The Government will explore rooftop solar installations on existing public rental housing estates where technically feasible.
source_quote: Since May 2011, the Housing Authority has been installing solar energy generation systems at domestic blocks of new public rental housing estates where it is technically feasible and the rooftop conditions permit, with the target to provide at least 1.5% of the communal electricity consumption. In addition to new domestic blocks, the Government will explore the installation of solar energy generation systems on the rooftops of domestic blocks of existing public rental housing estates where technically feasible.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is a specific deployment commitment for public housing, supported by an existing quantified target for communal electricity contribution. It qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: The Government will facilitate private-sector installation of renewable energy systems on land and properties, including open car parks.
source_quote: To assist the private sector in developing and applying RE, the Government will explore ways to facilitate the installation of RE systems by the private sector on their land and properties, such as measures to facilitate installation of solar energy generation systems by the private sector in open car parks. Coupled with the FiT Scheme, this can help foster the development of RE.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete enabling policy for private renewable energy deployment. It is somewhat open-ended on mechanism, but still qualifies because it commits to facilitative measures for a named intervention.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will enhance regional cooperation and seek joint investment and development opportunities in zero-carbon energy projects near Hong Kong.
source_quote: The Government, together with the power companies, will also explore ways to enhance regional cooperation on zero-carbon energy and identify sources of zero-carbon energy in neighbouring regions, including seeking joint investment and development opportunities for participating in and operating zero-carbon energy projects near Hong Kong. We will also keep abreast of developments in technologies that utilise RE for electricity generation.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is a specific strategic commitment to regional zero-carbon energy sourcing and project participation. It qualifies as a policy action under the electricity strategy.

policy_statement: Hong Kong aims to raise the share of zero-carbon energy in the electricity fuel mix to about 60% to 70% before 2035.
source_quote: To achieve the target of reducing the total carbon emissions by 50% from the 2005 level before 2035, more options are needed for raising the share of zero-carbon energy in the fuel mix for electricity generation to about 60% to 70%.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Phasing out coal for electricity generation · Developing RE
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified fuel-mix target tied to the 2035 emissions goal. Although phrased as needing more options, it still states a clear intended target level.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will reduce building electricity consumption through energy saving and green building measures, with long-term and medium-term targets for commercial and residential buildings.
source_quote: In order to achieve carbon neutrality, we need to step up efforts in promoting energy conservation in buildings, and set a more proactive and targeted energy saving goal. In this connection, we will strive to gradually reduce the electricity consumption of new and existing commercial buildings by 30% to 40%, and that of residential buildings by 20% to 30% by 2050, using the operational conditions of 2015 as the comparison basis.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella initiative with multiple sub-actions on standards, audits, district cooling, benchmarking, and appliance efficiency. It qualifies as a parent policy.

parent_statement: Energy Saving and Green Buildings
policy_statement: Hong Kong will reduce electricity consumption of commercial buildings by 30% to 40% and residential buildings by 20% to 30% by 2050 relative to 2015 operating conditions.
source_quote: In order to achieve carbon neutrality, we need to step up efforts in promoting energy conservation in buildings, and set a more proactive and targeted energy saving goal. In this connection, we will strive to gradually reduce the electricity consumption of new and existing commercial buildings by 30% to 40%, and that of residential buildings by 20% to 30% by 2050, using the operational conditions of 2015 as the comparison basis.
section_header: Long-term targets: Reduce the electricity consumption of commercial buildings by 30% to 40%, and that of residential buildings by 20% to 30% by 2050
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified long-term building energy target with baseline and deadline. It is a clear policy commitment.

parent_statement: Energy Saving and Green Buildings
policy_statement: Hong Kong will reduce electricity consumption of commercial buildings by 15% to 20% and residential buildings by 10% to 15% by 2035 relative to 2015 operating conditions.
source_quote: To promote continuous decarbonisation in buildings, we have also set a medium-term target of reducing the electricity consumption of new and existing commercial buildings by 15% to 20%, and that of residential buildings by 10% to 15% by 2035, using the operational conditions of 2015 as the comparison basis. More green innovations and energy efficient elements will also be added to the design of new government buildings to achieve an energy efficiency performance of 10% better than statutory level, with a view to leading the trades to further optimise the energy efficiency performance of new buildings.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Reduce the electricity consumption of commercial buildings by 15% to 20%, and that of residential buildings by 10% to 15% by 2035
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified medium-term building energy target with baseline and deadline. It clearly qualifies as a policy.

parent_statement: Energy Saving and Green Buildings
policy_statement: The Government will explore expanding building energy regulation to all high-energy-use buildings such as data centres.
source_quote: To continuously improve the energy efficiency standards of buildings, we will make reference to the international standards and harness innovative and intelligent technologies to ensure the energy efficiency standards of building services installations are up to date. We will actively explore the possibility of expanding the scope of regulation to cover all buildings with high energy consumption, such as data centres, so as to further enhance the overall energy efficiency performance of buildings in Hong Kong.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Reduce the electricity consumption of commercial buildings by 15% to 20%, and that of residential buildings by 10% to 15% by 2035
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory exploration commitment tied to a named intervention and target sector. It qualifies as a policy, though the exact legal mechanism remains to be finalized.

parent_statement: Energy Saving and Green Buildings
policy_statement: The Government will consider more frequent energy audits, mandate identified energy management opportunities, and require regular commissioning in large commercial buildings.
source_quote: To explore and utilise decarbonisation opportunities in a systematic manner, we will consider conducting energy audits more frequently and mandating the implementation of identified energy management opportunities. At the same time, we will strengthen the promotion of RCx to check the performance of the existing buildings in energy and other areas and make appropriate adjustments to the systems, with a view to reducing electricity consumption. We will consider requiring large commercial buildings to carry out regular commissioning of air-conditioning systems and major building services installations to achieve optimal operational efficiency.
section_header: Medium-term targets: Reduce the electricity consumption of commercial buildings by 15% to 20%, and that of residential buildings by 10% to 15% by 2035
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete package of prospective regulatory and operational measures for building energy management. It qualifies despite some 'consider' language because it specifies named interventions and intended mandates.

parent_statement: Energy Saving and Green Buildings
policy_statement: The Government will tighten Overall Thermal Transfer Value standards by 2025 and complete Residential Thermal Transfer Value reviews by 2023 and 2030, while requiring new government buildings to exceed OTTV standards by at least 10%.
source_quote: The Government is conducting a review on the OTTV, and plans to complete the review for tightening up the statutory standards by 2025. The Government also plans to complete two reviews on the Residential Thermal Transfer Value (RTTV) by 2023 and 2030. To lead by example, the OTTV of new government buildings will be at least 10% above the statutory standards.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear standards-based policy with deadlines and a quantified requirement for government buildings. It qualifies as a regulatory commitment.

parent_statement: Energy Saving and Green Buildings
policy_statement: Construction of district cooling systems in Tung Chung New Town Extension and Kwu Tung North New Development Area will proceed, and the Government will study district cooling in additional new development areas.
source_quote: As for infrastructure, following the Kai Tak Development, construction works of two more DCS projects in the Tung Chung New Town Extension (East) and Kwu Tung North New Development Area have commenced. When the two DCSs come into full operation, it is estimated that about 70 million kWh of electricity can be saved annually, and about 49 000 tonnes of carbon emissions can be reduced (i.e. around 0.12% of Hong Kong's total carbon emissions).
extraction_rationale: This is a specific infrastructure commitment with quantified energy and emissions impacts. It qualifies as a policy action.

parent_statement: Energy Saving and Green Buildings
policy_statement: The Government will release energy data and introduce benchmarking tools to compare building energy performance, while smart meters will support demand-side management such as possible time-of-use tariffs.
source_quote: We plan to, through releasing energy data and introducing energy benchmarking tools, facilitate the comparison of building energy consumption performance and establish a two-way partnership in carbon reduction. Indeed, the two power companies are progressively installing smart meters for their customers across the territory according to their plans, so as to help their customers monitor and manage electricity consumption more effectively and encourage energy conservation. Smart meters also provide the smart infrastructure required for introducing demand-side management measures, such as consideration of setting time-of-use tariffs as in some other economies to encourage users to change their habits and reduce electricity consumption during peak demand hours.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete operational policy package around transparency, benchmarking, and enabling demand-side management. The tariff element is exploratory, but the broader commitment is specific enough to qualify.

parent_statement: Energy Saving and Green Buildings
policy_statement: The Government will review and potentially strengthen the Mandatory Energy Efficiency Labelling Scheme by upgrading grading standards, setting minimum efficiency requirements, and expanding coverage to commercial appliances.
source_quote: We will keep the scheme under review. Apart from upgrading the grading standards, we will also consider setting a minimum energy efficiency requirement so that certain appliances must meet the minimum energy efficiency standards before they can be supplied in Hong Kong, with a view to further raising the energy efficiency performance of products. Moreover, we will consider expanding the scope of the scheme to cover non-domestic or commercial appliances.
extraction_rationale: This is a named regulatory scheme with explicit contemplated strengthening measures. It qualifies as a policy because it concerns standards and market access requirements.

policy_statement: The Government has set a new Green Energy Target to improve the energy performance of the whole Government by 6% by 2024-25.
source_quote: The Government has been taking the lead in energy saving. As mentioned in Chapter 2 above, the Government achieved the five-year target of reducing electricity consumption in government buildings by 5% in 2018-19, one year ahead of schedule, and achieved a final electricity saving of about 7.8%. We have also set a new Green Energy Target to further improve the energy performance of the whole Government by 6% by 2024-25.
section_header: For energy saving, many a little makes a mickle
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified government operations target with a deadline. It qualifies as a standalone policy.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will achieve zero carbon emissions from vehicles and the transport sector before 2050 through electrification, new energy transport, and traffic management.
source_quote: We expect to achieve the long-term target of zero carbon emissions from vehicles and the transport sector before 2050 through the electrification of vehicles and ferries, development of new energy transport and implementation of measures to improve traffic management.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella transport decarbonisation strategy with multiple subordinate actions on EVs, hydrogen, ferries, rail, and traffic management. It qualifies as a parent policy.

parent_statement: Green Transport
policy_statement: Hong Kong will cease new registration of fuel-propelled and hybrid private cars in 2035 or earlier.
source_quote: The measures outlined in the Hong Kong Roadmap on Popularisation of Electric Vehicles announced by the Government in 2021 cover various aspects, including ceasing the new registration of fuel-propelled and hybrid private cars in 2035 or earlier, as well as setting strategies and targets for providing charging facilities. Besides private cars, commercial vehicles, including goods vehicles, buses, light buses and taxis, are also major sources of carbon emissions.
section_header: Medium-term target: Set a concrete timetable for adopting new energy public transport
extraction_rationale: This is a clear regulatory phase-out target with a deadline. It qualifies as a policy commitment.

parent_statement: Green Transport
policy_statement: The Government will test electric and new energy public transport and commercial vehicles and set a more concrete timetable around 2025.
source_quote: The Government will play an active role in developing new energy transport, and will partner with different sectors in the coming years to actively test the technological and commercial viability of various electric and new energy public transport and commercial vehicles, with a view to setting a more concrete way forward and timetable in around 2025. A full-fledged charging network is also indispensable for supporting the popularisation of EVs.
section_header: Medium-term target: Set a concrete timetable for adopting new energy public transport
extraction_rationale: This is a specific testing and planning commitment for public and commercial transport decarbonisation. It qualifies because it names interventions and a timeline for decision-making.

parent_statement: Green Transport
policy_statement: The Government will review EV charging facility targets around 2025 to keep pace with EV developments.
source_quote: A full-fledged charging network is also indispensable for supporting the popularisation of EVs. In around 2025, we will review this year's target for the installation of charging facilities to keep up with the latest developments in EV.
section_header: Medium-term target: Set a concrete timetable for adopting new energy public transport
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete review commitment tied to EV charging infrastructure targets. It is somewhat procedural but still policy-relevant because it concerns infrastructure target-setting.

parent_statement: Green Transport
policy_statement: The Government will collaborate over the next three years to test hydrogen fuel cell electric buses and heavy vehicles.
source_quote: Following the release of the Plan, the Government has set up an Interdepartmental Working Group on the application of hydrogen energy in Hong Kong. We plan to collaborate with the franchised bus companies and other stakeholders in the next three years to test out hydrogen fuel cell electric buses and heavy vehicles.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific trial commitment with a defined timeframe and named vehicle technologies. It qualifies as a policy action.

parent_statement: Green Transport
policy_statement: The Government will study the feasibility of hydrogen-fuelled transport in Hong Kong, including hydrogen filling facilities and technician training.
source_quote: We will also study the feasibility of using hydrogen-fuelled transport in Hong Kong, and consider the necessary supporting facilities, including construction of hydrogen filling facilities that meet the specifications, and train relevant technicians in the safe use and maintenance of hydrogen fuel cell EVs, etc.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete feasibility and enabling-infrastructure commitment for hydrogen transport. It qualifies as a policy despite being exploratory.

parent_statement: Green Transport
policy_statement: The Government will subsidise trials of electric and hybrid ferries and explore replacing traditional ferries with new energy ferries before 2035.
source_quote: As regards ferries, the Government will subsidise ferry operators to conduct trials for electric and hybrid ferries. Subject to the trial results and relevant technological developments, the Government will explore with the ferry operators the possibility of progressively replacing traditional ferries with new energy ferries before 2035. To tie in with the application of new energy in various means of transport, government departments will step up efforts to support and facilitate the development of relevant infrastructure and ancillary facilities.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific subsidy-backed trial and transition commitment with a target date for ferry replacement. It qualifies as a policy and includes a financial instrument component.

parent_statement: Green Transport
policy_statement: The Government will maintain a railway-based public transport system, roll out free-flow tolling, advance congestion charging, and continue promoting cycling and walkability.
source_quote: The Government will continue the current approach of maintaining a public transport system with railway as the backbone, and will adopt different new technologies as well as traffic management measures. For instance, the Free-flow Tolling System will be rolled out at government tolled tunnels and the Tsing Sha Control Area, while 'congestion charging' will be pressed ahead actively, with a view to charging different toll levels according to the traffic condition of the tunnels and the Control Area during different time periods. We hope the above traffic management measures will be able to enhance the road network efficiency and reduce carbon emissions from traffic congestion. Furthermore, the Government will continue to promote cycling for short-distance commuting and enhance walkability.
extraction_rationale: This is a package of concrete transport management and modal-shift measures. Congestion charging is a pricing tool, but the overall policy is broader than a single financial instrument.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will pursue waste reduction, recycling, and waste-to-energy development to move away from landfill dependence and achieve carbon neutrality in waste management.
source_quote: If we can develop adequate waste-to-energy facilities so as to move away from over-reliance on landfills for municipal waste disposal by 2035 as planned, there will be no more municipal waste disposal at landfills. By 2050, most of the landfilled waste will have been decomposed, which will significantly reduce GHG emissions, thus helping us achieve the target of carbon neutrality before 2050.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella waste strategy with multiple subordinate actions on charging, recycling, plastics, landfill gas, and waste-to-energy infrastructure. It qualifies as a parent policy.

parent_statement: Waste Reduction
policy_statement: Hong Kong aims to move away from reliance on landfills for municipal waste disposal by 2035 through adequate waste-to-energy facilities.
source_quote: If we can develop adequate waste-to-energy facilities so as to move away from over-reliance on landfills for municipal waste disposal by 2035 as planned, there will be no more municipal waste disposal at landfills. By 2050, most of the landfilled waste will have been decomposed, which will significantly reduce GHG emissions, thus helping us achieve the target of carbon neutrality before 2050.
section_header: Long-term target: Carbon neutrality in waste management
extraction_rationale: This is a clear long-term waste-system transformation target with a target year and climate rationale. It qualifies as a policy commitment.

parent_statement: Waste Reduction
policy_statement: The Government will develop another waste-to-energy facility, expand food waste recycling infrastructure, and use biogas from food waste treatment as renewable energy.
source_quote: We also need to develop another waste-to-energy facility to process municipal waste, continue to expand our food waste recycling infrastructure, and make use of the biogas generated during the food waste treatment process as an additional source of RE. Only by doing so can we move away from reliance on landfills for municipal waste disposal.
section_header: Long-term target: Carbon neutrality in waste management
extraction_rationale: This is a specific infrastructure and resource-recovery package under the waste strategy. It qualifies as a policy due to named interventions.

parent_statement: Waste Reduction
policy_statement: Hong Kong will pursue a multi-pronged strategy to go plastic-free by reducing single-use plastics through policies, regulations, publicity, recycling facilities, and alternatives.
source_quote: We will map out a long-term solution and go 'plastic-free' by adopting a multi-pronged approach, which includes formulating suitable policies and regulations, stepping up publicity, and expanding waste plastics recycling supporting facilities for turning waste into resources, as well as encouraging the public to replace single-use plastics with reusable or alternative materials.
section_header: Long-term target: Carbon neutrality in waste management
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete policy direction with named instruments and interventions. It is somewhat broad, but sufficiently anchored by regulatory and infrastructure measures.

parent_statement: Waste Reduction
policy_statement: Hong Kong will reduce per capita municipal solid waste disposal by 40% to 45% and raise the recovery rate to about 55%.
source_quote: Through implementing MSW charging and other waste reduction and recycling initiatives, and encouraging the whole community to work together, we aim to progressively reduce the per capita MSW disposal by 40% to 45% and raise the recovery rate to about 55%.
section_header: Medium-term target: Enhance waste reduction and recycling
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified waste reduction and recycling target. It clearly qualifies as a policy commitment.

parent_statement: Waste Reduction
policy_statement: The Government will expand and enhance central collection services and the community recycling network for food waste, plastics, and paper, while supporting low-carbon transformation of the recycling trade.
