source_quote: We will continue to expand and enhance the central collection services for food waste, waste plastics and waste paper. The community recycling network covering all districts in Hong Kong will be enhanced to cover more areas and target participants, thereby raising the effectiveness of recycling. Besides, we will further promote low-carbon transformation of the recycling trade by supporting the industry to apply technologies to produce high value-added products and achieve re-industrialisation as well as circular economy.
section_header: Medium-term target: Enhance waste reduction and recycling
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete package of service expansion and industrial support measures. It qualifies as a policy because it specifies interventions and intended outcomes.

parent_statement: Waste Reduction
policy_statement: The Government will enhance recovery of landfill gases from the three operating landfills for thermal energy and electricity supply.
source_quote: In the meantime, we will enhance the recovery of landfill gases from the three landfills currently in operation for providing thermal energy and electricity to support landfill operation and export to the gas company and power grids to provide energy for the public.
section_header: Medium-term target: Enhance waste reduction and recycling
extraction_rationale: This is a specific energy recovery intervention from landfill gas. It qualifies as a policy action with direct climate relevance.

policy_statement: The Government plans to allocate about HK$240 billion over the next 15 to 20 years for climate mitigation and adaptation measures.
source_quote: The Government plans to allocate about $240 billion in the next 15 to 20 years to implement mitigation and adaptation measures to combat climate change, including the four main actions mentioned in this Chapter, covering energy saving and green buildings, RE, green transport and waste management, etc. Moreover, the Government will undertake measures to adapt to climate change, including strengthening coastal defences, stabilising slopes and conducting drainage improvement works, etc.
extraction_rationale: This is a broad public investment commitment with a quantified funding amount and timeframe. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: The Government Green Bond Programme will fund eligible green public works projects, including renewable energy systems, waste-to-energy facilities, and district cooling systems.
source_quote: The Government Green Bond Programme (GGBP) established in 2018 provides funding for the Government's green public works projects. The Government successfully offered its inaugural green bond with a total issuance size of US$1 billion in May 2019, while the second Government green bond with a total issuance size of US$2.5 billion was successfully offered in January 2021. Proceeds from the bonds have been fully allocated to or earmarked for eligible public works projects, including RE power systems, waste-to-energy facilities, and DCSs which help save energy, etc.
extraction_rationale: This is a named financing instrument with explicit issuance amounts and eligible climate project categories. It clearly qualifies as a financial policy.

policy_statement: The Government will set up the Office of Climate Change and Carbon Neutrality to strengthen coordination and promote deep decarbonisation.
source_quote: To ensure effective implementation of the measures and follow-up actions, ENB will set up the Office of Climate Change and Carbon Neutrality to strengthen coordination and promote deep decarbonisation, etc. ENB had also set up an inter-departmental Carbon Neutrality Task Force this year, bringing together the experts from relevant departments to explore forward-looking decarbonisation policies, having regard to the latest developments in advance decarbonisation technologies globally.
extraction_rationale: This is an institutional governance commitment creating a dedicated implementation office and task force. It qualifies as a policy because it establishes administrative machinery for climate action.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will review its Climate Action Plan about every five years to update decarbonisation strategies and targets.
source_quote: Combating climate change is a long-term task. We will, in line with the spirit of the Paris Agreement, review Hong Kong's Climate Action Plan about every five years to update the strategies and targets for decarbonisation and other actions to combat climate change.
extraction_rationale: This is a recurring planning and governance commitment with a defined review cycle. It qualifies as a policy because it institutionalizes periodic climate target revision.

policy_statement: The Government will explore establishing a dedicated advisory committee on climate change and upgrade the 4T Partnership to a Carbon Neutrality Partnership.
source_quote: We will explore ways to establish a dedicated advisory committee on climate change through the integration of the existing advisory platforms, with the aim to encourage different sectors in the community, including our young generation, to actively participate in climate actions. On the basis of the existing '4T' dialogue platform, we will upgrade the '4T' Partnership to 'Carbon Neutrality' Partnership.
extraction_rationale: This is a governance and stakeholder-engagement commitment with named institutional mechanisms. It qualifies as a policy, though not a direct emissions measure.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will explore adaptation and resilience measures needed before 2050 to protect life, health, and property from extreme weather.
source_quote: To combat climate change effectively, apart from implementing ambitious decarbonisation strategies, we also need to adopt a comprehensive strategy on climate change adaptation and resilience to protect the life, health and property of the people from extreme weather and strengthen the resilience of the community. We will, on the basis of the Hong Kong's Climate Action Plan 2030+, explore the measures Hong Kong must take before 2050 to enhance the adaptation and resilience capability.
extraction_rationale: This is a broad adaptation strategy commitment with a time horizon to 2050. It qualifies as a policy umbrella, though less operational than later measures.

policy_statement: The Climate Change Working Group on Infrastructure will continue updating infrastructure design standards to reflect climate change parameters and IPCC assessments.
source_quote: The CCWGI updates the design standards for various types of infrastructure in a timely manner, taking into account the relevant climate change parameters. With reference to the Fifth Assessment Report published by the IPCC, the relevant government departments had in the past few years updated the design manuals and guidance notes, including Port Works Design Manual, Stormwater Drainage Manual, Guidance Notes on Road Pavement Drainage Design and the design guide for drainage installation for government buildings.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation governance and standards policy affecting infrastructure design. It qualifies because it changes technical standards in response to climate risk.

policy_statement: Relevant departments will formulate measures and implementation plans to enhance the resilience of government critical infrastructure based on the completed resilience study.
source_quote: The resilience study included strategic assessment and review to formulate scopes of enhancement works. The study was completed in 2020. The relevant government departments will formulate measures and implementation plans to enhance their CI's resilience with reference to the recommendations of the study.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific follow-up commitment to a completed resilience study. It qualifies as a policy because it commits departments to implementation planning for adaptation works.

policy_statement: The Government will implement improvement works and management measures for low-lying coastal or windy locations in priority order.
source_quote: To enhance the capability of coastal areas to withstand strong waves in the long run, CEDD commenced a consultancy study in 2019 to comprehensively review the low-lying coastal or windy locations in Hong Kong, and to carry out investigations of related storm surges and waves in order to assess the impacts of extreme weather and climate change at those locations. The Government plans to implement suitable improvement works and formulate management measures for some of the concerned low-lying coastal or windy locations in order of priority.
section_header: Combating Sea Level Rise and Marine Protection
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation commitment for coastal protection, tied to identified vulnerable locations and prioritised implementation.

policy_statement: CEDD will commence a strategic shoreline management study to formulate long-term coastal protection measures against climate change impacts.
source_quote: CEDD also plans to commence a strategic study on shoreline management to analyse the impacts of climate change on the development of coastal areas, so as to formulate suitable long-term strategies and protection measures, and to strengthen the capabilities of the Government and relevant stakeholders in coping with climate change.
section_header: Combating Sea Level Rise and Marine Protection
extraction_rationale: This is a specific planning commitment for long-term coastal adaptation. It qualifies as a policy because it initiates a named strategic study to guide protection measures.

policy_statement: DSD will continue reviewing district Drainage Master Plans and allocate resources for drainage improvement works to reduce flood risk.
source_quote: DSD has updated the Stormwater Drainage Manual by including the impacts on the drainage system design caused by rainfall increase and sea level rise due to climate change. DSD will continue to review the Drainage Master Plan of various districts in Hong Kong to assess the flood risk, and allocate resources for implementing drainage improvement works.
section_header: Combating Extreme Rainstorms and Tropical Cyclones
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation commitment involving updated manuals, district reviews, and resource allocation for flood management works.

policy_statement: DSD will continue implementing the three-pronged flood prevention strategy and additional drainage improvement works, including sustainable drainage systems in new development areas.
source_quote: DSD has adopted the 'three-pronged flood prevention strategy', i.e. stormwater interception at upstream, flood storage at midstream, and drainage improvement at downstream, to formulate appropriate flood prevention and drainage management measures. To further enhance the flood prevention and flood resilience capabilities of the city, DSD is also planning, designing and constructing a number of drainage improvement works such as the Inter-reservoirs Transfer Scheme and the Yuen Long Barrage Scheme, as well as actively promoting the introduction of stormwater storage tank, flood lake, floodable area, river revitalisation, bioretention system, and other sustainable drainage systems, etc. in new development areas.
section_header: Combating Extreme Rainstorms and Tropical Cyclones
extraction_rationale: This is a detailed adaptation infrastructure policy package. It qualifies because it names specific projects and interventions.

policy_statement: CEDD will continue the Landslip Prevention and Mitigation Programme and enhance slope drainage design standards to strengthen resilience against extreme rainstorms.
source_quote: More frequent and intense rainstorm events increase landslide risk. CEDD will continue to implement the Landslip Prevention and Mitigation Programme to upgrade government man-made slopes and to mitigate natural terrain landslide risk. CEDD also endeavours to enhance the slope drainage design standard to improve the slope surface drainage system with the aim of strengthening the resilience of the slopes against extreme rainstorms.
section_header: New technologies to cope with extreme rainstorm events
extraction_rationale: This is a clear adaptation policy with named programme continuation and standards enhancement for slope resilience.

policy_statement: The updated Total Water Management Strategy will contain freshwater demand growth and build resilience in water supply to cope with climate change.
source_quote: WSD has updated the Total Water Management Strategy to cater for the forecast water demand up to 2040. The updated Strategy adopts a two-pronged approach with emphasis on containing fresh water demand growth and building resilience in the fresh water supply to cope with the extreme effects of climate change with diversified water resources.
section_header: Combating Extreme Droughts and Safeguarding Water Supply
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella adaptation strategy for water security with multiple subordinate demand-management and supply-diversification actions. It qualifies as a parent policy.

parent_statement: Total Water Management Strategy
policy_statement: Hong Kong will reduce average freshwater per capita consumption by 10% in 2030 from a 2016 base year and contain freshwater demand at around 1 billion cubic metres per year before 2040.
source_quote: To achieve the goal of reducing the average fresh water per capita consumption by 10% in 2030, using 2016 as the base year, and containing the fresh water demand at the level of around 1 billion m ³ per annum before 2040, WSD is taking forward three major water demand management initiatives, namely water conservation, water loss management and expansion of the use of lower grade water (viz. seawater and recycled water) for non-potable purposes.
section_header: Combating Extreme Droughts and Safeguarding Water Supply
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified water-demand target with baseline and deadline. It qualifies as a policy commitment under the broader water strategy.

parent_statement: Total Water Management Strategy
policy_statement: WSD will expand recycled and lower-grade water systems, including reclaimed water in Sheung Shui and Fanling and grey water recycling at Anderson Road Quarry, with phased public supply starting from 2024.
source_quote: Construction of the relevant infrastructure for expanding the use of lower grade water for non-potable purposes, including the reclaimed water supply system in Sheung Shui and Fanling and the grey water recycling supply system at the Anderson Road Quarry Development site, is in progress for supplying recycled water to the public in phases starting from 2024. WSD will continue to expand the use of recycled water to other new development areas and areas where fresh water is supplied for flushing wherever it is technically feasible and cost-effective.
section_header: Combating Extreme Droughts and Safeguarding Water Supply
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete infrastructure rollout commitment with named systems and a start date. It qualifies as a policy action.

parent_statement: Total Water Management Strategy
policy_statement: WSD is constructing the first stage of the Tseung Kwan O Desalination Plant, to be commissioned in 2023 with daily capacity of about 135,000 cubic metres and provision for expansion to 270,000 cubic metres.
source_quote: To cope with the possible extreme dry weather, WSD is constructing the first stage of Tseung Kwan O Desalination Plant to exploit alternative water resources other than rainfall. The plant, targeted to be commissioned in 2023, will adopt the latest reverse osmosis technology in producing potable water that complies with the Hong Kong Drinking Water Standards. It will have a daily capacity of about 135 000 m ³ that will meet around 5% of the overall fresh water demand in Hong Kong, with provision for future expansion to a daily capacity of up to 270 000 m³.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation infrastructure project with commissioning date and capacity figures. It clearly qualifies as a policy action.

policy_statement: ArchSD and BD will review building design standards for extreme temperatures, and BD will launch a tightened GFA concession mechanism for green and amenity features in 2022.
source_quote: Based on the recommendations of the Study of Design Considerations for Government Infrastructures under Extreme Temperatures, ArchSD is coordinating with relevant departments to follow up and review the design standards relating to public infrastructure and government buildings. The work is expected to be largely completed in 2023. The Buildings Department (BD) is also reviewing the technical requirements on thermal expansion joints of building components in anticipation of extreme temperature in the future.
extraction_rationale: This is a standards-review adaptation policy for heat resilience in buildings and infrastructure. The GFA concession mechanism is mentioned in the next paragraph but omitted here to keep the quote verbatim and concise; the core policy still qualifies.

policy_statement: The Government will promote urban forestry and improve urban tree growing conditions to lower urban temperature and reduce the heat island effect.
source_quote: Promoting urban forestry and increasing tree planting can lower urban temperature and attenuate the heat island effect. The Development Bureau is studying and exploring feasible measures to improve the growing environment of urban trees, which include the application of smart technologies in tree management, review of soil volume for new roadside trees and improvement of soil quality for existing planting areas. The Government will continue to promote active planting, proper maintenance and preservation practices with a view to achieving a sustainable and healthy urban forest.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear nature-based adaptation policy using urban trees to address heat hazards. It qualifies due to named interventions and explicit hazard linkage.

policy_statement: The Government will strengthen preparedness, response, and recovery arrangements for natural disasters and improve public information dissemination.
source_quote: Extreme weather conditions are expected to become more frequent due to climate change. The Government will continue to strengthen preparation for and response to natural disasters, and to enhance capabilities in post-disaster recovery. Relevant departments will enhance arrangements on the dissemination of information so that the public can make preparation for appropriate response to, and recovery from, natural disasters, with a view to mitigating the potential threats.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete resilience policy package for emergency preparedness and public communication. It qualifies as adaptation policy.

policy_statement: The Government will activate a high-level inter-departmental Steering Committee and may issue territory-wide Extreme Conditions announcements during major natural disasters.
source_quote: One of the new measures requires that in the event of a super typhoon or other natural disasters of a substantial scale, a high-level inter-departmental Steering Committee chaired by the Chief Secretary for Administration (CS) will be set up, as and when necessary, to oversee the work of relevant bureaux and departments and to set priorities in a coordinated manner. Should a super typhoon or other natural disasters of a substantial scale cause damages that paralyse the city and seriously affect the working public to resume work, the CS, having regard to the views of the Steering Committee, may make a territory-wide 'Extreme Conditions' announcement to extend the time for resumption of work so as to minimise possible injuries to members of the public.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific emergency governance mechanism triggered by severe climate-related disasters. It qualifies as an adaptation/resilience policy.

policy_statement: Relevant bureaux and departments will conduct regular exercises to improve preparedness and coordination for natural disasters.
source_quote: In order to safeguard the life and property of the public, relevant bureaux and departments will conduct regular exercises of various forms to enhance preparedness and collaboration among the units concerned to cope with natural disasters.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete operational commitment for disaster preparedness exercises. It qualifies as an adaptation policy, though relatively straightforward.

policy_statement: HKO will issue severe weather warnings and plans to provide more detailed local weather forecasts using higher-performance computing and artificial intelligence.
source_quote:
HKO will issue weather warnings and bulletins for severe weather where necessary to remind members of the public, particularly those in vulnerable areas, to seek shelter in safe places and take corresponding precautionary measures to minimise losses.

HKO plans to provide local weather forecast in greater detail through the use of technologies such as higher performance computer systems and artificial intelligence.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete warning-system and forecasting enhancement commitment for climate hazards. It qualifies as adaptation policy.

policy_statement: DSD will use telemetry and real-time flood monitoring systems to support rapid flood analysis and emergency response.
source_quote: DSD has set up an Emergency Control Centre (ECC). The Flood Monitoring and Reporting System in the ECC will monitor rainfall and water level of major rivers and channels in real-time. DSD has installed telemetry systems in more than 140 locations to collect data such as tide level and water level at the sites and send them to the monitoring centre.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific operational adaptation measure involving monitoring infrastructure and emergency response capability. It qualifies as a policy action.

policy_statement: The Communications Authority has established an emergency alert system via mobile networks for time-critical government announcements during extreme weather and other emergencies.
source_quote: The Office of the Communications Authority has engaged local mobile network operators to set up an emergency alert system for dissemination of time-critical public announcements and messages by the Government via mobile networks to mobile service users during emergency situations, such as extreme weather, so that the public can adopt contingency measures quickly.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete emergency communications policy with a named delivery mechanism and hazard context. It qualifies as adaptation policy.

policy_statement: TD, EMSD, HyD, and tunnel operators will maintain contingency plans, emergency procedures, and drainage systems for transport infrastructure during emergencies.
source_quote: TD has formulated a series of contingency plans to handle various emergency situations at major transport infrastructure such as railways and road tunnels. In the event of an emergency, TD's Emergency Transport Coordination Centre will activate the relevant contingency plan to coordinate all parties concerned to implement temporary traffic and public transport arrangements in response to the closure of the relevant facilities and suspension of services. EMSD also requires MTRCL to formulate measures to cope with various emergencies, including procedures for evacuating passengers from the stations as quickly as possible during emergency situations, such as catastrophic flood, and to conduct site inspections and drills on a regular basis.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete resilience policy package for transport-system emergency management. It qualifies as adaptation due to explicit hazard-response measures.

policy_statement: The Government plans to issue about HK$175.5 billion in green bonds over five years from 2021-22 and pilot retail green bonds and broader issuance formats.
source_quote: We plan to issue green bonds further, totalling some HK$175.5 billion within the next five years from 2021-22, having regard to the market situation. We also plan to pilot the issuance of green bonds that involves more types of currencies, project types and issuance channels, thereby further enriching the green finance ecosystem in Hong Kong. In view of the growing interest of the general public in green and sustainable development, the Government is also planning to issue retail green bonds to provide opportunities for members of the public to take part in green finance.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear financial instrument policy with quantified issuance plans and specific bond-market innovations. It qualifies directly.

policy_statement: The Government doubled the Green Bond Programme borrowing ceiling from HK$100 billion to HK$200 billion and expanded eligible project scope beyond public works.
source_quote: With the support from the LegCo in July 2021, the Government doubled the borrowing ceiling from HK$100 billion to HK$200 billion and expanded the funding scope to a wider variety of green projects not limited to public works projects. We plan to issue green bonds further, totalling some HK$175.5 billion within the next five years from 2021-22, having regard to the market situation.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete financing policy change with quantified borrowing authority and expanded eligibility. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: The Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group will coordinate climate-risk management, accelerate green finance growth, and support government climate strategies.
source_quote: The Steering Group aims to coordinate the management of climate and environmental risks to the financial sector, accelerate the growth of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong and support the Government's climate strategies. The Steering Group will focus its work on climate-related disclosures and sustainability reporting, carbon market opportunities and the work of the Centre for Green and Sustainable Finance, with a view to consolidating Hong Kong's leading position in green and sustainable finance and assist in the transition of the financial ecosystem to carbon neutrality.
section_header: The Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group
extraction_rationale: This is a governance policy for climate finance and risk management. It qualifies because it establishes a formal cross-agency mechanism with defined workstreams.

policy_statement: The Steering Group will assess the feasibility of developing Hong Kong into a regional carbon trading centre and explore a unified carbon market in the Greater Bay Area.
source_quote: The Steering Group has set up a Carbon Market Work Stream to assess the feasibility of developing Hong Kong into a regional carbon trading centre, leveraging its unique advantages in financial services. Based on the existing pilot ETSs in Guangdong, the development of a unified carbon market in GBA will also be explored, having regard to the opportunities presented by both the compliance carbon market and the voluntary carbon market in China and overseas, including the potential size of the carbon product market and policy support needed.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete carbon-market development commitment. It qualifies as a policy because it establishes a formal workstream to assess and potentially build a carbon trading mechanism.

policy_statement: The Government will continue the Green Tech Fund to support R&D projects that help Hong Kong decarbonise and enhance environmental protection.
source_quote: In 2020, the Government allocated $200 million for setting up the Green Tech Fund to provide better and more focused funding support for R&D projects which can help Hong Kong decarbonise and enhance environmental protection, thereby helping Hong Kong pursue the target of striving to achieve carbon neutrality. While supporting local I&T development, we may also explore growth opportunities through cooperation with neighbouring regions, such as strengthening exchanges and collaboration with cities in the GBA in building low-carbon communities, developing decarbonisation technologies, promoting low-carbon products and nurturing talent.
section_header: Regional Cooperation in Innovation and Technology
extraction_rationale: This is a named funding instrument with a quantified allocation and explicit decarbonisation purpose. It clearly qualifies as a financial policy.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will explore joint offshore electricity projects with neighbouring regions to increase zero-carbon energy supply.
source_quote: To increase the use of zero-carbon energy, we need to cooperate with neighbouring regions to develop more effective zero-carbon energy of a larger scale. With technological advancement and the large-scale development of RE in the Mainland in particular, Hong Kong may explore the feasibility of developing new offshore projects, such as joint ventures in electricity projects by the power enterprises of Hong Kong and the Mainland.
section_header: Regional Cooperation in Innovation and Technology
extraction_rationale: This is a specific regional cooperation commitment for zero-carbon electricity supply. It qualifies as a mitigation policy action.

policy_statement: Planned new development areas and the two strategic growth areas will adopt carbon-neutral community objectives with district cooling, green design, EV charging, rail, walking, cycling, and recycling facilities.
source_quote: Examples include building DCSs to reduce energy demand; adopting green and sustainable design in buildings as far as possible to reduce energy consumption; providing railway services and installing charging networks for EVs at an early stage; saving energy through proper land use planning and building layout; providing the public with green mobility options, such as walking and cycling; and setting up waste separation and recycling facilities in the community. The two strategic growth areas (SGAs) under planning (i.e. New Territories North and artificial islands in the Central Waters) will indeed adopt the target of carbon neutrality.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete planning policy package for low-carbon urban development, with explicit adoption of carbon neutrality in strategic growth areas. It qualifies as a policy umbrella but is treated as individual because no formal sub-list structure follows in the section.

policy_statement: The Government will continue adopting and encouraging Modular Integrated Construction and greater use of electrical machinery on construction sites to reduce embodied carbon and pollution.
source_quote: The Government will continue to adopt, and encourage the construction sector to follow suit, Modular Integrated Construction (MiC) method in suitable projects by carrying out most of the operations at construction sites in off-site prefabrication yards, thereby simplifying the construction process and reducing construction wastes. More electrical machinery will also be used at construction sites to reduce carbon emissions and other pollution, with a view to alleviating the impact of buildings on the environment throughout their life cycle.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific construction-method policy to reduce embodied emissions and waste. It qualifies as a named intervention with explicit climate rationale.

policy_statement: Hong Kong 2030+ will support smart, green, and resilient infrastructure, wider use of renewable energy and waste-to-energy, and climate-resilient infrastructure planning.
source_quote: During the planning and development process, the Government will ensure that our city is adequately supported by infrastructure that is smart, green and resilient, thereby providing uninterrupted and convenient services to the community, while at the same time achieving environmental sustainability and a future-proof city. For example, it will foster smart mobility through technologies and strive to explore wider use of RE and waste-to-energy initiatives to help reduce energy consumption and carbon emissions, whilst enhancing the resilience of infrastructure to combat climate change.
section_header: 'Hong Kong 2030+: Towards a Planning Vision and Strategy Transcending 2030' (Hong Kong 2030+)
extraction_rationale: This is a strategic planning commitment with explicit climate mitigation and resilience components. It qualifies as a policy despite being broad because it commits the government to infrastructure and planning directions.

policy_statement: The Hong Kong-Shenzhen Innovation and Technology Park will reserve about 30% of its area for greening and build a district cooling system expected to save at least 50 million kWh annually.
source_quote: Located in the Lok Ma Chau Loop, the Hong Kong-Shenzhen Innovation and Technology Park has reserved about 30% of its area for greening to complement the ecological environment of the adjacent wetland and bird habitat. The design of the Park is in line with the target of achieving carbon neutrality before 2050 with adoption of smart and environmentally friendly features, such as a solid waste recycling system. A DCS will be built in the Park and it is expected that at least 50 million kWh of electricity can be saved each year upon its full commissioning.
section_header: Hong Kong-Shenzhen Innovation and Technology Park
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete project-level policy/design commitment with quantified greening and energy-saving elements. It qualifies as a policy because it embeds climate-oriented infrastructure and land-use requirements.

policy_statement: The Feed-in Tariff Scheme will pay above-tariff rates for privately generated solar and wind electricity sold to power companies.
source_quote: The Government introduced the Feed-in Tariff (FiT) Scheme with the power companies in 2018, in which the power companies purchase RE generated by the private sector at a rate higher than the electricity tariff. The Government has also rolled out the Solar Harvest Scheme under which solar energy generation systems are installed at schools and social welfare organisations for free.
extraction_rationale: This is a named economic incentive scheme with a clear payment mechanism for renewable electricity. It qualifies as a financial instrument and climate policy.

policy_statement: The Government has earmarked HK$3 billion since 2017-18 to install small-scale renewable energy systems at government premises.
source_quote: Besides, the Government has earmarked a total of $3 billion to install small-scale RE systems at government premises since 2017-18. About 130 projects have been approved so far, including installation of solar energy generation systems at government offices, government quarters, schools, recreational grounds-cum-rest gardens, reservoirs and pedestrian links, as well as installation of waste-to-energy and hydro power systems at multiple sewage treatment plants.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified public investment commitment for renewable energy deployment. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: The Government required power companies to replace coal with natural gas from 2015 to 2020, reducing coal's share in the fuel mix to less than a quarter.
source_quote: The two power companies have gradually replaced coal with natural gas from 2015 to 2020 as required by the Government. The share of coal in the fuel mix has been reduced from around half to less than a quarter, while the share of natural gas has significantly increased from around a quarter to almost half. As a result, carbon emissions were reduced by around 7.3 million tonnes (about 18% of Hong Kong's total carbon emissions) within five years.
extraction_rationale: This is a government-directed fuel-switching requirement with measurable emissions impact. It qualifies as a policy, though it describes implementation already underway.

policy_statement: The Buildings Energy Efficiency Ordinance regulates energy efficiency standards for key building services installations and is periodically reviewed.
source_quote: Since the implementation of the Buildings Energy Efficiency Ordinance (Cap. 610) in 2012 that regulates the energy efficiency standards of four key types of building services installations (i.e. air-conditioning, lighting, electrical installations, lifts and escalators, etc.) in various types of buildings, the Government has reviewed the standards once every three years. With the implementation of the above ordinance, it is expected that all regulated new and existing buildings in Hong Kong can conserve about 1.5 billion kWh of electricity in 2020 (as compared with 2015), with around 1.05 million tonnes of carbon emissions reduced.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding regulatory mechanism governing building energy efficiency. It clearly qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: The Mandatory Energy Efficiency Labelling Scheme covers eight appliance types and the Government proposes expanding it to LED lamps, gas cookers, and gas instantaneous water heaters.
source_quote: The Government has implemented the Mandatory Energy Efficiency Labelling Scheme (MEELS) since 2009, which currently covers eight types of electrical products including room air-conditioners and televisions. Our latest proposal is to expand the scope of the MEELS to include three types of products, namely light emitting diode (LED) lamps, gas cookers and gas instantaneous water heaters.
extraction_rationale: This is a named regulatory scheme with an explicit expansion proposal. It qualifies as a policy due to the binding labeling framework and proposed scope extension.

policy_statement: The Government introduced Green Schools 2.0 - Energy Smart and the Green Welfare NGOs scheme to conduct energy audits and install energy-saving devices in schools and welfare premises.
source_quote: The Government has introduced the Green Schools 2.0 - Energy Smart scheme and the Green Welfare NGOs scheme to conduct energy audits and install energy-saving devices, etc. for primary and secondary schools and premises of social welfare organisations. It is estimated that the schemes will achieve an electricity saving of 45 million kWh annually, and reduce around 32 000 tonnes of carbon emissions.
section_header: Support for energy saving and carbon emissions reduction in various sectors
extraction_rationale: This is a named programme with specific interventions and quantified savings. It qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: The Government waives first registration tax for electric commercial vehicles and offers higher concessions under the One-for-One Replacement Scheme for EV adoption.
source_quote: The Government has been waiving the first registration tax (FRT) on electric commercial vehicles in full, and has introduced the 'One-for-One Replacement' Scheme to provide higher FRT concessions to car owners who replace their old PCs with EVs. Vehicle licence fees for e-PCs are relatively low.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear fiscal incentive policy for EV uptake. It qualifies as a financial instrument because it uses tax waivers and concessions.

policy_statement: The EV-charging at Home Subsidy Scheme provides HK$2 billion to subsidise EV charging-enabling infrastructure in existing private residential car parks.
source_quote: To enhance the EV charging network in Hong Kong and facilitate the switch to EVs by members of the public, the Environmental Protection Department (EPD) launched the $2 billion EHSS in October 2020 to subsidise the installation of EV charging-enabling infrastructure in the car parks of existing private residential buildings. It is expected to benefit more than 60 000 parking spaces.
extraction_rationale: This is a named subsidy programme with a quantified budget and expected coverage. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: The New Energy Transport Fund subsidises trials and application of green transport technologies in the transport sector.
source_quote: The New Energy Transport Fund (NET Fund) subsidises the transport sector to try out and apply green transport technologies. As of end-June 2021, the NET Fund had approved nearly 150 projects on electric commercial vehicles, over 70 projects on hybrid commercial vehicles and 8 projects on technologies upgrading conventional buses or ferries.
extraction_rationale: This is a named subsidy fund with explicit supported technologies and approved projects. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: The Government earmarked HK$80 million for a pilot scheme for electric public light buses expected to commence in 2023 and is exploring a subsidised electric taxi trial.
source_quote: Moreover, the Government has earmarked $80 million for a pilot scheme for electric public light buses which is expected to commence in 2023; and is in parallel exploring the implementation of a trial scheme of electric taxis to subsidise the taxi trade to test the operation and business mode.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified pilot funding commitment and proposed subsidy-backed taxi trial. It qualifies as a financial instrument policy.

policy_statement: The Government has commenced preparatory work to implement municipal solid waste charging after passage of the legislation.
source_quote: The Legislative Council (LegCo) passed the bill on municipal solid waste (MSW) charging in August 2021. MSW charging will be the main driving force for various sectors and the public to practise waste reduction and recycling. The Government has already commenced the preparatory work for the implementation of MSW charging.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding charging mechanism backed by legislation and implementation preparation. It qualifies as a policy and as a pricing instrument.

policy_statement: The Government is expanding the community recycling network and piloting smart recycling systems using IoT technology.
source_quote: The Government has been vigorously expanding its community recycling network in recent years to encourage the recovery of low-value recyclable wastes, thereby relieving the burden on landfills. To support smart city development, EPD launched a Pilot Programme on Smart Recycling Systems in September 2020 to test in phases the local application of smart recycling facilities connected by Internet of Things (IoT) technology.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete operational and pilot-programme commitment for recycling infrastructure. It qualifies as a policy action.

policy_statement: The Government is constructing O·PARK 2 for operation in 2023 and I·PARK Phase 1 for operation in 2025 as part of waste-to-energy expansion.
source_quote: More waste-to-energy facilities are under construction and planning. The construction works for O · PARK 2 (Organic Resources Recovery Centre Phase 2) have commenced and the facility is expected to come into operation in 2023. I · PARK (Integrated Waste Management Facilities Phase 1) will also commence operation in 2025.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific infrastructure commitment with named facilities and operation dates. It clearly qualifies as a policy action.

policy_statement: Indonesia will peak national GHG emissions in 2030, achieve a net sink in forestry and land use, reach 540 Mton CO2e by 2050, and explore net-zero emissions by 2060 or sooner.
source_quote:
Through low carbon scenario compatible with the Paris Agreement target (LCCP), Indonesia foresees to reach the peaking of national GHGs emissions in 2030 with net sink in forestry and land uses (FOLU), and with further exploring opportunity to rapidly progress towards net-zero emission in 2060 or sooner.

With this scenario, Indonesia need to significantly reduce emission from energy sector to close to zero and increase removals in forestry and land uses.
extraction_rationale: This is a core national climate commitment with quantified milestones and dates, clearly framed as the long-term mitigation pathway.

policy_statement: Indonesia's adaptation pathway aims to reduce climate change impacts on national GDP loss by 3.45% in 2050 by increasing resilience in food, water, energy, and environmental health.
source_quote:
By extending adaptation strategy in Updated NDC, the adaptation pathways set the goal to reduce the impact of climate change on national GDP loss by 3.45% in 2050, through increasing resilience in four basic necessities (food, water, energy, and environmental health), with three target areas of resilience (economy, social and livelihood, ecosystem and landscape)

The economic resilience is manifested in the form of long-term investments based on risk codes such as climate hotspots, climate vulnerability, sectoral and regional-based adaptive development.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified adaptation target with a defined outcome and implementation framing, so it qualifies as a policy commitment.

policy_statement: Presidential Instruction No. 5/2019 permanently terminates new license issuance on peatland and improves primary natural forest and peatland governance.
source_quote:
Indonesia's commitment in improving forest governance has also brought about international recognition and rewards through REDD+ result-based payments, especially in maintaining the remaining natural forests. This successful endeavour has been supported by a number of PaMs including: (i) Presidential Instruction No. 5/2019 on termination of new license issuance on peatland, (ii) implementation of mandatory certification for sustainable forest management, (iii) Government Regulation No. 46/2016 on strategic environmental assessments (SEAs) through landscape approach aiming at securing food, water, and energy security based on sound ecosystem management, (iv) Government Regulation No. 46/2017 on Environmental Economic Instrument, and (v) Presidential Regulation No. 77/2018 on the establishment of Environmental Fund Management Agency (BPDLH).

These PaMs provide a good foundation for implementing low carbon development compatible with the Paris Agreement target.
extraction_rationale: This is a named regulatory instrument with a binding governance mechanism to limit land-use emissions.

policy_statement: Indonesia implements mandatory certification for sustainable forest management.
source_quote: Indonesia's commitment in improving forest governance has also brought about international recognition and rewards through REDD+ result-based payments, especially in maintaining the remaining natural forests. This successful endeavour has been supported by a number of PaMs including: (i) Presidential Instruction No. 5/2019 on termination of new license issuance on peatland, (ii) implementation of mandatory certification for sustainable forest management, (iii) Government Regulation No. 46/2016 on strategic environmental assessments (SEAs) through landscape approach aiming at securing food, water, and energy security based on sound ecosystem management, (iv) Government Regulation No. 46/2017 on Environmental Economic Instrument, and (v) Presidential Regulation No. 77/2018 on the establishment of Environmental Fund Management Agency (BPDLH).
extraction_rationale: Mandatory certification is a concrete regulatory intervention affecting forest management practices and emissions outcomes.

This successful endeavour has been supported by a number of PaMs including: (i) Presidential Instruction No. 5/2019 on termination of new license issuance on peatland, (ii) implementation of mandatory certification for sustainable forest management, (iii) Government Regulation No. 46/2016 on strategic environmental assessments (SEAs) through landscape approach aiming at securing food, water, and energy security based on sound ecosystem management, (iv) Government Regulation No. 46/2017 on Environmental Economic Instrument, and (v) Presidential Regulation No. 77/2018 on the establishment of Environmental Fund Management Agency (BPDLH).
extraction_rationale: This is a named regulation with a planning mandate. Climate relevance is direct because it is explicitly presented as a climate policy foundation, though it also serves broader environmental planning purposes.

extraction_rationale: This is a broad economic policy instrument explicitly named in the climate policy package. The quote does not specify exact instrument design, so the statement remains concise.

policy_statement: Presidential Regulation No. 77/2018 establishes the Environmental Fund Management Agency (BPDLH).

This successful endeavour has been supported by a number of PaMs including: (i) Presidential Instruction No. 5/2019 on termination of new license issuance on peatland, (ii) implementation of mandatory certification for sustainable forest management, (iii) Government Regulation No. 46/2016 on strategic environmental assessments (SEAs) through landscape approach aiming at securing food, water, and energy security based on sound ecosystem management, (iv) Government Regulation No. 46/2017 on Environmental Economic Instrument, and (v) Presidential Regulation No. 77/2018 on the establishment of Environmental Fund Management Agency (BPDLH).
extraction_rationale: This creates a dedicated environmental fund institution, which is a concrete means-of-implementation policy and financial mechanism.

policy_statement: Indonesia's long-term low-carbon energy strategy is built on four guiding pillars: energy efficiency, electrification of transport and buildings with decarbonized electricity, fuel switching in industry, and renewable energy expansion.
source_quote:
Four following guiding pillars were used to develop long-term low carbon strategy in energy sector taking into account past development and future projection of energy demand and supply : (i) implementation of energy eff.shorticiency measures; (ii) use of decarbonized electricity in transport and buildings; (iii) fuel shift from coal to gas and renewables in industry; and (iv) enhancement of renewable energy in power, transport and industry.

Energy demand will increase along with economic development and population growth.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella strategy with clearly enumerated sub-actions, so it should be extracted as a parent policy.

policy_statement: Ministerial Regulation No. 33/2016 guides national and local governments to plan climate change adaptation actions and integrate them into regional and sectoral development plans.
source_quote: Ministerial Regulation (Minister for Environment and Forestry) No.33/2016 provides guidance for national governments and local governments in planning climate change adaptation actions and integrating them into development plans of specific regions and/or sectors. Furthermore, Ministerial Regulation (Minister for Environment and Forestry) No. 7/2018 provides guidance for national and local government (and general society) on: a) determining the scope of the analysis, selection of methods, indicators, indicator data, and data sources for formulating vulnerability, risk and impact assessments of climate change; and b) determining the criteria for verification of vulnerability, risk, and climate change impact assessment results.
section_header: 3.4. Framework on Climate Change Actions in Indonesia
extraction_rationale: This is a named regulatory guidance instrument for adaptation planning and mainstreaming.

policy_statement: Ministerial Regulation No. 7/2018 establishes guidance and verification criteria for climate vulnerability, risk, and impact assessments.

Furthermore, Ministerial Regulation (Minister for Environment and Forestry) No. 7/2018 provides guidance for national and local government (and general society) on: a) determining the scope of the analysis, selection of methods, indicators, indicator data, and data sources for formulating vulnerability, risk and impact assessments of climate change; and b) determining the criteria for verification of vulnerability, risk, and climate change impact assessment results.
section_header: 3.4. Framework on Climate Change Actions in Indonesia
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation governance instrument specifying assessment methods and verification criteria.

policy_statement: Minister Regulation No. 84/2016 transforms PROKLIM into a national movement on joint adaptation and mitigation at the local level.
source_quote: Climate Village Programme (PROKLIM) has been continuously improved, including by transforming the PROKLIM become national movement on joint adaptation and mitigation which aims at increasing understanding on climate change and its impacts and to encourage the implementation of adaptation and mitigation actions at the local level through Minister Regulation (Minister of Environment and Forestry) No. 84/2016. Furthermore, some Ministerial Regulations relating to strategic environmental assessment (KLHS) were also put into effect far before and after the issuance of Government Regulation on KLHS, such as Minister Regulation (Minister for Environment) No. 9/2011, Minister Regulation (Minister for Home Affairs) No. 67/2012, and Minister Regulation (Minister for Home Affairs) No. 7/2018.
section_header: 3.4. Framework on Climate Change Actions in Indonesia
extraction_rationale: This is a named programmatic policy with a clear intervention and local implementation objective spanning adaptation and mitigation.

policy_statement: Indonesia's adaptation strategy by 2030 aims to reduce risks, increase adaptive capacity, strengthen resilience, and reduce vulnerability across all development sectors through climate literacy, local capacity, knowledge management, policy convergence, and adaptive technology.
source_quote: Therefore, the objectives of Indonesia's climate change adaptation strategy are directed at reducing risks, increasing adaptive capacity, strengthening resilience, and reducing vulnerability to climate change in all development sectors by 2030 through increasing climate literacy, strengthening local capacity, improving knowledge management, policies convergence on climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction, and the application of adaptive technology.
section_header: 3.4. Framework on Climate Change Actions in Indonesia
extraction_rationale: This is a time-bound adaptation strategy with specific intervention mechanisms, though not all are quantified.

policy_statement: RPJMN 2020-2024 includes coastal protection programmes for adaptation in coastal and fishery sectors.
source_quote: This climate-related evidence suggested the important role of ocean in adaptation to climate change and Indonesia has included ocean in adaptation component of the NDC. The National Medium-Term Plan (RPJMN) 20202024 has put adaptation in coastal and fishery through coastal protection programmes, which is in-line with NDC.
section_header: 3.3. Role of Ocean and Integrated Terrestrial and Marine Ecosystem Management and Conservation
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation programme embedded in the national medium-term plan.

policy_statement: Government Regulation No. 32/2019 on Ocean Spatial Planning explicitly recognizes the role of ocean and associated ecosystems in climate change adaptation and mitigation.
source_quote: Some regulatory frameworks which can be the basis for ocean-based adaptation and mitigation have been in place, for example Law No. 27/2007 on Coastal Zone Management, Law No.31/2004 on Fishery (amended with Law No 45/2009), and more recently Government Regulation No 32/2019 on Ocean Spatial Planning, which clearly states the role of ocean and its associated ecosystems in climate change adaptation and mitigation.
section_header: 3.3. Role of Ocean and Integrated Terrestrial and Marine Ecosystem Management and Conservation
extraction_rationale: This is a named regulatory framework explicitly tied to climate adaptation and mitigation through ocean spatial planning.

policy_statement: COVID-19 recovery programmes included 15,000 hectares of mangrove planting and 50 hectares of coral reef restoration in Bali in 2020.
source_quote: Coastal and marine based activities have also been part of COVID-19 recovery programme, including 15 thousands hectare mangrove planting and 50 hectare coral reef restoration in marine tourism area in Bali in 2020.
section_header: 3.3. Role of Ocean and Integrated Terrestrial and Marine Ecosystem Management and Conservation
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified ecosystem restoration intervention. It is climate-relevant because it appears in the climate strategy context, though partly framed as recovery activity.

policy_statement: Indonesia is in the process of issuing an innovative policy on the economic value of carbon.
source_quote: Indonesia has committed through REDD+ to maintain the remaining natural forest. Policies that have been issued include (i) permanent extension of the forest and peatland moratoriums (Presidential Instruction 5/2019); (ii) implementation of mandatory certification for sustainable forest management; (iii) integrated, comprehensive, spatially explicit land use planning at national and sub-national level guided by the Government Regulation 46/2016 on strategic environmental assessments (SEAs) through landscape approach aiming at securing food, water, and energy security based on sound ecosystem management; (iv) establishment of new financial models for conservation and restoration in sustainable jurisdictions with the issuance of Government Regulation No. 46/2017 on Environmental economic instrument and other fiscal incentives; and (v) establishment of Indonesia Environmental Fund ( Badan Pengelola Dana Lingkungan Hidup /BPDLH) through Presidential Regulation No. 77/2018 concerning Management of Environmental Fund. Indonesia is also in the process of issuing another innovative policy on economic value of carbon.
section_header: 4.2.1. Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Uses (AFOLU)
extraction_rationale: This is a forthcoming carbon-pricing-related policy. It is somewhat less concrete because still in process, but it is a named policy commitment.

policy_statement: BPDLH will manage environmental funds across sectors to optimize and mobilize domestic and international funding.
source_quote: BPDLH will manage funds related to forestry, energy and mineral resources, carbon trading, environmental services, industry, transportation, agriculture, marine and fisheries, and other fields related to the environment. The goal is to be able to manage funds more optimally and synergistically, as well as optimise the use of funds and mobilise funding resources both domestic and international sources.
section_header: 4.2.1. Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Uses (AFOLU)
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete institutional finance mechanism with a defined funding management role.

policy_statement: Indonesia's forestry and other land use strategy to reach net sink relies on six actions: reducing deforestation and peat emissions, increasing natural forest sequestration, restoring peatland, forest restoration, sustainable forest management, and maximizing use of idle lands.
source_quote: Efforts to significantly reduce the emission of this sector and turn it into net sink by 2050 under CPOS and by 2030 under LCCP depends primarily on the success of the following actions: (i) reducing emission from deforestation and peatland (peat decomposition and peat fire); (ii) increasing the capacity of natural forest in sequestering carbon (by reducing degradation and enhancing the regeneration); (iii) restoring peatland, (iv) implementing forest restoration (enrichment planting/sink enhancement), (v) adopting sustainable forest management practices; and (vi) maximizing the use of unproductive lands (idle lands) for the establishment of forest and agriculture plantations (see Figure 6).
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella initiative with enumerated sub-actions and explicit net-sink objective.
