policy_statement: Adopt sustainable forest management practices.
source_quote: Efforts to significantly reduce the emission of this sector and turn it into net sink by 2050 under CPOS and by 2030 under LCCP depends primarily on the success of the following actions: (i) reducing emission from deforestation and peatland (peat decomposition and peat fire); (ii) increasing the capacity of natural forest in sequestering carbon (by reducing degradation and enhancing the regeneration); (iii) restoring peatland, (iv) implementing forest restoration (enrichment planting/sink enhancement), (v) adopting sustainable forest management practices; and (vi) maximizing the use of unproductive lands (idle lands) for the establishment of forest and agriculture plantations (see Figure 6).
extraction_rationale: Specific management action under the parent forestry strategy.

parent_statement: Indonesia's forestry and other land use strategy to reach net sink
policy_statement: Maximize use of unproductive lands for forest and agriculture plantations.
source_quote: Efforts to significantly reduce the emission of this sector and turn it into net sink by 2050 under CPOS and by 2030 under LCCP depends primarily on the success of the following actions: (i) reducing emission from deforestation and peatland (peat decomposition and peat fire); (ii) increasing the capacity of natural forest in sequestering carbon (by reducing degradation and enhancing the regeneration); (iii) restoring peatland, (iv) implementing forest restoration (enrichment planting/sink enhancement), (v) adopting sustainable forest management practices; and (vi) maximizing the use of unproductive lands (idle lands) for the establishment of forest and agriculture plantations (see Figure 6).
extraction_rationale: Specific land-use efficiency action under the parent forestry strategy.

policy_statement: Indonesia's avoiding deforestation strategy uses regulatory controls on forest conversion, peatland governance, and strategic environmental assessment.
source_quote:
To avoid further conversion of forest, Indonesia has issued a number of regulations. Some of key regulations are:

1. Government Regulation No.104/2015 on the changes of forest land use and function, which ban the conversion of forested land (productive production forest) in forest area for APL, except in the province where the non-forested lands in the production forest are not available; 2020
2. Presidential Instruction No. 5/2019 on Termination of New Permit and Improvement of Primary Natural Forest and Peatland Governance; and
3. Government Regulation No. 46/2016 on strategic environmental assessments (SEAs), which provide guidance on the integrated, comprehensive, spatially explicit land use planning at national and subnational level aiming at food, water, and energy security based on sound ecosystem management.
extraction_rationale: This is a parent grouping with numbered regulatory sub-items.

parent_statement: Indonesia's avoiding deforestation strategy
policy_statement: Government Regulation No. 104/2015 bans conversion of forested productive production forest to other land use, except where non-forested production forest land is unavailable.
source_quote: 1. Government Regulation No.104/2015 on the changes of forest land use and function, which ban the conversion of forested land (productive production forest) in forest area for APL, except in the province where the non-forested lands in the production forest are not available;
extraction_rationale: This is a clear regulatory prohibition with direct mitigation effect through avoided deforestation.

parent_statement: Indonesia's avoiding deforestation strategy
policy_statement: Presidential Instruction No. 5/2019 terminates new permits and improves governance of primary natural forest and peatland.
source_quote: 2. Presidential Instruction No. 5/2019 on Termination of New Permit and Improvement of Primary Natural Forest and Peatland Governance; and
extraction_rationale: This is a named regulatory action directly targeting land-use emissions.

parent_statement: Indonesia's avoiding deforestation strategy
policy_statement: Government Regulation No. 46/2016 requires strategic environmental assessments for integrated, spatially explicit land-use planning based on sound ecosystem management.
source_quote: 3. Government Regulation No. 46/2016 on strategic environmental assessments (SEAs), which provide guidance on the integrated, comprehensive, spatially explicit land use planning at national and subnational level aiming at food, water, and energy security based on sound ecosystem management.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete planning regulation listed as part of the deforestation-avoidance package.

policy_statement: RPJMN 2020-2024 expands forest area under protection based on ecosystem service value from 51.8 Mha to 65.3 Mha.
source_quote: In the National Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMN) 2020-2024, forest area that need to be protected based on the value of ecosystem services of the forest, are expanded from 51.8 Mha to 65.3 Mha, which are located inside and outside forest area. This has to be considered in the process of developing land use planning at sub-national level.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified land protection target embedded in the national development plan.

policy_statement: Ministerial Regulation No. 70/2017 makes local governments and concessions eligible for REDD+ result-based payments when they conserve forests beyond existing regulation.
source_quote: Under the implementation of REDD+, the local governments and concessions who can conserved the forest beyond the existing regulation, are eligible for receiving Result-based Payment (RBP) under the Ministerial Regulation (Minister for Environment and Forestry) No. 70/2017. In addition, Indonesia is also in the process of preparing innovative regulation related to fiscal incentive, as part of the implementation of Government Regulation No. 46/2017.
extraction_rationale: This is a named financial incentive mechanism tied to forest conservation performance.

policy_statement: Indonesia increased forest area under protection zone to about 65 Mha in RPJMN 2020-2024, reallocating some production forest to protection status.
source_quote: Government Regulation No.104/2015 provides an opportunity to increase forest area under protection zone, based on the value of ecosystem services of the area. Total area of forest under the protection zone at present is about 51.8 Mha (i.e. conservation forest: 22.1 Mha, protection forest: 29.7 Mha) and under production zone is about 68.8 Mha. In the RPJMN 2020-2024, Indonesia has increased the area of forest under the protection zone to about 65 Mha, in which some of forest area under the production zone are allocated as protection zone.
section_header: b. Conservation and Sustainable Forest Management
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified land protection commitment with clear conservation and climate implications.

policy_statement: Ministerial Regulation No. 30/2016 mandates certification systems to drive sustainable management practices in production forests.
source_quote: Reducing forest degradation due to excessive logging and encroachment in the production forests has been put as other priority. Indonesia has issued mandatory certification systems (Ministerial Regulation No. 30/ 2016 by the Minister of Environment and Forestry) that push the adoption of sustainable management practices in the production forests. With this policy, many forest concessions have improved their management practices.
section_header: b. Conservation and Sustainable Forest Management
extraction_rationale: This is a named regulatory mechanism requiring certification and improved forest management.

policy_statement: Under LCCP, all forest concession companies are expected to implement sustainable harvesting practices by 2050.
source_quote: With this policy, many forest concessions have improved their management practices. Under LCCP, by 2050 all forest concession companies have implement sustainable harvesting practices. At present, the forest concessions that have received the good forest certification reach about 76%.
section_header: b. Conservation and Sustainable Forest Management
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified future implementation target for sustainable forest management, though framed within scenario assumptions.

policy_statement: Indonesia will expand enhanced natural regeneration and forest restoration in production forests to 8.8 Mha by 2050 under LCCP.
source_quote: Efforts to restore the degraded production forest through enhanced natural regeneration (ENR) or forest restoration will also be increased. It is expected that under LCCP, area of production forest that being restored through the ENR programme after 2030 should reach about 1.70 Mha, about 2 times of the CPOS, and by 2050 it will reach 8.8 Mha or about 6 times of the CPOS.
section_header: b. Conservation and Sustainable Forest Management
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified restoration target and therefore a concrete policy commitment.

policy_statement: Presidential Instruction No. 5/2019 prohibits new permits for peatland use.
source_quote: Significant amount of greenhouse gas emissions has been released from the use of peatland through decomposition and peat fire. At present emission from these sources contribute to about 50% of the total emission from AFOLU sector. Indonesia has issued a number of key policies to protect peatland and improve its management. Under Presidential Instruction No. 5/2019, there will not be any new permit for the use of peatland.
section_header: c. Protection and Restoration of Peatland
extraction_rationale: This is a direct regulatory prohibition on peatland permitting with clear mitigation purpose.

policy_statement: Ministerial Regulation No. 15/2017 mandates private sector and local governments to improve peatland use and water management.
source_quote:
In addition, the Ministerial Regulation No. 15/2017 (Minister for Environment and Forestry) mandates private sector and local governments to improve the use of peatland and water management.

Under CPOS, it is expected that the improvement of peatland and water management by 2030 and 2050 reaches 0.86 Mha and 1.04 Mha consecutively, while under LCCP it should reach 0.95 Mha by 2030 and 1.04 Mha by 2050.
section_header: c. Protection and Restoration of Peatland
extraction_rationale: This is a named mandate with explicit implementation targets for peatland and water management.

policy_statement: Indonesia targets degraded peatland restoration of 2.7 Mha by 2030 and 4.2 Mha by 2050 under LCCP.
source_quote: For peatland restoration, CPOS figures the area of degraded peatland being restored should reach 1.03 Mha by 2030 and 1.7 Mha by 2050. While under LCCP, the target will be increased to 2.7 Mha by 2030 and 4.2 Mha by 2050.
section_header: c. Protection and Restoration of Peatland
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified restoration target with clear climate mitigation relevance.

policy_statement: Indonesia will accelerate afforestation, reforestation, and urban revegetation to increase carbon sinks.
source_quote: Indonesia will accelerate afforestation and reforestation of degraded land inside and outside forest area as well as urban revegetation for increasing sink. At present many lands inside and outside forest areas are unproductive lands (Table 1). These lands are in the form of shrubs, grassland, and bare-lands.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific ecosystem restoration intervention explicitly aimed at increasing sinks.

policy_statement: Indonesia aims to rehabilitate 8.6 Mha of unproductive land by 2050 under CPOS and 10.6 Mha by 2050 under LCCP.
source_quote: Under CPOS, Indonesia aims to rehabilitate the unproductive lands with priority in critical and very critical lands about 4.32 Mha by 2030 and 8.6 Mha by 2050. Under the LCCP, this target is increased to 5.3 Mha by 2030 and 10.6 Mha by 2050.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified land rehabilitation target and therefore a concrete policy commitment.

policy_statement: Indonesia has launched social forestry, land rehabilitation, and multi-permit concession policies to accelerate land rehabilitation and agroforestry on degraded lands.
source_quote: Several programmes have been launched for accelerating the rehabilitation of the land, i.e. social forestry and land rehabilitation programmes and multi permit policies for forest concessions that allow to use the degraded lands for agriculture commodities in the form of agroforestry.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete package of named interventions supporting rehabilitation and agroforestry.

policy_statement: Agricultural mitigation technologies include low-emission rice varieties, water-saving paddy cultivation, livestock waste biogas, livestock feed improvement, and reduced synthetic fertilizer use.
source_quote: The mitigation technologies accounted for in this sector are the adoption of low emission variety and water-saving paddy cultivation system (hereinafter referred to as SPR/STT) in the rice field, and utilization of livestock waste for biogas and livestock feed improvement in livestock management, and the reduction in using synthetic fertilizer.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete list of named interventions for agricultural mitigation, though it functions as a grouped policy package rather than a formal parent list.

policy_statement: Indonesia targets adoption of low-emission rice varieties on 1.96 Mha by 2050 under CPOS and 2.07 Mha by 2050 under LCCP.
source_quote: Under CPOS, the adoption of low emission variety is expected to be 0.93 Mha by 2030 and 1.96 Mha by 2050. Under LCCP, an ambitious target is set to 0.97 Mha by 2030 and 2.07 Mha by 2050.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified technology adoption target in agriculture.

policy_statement: Indonesia will scale up the SPR/STT water-saving paddy cultivation programme to 1.18 Mha under CPOS and 1.31 Mha under LCCP by 2050.
source_quote: Currently, SPR/STT is implemented as a pilot activity and the attainment from the pilot programme will be replicated to the other region. By 2050, the technology programme is expected to be scaled up to 1.18 M ha and 1.31 M ha under CPOS and LCCP, respectively.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified scale-up commitment for a named agricultural mitigation technology.

policy_statement: Indonesia targets biogas implementation for livestock waste management covering 94,000 head by 2050.
source_quote: The CPOS and LCCP are setting a similar target for biogas implementation, accounted for 41,000 head in 2030 and 94,000 head in 2050. However, the number is considerably low compared to the national livestock population as this activity requires high investment for biodigester and flaring facility and continues supply of livestock waste.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified mitigation target for livestock waste-to-biogas deployment.

policy_statement: Indonesia targets livestock feed supplementation for 3.42 million head under CPOS and 6.58 million head under LCCP by 2050 to reduce methane emissions.
source_quote: Research finds that shifting from high concentrate livestock feed to greenery feed, specifically in beef and dairy cattle, is potentially reduce methane emission from enteric fermentation. The feed supplement is a combination of the greenery and an additional feed supply of tannin from legume crops or urea molasses block. The target in CPOS and LCCP scenarios in 2050 is 3.42 million head and 6.58 million head, respectively.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified methane-reduction intervention in livestock management.

policy_statement: Indonesia encourages cropland farmers to substitute organic fertilizer for urea and targets substantial reductions in urea use by 2050.
source_quote: Applying organic fertilizer is expected to reduce dependency on nitrogen fertilizer usage. Cropland farmers are encouraged to use organic fertilizer to substitute the urea application. Under CPOS, the adoption of this mitigation action in 2030 and 2050 are expected to reduce the use of urea amounted to 3,089 ton and 58,513 ton, respectively. Under LCCP, the reduction of total urea used in 2030 and 2050 is expected to be 5,374 ton and 65,697 ton, respectively.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific agricultural mitigation intervention with quantified reductions in fertilizer use.

policy_statement: Indonesia's strategy for avoiding deforestation while maintaining sectoral targets relies on improving productivity and cropping intensity, integrated farming, use of idle lands, and reducing food loss and waste.
source_quote: The strategy for avoiding deforestation while maintaining sectoral target is by improving crop productivity and cropping intensity, implementing integrated farming or complex agroforestry, optimizing the use of unproductive lands (idle lands) and reducing food loss and waste.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella strategy followed by lettered sub-sections that elaborate each action.

parent_statement: Indonesia's strategy for avoiding deforestation while maintaining sectoral targets
policy_statement: Improve crop productivity and cropping intensity to meet food demand while reducing deforestation.
source_quote: Increasing agricultural productivity and cropping intensity are key factors in meeting food demand in line with population and GDP growth, at the same time maintaining emission by reducing deforestation. This can be achieved by using high quality seeds, fertilizing, and adoption of agricultural technology.
section_header: a. Improvement of Crop Productivity and Cropping Intensity
extraction_rationale: This is a specific intervention under the parent strategy, explicitly linking efficiency gains to reduced deforestation.

parent_statement: Indonesia's strategy for avoiding deforestation while maintaining sectoral targets
policy_statement: Implement integrated farming systems, especially oil palm-livestock integration, to improve efficiency, productivity, and reduce deforestation.
source_quote: The application of integrated farming in several agriculture and other land use sectors (food crop, fishery, livestock, plantation and forestry) will increase the eff.shorticiency and productivity rate and its economic value. Integrated farming that will be developed in the future is the integration of oil palm-livestock (cows, sheeps, and goats). This integration of raising livestock within oil palm plantation is in line with an effort to support palm oil production and strengthen food security (reducing meat imports) under low carbon framework (reduces deforestation and conducting waste management).
extraction_rationale: This is a named intervention under the parent strategy with explicit low-carbon rationale.

parent_statement: Indonesia's strategy for avoiding deforestation while maintaining sectoral targets
policy_statement: Optimize use of unproductive land and enforce restrictions on conversion of agricultural land.
source_quote: The use of current unproductive land in non-forest area will be optimised for expansion of cropland. In addition, the use of non-forested land in forest areas for agriculture production under the scheme of Social Forestry Programme will also be accelerated as well as the issuance of multi permit for concession to allow for producing non-timber forest products, including agriculture production through partnership with communities as part of approaches in addressing land tenure issues. Restriction of conversion of agriculture lands as mandated by the Law No. 41/2009 on sustainable agriculture land is enforced.
section_header: c. Optimizing Use of Unproductive Land
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete land-use efficiency and land protection policy package under the parent strategy.

parent_statement: Indonesia's strategy for avoiding deforestation while maintaining sectoral targets
policy_statement: Reduce food loss and food waste through improved harvesting, cold storage, packaging, campaigns, and green certification.
source_quote: Reducing food loss and food waste is one of strategy to reduce greenhouse gas emission. Without reducing food loss and food waste, the land required to produce food is going to increase. Modernization of harvesting tools is needed to improve harvesting techniques and reduce yield losses. Furthermore, assistance with cold storage facilities and packaging technology are essential to reduce food loss during food distribution.
section_header: d. Reducing Food Loss and Food Waste
extraction_rationale: This is a specific intervention under the parent strategy with explicit emissions rationale and named measures.

policy_statement: Indonesia considers the Social Forestry Programme a key solution for tenure issues, community access to forest areas, and poverty reduction through agroforestry.
source_quote: By granting legal access through Social Forestry Programme, the farmers are eligible to receive supports from the government for the improvement of the farming activities by integrating the agriculture commodities with forest trees as agroforestry. Indonesia considers the Social Forestry Programme is a part of key solutions for addressing tenure issues and providing more access for community to utilise forest area and reducing poverty.
section_header: a. Improvement of Crop Productivity and Cropping Intensity
extraction_rationale: This is a named programme with a specific intervention and governance mechanism, though climate benefits are partly indirect through reduced pressure on forests.

policy_statement: Government provides land rights through the TORA Programme to communities occupying forest land for agriculture, enabling access to support and partnerships.
source_quote: Furthermore, Government provides land right to the farmers through agrarian reform (TORA Programme). With this policy, communities who have occupied land in forest area under TORA Programme for agriculture activities will have the ownership right and access to government supports as well as partnership with estate companies for yield improvement and market.
section_header: a. Improvement of Crop Productivity and Cropping Intensity
extraction_rationale: This is a named land-tenure reform policy with concrete implementation effects; climate relevance is indirect because the text links it to productivity and land-use outcomes rather than explicitly to climate in this quote.

policy_statement: Government has encouraged agricultural technology and machinery adoption and provided assistance to farmers.
source_quote: The intensification in agriculture by technology adoption is expected to increase productivity. Government has encouraged the use of technology and machinery in agricultural production and provided assistance to support the adoption of technology by farmers. However, the technology adoption rate is limited due to financial constraints.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete support programme for agricultural mechanization, though not highly quantified in this passage.

policy_statement: Under CPOS, government will continue agricultural machinery support to farmers and farmer groups.
source_quote: Under CPOS, the government is expected to continue agricultural machinery support to farmers/farmer groups. In this case, the role of field extension workers and universities is very important to ensure the adoption of agricultural technology in the field.
extraction_rationale: This is a forward-looking continuation commitment for a specific support programme.

policy_statement: Under CPOS, value chain finance schemes such as warehouse receipt systems, peer-to-peer lending, and credit programmes will provide credit for agricultural inputs and technology adoption to support low-carbon agriculture.
source_quote: Under CPOS, value chain finance such as Warehouse receipt system, Peer to Peer lending (P2P) and credit programme provide credits to buy agricultural inputs and tools for technology adoption to support low carbon agriculture. Optimizing the implementation of the National Strategy for Financial Inclusion (SNKI) by actively involving the financial services industry (bank) and NBFIs and related institutions is important to increase financing for the agricultural sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete finance policy package providing credit for low-carbon agriculture, making it a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Indonesia will revitalize agricultural institutions and extension services under CPOS to improve agricultural human resources.
source_quote: Under CPOS, revitalization of institutional and agricultural extension institutions will make a positive contribution to improving agricultural human resources. Under LCCP, providing suff.shorticient space for the private sector (traders, modern market) and research agencies/universities to actively engage in empowerment programme can be a solution to increase production and market.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete institutional strengthening measure, though climate relevance is indirect via sustainable agriculture capacity.

policy_statement: Indonesia targets oil palm-livestock integrated farming to reach 3.25 Mha under CPOS and 4.91 Mha under LCCP by 2050.
source_quote: Under CPOS, integrated farming of oil palm-livestock is targeted to reach 11.70% (1.68 Mha) in 2030 and 22.72% (3.25 Mha) in 2050. Under LCCP, the target is increased to 21.11% (3.02 Mha) in 2030 and to 34.33% ( 4.91 Mha) in 2050.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified target for a named integrated farming intervention.

policy_statement: Ministerial Regulation No. 105/2014 regulates integration of plantation and animal production.
source_quote: The integration of plantation and animal production has also been regulated under the Ministerial Regulation No. 105/2014 (Minister for Agriculture). There are more than 14.3 Mha of oil palm plantation potential for integrated farming.
extraction_rationale: This is a named regulatory instrument governing integrated farming practices.

policy_statement: Government will examine possible incentives to encourage climate-friendly integrated farming practices, particularly for large-scale plantations.
source_quote: However, the current implementation is only 3% of the total potential. To increase the adoption of the integrated farming practices, particularly for large scale plantations, Government will examine possible incentive for encouraging climate-friendly farming practices.
extraction_rationale: This is a prospective incentive policy commitment, though somewhat vague because the incentive design is not specified.

policy_statement: Law No. 41/2009 restricting conversion of agricultural land is enforced.
source_quote:
Restriction of conversion of agriculture lands as mandated by the Law No. 41/2009 on sustainable agriculture land is enforced.

Under CPOS, the conversion of rice paddy land in Java will reduce significantly from 1.34% per year to 0.60% per year, while in LCCP it will reduce to 0.10%.
section_header: c. Optimizing Use of Unproductive Land
extraction_rationale: This is a binding legal mechanism with explicit enforcement and land-use implications.

policy_statement: Indonesia's energy sector mitigation options include energy efficiency, renewable substitution for fossil fuels, and electrification of end uses with decarbonized electricity.
source_quote: The mitigation options in energy sector includes: (i) energy eff.shorticiency measures in all subsectors; (ii) substitution of fossil fuel by renewable in power generation and transport; and (iii) electrification of end use in building and in transportation (must be accompanied by decarbonisation of electricity).
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella mitigation package with enumerated sub-actions.

parent_statement: Indonesia's energy sector mitigation options
policy_statement: Implement energy efficiency measures in all energy subsectors.
source_quote: The mitigation options in energy sector includes: (i) energy eff.shorticiency measures in all subsectors; (ii) substitution of fossil fuel by renewable in power generation and transport; and (iii) electrification of end use in building and in transportation (must be accompanied by decarbonisation of electricity).
extraction_rationale: Specific sub-action under the parent energy mitigation package.

parent_statement: Indonesia's energy sector mitigation options
policy_statement: Substitute fossil fuels with renewables in power generation and transport.
source_quote: The mitigation options in energy sector includes: (i) energy eff.shorticiency measures in all subsectors; (ii) substitution of fossil fuel by renewable in power generation and transport; and (iii) electrification of end use in building and in transportation (must be accompanied by decarbonisation of electricity).
extraction_rationale: Specific sub-action under the parent energy mitigation package.

parent_statement: Indonesia's energy sector mitigation options
policy_statement: Electrify end uses in buildings and transportation with decarbonized electricity.
source_quote: The mitigation options in energy sector includes: (i) energy eff.shorticiency measures in all subsectors; (ii) substitution of fossil fuel by renewable in power generation and transport; and (iii) electrification of end use in building and in transportation (must be accompanied by decarbonisation of electricity).
extraction_rationale: Specific sub-action under the parent energy mitigation package.

policy_statement: Indonesia targets universal household electricity access through grid, non-grid, and rooftop solar PV.
source_quote: In 2020, Indonesia household electrification reached 98% (MEMR 2020), which was connected to on-grid (large power plants) and off grid electricity (smaller plants, mostly renewables). It is targeted that in the future all household will have electricity access through grid and non-grid as well as roof-top solar PV.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear future target with named delivery mechanisms, though climate relevance is indirect because access is the primary objective.

policy_statement: Indonesia expects the power sector to be nearly decarbonized by 2050 through massive renewable deployment, CCS/CCUS on most coal plants, and BECCS.
source_quote: It is expected that in 2050 the power sector will nearly decarbonised, through: (i) utilization of renewables (hydro, geothermal, solar, wind, biomass) in massive scale; (ii) most coal powerplants are equipped with CCS/CCUS; and (iii) biomass-coal cofiring power plants are connected to CCS (Biomass Energy with Carbon Capture and Storage or BECCS). Since Indonesia is an archipelago, the power system will be developed in the form of distributed power, instead of large centralised system.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete long-term decarbonization strategy with named technologies and a date.

policy_statement: Under LCCP in 2050, Indonesia's power generation mix is envisaged as 43% renewables, 38% coal, 10% natural gas, and 8% BECCS.
source_quote:
It is envisaged that the power situation in 2050 under LCCP will be as follows:

- Power generation mix are: renewables (43%), coal (38%), natural gas (10%) and BECCS (8%).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified long-term power mix target under the mitigation scenario.

policy_statement: Around 76% of coal power plants will be equipped with CCS under LCCP to achieve zero emissions from coal power plants.
source_quote:
- Around 76% of the coal power plant are equipped with CCS to achieve zero emissions in coal power plants.
- Installed capacity of renewable power generation mix are: solar PV 113 GW, hydro 68 GW, geothermal 23 GW, wind power 17 GW, biomass 13 GW, biofuel 14 GW and BECCS 23 GW with negative emissions.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified technology deployment target for coal power decarbonization.

policy_statement: Indonesia targets renewable power capacities by 2050 of 113 GW solar PV, 68 GW hydro, 23 GW geothermal, 17 GW wind, 13 GW biomass, 14 GW biofuel, and 23 GW BECCS.
source_quote:
- Installed capacity of renewable power generation mix are: solar PV 113 GW, hydro 68 GW, geothermal 23 GW, wind power 17 GW, biomass 13 GW, biofuel 14 GW and BECCS 23 GW with negative emissions.
- The supply availability of some renewable power plants are intermittent, and therefore, in order to have a reliable supply system it will require integration with continuous stable power supply system (baseload) such as coal power plants.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified renewable deployment target with explicit capacities.

policy_statement: Indonesia will develop off-grid and micro-grid systems, smart grids, and smart micro-grids for remote areas as renewable deployment expands.
source_quote:
- Increasing development of 'off-grid' and 'micro-grid'.
- Due to significant portion of intermittent renewable (solar and wind) will be deployed in the future, it will require development of smart grid that can handle large supply intermittency.
- Power plant with 100% renewable energy in remote areas will need Smart Micro Grid.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific infrastructure development commitment supporting renewable integration.

policy_statement: Transport mitigation will be achieved through electrification, expanded biofuel supply for diesel and gasoline substitution, and continuation of the biodiesel blending programme toward higher blends through 2050.
source_quote:
Mitigation target in transport will be achieved by: (i) electrification of transport; (ii) supplying more biofuels for diesel substitute (fatty acid methyl-esther and bio-hydrocarbon or green diesel); and (iii) gasoline substitute (bioethanol and CPO-based gasoline). Since the past 10 years the government has introduce biofuels made from CPO, which is blended with petroleum diesel and called B20 (20% biodiesel plus 80% petroleum diesel).

It is envisaged that Indonesian transport situation in 2050 under LCCP will be as follows:
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete transport mitigation package with named interventions and continuation of an existing blending programme.

policy_statement: Indonesia will continue the CPO-based biofuel programme to 2050 with higher biodiesel blends such as B30, B40, and B50 from sustainable sources.
source_quote: - The breakdown of transport energy in 2050 are: biofuels (46%), oil fuels (20%), electricity (30%) and natural gas (4%). The biofuel (CPO-based) programme is considered successful and will be continued to 2050 by supplying biofuel with higher biodiesel proportions (B30, B40, B50), which will be produced from sustainable sources.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific continuation and scale-up commitment for a named biofuel programme.

policy_statement: Existing plans will build 3,200 km of train tracks in Sumatra, Java, Kalimantan, and Sulawesi.
source_quote: - Many cities are connected by inter-city trains especially in Java. Existing plan shows that 3,200 km of train tracks will be built to serve transport in Sumatra, Java, Kalimantan, and Sulawesi.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified transport infrastructure commitment. Climate relevance is indirect because rail expansion supports lower-carbon mobility but is not solely framed as climate policy here.

policy_statement: Indonesia's general energy mitigation guidelines focus on power, energy demand reduction, efficient transport and electrification, biofuels, industrial fuel switching, renewable energy, and CCS/BECCS.
source_quote:
Based on the understanding of type of fuels and energy-consuming sectors, taking into account past development and future projection of energy demand and supply, the LTS-LCCR was developed using the following general guidelines:

1. Focussing on power sector.
2. Minimize energy demand without sacrificing people welfare and economic development (energy eff.shorticiency measure),
3. Develop more eff.shorticient transport system (promote mass public transport), electrification of vehicles and other equipment at end-users (residential and commercial) with decarbonized electricity.

4. Develop biofuels for transport and power plants, including biofuel resource base (feedstock, plantation).
5. Shifting fuel from coal to gas and renewable in industry.
6. Develop renewable energy (hydro, geothermal, solar PV and wind, including capacity development to produce solar PV and batteries) in power, transport and industry, which will consequently reduce coal for power.
7. BECCS (negative emission) will be used and the remaining coal power plants will be equipped with CCS/CCUS.
section_header: 4.2.2.3. GHG Emission Projections and Mitigation Strategy
extraction_rationale: This is a parent strategy with numbered sub-actions.

policy_statement: Focus mitigation efforts on the power sector.
source_quote: 1. Focussing on power sector.
section_header: 4.2.2.3. GHG Emission Projections and Mitigation Strategy
extraction_rationale: Specific strategic sub-action under the parent guideline set.

policy_statement: Minimize energy demand through energy efficiency without sacrificing welfare and economic development.

policy_statement: Indonesia's long-term waste strategy is guided by methane reduction, avoidance, destruction, and utilization across municipal solid waste, domestic wastewater, and industrial waste.
source_quote: Four following pillars of guidance are used to develop a long-term low-carbon strategy toward zero emissions in the waste sector, taking into account past development and projection of future waste management activities through reduction, avoidance, destruction, and utilization of GHG emissions, particularly methane (CH 4 ) gas, which generated during the treatment of municipal solid waste (MSW), domestic wastewater, and industrial solid waste and wastewater.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella strategy for the waste sector, though the four pillars are described narratively rather than as a formal list.

policy_statement: Law No. 18/2008 obliges local governments to manage municipal solid waste, supported by Jakstranas, Jakstrada, and Presidential Regulation No. 35/2018 on waste-to-energy.
source_quote: Law No. 18/2008 regarding MSW management obliges local governments to manage MSW. In addition, there are National Policy and Strategy (Jakstranas) and Provincial Policy and Strategy (Jakstrada) in waste management as well as Presidential Regulation No. 35/2018 concerning MSW utilization for electricity generation in PLTSa or RDF (refuse-derived fuels) that support GHG emission reduction.
extraction_rationale: This is a package of named regulatory instruments governing waste management and waste-to-energy.

policy_statement: Under CPOS, municipal solid waste will be managed through 30% source reduction and 70% treatment via landfilling, composting, and waste-to-energy.
source_quote: Under CPOS, the MSW will be managed through waste reduction at sources (30%) by 3R (reduce-reuse-recycle) and waste treatment (70%) through landfilling, composting, and converting waste to energy. This 3R is a part of Circular Economy which is promoted in Indonesia.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified waste management target and operational strategy.

policy_statement: Under CPOS, waste mitigation includes 30% waste reduction, treatment in SWDS with some LFG recovery, waste-to-energy, additional septic tanks with biogas and sludge recovery, aerobic systems, and industrial waste use for energy.
source_quote: Under CPOS, the mitigation include 30% waste reduction and 70% of the waste is treated in SWDS (some of them equipped with LFG recovery) and utilized for energy (PLTSa and RDF), which in turn reduce open burning significantly. The mitigation also covers additional septic tank (equipped with biogas and sludge recovery), implementation of aerobic system, and the use of industrial liquid / solid waste for energy production.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete package of named mitigation interventions in the waste sector.

policy_statement: Under LCCP, Indonesia will maximize waste mitigation by expanding LFG recovery, PLTSa and RDF/SRF, biodigesters with biogas and sludge recovery, paper recycling, composting, and septic tanks with methane recovery or aerobic systems for all new houses.
source_quote: LCCP increases the potential of TRNS and CPOS mitigation significant adding the number of SWDS equipped with LFG recovery, the amount of MSW used for PLTSa and RDF/SRF, the number of biodigester equipped with biogas and sludge recovery, and the number of paper recycling and composting. The mitigation also covers the increase of septic tanks utilisation (100% new houses) equipped with biogas recovery or aerobic, sludge recovery systems and increased utilization of waste for energy.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete scale-up commitment with specific technologies and a quantified coverage element.

policy_statement: Government plans universal toilet access, with mitigation through lower-emission wastewater technologies.
source_quote: The government long-term plan has target that all people have access to toilet whether it is individual or communal toilets. Most of those toilets have septic tank/latrine to treat the black water, while small fraction of those toilets has channel to a wastewater sewerage to treat the grey water in a centralised WWT plant. The remaining population cannot access the toilet as well as the septic tank (households or population with no septic tank).
extraction_rationale: This is a clear service-access target. Climate relevance is indirect because sanitation access is primary, though the section explicitly links treatment technologies to emissions.

policy_statement: Beyond 2030, Indonesia estimates septic tank use will decline as more wastewater is treated in centralized aerobic systems.
source_quote: Figure 21 shows that currently more people have access to toilet equipped with septic tank in line with the government programme for the improvement of sanitation and health. However, beyond 2030, it is estimated that the use of septic tank will be reduced by increasing wastewater treated in the centralised (aerobic) system.
extraction_rationale: This is a directional infrastructure transition commitment in wastewater treatment, though framed as projection language.

policy_statement: Under TRNS and LCCP, Indonesia will deploy additional aerobic septic tanks, biodigester septic tanks with methane recovery, and centralized domestic wastewater treatment.
source_quote: Under TRNS and LCCP, more ambitious mitigation mitigation can be deployed to decrease the level of GHG emissions through the additional aerobic septic tank, biodigester septic tank equipped with methane recovery for new toilet/septic-tank, and centralised WWT for domestic wastewater. Under TRNS, it is assumed that the use of aerobic centralised will increase from 1% of people live in urban in 2020 to 14% in 2050 while under LCCP it will increase to 36% in 2050.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete mitigation package with a quantified centralized treatment target.

policy_statement: Government programmes will increase septic tank access from 71% to 85% in rural areas and from 88% to 99% in urban areas by 2050.
source_quote: Government programs to increase the number of septic-tank from 71% in 2020 to 85% in 2050 for people live in rural and from 88% in 2020 to 99% in 2050 for people live in urban are implemented in order to increase the access of people to the toilet (individual and communal) could be implemented as mitigation measures by introducing technologies that reduces or lower the GHG emissions.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified sanitation access target with explicit mitigation framing through technology choice.

policy_statement: Under CPOS, industrial waste mitigation reduces emissions through treatment changes in major emitting industries such as palm oil mills, pulp and paper, vegetable-fruit-juice, organic chemicals, and vegetable oils.
source_quote: Under CPOS, GHG emissions can be reduced through the majority of mitigation in several significant GHG emissions contributor industries, i.e. palm oil mills, pulp paper, vegetable-fruit-juice, organic chemicals, and vegetable oil industries. Under TRNS and LCCP, most of wastewater from significant emissions contributor industries will be treated for energy and material sources, such as the use of anaerobic digester equipped with methane gas recovery and utilizing the sludge from WWT unit for energy, compost and materials sources.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete industrial waste mitigation package with named sectors and technologies.

policy_statement: Under LCCP, industrial waste mitigation is expected to reduce emissions to 62 Mton CO2e by 2050.
source_quote: Under LCCP, all of the above mitigation actions are expected to increase significantly. Beyond 2030, mitigation under LCCP are expected to reduce GHG emissions to 62 Mton CO 2 e in 2050.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified emissions outcome tied to a defined mitigation package.

policy_statement: Under CPOS, IPPU mitigation includes blended cement in 50% of cement production and advanced ammonia plant technology reaching 40 GJ per ton NH3 by 2050.
source_quote: Under CPOS, it is assumed that mitigation actions include (a) 50% of national cement productions implement blended cement with a clinker/cement ratio of 0.75 in 2050 and (b) 38% of national ammonia production using advanced technology with natural gas consumption at a rate of 40 GJ per ton NH 3 in 2050.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified industrial mitigation package with specific technology parameters.

policy_statement: Under TRNS, IPPU mitigation adds blended cement expansion, advanced ammonia technology, N2O destruction in nitric acid production, improved aluminium processing, and scrap use in iron and steel.
source_quote: Under TRNS, it is assumed that mitigation actions include (a) significant increase of cement production using blended cement technology with a clinker/cement ratio 0.75 in 2050, (b) the additional of ammonia production using advanced and eff.shorticient technology with natural gas consumption at a rate of 40 GJ per ton NH 3 in 2050, (c) the use of secondary catalyst for N 2 O digestion/destruction in nitric acid production industry, (d) the use of improved (advanced) processing technology for Aluminium production, and (e) the utilization of scrap up to 10% as raw material in iron and steel industries.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete package of named industrial mitigation actions.

policy_statement: Under LCCP, IPPU mitigation increases blended cement to a 0.70 clinker/cement ratio, improves ammonia efficiency to 35 GJ per ton NH3, expands N2O destruction, improves aluminium processing, and raises scrap use to 20%.
source_quote: Under LCCP, it is assumed that mitigation actions include (a) significant increasing of cement production using blended cement technology with clinker/cement ratio of 0.70 in 2050, (b) increasing ammonia production using advanced and eff.shorticient technology with natural gas consumption at a rate of 35 GJ per ton NH 3 in 2050, (c) increasing the use of secondary catalyst for N 2 O digestion/destruction in nitric acid production industry ((higher than those in TRNS), (d) the use of improved (advanced processing technology for Aluminium production, and (e) the use of scrap up to 20% (higher than those in TRNS) as raw material in iron and steel industries but it is limited by the availability of the scrap materials.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified and technology-specific industrial mitigation package.

policy_statement: Blended cement mitigation extends clinker-to-cement ratio reductions through 2050, reaching 0.70 for most cement production under LCCP.
source_quote: Blended cement mitigation under CPOS are the extend of clinker to cement ratio in 50% of cement production capacities at the level of clinker to cement ratio of 0.75 to 2050. Under TRNS, blended cement mitigation under CPOS is increased by implementing clinker to cement ratio of 0.75 from 2030 to 2050 for most cement productions. Under LCPP, blended cement mitigation are increased by implementing clinker to cement ratio up to 0.70 for most cement productions in 2030 to 2050.
section_header: a. Blended Cement in Cement Industry
extraction_rationale: This is a specific industrial process mitigation measure with quantified technical standards.

policy_statement: Indonesia will improve ammonia-urea plant technology, with most plants reaching at least 36.6 GJ natural gas per ton NH3 by 2050 under LCCP.
source_quote: Under CPOS, it is assumed that 38% of most ammonia productions consume natural gas at the rate of 40 GJ/ton NH 3 in 2050. Under TRNS, mitigation under CPOS are increased by implementing more improved technology therefore most ammonia productions consume natural gas at the rate of 40 GJ/ton NH 3 in 2050. Under LCCP, the natural gas consumption in the most plant should at least have natural gas consumption rate of 36.6 GJ natural gas /ton NH 3 or at least Best Practice Technology (BPT) in 2050.
section_header: b. Technology Improvement of New Ammonia Urea Plants
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified industrial efficiency and mitigation standard.

policy_statement: Secondary catalyst reduction for N2O destruction will be applied in nitric acid production, with future deployment under LCCP.
source_quote:
Other selective catalytic process, e.g. secondary catalyst reduction (SCR) will also be applied as secondary mitigation for the N 2 O emissions destruction in nitric acids productions in 2022, with the EF decreased to 2.5 Kg N 2 O per ton HNO 3 .

The deployment potential for future mitigation is relatively small due to high cost, therefore, this mitigation will be deployed under the LCCP.
section_header: c. Secondary Catalyst for N2O Destruction in Nitric Acid Industry
extraction_rationale: This is a specific named mitigation technology with an emissions factor outcome and deployment commitment.

policy_statement: Improved aluminium processing technology to reduce anode effects and PFC emissions is planned for deployment under TRNS and LCCP.
source_quote: AE reduction is achieved by replacing software and hardware, and incorporating a new algorithm in the control system so that reduces AE frequency, duration, and over voltage. This mitigation is planned to be deployed in the aluminium industry for additional mitigation potential in 2050 under TRNS and LCCP. By maintaining this mitigation technology, in 2050, PFC emissions level under TRNS and LCCP can be reduced from 577 Kton CO 2 e (CPOS) to 462 Kton CO 2 e.
section_header: d. Improvement of Aluminium Processing Technology
extraction_rationale: This is a specific industrial mitigation technology with quantified emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Adaptation strategy toward climate resilience will be carried out through investment, human resource capacity and green job opportunities, and land and seascape management.
source_quote: The strategy towards climate resilience is carried out by through means of investment, human resources capacity / green job opportunity, and land & seascape management. As a result, through climate resilience strategy the development plan becomes more climate responsive by using important aspects such as the climate risk code, climate resources, climate zone, and heat island.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation strategy package with named implementation channels.

policy_statement: Adaptation actions should also decrease GHG emissions as a co-benefit, focusing on water, food, energy, environmental health, ecosystem, and disaster.
source_quote: Furthermore, adaptation actions as an important part of climate resilience should also decrease GHGs emissions as a co-benefit mitigation effort, with a focus on adaptation in 6 areas (water, food, energy, environmental health, ecosystem, disaster) in accordance with the NDC adaptation strategy.
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit adaptation policy statement with a named mitigation co-benefit and defined focus areas.

policy_statement: Regional adaptation pathways prioritize interventions in regions identified through climate hotspots and vulnerability analysis.
source_quote: Regional pathway focuses on the priority areas to implement the adaptation actions based on several basic necessities such as food, water, energy, and environmental health (see Figure 41). The basic analysis on the development of regional pathway is the climate change hotspot, as the Pathway focuses on the activities in the regions that are impacted by climate change. The Pathway, then, is combined with priority areas to identify regions that are mostly affected by climate change, which can be used to determine the priority regions for adaptation interventions.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation planning approach with a defined targeting mechanism.

policy_statement: Sectoral adaptation planning must be based on basic necessities and avoid maladaptation through coordination among sectors, while strengthening community climate action through PROKLIM and low-carbon lifestyles.
source_quote: Planning and implementing adaptation in sectoral pathway must be conducted based on basic necessities (see Figure 45). It is also important to avoid mal-adaptation that potentially occur if the adaptation is carried out without coordination amongst sectors. The synergy between sectoral ministries/agencies is needed in climate change adaptation. All sectors should also consider cross-cutting issues, such as knowledge management sharing (i.e., increasing literacy) and community engagement for local climate actions. As a real example, Indonesia will continue to strengthen climate change actions of the community through PROKLIM implementation, in parallel with the adoption of low carbon lifestyle.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation governance commitment with explicit continuation of PROKLIM and coordination requirements.

policy_statement: Indonesia estimates adaptation funding needs of at least IDR 33.12 trillion to IDR 173.10 trillion, up to IDR 577.01 trillion, with 5-10% for governance and 90-95% for implementation.
source_quote: Referring to the impacts of climate change which can affect 0.66% to 3.45% of national GDP or around IDR 110.38 T to 577.01 T (2020 value, without considering the incidence of COVID-19), the estimated need for adaptation costs to climate change in Indonesia reaches at least about IDR 33.12 T to 173.10 T (assuming an investment ratio of 30%) to IDR 577.01 T (assuming the same amount of investment as the impact costs). Funding needs for adaptation are divided into two parts, namely funding for road map governance (5% - 10%) and funding for adaptation implementation (90% - 95%).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified funding commitment framework for adaptation, though presented as estimated needs rather than appropriated budget.

policy_statement: Indonesia estimates IDR 12.84 trillion is required for adaptation roadmap governance and enabling conditions.
source_quote: As for funding for the road map governance (i.e., enabling condition for the implementation of adaptation actions), the estimated total funding required is about IDR 12.84 trillion. The largest allocation of funding needs is needed for the adaptive technology implementation strategy (~27.19%), while the least amount is for policy formulation and strengthening commitment by 2.24%.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified adaptation finance requirement for governance functions.

Reducing food waste: for private household through systemic campaign and awareness raising; for large- scale consumers through green certification

policy_statement: Indonesia's pre-2030 just transition framework includes interventions on governance, green investment, workforce skills, and participatory dialogue.
source_quote: In line with the LTS-LCCR objectives to guide the implementation of NDC and the development of the subsequent NDCs beyond 2030, interventions to address just transition issues are divided into two following phases : (i) pre 2030 (20212030, the period of Indonesia first NDC), and (ii) post 2030 (2031 - 2050, the subsequent NDCs). Table 5 describes key interventions to be carried out during the first phase (2021 to 2030), along with the transition towards Indonesia 2045 and 2050 climate goals.
extraction_rationale: This is a parent framework introducing a structured list of just transition interventions.

parent_statement: Indonesia's pre-2030 just transition framework
policy_statement: Strengthen climate governance and implementation of sustainable development goals at all levels to support just transition.
source_quote: Addressing challenges faced by sectors, cities and regions in transitioning to low carbon development and in ensuring a decent future for workers affected by the transition. Strengthening climate governance and implementation of sustainable development goals at all levels
extraction_rationale: This is a specific policy measure in Table 5 supporting transition resilience.

parent_statement: Indonesia's pre-2030 just transition framework
policy_statement: Enhance green investments and align investment with climate policies and programmes, including COVID-19 recovery alignment.
source_quote: Promoting low greenhouse gas emission and sustainable economic activities that will create quality jobs in cities and regions. Enhancement of green investments and alignment between investment and climate policies and programmes, including alignment of COVID-19 recovery with climate policies
extraction_rationale: This is a specific investment-oriented just transition measure in Table 5.

parent_statement: Indonesia's pre-2030 just transition framework
policy_statement: Strengthen and evolve skilling, upskilling, reskilling, and broader human resource development programmes.
source_quote: Enhancing capacity of workforces to facilitate access to decent work and quality jobs, taking into account gender and inter-generational equalities, as well as the needs of vulnerable groups. Strengthening and evolving programmes on 'skilling - upskilling - reskilling' and human resource development in general,
extraction_rationale: This is a specific workforce transition measure in Table 5.

parent_statement: Indonesia's pre-2030 just transition framework
policy_statement: Increase effectiveness of communication mechanisms and platforms for participatory public dialogue on employment, social protection, labour standards, and wellbeing.
source_quote: Enhancing participatory public dialogue to foster high employment rates, adequate social protection, labour standards and wellbeing of workers and their communities. Increase effectiveness of existing communication mechanisms and platforms.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific institutional measure in Table 5 supporting social resilience during transition.

policy_statement: Presidential Instruction No. 9/2000 mandates gender mainstreaming in national development.
source_quote: Indonesia promulgated Presidential Instruction No. 9/2000 regarding Gender Mainstreaming into National Development, which have been followed up by Ministerial Decrees in most of the Ministries. The gender mainstreaming into national development planning including reference for gender responsive budget and gender budget tagging has started since 2015, with target achievements, among others, in terms of : (i) gender mainstreaming index ( Indeks Pengarusutamaan Gender/IPG ), (ii) gender empowerment index ( Indeks Pemberdayaan Gender/IDG ), (iii) eradication of all forms of violence to woman, and (iv) family development index ( Indeks Pembangunan Keluarga/IPK ).
extraction_rationale: This is a named policy instrument with implementation mechanisms including gender-responsive budgeting. Climate relevance is peripheral because it is included as a strategic supporting issue rather than a climate-specific policy.

policy_statement: Indonesia's National Strategy for Acceleration of Gender Mainstreaming Implementation will serve as a basis for addressing gender issues under LTS-LCCR 2050.
source_quote: Strategies to be implemented includes : (i) strengthening policy and regulation, (ii) accelerating gender mainstreaming, (iii) awareness raising, (iv) enhancing role and participation of women in development, and (v) improving network and coordination among stakeholders, which are part of 'National Strategy for Acceleration of Gender Mainstreaming Implementation'. This national strategy will be a strong basis for addressing gender issues under LTS-LCCR 2050 and Indonesia Vision 2045.
extraction_rationale: This is a named strategy with explicit implementation components, though climate relevance is peripheral.

policy_statement: National Action Plan on Children Friendly Cities and Municipalities (RAN-KLA) 2021-2024 will be a basis for addressing children's needs under LTS-LCCR 2050.
source_quote: Furthermore, the government has developed National Action Plan on Children Friendly Cities and Municipalities ( Rencana Aksi Nasional Kota Layak Anak or RAN-KLA) 2021-2024. The RAN-KLA will be a strong basis for addressing the needs of children under LTS-LCCR 2050 and Indonesia Vision 2045.
section_header: 6.2.3. Intergenerational Equity and the Needs of People in Vulnerable Situations
extraction_rationale: This is a named action plan linked to LTS-LCCR implementation, though climate relevance is peripheral.

policy_statement: Indonesia's laws and programmes on elderly welfare will be aligned with LTS-LCCR 2050 and Indonesia Vision 2045.
source_quote: The Law No. 43/2004, policies and programmes to address elderly population issues by different responsible Ministries, and lessons learned for the past years will be the basis to align the policies and programmes with LTS-LCCR 2050 as well as Indonesia Vision 2045.
section_header: 6.2.3. Intergenerational Equity and the Needs of People in Vulnerable Situations
extraction_rationale: This is a commitment to align existing policy frameworks with the climate strategy, but it is broad and climate relevance is peripheral.

policy_statement: Existing laws and action plans on disability inclusion will serve as the basis for addressing people with disabilities under LTS-LCCR 2050.
source_quote: Other regulatory frameworks and National Action Plan to enhance inclusiveness of people with disabilities in justice, work, infrastructure, politic, economy, public health and others have been in place. Similar to other issues, existing laws and other regulatory frameworks are strong basis for addressing the people with disabilities under LTS-LCCR 2050 and Indonesia Vision 2045.
section_header: 6.2.3. Intergenerational Equity and the Needs of People in Vulnerable Situations
extraction_rationale: This is a policy alignment statement for vulnerable groups under LTS-LCCR, but climate relevance is peripheral.

policy_statement: Adat community and local communities will play strategic roles in reducing GHG emissions and building resilience under LTS-LCCR.
source_quote: With their nature of relationship with forest resources, local wisdom and experiences in managing forest resources on the one hand, and role of forestry and other land use sector in contributing to Indonesia's commitment under the Paris Agreement on the other hand, Adat community and Local Community will play strategic roles in reducing GHGs emissions and in building resilience under LTS-LCCR.
section_header: 6.2.4. Masyarakat Hukum Adat (MHA) and Local Communities
extraction_rationale: This is a strategic implementation commitment involving indigenous and local communities, though it is broad and not highly operationalized in this passage.

policy_statement: Government will create trading and investment environments that promote sustainable supply chains, product certification, and future means to address unsustainable production practices under RCEP implementation.
source_quote: In order to contribute to the effectiveness of RCEP implementation, the government will create a trading and investment environments which promote sustainable supply chain initiatives, product certification and potential future means to address unsustainable production practices.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete trade and investment policy commitment with sustainability objectives; climate relevance is indirect.

policy_statement: Indonesia will strengthen domestic and international research collaboration to support mitigation and adaptation under LTS-LCCR.
source_quote: Indonesia will strengthen research collaboration among institutions within the country and national institutions with international partners, including think tanks and research institutions. There has been positive trend on the role of think tanks and research institutions in supporting governments, such as in improving public knowledge and engagement, providing issue-focused research, evidence-based policy advice to encourage greater action by non-state actors, 'push' and 'pull' private sectors towards greater climate ambition, assess the effectiveness of existing policies and identify solutions, and coordinating national and international expertise.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete means-of-implementation commitment on research collaboration.

policy_statement: Indonesia seeks technology cooperation under the Paris Agreement and Convention framework as a key element for achieving the ambitious LCCP scenario.
source_quote: With the ambitious target for the LTS-LCCR, Indonesia seeks opportunity for technology cooperation under the framework of technology development and transfer of the Paris Agreement and the Convention. Indonesia considers technology cooperation under this framework as a key element for the ambitious scenario of the LTS-LCCR.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear means-of-implementation commitment on international technology cooperation.

policy_statement: Indonesia's climate finance strategy includes diversifying finance sources, strengthening finance institutions, and strengthening stakeholder capacity to access finance.
source_quote: Therefore, the current efforts as part of the financing strategy for climate mitigation and adaptation includes increasing diversification of sources of finance, strengthening capacity of finance institutions, and strengthening capacity of stakeholders in accessing finance.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete climate finance strategy with defined implementation components.

policy_statement: Indonesia is exploring national climate finance instruments including green sukuk, green bonds, carbon pricing fees and levies, intergovernmental fiscal transfers, PAD, and other income sources.
source_quote: At the national level, the opportunities to optimise state budget are explored (e.g. using instruments of green sukuk or green bonds and draft of PERPRES NEK on Carbon Pricing Instruments such as fees and carbon levy; instruments of intergovernmental fiscal transfer; instruments of PAD and other sources of income). Furthermore, Indonesia continue to mobilise international financial sources through bilateral, regional, and multilateral channels, including result-based payment for REDD+ under the Paris Agreement, grant, and other potential sources and mechanisms.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete list of financial instruments under exploration for climate action.

policy_statement: Indonesia will develop an integrated capacity development approach aligned with Prosperous Indonesia 2045 and continue mobilizing international capacity-building support under the Paris Agreement.
source_quote: An integrated approach in capacity development to support the LTS-LCCR will be developed and aligned with capacity development to progress towards Prosperous Indonesia 2045. International support for capacity building under the Paris Agreement and the Convention will continue to be mobilised to support the achievement of the ambitious target under LCCP of LTS-LCCR.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete means-of-implementation commitment on capacity development and international support mobilization.

policy_statement: During 2021-2030, LTS-LCCR implementation will follow the Updated NDC through nine NDC Implementation Strategy Programmes.
source_quote: During the period of 2021-2030, implementation of LTS-LCCR will follow the implementation of first NDC (Updated NDC), which is guided by nine NDC Implementation Strategy Programmes as described in Updated NDC document.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete implementation governance commitment linking LTS-LCCR to the Updated NDC framework.

policy_statement: The draft Presidential Regulation on Carbon Pricing (PERPRES NEK) sets norms for NDC achievement, carbon economic instruments, transparency, and low-carbon development, and regulates roles of state and non-state actors.
source_quote: Presidential Regulation on Carbon Pricing (draft of PERPRES NEK) sets norms for four following main areas: (1) NDC target achievement, (2) carbon economic instrument, (3) transparency framework, and (4) low carbon development. The draft of PERPRES-NEK also regulates the roles of Parties and Non-Party Stakeholders in the NDC implementation.
extraction_rationale: This is a named draft regulation with clear policy scope including carbon pricing. It is still draft, but sufficiently concrete to extract.

policy_statement: NDC Road Maps provide detailed guidance on policies, programmes, actions, and periodic monitoring and evaluation to achieve the 2030 NDC target.
source_quote: Furthermore, NDC Road Maps (mitigation, adaptation, and means of implementation) provide detail guidance on policy, programme, and actions to achieve 2030 target of the NDC, as well as periodic monitoring and evaluation of the progress and achievement during this period .
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete implementation and monitoring framework for climate policy delivery.

policy_statement: Indonesia will continuously improve mechanisms for effective engagement of non-party stakeholders in LTS-LCCR implementation.
source_quote: Effective engagement of non-party stakeholders (NPS) will be a key driver of successful implementation of the LTS-LCCR. Therefore, taking into account relevant regulatory frameworks and policies, the mechanism for enhancing the effectiveness of NPS engagement will be continuously improved.
extraction_rationale: This is a governance commitment for implementation, though somewhat process-oriented; it qualifies because it commits to improving a specific mechanism.

policy_statement: Indonesia's LTS-LCCR 2050 will be monitored, reviewed, and updated as necessary in light of national circumstances, capacity, capability, and Paris Agreement provisions.
source_quote: In this regard, the Indonesia's LTS-LCCR 2050 will be monitored, reviewed and updated, as necessary, taking into consideration national circumstances, capacity and capability, and the provision under the Paris Agreement.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete review and update commitment for the climate strategy itself.

policy_statement: Set 2030 as an interim milestone toward full decarbonisation of the energy sector by 2050.
source_quote:
a) Accelerate the decarbonisation process by setting 2030 as an interim milestone for achieving  full  decarbonisation  of  the  energy  sector  by  2050  and  integrating environmental factors in other public policies.
- b) Place a central emphasis on citizens and businesses (in particular SMEs), in such a way that they become key players and beneficiaries of the energy transition and not just the financiers of active policies.
section_header: ii. Strategy relating to the five dimensions of the Energy Union
extraction_rationale: This is a clear target-setting commitment with a deadline and defined outcome, so it qualifies as a policy. It is broad and strategic rather than operational, but the 2030 and 2050 milestones provide sufficient policy anchor.

policy_statement: Promote self-consumption and renewable energy communities while improving regulation and transparency in energy sales.
source_quote: b) Place a central emphasis on citizens and businesses (in particular SMEs), in such a way that they become key players and beneficiaries of the energy transition and not just the financiers of active policies. This requires the promotion of self-consumption and renewable energy communities, but also the greatest possible degree of regulation and transparency of the sales segment, so that consumers may reap the benefits of a competitive market.
section_header: ii. Strategy relating to the five dimensions of the Energy Union
extraction_rationale: This qualifies because it names specific interventions: promotion of self-consumption and renewable energy communities, plus regulatory action on the sales segment. It is somewhat broad, but still concrete enough to count as a policy commitment.

policy_statement: Promote energy efficiency across all sectors to protect the environment, improve energy security and reduce energy costs.
source_quote:
f) Promote  energy  efficiency  across  all  sectors  as  an  instrument  for  protecting  the environment, improving energy security and reducing energy costs for families and businesses.
- g) Promote electrification of consumption, in particular in the civil and transport sectors, as an instrument for additionally improving air and environmental quality.
section_header: ii. Strategy relating to the five dimensions of the Energy Union
extraction_rationale: This is a cross-sector policy commitment with a named intervention—energy efficiency—and explicit intended outcomes. It is strategic and not quantified here, but still qualifies under the named intervention criterion.

policy_statement: Promote electrification of consumption, especially in buildings and transport.
source_quote:
g) Promote electrification of consumption, in particular in the civil and transport sectors, as an instrument for additionally improving air and environmental quality.
- h) Guide the evolution of the energy system through research and innovation activities to develop, in line with European  guidelines  and  the requirements  for full decarbonisation, solutions able to achieve sustainability, security, continuity and cost effectiveness of supply based increasingly on renewable energy in all usage sectors.
section_header: ii. Strategy relating to the five dimensions of the Energy Union
extraction_rationale: This is a specific strategic intervention focused on electrification in named sectors. Climate benefits are substantial, but the text frames air and environmental quality as the immediate rationale, so relevance is indirect.

policy_statement: Implement horizontal measures to govern, streamline, coordinate and support delivery of the Plan.
source_quote:
The horizontal measures will include the following.

- -Careful  governance  of  the  plan  that  will  enable  it  to  be  implemented  in  a  coordinated manner and which ensures uniformity of action, in particular in terms of the timeframes and  processes  for  authorising  and  building  physical  infrastructure,  the  coordination  of research and innovation activities, and, more generally, the monitoring of the effects of the plan in terms of the reorientation of the production system, and of and costs and benefits.
section_header: ii. Strategy relating to the five dimensions of the Energy Union
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella initiative explicitly followed by a list of sub-measures, so it should be extracted as a parent. It qualifies because it commits to a named governance package for implementation of the Plan.

parent_statement: Implement horizontal measures to govern, streamline, coordinate and support delivery of the Plan.
policy_statement: Establish coordinated multi-level governance for implementing the Plan and monitoring its effects.
source_quote: - -Careful  governance  of  the  plan  that  will  enable  it  to  be  implemented  in  a  coordinated manner and which ensures uniformity of action, in particular in terms of the timeframes and  processes  for  authorising  and  building  physical  infrastructure,  the  coordination  of research and innovation activities, and, more generally, the monitoring of the effects of the plan in terms of the reorientation of the production system, and of and costs and benefits. In light of the cross-cutting nature of the plan, which affects the tasks and remits of many State administrations, and  the system  of competences  established  by  the Italian Constitution,  this  governance  will  encompass  various  ministries.
section_header: ii. Strategy relating to the five dimensions of the Energy Union
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete implementation commitment under the horizontal measures list. It is not quantified, but it specifies a named intervention—governance architecture—and therefore qualifies.

parent_statement: Implement horizontal measures to govern, streamline, coordinate and support delivery of the Plan.
policy_statement: Evaluate and streamline procedures for implementing measures within the identified timeframes.
source_quote: - -An  evaluation  of  the  actions  needed  to  effectively  streamline  the  procedures  for implementing  the  measures  within  the  timeframes  identified.  Taken  together  with  the stability  of  the  legislative  and  regulatory  framework,  and  where  compatible  with  the requirement to periodically update the processes established as a result of technological developments and the monitoring of the costs and benefits of each measure, this will help to ensure that steady progress is made towards achieving the objectives.
section_header: ii. Strategy relating to the five dimensions of the Energy Union
extraction_rationale: This is a procedural reform commitment tied to implementation of climate measures. It qualifies because it commits to a specific intervention—streamlining procedures—to achieve plan objectives.

parent_statement: Implement horizontal measures to govern, streamline, coordinate and support delivery of the Plan.
policy_statement: Update and, if necessary, revise the tasks of public bodies to align them with the Plan and 2050 decarbonisation objectives.
source_quote: - -Updating - and, if necessary, revising - the tasks of the various public bodies working on energy and environmental matters to ensure that their roles and activities are coordinated and coherent with the objectives of the plan and, more generally, the objectives of full decarbonisation by 2050.
section_header: ii. Strategy relating to the five dimensions of the Energy Union
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete institutional reform commitment with a clear climate objective. It qualifies as a policy because it specifies an administrative intervention to support decarbonisation.

parent_statement: Implement horizontal measures to govern, streamline, coordinate and support delivery of the Plan.
policy_statement: Promote research on integrating electricity, gas and water systems, including use of existing infrastructure to store renewable energy.
