source_quote: - -Promoting research activities, with the involvement of network operators, on methods for enhancing the integration of the systems (electricity, gas, water), by exploring, for example, the possibility of using pre-existing infrastructure to store renewable energy, including in the long term, with solutions that are effective in terms of economic and environmental costs/benefits.
section_header: ii. Strategy relating to the five dimensions of the Energy Union
extraction_rationale: This is a named research intervention under the horizontal measures. It qualifies because it commits to specific research activity supporting renewable integration and storage.

parent_statement: Implement horizontal measures to govern, streamline, coordinate and support delivery of the Plan.
policy_statement: Integrate new technologies, especially information technologies, into the energy system to support distributed generation, resilience, efficiency and active consumers.
source_quote: - -Integrating new technologies into the energy system, starting with information technologies,  in  order  to  facilitate  distributed  generation,  security,  resilience,  energy efficiency, and the active participation of consumers in energy markets.
section_header: ii. Strategy relating to the five dimensions of the Energy Union
extraction_rationale: This is a specific technology integration commitment. It qualifies because it names concrete interventions and explicitly includes resilience and energy efficiency.

parent_statement: Implement horizontal measures to govern, streamline, coordinate and support delivery of the Plan.
policy_statement: Consider additional instruments such as reviewing energy taxation based on polluting and climate-changing emissions.
source_quote: - -A willingness to consider additional instruments if necessary, such as, for example, a review of energy taxation, diversified on the basis of polluting and climate-changing emissions, and in any case in line with the Community approach to this issue. In this, consideration would be given to the vulnerable sections of the population and to those production sectors that are still without alternative options to traditional fuel.
section_header: ii. Strategy relating to the five dimensions of the Energy Union
extraction_rationale: This is borderline because it is framed as willingness to consider, but it identifies a specific policy instrument—energy taxation differentiated by emissions. Because the instrument is named and clearly contemplated as part of implementation, it is included with noted vagueness.

policy_statement: Phase out coal-fired electricity generation by the end of 2025, subject to timely construction of replacement plants and infrastructure.
source_quote: For those sectors covered by the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) - primarily the thermoelectric sector and energy-intensive industries - factors contributing to this goal include: the phasing out of coal, scheduled by the end of 2025, as mentioned within the limits of, and as long as the replacement plants and necessary infrastructure are constructed in good time; a higher CO2 price level than in  recent  years;  and  a  significant  acceleration  of  renewables  and  energy  efficiency  in manufacturing processes.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear, dated mitigation commitment and one of the most concrete policies in the document. The caveat about replacement infrastructure introduces implementation uncertainty but does not negate the policy commitment.

policy_statement: Develop measures for ESR sectors, especially transport and buildings, combining renewable energy use and efficiency improvements.
source_quote: For those other sectors included in the objectives established by the Effort Sharing Regulation (ESR), measures that take into account the potential and costs of reducing emissions will be developed; the most important contribution will, in any case, come from the transport and civil (residential and tertiary) sectors, combining measures for using and increasing the efficiency of renewables.
extraction_rationale: This is a policy commitment to develop measures in named sectors under the ESR framework. It is somewhat general, but it specifies sectors and mechanisms, so it qualifies.

policy_statement: Exceed if possible the 30% renewable energy target while limiting soil consumption and environmental impacts.
source_quote: Italy will promote the further development of renewables while also protecting and enhancing pre-existing products, by exceeding, if possible, the 30% target set, which must, in any event, be assumed to be a contribution towards meeting the EU target. This will be achieved through the use of instruments calibrated on the basis of the sectors of use, types of measures and size of  the  plants,  with  an  approach  aimed  at  limiting  soil  consumption  and  the  impact  on  the landscape  and  environment,  including  requirements  on  air  quality.
extraction_rationale: This qualifies because it contains a quantified target and a stated implementation approach. The phrase 'if possible' adds some softness, but the 30% target itself is concrete.

policy_statement: Promote self-consumption, distributed generation and storage using built-up or already-used areas for renewable electricity.
source_quote: With regard  to  the electricity  sector,  and  with  an  additional  view  to  the  electrification  of consumption,  the intention is to make widespread use of built-up areas or areas already in use in some other way, by raising the profile of the different forms of self-consumption, including through distributed generation and storage.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific intervention naming self-consumption, distributed generation and storage, and it identifies siting preferences. It qualifies as a policy despite lacking a numeric target.

policy_statement: Trial accelerated decarbonisation and electrification with renewable sources on small islands disconnected from national networks.
source_quote: A further aim is to promote the creation of systems, starting with a few small islands disconnected from the national networks, in which an accelerated decarbonisation process  and electrification  of  consumption  with  renewable  sources  can  be trialled.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete pilot-policy commitment focused on a defined geography and intervention type. It qualifies because it names a specific programmatic action.

policy_statement: Integrate energy efficiency into broader building renovation, earthquake-proofing and refurbishment measures in line with the 2050 renovation strategy.
source_quote:
However, attempts will be also be made to integrate the energy efficiency aspect into policies and measures whose main purpose is something other than efficiency, in order to optimise the

cost-benefit ratio of the actions. In this respect, the significant potential for efficiency in the building sector may be better exploited through measures aimed at, for example, the energy renovation  of  buildings  and  neighbourhoods,  together  with  the  structural  renovation, earthquake-proofing, systems upgrading and refurbishment thereof, in line with the strategy for  energy  renovation  of  the  building  stock  by  2050.
extraction_rationale: This qualifies because it commits to a specific intervention package in buildings and links it to the 2050 renovation strategy. It is broad but operationally anchored in named measures.

policy_statement: Prioritise reducing mobility demand, increasing collective mobility and shifting freight from road to rail.
source_quote: With regard to transport, priority is  given to  policies  for  reducing demand  for  mobility  and increasing  collective  mobility,  in  particular  rail  transport,  which  includes  shifting  freight transport from road to rail. 'Improve' measures (regarding vehicle efficiency and emissions) must be supplemented with instruments to reduce mobility needs ('avoid' measures) and with efficiency in travel ('shift' measures).
extraction_rationale: This is a clear transport policy package with named interventions—avoid, shift, improve—and modal shift. It qualifies as a policy commitment even though no numeric target is attached here.

policy_statement: Promote alternative fuels, especially electricity, for remaining private and freight mobility through economic and regulatory instruments.
source_quote: As  for  the  remaining  demand  for  private  mobility  and  the  mobility  of  goods,  the  aim  is  to promote the use of alternative fuels and, in particular, electricity. This will be done by increasing the share of renewables through economic and regulatory instruments, in coordination with local government bodies.
extraction_rationale: This qualifies because it specifies the intervention, target sectors and implementation tools. It is not quantified, but it is a concrete policy direction.

policy_statement: Use 2021-2027 EU development and cohesion resources for a national energy programme supporting efficient buildings and sustainable mobility infrastructure.
source_quote: Along with the ordinary instruments, it will also be possible to use resources from the EU's development and cohesion programming cycle for 2021-27. In this regard, in the discussions with partners, which involve the Regions, among others, a specific national energy programme has been proposed. Taking the INECP as reference, this is intended to support initiatives to modernise  and  improve  the  efficiency  of  buildings  and  build  new  infrastructure,  including infrastructure  for  sustainable  mobility.
extraction_rationale: This is a resource allocation and programme commitment with a defined funding source and period. It clearly qualifies as a policy and as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Explore power-to-gas solutions and hydrogen to absorb imbalances between renewable electricity production and demand.
source_quote:
In  addition,  to  achieve the  security and  flexibility  objectives, the  intention  is  to  explore  the potential offered by growing integration of the electricity and gas network infrastructure. In

this context, it will be important to explore the costs and benefits of power-to-gas technological solutions  which,  especially  over  the  long  term,  make  it  possible  to  absorb  any  imbalances between renewable electricity production and energy demand, especially with high levels of photovoltaic  penetration.  Hydrogen  could  contribute  to  this,  including  for  non-electricity consumption.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific technology and infrastructure exploration commitment. It qualifies because it names concrete interventions and their system function.

policy_statement: Adopt preventive measures and operational rules to improve resilience of transmission and distribution networks against extreme events and heavy loads.
source_quote: Particular attention will be paid to the resilience of the systems, in particular of transmission and  distribution  networks,  through  preventive  measures  proportionate  to  the  expected increase in extreme events and periods of heavy load, and operational rules that enable the systems to be quickly restored to normal functioning levels.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear adaptation-oriented infrastructure resilience commitment tied to climate hazards. It qualifies because it specifies preventive measures and operational rules.

policy_statement: Adopt the Plan for the Sustainable Energy Transition of Suitable Areas (PSETSA) by the end of 2020.
source_quote: In addition, by the end of 2020 the Plan for the Sustainable Energy Transition of Suitable Areas (PSETSA)  will  be  adopted.  This  document  will  make  it  possible  to  establish  a  framework  of reference of those areas in Italy in which hydrocarbon exploration, research and production activities  would  be  planned,  with  the  aim  of  improving  their  environmental,  social  and economic sustainability.
extraction_rationale: This is a dated planning commitment with a named instrument and explicit adoption deadline. Climate relevance is peripheral because the focus is hydrocarbon planning and sustainability rather than climate mitigation itself.

policy_statement: Revise Terna's development plans to include additional measures such as centralised storage systems for safe renewable integration and reduced over-generation.
source_quote: In terms of transmission infrastructure, the references are Terna S.p.A.'s development plans, which  will  be  revised  with  a  view  to  introducing  additional  measures,  such  as  centralised storage  systems,  needed  to  ensure  safe  integration  of  renewable  sources,  and  reducing over-generation,  to  be  implemented  in  compliance  with  the  provisions  of  the  latest  EU guidelines.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete planning and infrastructure commitment tied to renewable integration. It qualifies because it names a specific intervention—centralised storage systems.

policy_statement: Analyse market and regulatory changes to foster electricity-gas integration and long-term storage technologies.
source_quote:
Appropriate changes to the market and to the regulatory system could be analysed to foster the electricity-gas integration of technologies that convert electricity into a gas that can be injected to the network, in line with the provisions for energy storage systems in the recently

approved Electricity Market Directive and Regulation. This would be done taking developments in storage systems, including those enabled by technologies that convert one form of energy to another, and the need to develop seasonal and long-term storage into special consideration.
extraction_rationale: This is somewhat exploratory, but it identifies a specific regulatory intervention area and technology class. It qualifies because it is tied to concrete market-rule changes under EU legislation.

policy_statement: Introduce efficiency measures and renewable self-consumption installations to address energy poverty.
source_quote: With regard to energy poverty, to supplement the measures described below, studies are under way to introduce efficiency measures and measures for the installation of renewable energy plants with self-consumption.
extraction_rationale: This is borderline because it refers to studies under way, but it clearly identifies intended measures—efficiency and renewable self-consumption for energy poverty. Included because the interventions are specific and recur later in the Plan.

policy_statement: Create green government securities proportionate to budget-funded interventions on climate change, energy conversion and the circular economy.
source_quote: However, it is worth noting in this section  the  creation  of  'green'  government  securities.  Issuances  of  Green  Bonds  will  be proportionate  to  interventions  funded  from  the  State  budget  to  combat  climate  change, promote energy conversion and the circular economy, protect the environment and foster social and territorial cohesion.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear financial instrument: green bonds linked to climate and energy spending. It qualifies because it commits to a named financing mechanism.

policy_statement: Set up a permanent technical office, the INECP Observatory, to support implementation and monitoring of the Plan.
source_quote: In the context of the 'concurrent competences' between State and Regions, and with due regard for the roles of the regulator, the network operators and market operators, and with a view to ensuring that the Plan is implemented correctly, a permanent technical office will be set up (INECP Observatory, which will absorb the existing Renewables Observatory). The role of the office will be to discuss, share and agree and cooperate on topics regarding the implementation of the Plan, with particular reference to the following:
section_header: iv. Administrative structure of implementing national energy and climate policies
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete institutional commitment with a named body and implementation role. It qualifies as a policy because it establishes governance infrastructure for climate policy delivery.

policy_statement: INECP Observatory implementation functions.
source_quote:
The role of the office will be to discuss, share and agree and cooperate on topics regarding the implementation of the Plan, with particular reference to the following:

- establishing implementation provisions and decrees for the transposition of the relevant European directives;
section_header: iv. Administrative structure of implementing national energy and climate policies
extraction_rationale: This is a parent because it introduces a list of specific implementation functions for the Observatory. The listed items are concrete sub-actions.

parent_statement: INECP Observatory implementation functions.
policy_statement: Prepare implementation provisions and decrees for transposing relevant European directives.
source_quote:
- establishing implementation provisions and decrees for the transposition of the relevant European directives;

- reform to simplify authorisation procedures (dynamic repowering/revamping/permitting);
section_header: iv. Administrative structure of implementing national energy and climate policies
extraction_rationale: This is a specific implementation action under the Observatory. It qualifies because it commits to preparing legal instruments for directive transposition.

parent_statement: INECP Observatory implementation functions.
policy_statement: Reform and simplify authorisation procedures for repowering, revamping and permitting.
source_quote:
- reform to simplify authorisation procedures (dynamic repowering/revamping/permitting);

- -monitoring the state of progress of the Plan objectives;
section_header: iv. Administrative structure of implementing national energy and climate policies
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete procedural reform action under the Observatory's remit. It qualifies because it names a specific regulatory intervention.

parent_statement: INECP Observatory implementation functions.
policy_statement: Monitor progress toward the Plan objectives.
source_quote:
- -monitoring the state of progress of the Plan objectives;
- -developing plants, electricity grid and storage systems;
section_header: iv. Administrative structure of implementing national energy and climate policies
extraction_rationale: Monitoring is a concrete implementation commitment tied to plan delivery. It qualifies because it establishes an operational accountability mechanism.

parent_statement: INECP Observatory implementation functions.
policy_statement: Coordinate development of plants, electricity grids and storage systems.
source_quote:
- -developing plants, electricity grid and storage systems;
- -coordinating, in a framework of overarching national rules, the promotion of recharging infrastructure for electric vehicles;
section_header: iv. Administrative structure of implementing national energy and climate policies
extraction_rationale: This is a specific implementation action concerning infrastructure development. It qualifies because it names concrete assets and system components.

parent_statement: INECP Observatory implementation functions.
policy_statement: Coordinate promotion of electric vehicle charging infrastructure under national rules.
source_quote:
- -coordinating, in a framework of overarching national rules, the promotion of recharging infrastructure for electric vehicles;
- -checking  and  drafting  improvement  proposals,  including  in  coordination  with  INECP environmental monitoring, regarding the arrangements and implementation times for the roadmap through which the effects of climate change will be integrated, in the two RCP 4.5 and 8.5 scenarios, in the first update of the INECP for 2023.
section_header: iv. Administrative structure of implementing national energy and climate policies
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete coordination commitment for EV charging infrastructure. It qualifies because it specifies a named intervention and governance framework.

parent_statement: INECP Observatory implementation functions.
policy_statement: Draft improvement proposals for integrating climate change effects into the first 2023 INECP update using RCP 4.5 and 8.5 scenarios.
source_quote: - -checking  and  drafting  improvement  proposals,  including  in  coordination  with  INECP environmental monitoring, regarding the arrangements and implementation times for the roadmap through which the effects of climate change will be integrated, in the two RCP 4.5 and 8.5 scenarios, in the first update of the INECP for 2023.
section_header: iv. Administrative structure of implementing national energy and climate policies
extraction_rationale: This is a dated and specific planning commitment related to climate scenario integration. It qualifies because it names the update year and the scenarios to be used.

policy_statement: Allocate specific resources for periodic statistical surveys to model sectoral energy consumption using Eurostat-harmonised methods.
source_quote: To allow Italy to keep pace with this evolving scenario, provision has been made for specific resources to be allocated to the performance of periodical statistical surveys, on the basis of which a model of the structure and characteristics of energy consumption across different sectors (residential, tertiary, industrial, transport) can be developed  using Eurostat harmonised procedures, definitions and methodologies.
section_header: iv. Administrative structure of implementing national energy and climate policies
extraction_rationale: This qualifies because it includes explicit resource allocation for a defined implementation function. It is not a climate policy in itself, but it materially supports climate and energy policy monitoring, so relevance is indirect.

policy_statement: Set up a Plan-monitoring platform through GSE to collect data and support reporting and environmental monitoring.
source_quote: To this end, for the purposes of the INECP Observatory and to provide timely, up-to-date information to citizens and central and local government bodies, GSE will set up a Plan-monitoring platform to which data and information from different sources will be channelled. This platform will also provide input data for the environmental monitoring plan, for the tasks for which the Ministry of the Environment and ISPRA are responsible in the communications sphere under the  above-mentioned  MMR  and  Governance  Regulations,  for  the  drafting  of  the  annual report on the implementation of the Plan envisaged in the context of the INECP Observatory, and for the drafting of the two-yearly reports to be sent to the European Commission.
section_header: iv. Administrative structure of implementing national energy and climate policies
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete operational commitment with a named implementing body and clear outputs. It qualifies as a policy because it establishes a monitoring system for climate plan implementation.

policy_statement: Continue burden-sharing of renewable energy objectives with Regions beyond 2020.
source_quote: This approach,  based  on  a  distribution  of  effort between the various Regions, will also be proposed beyond 2020, in order to ensure sharing of objectives and to call on regional governments to contribute in a coherent manner to their attainment.
section_header: iv. Administrative structure of implementing national energy and climate policies
extraction_rationale: This is a clear continuation commitment for a named governance mechanism. It qualifies because it specifies a policy approach for post-2020 implementation.

policy_statement: Reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 33% from 2005 levels in non-ETS sectors by 2030.
source_quote: Regulation (EU) 2018/842 on binding annual greenhouse gas emission reductions by Member States from 2021 to 2030 contributing to climate action to meet commitments under the Paris Agreement (the Effort Sharing Regulation, ESR) sets Italy a reduction  target of -33% compared with 2005 levels for non-ETS sectors. This target must be achieved by following a linear reduction trajectory that will identify an emissions limit for each year.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified, binding target with a defined baseline and trajectory. It clearly qualifies as a climate policy target.

policy_statement: Pursue a 30% share of renewable energy in gross final consumption by 2030.
source_quote: Italy plans to pursue the target of obtaining 30% of gross final consumption of energy from renewable  sources  in  2030  by  defining  a  pathway  of  sustainable  growth  for  renewable sources and the full integration thereof into the system. In particular, the target for 2030 projects a gross final consumption of energy of 111 Mtoe, with approximately 33 Mtoe of that  coming  from  renewable  sources.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified national renewable energy target with supporting energy values. It clearly qualifies as a policy target.

policy_statement: Reach a 55.0% renewable share in the electricity sector by 2030.
source_quote:
Without prejudice to the statement made at the end of section i. above (which applies to all of the following information, including section iii.), the contribution of renewables to meet total gross final consumption by 2030 (30%) is expected to have the following distribution between the different sectors:

- -55.0% renewables share in the electricity sector;
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified sectoral target and therefore clearly qualifies. It is one of the core renewable energy commitments in the Plan.

policy_statement: Reach a 33.9% renewable share in heating and cooling by 2030.
source_quote:
- -33.9% renewables share in the heating sector (for heating and cooling);
- -22.0%  with  regard  to  the  incorporation  of  renewables  in  the  transport  sector (calculated using the target accounting criteria established by RED II).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified sectoral target with a clear 2030 endpoint. It qualifies as a policy target.

policy_statement: Reach a 22.0% renewable share in transport by 2030 under RED II accounting criteria.
source_quote: - -22.0%  with  regard  to  the  incorporation  of  renewables  in  the  transport  sector (calculated using the target accounting criteria established by RED II).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified transport-sector target and clearly qualifies as a policy commitment.

policy_statement: Increase renewable electricity capacity to 95,210 MW by 2030, including 52,000 MW solar and 19,300 MW wind.
extraction_rationale: This table contains explicit quantified capacity targets by technology and year, which clearly qualify as policy targets. The quote is tabular but verbatim and self-contained.

policy_statement: Pursue a 43% reduction in primary energy consumption and 39.7% reduction in final energy consumption by 2030 relative to PRIMES 2007.
source_quote: Italy  intends to pursue an indicative reduction target for 2030 of 43% for primary energy consumption  and  of  39.7%  for  final  energy  consumption,  with  respect  to  the  reference PRIMES 2007 scenario.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified national energy efficiency target with a clear reference scenario. It clearly qualifies as a policy target.

policy_statement: Target 125.1 Mtoe of primary energy consumption and 103.8 Mtoe of final energy consumption in 2030.
source_quote: By  contrast,  with  regard  to  the  absolute  level  of  energy  consumption  for  2030,  Italy  is pursuing a target of 125.1 Mtoe of primary energy and 103.8 Mtoe of final energy, following the trajectory indicated in the following figure, starting with the estimated consumption for 2020.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified absolute consumption target for 2030. It qualifies as a policy target under the quantifiable target criterion.

policy_statement: Achieve 50.98 Mtoe cumulative end-use energy savings in 2021-2030 under Article 7 of the EED.
source_quote:
Therefore, it is estimated that new measures will produce a 0.927 Mtoe incremental saving of final energy per year for the period 2021-2030, which is primarily attributable to the civil and transport sectors.

In terms of the overall cumulative amount, this translates into a 50.98 Mtoe saving of final energy to be attained through active policies during the period 2021-2030.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified cumulative savings commitment over a defined period. It clearly qualifies as a policy target.

policy_statement: Continue PREPAC in 2021-2030 and renovate 3.2 million m2 of central public administration buildings.
source_quote:
Provision is also made to continue with the Energy Renovation Programme for the Central Public  Administration  (PREPAC)  during  the  period  2021-2030,  which  programme  will  be enhanced as a result of the experience gained during the seven-year period 2014-2020.

In  particular,  considering  an  overall  floor  area  of  buildings  subject  to  the  provisions  of Article 5 of the EED equal to 15.2 million m 2 in Italy per 4 102 occupants, during the period 2021-2030,  3.2 million m 2 of  floor  area  of  buildings  associated  with  the  central  public administration will be subjected to energy renovation.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete programme continuation with a quantified renovation area and timeframe. It clearly qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Expand district heating and cooling networks by about 900 km to deliver around 4,000 GWh of additional energy.
source_quote: In particular, according to the results of the report drafted by GSE on the assessment of the national  potential  for  the  application  of  HEC  and  efficient  district  heating  established  by Article 14 of the EED, the economically sustainable growth potential for energy provided by district  heating  is  approximately  4,000 GWh, to be attained by extending national district heating  and  district  cooling  networks  by  approximately  900 km,  on  top  of  the  current network size of approximately 4 100 km.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified infrastructure development commitment. It qualifies because it specifies both output and network expansion.

policy_statement: Reduce energy dependence to about 68% by 2030.
source_quote: The  objective  of  increasing  energy  independence  will  be  pursued  primarily  through  an increased production of renewable energy and energy efficiency, in a manner that will be clarified  in  the  relevant  chapters.  On  the  basis  of  the  scenario  with  targets,  energy dependence  should  decrease  from  77.7%  in  2016  to  approximately  68%  in  2030.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified energy security target with a baseline and target year. It qualifies as a policy target.

policy_statement: Install at least 6 GW of new storage systems by 2030, with at least 50% provided by pumping systems.
source_quote:
- -Installation of new storage systems amounting to at least 6 GW by 2030, mainly to offer  network  services  and  located  primarily  in  the  south,  followed  by  Sicily  and Sardinia,  on  the  market.  For  these  systems  -  following  the  establishment  of requirements  by  market  area  and  before  launching  implementation  projects  location criteria will first be established jointly with the Regions.
- -At least 50% of the storage power required of the electricity system will be provided by pumping systems, and the remainder by electrochemical  storage  systems  with  a  capacity/power  ratio  of  about  8 kWh/kW.
extraction_rationale: This is a highly concrete infrastructure target with quantity, timing and technology split. It clearly qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Deploy about 4.5 GW of storage systems coupled with distributed systems mainly to maximise self-consumption.
source_quote: - -A  high  penetration  of  storage  systems  coupled  with  distributed  systems  (about 4.5 GW) is envisaged, mainly to maximise self-consumption (charging in the central hours of the day and discharging in the evening).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified deployment commitment for distributed storage. It qualifies because it specifies scale and purpose.

policy_statement: Reduce renewable over-generation to around 1 TWh by 2030 through network upgrades, dispatching resources and storage.
source_quote: - -Reduction of over-generation to values of around 1 TWh by 2030, by upgrading the network,  introducing  new  dispatching  resources  and  storage  systems  and  making more use of existing storage systems.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified system-management target with named interventions. It qualifies as a policy commitment.

policy_statement: Promote more proactive and flexible electricity demand, including electric vehicle recharging, through technological and market instruments.
source_quote: - -Encouragement  of  more  pro-active  and  flexible  electricity  demand  (demand  side response)  that  could  be  an  important  resource,  as  in  the  case  of  electric  vehicle recharging,  for  which  it  is  necessary  to  foster  the  convergence of demand and supply peaks for non-programmable renewable sources through appropriate technological and market instruments and measures.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific demand-side management commitment with named mechanisms. It qualifies because it identifies a concrete intervention area.

policy_statement: Increase network resilience against extreme weather events through specific action plans starting with higher-risk areas.
source_quote: - -Increased network resilience, including against extreme weather events, by adopting and implementing specific action plans, starting with higher risk areas, in order to protect continuity of supply and the safety of individuals and property.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation commitment tied to a named hazard and implementation mechanism. It clearly qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Target 35% interconnection capacity relative to peak load by 2030.
source_quote: With regard to indicator 2), the estimated value for 2030 in the scenario with targets is 35%, which does not highlight any need for the development of further interconnections.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified interconnection planning benchmark for 2030. It qualifies as a policy-relevant target even though framed through the EU indicator methodology.

policy_statement: Target 25% interconnection capacity relative to installed renewable generation by 2030.
source_quote: With regard to indicator 3), the estimated value for 2030 in the scenario with targets is 25%, which  does  not  highlight  any  need  for  the  development  of  further  interconnections.
extraction_rationale: This is another quantified interconnection benchmark under the EU methodology. It qualifies because it is a concrete planning indicator for 2030.

policy_statement: Promote active consumer participation, self-production, storage and demand response in electricity markets.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete market participation policy with three named forms of consumer action. It qualifies because it specifies interventions and market roles.

policy_statement: End regulated electricity price protection for domestic consumers and small enterprises on 1 January 2022.
source_quote: These are  necessary  steps  towards  greater  consumer  awareness  and  protection, prerequisites  for  the  abolition  of  price  protection  schemes,  which  the  Italian  authorities recently  established  should  take  place  on  1 January  2022  (Article 12  of  Decree-Law No 162/2019).
extraction_rationale: This is a dated regulatory reform commitment. Climate relevance is peripheral because it concerns market liberalisation rather than climate objectives directly.

policy_statement: Reduce energy poverty to between 7% and 8%, about one percentage point below the 2016 level.
source_quote: Taking these and other factors into account, it can be assumed that the incidence of energy poverty  could  decrease  in  the  coming  years,  to  remain  at  between  7%  and  8%,  with  a reduction  of  about  1  percentage  point  with  respect  to  the  2016  figure  (which  would correspond to a reduction of about 230,000 households in energy poverty, again with respect to 2016).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified social target related to energy poverty. It is somewhat framed as an assumption, but it functions as the stated reduction objective in the section.

policy_statement: Double public research resources for clean energy from about €222 million in 2013 to about €444 million from 2021.
source_quote: As regards financial resources in the context of Mission Innovation, Italy has undertaken to double the value of the resources portfolio for public research in the field of clean energy, from around €222 million in 2013 (the year taken as the baseline) to around €444 million from  2021,  which  represents  for  all  intents  and  purposes  the  minimum  commitment necessary to guarantee that the indicated targets will be reached.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified funding commitment with a baseline and target year. It clearly qualifies as a policy and as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Implement circular economy strategies such as extending product life, reuse, lighter materials, industrial symbiosis and recycling.
source_quote:
Recent  international  studies  (https://www.resourcepanel.org/)  are  starting  to  look  more closely  at  the  efficient  use  of  materials  and  their  potential  contribution  to  reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Some studies have identified the following strategies to that end:

- extending the service life of products
- reuse-repair
- opting for less carbon-intensive materials at production stage
- reducing materials used and opting for lighter materials
- improving the production process
- sharing goods
- industrial symbiosis

## - recycling and end-of-waste status
extraction_rationale: This is somewhat unusual because it is framed through studies, but it introduces the strategic circular economy measures that the section then operationalises. Included because it names specific interventions central to the waste and circular economy policy package.

policy_statement: Apply the Programme Agreement for coordinated measures to improve air quality in the Po basin, including agricultural emission reduction practices.
source_quote: The Po Basin Agreement 2017 identifies joint measures and actions to combat emissions, including greenhouse emissions and fine particles. Regarding measures in the agricultural and animal husbandry sectors, the Italian Regions must, as part of the air quality plans, apply practices  aimed  at  the  reduction  of  emissions  produced  by  agricultural  activity,  including coverage of structures for storing sewage, using the correct methods for spreading of manure and the burial of soil surfaces used to apply fertilisers, where these practices are technically feasible and economically sustainable.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete regional regulatory/planning measure with named agricultural practices. It qualifies because it specifies interventions and implementation through regional plans.

policy_statement: Adopt a national code of good agricultural practices to control ammonia emissions.
source_quote:
The code, which will become part of the national programme for controlling atmospheric pollution, takes account of the following factors for reducing ammonia emissions:

- -nitrogen management, taking into account the whole nitrogen cycle;
extraction_rationale: This is a named planning/regulatory instrument with a defined purpose. It qualifies because it establishes a specific code and reduction focus.

policy_statement: Use the 2021-2027 Common Agricultural Policy to reinforce environmental conditionality and ecological regimes.
source_quote:
The measures indicated in the aforementioned national code are reflected in terms of both budget and application in the instruments of the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP), which, in comparison to the 2014-2020 CAP, places greater focus on improving the environment. These measures will be viable in the period 2021-2027 and provide for:

- -reinforcement of the cross-compliance that will involve direct payments subject to more rigorous environmental requirements;
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete policy package tied to a funding period and named CAP instruments. It qualifies because it specifies implementation mechanisms and timing.

policy_statement: Assess measures to promote CO2 sequestration in agricultural soils and forest systems, including ecosystem service payments.
source_quote: With due consideration for the outcome of the public consultation, an assessment will be made of potential measures to promote initiatives aimed at CO2 sequestration in agricultural soils and forest systems (soils, subterranean and above-ground biomass, wood, etc.). This will also take into account potential payment measures for ecosystem services for forestry and those  linked  to  agricultural  soils  and  to  herbaceous  (arable,  etc.)  and  arboreal  farming systems.
extraction_rationale: This is somewhat exploratory, but it identifies a specific intervention area and possible payment mechanism. Included because it is a concrete contemplated policy on sequestration.

policy_statement: Prepare the Annual Report on Italian Forests to consolidate up-to-date knowledge on forests.
source_quote: The  report  foresees  consolidation  of  up-to-date  understanding  of  Italian  forests  in  every aspect:  natural,  productive,  economic,  etc.  Collection  of  information  from  all  of  the stakeholders involved is also envisaged, including the Regions, regional bodies, ISTAT, and the economic and scientific sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a named planning and information instrument. It qualifies because it commits to producing a recurring report to support forestry policy.

policy_statement: Implement the Consolidated Law on Forests and Forest Supply Chains to support sustainable forest management and increased carbon absorption.
source_quote: On 3 April 2018, the new Italian Consolidated Law in relation to forests and forest supply chains (TUFF) was enacted, with Legislative Decree 34/2018, which repeals Legislative Decree 227/2001, 'direction and modernisation of the forestry sector'. The TUFF provides advice and guidelines to support regional administrations in relation to forestry management.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding legislative instrument and clearly qualifies. The broader paragraph also explicitly links it to sustainable forest management and carbon absorption.

policy_statement: Develop a new National Forestry Strategy supported by the White Paper on the forests of Italy.
source_quote: In order to support the process of drafting a new national forestry strategy, the white paper on  the  forests  of  Italy  has  been  published  and  is  open  for  consultation,  with  the  aim  of providing  support  to  the  establishment  of  the  new  National  Forestry  Strategy  (NFS).  The white paper collects and summarises the views, requirements and needs of civil and business society and the scientific and institutional world on the role of the forestry sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a planning commitment toward a named national strategy. It qualifies because it is tied to a formal strategy-development process.

policy_statement: Implement Legislative Decree No 81/2018 to reduce atmospheric pollutants through national air pollution control programmes and inventories.
source_quote:
Italian Legislative Decree No 81/2018, transposing Directive (EU) No 2016/2284, provides for the  reduction  of  certain  atmospheric  pollutants  (sulphur  dioxide,  nitrogen  oxides,  nonmethane volatile organic compounds, ammonia and fine particulate matter) by means of:

- -the  drawing  up,  adopting  and  implementing  of  national  air  pollution  control programmes in conjunction with policies adopted in relation to climate change;
extraction_rationale: This is a binding transposition measure with specific implementation actions. Climate relevance is indirect because the primary objective is air pollution control, though climate coordination is explicit.

policy_statement: Apply certification rules for solid biomass heat generators under Ministerial Decree No 186/2017.
source_quote: The  Decree  establishes  the  requirements,  procedures  and  responsibilities  for  issuing  an environmental certificate for heat generators powered by firewood, charcoal and combustible  biomass.  The Decree  identifies, additionally,  the  emission  performance standards for different quality classes, the related test methods and checks to be carried out for the purposes of issuing the environmental certification, and specific obligations relating to guidance to be provided about the correct methods of installation and management of heat generators which have obtained the environmental certificate.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear regulatory standard with defined requirements and procedures. It qualifies as a policy due to its binding certification mechanism.

policy_statement: Adapt the certification system and create a database for fluorinated greenhouse gases and related equipment.
source_quote: In order to reduce emissions of fluorinated greenhouse gases that occur during operations for the installation, maintenance, repair and dismantling of equipment that contain these gases,  the  new  Italian  Presidential  Decree  adopted  in November  2018  provides  for  the adaptation of the certification system for natural persons and for companies that carry out these operations, and the establishment of a 'database' for the collection and retention of information relating to sales of fluorinated greenhouse gases and of equipment containing these  gases,  as  well  as  all  of  the  registrations  relating  to  operations  for  the  installation, maintenance, repair and dismantling of such equipment.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete regulatory and monitoring measure targeting F-gas emissions. It clearly qualifies as a mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Use the Environmental Code to implement SEA, EIA, IPPC, waste, air pollution and environmental damage measures contributing to emission reductions.
source_quote:
The Environmental Code represents a tool, already active today on a national level, which contributes to reducing greenhouse gas emissions by means of:

- a) implementation  of  procedures  for  Strategic  Environmental  Assessment  (SEA),  for Environmental  Impact  Assessment  (EIA)  and  for  Integrated  Environmental  Authorisation (IPPC);
extraction_rationale: This is a binding regulatory framework with multiple concrete mechanisms. It qualifies because it is explicitly identified as contributing to GHG reductions.

policy_statement: Use the Energy Transition Fund for the industrial sector to finance decarbonisation and energy efficiency measures.
source_quote: Decree-Law No 101 of 3 September 2019 established the 'Fund for energy transition in the industrial sector' to support energy transition in sectors or sub-sectors that are considered to be at a high risk of re-localisation of carbon emissions owing to costs linked to greenhouse gas emissions being transferred onto the price of electricity. The fund is constituted by that part of the annual revenue deriving from EU ETS auctions that exceeds 1,000 million. This excess amount, up to a maximum of €100 million per year for 2020 and €150 million as of 2021, will be used to fund decarbonisation and energy efficiency measures in the industrial sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear financial instrument with named funding source and annual amounts. It qualifies strongly as a policy.

policy_statement: Implement the Action Plan for improving air quality through measures on agriculture, mobility, domestic heating, coal phase-out and subsidy reform.
source_quote: In June 2019 the 'Action plan for improving air quality' was launched. Signed by the Prime Minister's  Office,  six  Ministries,  and  the  Regions  and  Autonomous  Provinces,  the  plan contains  measures  on  transport,  agriculture  and  biomass-fuelled  domestic  heating,  the sectors most responsible for the current high levels of pollution.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella action plan with multiple concrete measures beneath it. It qualifies as a parent policy because the subsequent bullets are sub-actions.

parent_statement: Implement the Action Plan for improving air quality through measures on agriculture, mobility, domestic heating, coal phase-out and subsidy reform.
policy_statement: Link rural development funding to ammonia emission reduction and limit burning of plant residues.
source_quote:
 in the framework of future rural development programmes, forms of funding will be linked to  ammonia emissions reduction, in order to guarantee, for the 2021-2027 programming period, an increased use of such measures among farmers, with a concurrent reduction in polluting emissions;
-  amendment of Legislative Decree No 152/2006, which is intended to limit the practice of burning plant residues, also with a view to recovering and utilising those residues.
extraction_rationale: These are concrete agricultural sub-measures under the air quality action plan, including a funding linkage and legislative amendment. They qualify as policies.

parent_statement: Implement the Action Plan for improving air quality through measures on agriculture, mobility, domestic heating, coal phase-out and subsidy reform.
policy_statement: Introduce environmental traffic criteria, strengthen limited traffic zone enforcement, classify hybrids for incentives and trial electric personal mobility devices.
source_quote:
-  proposed amendment of Legislative Decree No 285 of 30 April 1992, designed to introduce environmental criteria for the adoption of traffic reduction provisions, limited to sections of motorway adjacent to urban centres and with particular reference to speed limits;
-  proposed  amendment  of  the  existing  legislation  in  order  to  explicitly  provide  for  the possibility of using devices to monitor limited traffic zones, including within those areas and not only at 'gateway' points;
extraction_rationale: These are specific regulatory transport measures under the action plan. They qualify because they identify concrete legal changes and interventions.

parent_statement: Implement the Action Plan for improving air quality through measures on agriculture, mobility, domestic heating, coal phase-out and subsidy reform.
policy_statement: Condition biomass heater incentives on certified fuels and analyse limits on biomass district heating in polluted areas.
source_quote:
-  Updates  to  the  sectoral  legislation  to  makes  incentives  to  replace  heaters  fuelled  by firewood, briquettes and wood chips conditional upon the certification of such solid biofuels, by the relevant bodies, as complying with the relevant technical standards (ISO UNI EN 17225 parts 3, 4 and 5). Also, compliance with appropriate forms of traceability and environmental sustainability criteria to ensure, energy production being equal, a reduction in the emission of pollutants and carbon dioxide;
-  Analysis  of  potential  limits  to  the  use  of  biomass  for  district  heating  plants  in  areas particularly affected by air pollution.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete regulatory and incentive-conditioning measure under the action plan. It qualifies because it specifies standards and a policy review area.

parent_statement: Implement the Action Plan for improving air quality through measures on agriculture, mobility, domestic heating, coal phase-out and subsidy reform.
policy_statement: Accelerate coal phase-out for thermoelectric plants in areas subject to infringement proceedings by closing or transforming them.
source_quote: -  Phase-out of coal, envisaged by 2025 in Italy, with an acceleration for thermoelectric power plants in areas subject to infringement proceedings, by closing or transforming them.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific sub-action under the air quality plan with a named intervention and target facilities. It qualifies as a mitigation policy.

parent_statement: Implement the Action Plan for improving air quality through measures on agriculture, mobility, domestic heating, coal phase-out and subsidy reform.
policy_statement: Cut back environmentally damaging subsidies through an interministerial working group and legislative proposals.
source_quote: -  Cross-cutting measures such as the reduction of environmentally damaging subsidies. In this context, and with reference to the planned phase-out of coal, the Budget Law for 2020 revises and increases the levies on energy products used to produce electricity. The sole aim of this measure is to introduce specific rates of excise duties determined on the basis of levels of emissions of greenhouse gases and fine particles.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete fiscal reform measure under the action plan. It qualifies because it identifies a specific tax instrument linked to emissions.

policy_statement: Implement Law No 141 of 12 December 2019 (Climate Decree) strategic measures.
source_quote: The Decree identifies actions in the sustainable mobility and reforestation sectors, setting up special funds to provide the resources necessary to implement them. The measures identified include the following.
extraction_rationale: This is a parent because the decree is followed by a list of specific funded measures. It qualifies as an umbrella policy package.

parent_statement: Implement Law No 141 of 12 December 2019 (Climate Decree) strategic measures.
policy_statement: Fund the Experimental Mobility Voucher Programme with €5 million in 2019, €70 million in 2020 and 2021, €55 million in 2022, €45 million in 2023 and €10 million in 2024.
source_quote: -  Incentives  for  sustainable  mobility  in  metropolitan  areas,  setting  up  a  special  fund called the 'Experimental Mobility Voucher Programme', with an allocation of €5 million for 2019, €70 million for 2020, €70 million for 2021, €55 million for 2022, €45 million for 2023 and €10 million for 2024.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear funded programme with explicit annual allocations. It strongly qualifies as a financial instrument.

parent_statement: Implement Law No 141 of 12 December 2019 (Climate Decree) strategic measures.
policy_statement: Provide mobility vouchers of €1,500 per scrapped passenger vehicle and €500 per scrapped motorcycle for public transport subscriptions or bicycles.
source_quote: -  establishing,  within  the  above-mentioned  spending  limits  and  until  resources  have been used up, a 'Mobility Voucher' of €1,500 per passenger vehicle and €500 per motorcycle scrapped. The voucher is to be used, within the following three years, to buy season tickets for local and regional public transport or bicycles, including e-bikes;
extraction_rationale: This is a specific subsidy instrument with quantified voucher values and eligible uses. It clearly qualifies as a policy.

parent_statement: Implement Law No 141 of 12 December 2019 (Climate Decree) strategic measures.
policy_statement: Allocate €20 million in 2020 and €20 million in 2021 for reserved lanes for local public transport.
source_quote: -  funding  for  projects  creating,  extending,  modernising  or  bringing  up  to  standard preferential  lanes for  local  public  transport  9LPT),  with  an  allocation  of  €20 million  to  be authorised for each of the years 2020 and 2021;
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete budget appropriation for transport infrastructure. It qualifies as a financial instrument.

parent_statement: Implement Law No 141 of 12 December 2019 (Climate Decree) strategic measures.
policy_statement: Allocate €10 million in 2020 and €10 million in 2021 for sustainable school transport using hybrid or electric vehicles.
source_quote: -  introducing  measures  to  promote  'Sustainable  school  transport',  with  €10 million earmarked for each of the years 2020 and 2021 to fund experimental programmes to set up and run a school transport service for children attending state and municipal infant schools and for pupils in their first cycle of state school, using hybrid or electric means of transport, selected by the Ministry of the Environment on the basis of the number of students involved and the estimated reduction in air pollution;
extraction_rationale: This is a funded programme with explicit amounts, timeframe and eligible intervention. It clearly qualifies.

parent_statement: Implement Law No 141 of 12 December 2019 (Climate Decree) strategic measures.
policy_statement: Allocate €15 million in 2020 and €15 million in 2021 for urban and suburban tree planting, replanting and forestry.
source_quote: -  reforestation measures, with a grant of €15 million for each of the years 2020 and 2021 for an experimental programme for tree planting, replanting and forestry and the creation of urban and suburban forests in metropolitan cities;
extraction_rationale: This is a funded urban forestry programme with explicit annual allocations. It clearly qualifies and is nature-based.

parent_statement: Implement Law No 141 of 12 December 2019 (Climate Decree) strategic measures.
policy_statement: Support businesses in Economic Environmental Zones within national parks for emissions reduction, renewables and energy efficiency.
source_quote: -  establishing Economic Environmental Zones (ZEAs) in areas within national parks. In such areas forms of support can be set up, in compliance with EU rules on State aid, for new and existing businesses that launch a programme of economic or investment activity aimed in  particular  at  reducing  greenhouse gas emissions and promoting renewable energy and energy efficiency.
extraction_rationale: This is a place-based support policy with explicit climate objectives and business eligibility. It qualifies as a financial instrument because it creates support mechanisms.

parent_statement: Implement Law No 141 of 12 December 2019 (Climate Decree) strategic measures.
policy_statement: Create a fund with at least €150 million annually in 2020-2022 for emissions reduction, renewables, efficiency, deforestation prevention, CO2 capture and sustainable mobility.
extraction_rationale: This is a major budget appropriation with explicit climate earmarking. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

parent_statement: Implement Law No 141 of 12 December 2019 (Climate Decree) strategic measures.
policy_statement: Finance projects of the city awarded the title 'Green Capital of Italy' up to €3 million.
source_quote: -  Setting  up the  'Green  Italy'  programme  to  encourage  initiatives  for  the  sustainable management of Italian cities and the spreading of good practices. To this end, each provincial capital can submit to the Ministry of the Environment and Protection of Natural Resources and the Sea an application detailing projects to increase urban sustainability, improve air quality and public health, and promote sustainable mobility and the circular economy, on which work could be started at once. The projects included in the bid dossier of the city awarded the title 'Green Capital of Italy' are financed by the Ministry of the Environment and Protection of Natural Resources and the Sea in the year in which the award us made, with a ceiling of €3 million.
extraction_rationale: This is a funded competitive programme with a clear cap and eligible project types. It qualifies as a policy and financial instrument.

parent_statement: Implement Law No 141 of 12 December 2019 (Climate Decree) strategic measures.
policy_statement: Transform CIPE into CIPESS to integrate sustainability criteria into economic planning.
source_quote: -  Planned  transformation  of  the  current  Interministerial  Committee  for  Economic Planning (CIPE) into the Interministerial Committee for Sustainable Development (CIPESS), within a year and a half. One aim is to carry out, in line with the Green New Deal, an extensive revision of the structure of State economic planning.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete institutional reform with a timeframe and sustainability objective. It qualifies as a policy commitment.

policy_statement: Electricity sector renewable energy measures.
source_quote:
The list  of  principal  measures  aimed  at  realising  objectives  relating  to renewable  energy, divided into the electricity, heating and transport sectors, is set out below.

## Electricity sector
extraction_rationale: This is a parent because the electricity sector subsection contains multiple distinct policy measures. It serves as the umbrella for the listed sub-actions.

parent_statement: Electricity sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Maintain tariff and system charge rules that favour instantaneous self-consumption and assess direct support for collective self-consumption.
source_quote: The  rules  governing  the  collection  of  general  system  charges  and  electricity  tariffs, introduced in 2018 as part of the plan for adaptation to EU guidelines on State aid for energy and  the  environment,  provide,  in  themselves,  a  regulatory  framework  that  favours instantaneous self-consumption. The collection tariff structure provides for the application of  variable  proportions of the tariff  (€/MWh) to  energy taken  from public  networks.  For collective self-consumption, especially in cases where the use of existing public networks is preferred, the possibility of introducing direct forms of support is currently being examined.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete regulatory and potential support measure for self-consumption. It qualifies because it identifies an existing framework and a contemplated direct support mechanism.

parent_statement: Electricity sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Develop net metering to reward self-consumption, storage and provision of system services.
source_quote: Work will also be carried out on development of the net metering mechanism (which enables the use of the network as a storage system), to promote rewards for plants on the basis of their quota of self-consumed energy, which can also be increased by installing accumulation systems, and for plants which go on to provide services to ensure the safety of the electricity system on medium- and low-voltage networks.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific reform of a named mechanism with clear intended incentives. It qualifies as a policy and financial instrument.

parent_statement: Electricity sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Reinforce and gradually extend minimum renewable energy obligations in buildings, including some categories of existing buildings.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear regulatory obligation with a defined extension pathway. It qualifies because it specifies the intervention and affected building categories.

parent_statement: Electricity sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Introduce simplified and harmonised procedures for constructing, connecting and operating renewable plants and small storage systems.
source_quote: - -To introduce simplified and homogeneous  procedures  for  the construction, commissioning and management of plants, including expanding the scope of the uniform model, currently operative for certain photovoltaic installations with power up to 20 kW: it involves  a  mechanism  which  allows,  with  a  single  procedure,  management  of  features relating  to  authorisation,  network  connection  and  accessing  support  mechanisms.  These procedures, aimed both at new RES plants and at the reconstruction of existing ones, can also be extended to small-scale storage systems, as well as plants connected to existing points of delivery (PODs) whose contracted demand is greater than the power of the plant.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete administrative reform with a named mechanism and scope. It clearly qualifies as a policy.

parent_statement: Electricity sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Extend the Simplified Authorisation Procedure to more renewable installations.
source_quote: - -In line with the outcome of the public consultation, there are plans to extend the use of the Simplified Authorisation Procedure (SAP), which today can be used for individual plants with power between a few dozen and several hundreds of kW;
extraction_rationale: This is a specific procedural reform commitment. It qualifies because it names the instrument and intended expansion.

parent_statement: Electricity sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Promote photovoltaic installations on agricultural structures not classified as buildings.
source_quote: - -To promote the installation of photovoltaic plants in existing agricultural structures that do not fall within the definition of a building, including by introducing the concept of 'rural building' to facilitate access to support measures.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific siting and definitional reform to enable PV deployment. It qualifies because it names the intervention and enabling legal concept.

parent_statement: Electricity sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Allow aggregation of small renewable plants to access incentive procedures.
source_quote: - -to  permit  the  aggregation  of  small-scale  energy  plants  to  enable  participation  in procedures  for  accessing  incentives  for  energy  delivered  to  the  grid  (see  the  section  on contracts for difference);
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete regulatory change linked to incentive access. It qualifies because it specifies the intervention and purpose.

parent_statement: Electricity sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Establish specific incentive tariffs for certain small plants where self-consumption is not viable.
source_quote: - -establish  specific  incentivising  tariffs,  for  cases  in  which  self-consumption  is  not viable, and provided that there is significant accessible potential and prospects for containing costs and the incentives themselves; combined heat and power generation from waste and residues from the Agri-industrial sector is of interest, in particular by means of plants forming part of the production cycle of companies.
extraction_rationale: This is a direct financial support commitment with a named instrument—specific incentivising tariffs. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

parent_statement: Electricity sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Reward photovoltaic plants that replace asbestos roofing.
source_quote: - -introduce rewards for construction of photovoltaic plants where the modules are installed as replacements for roofing containing asbestos.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific incentive measure with a named eligibility condition. It qualifies as a policy and financial instrument.

parent_statement: Electricity sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Promote renewable energy communities through direct support for production and locally consumed energy, with privileged access to support mechanisms.
source_quote: Renewable energy communities  will be promoted in economic terms by means of direct support  mechanisms  for  production,  including  by  more  than  one  plant  (similarly  to  the general production support mechanisms) and for locally consumed energy. The benefits to be reaped in terms of network use in this last case will be taken into account, with due regard to the rights and obligations of the members of the community as customers. These set-ups will have privileged access to support mechanisms.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear support policy for renewable energy communities with explicit preferential access. It qualifies as a financial instrument.

parent_statement: Electricity sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Use competitive tenders and contracts for difference as the main tool to support large renewable plants.
source_quote: We will continue to employ the mechanisms of competitive tender, which have already been trialled, adopting a neutral approach among groups of technologies with similar structure and levels of cost, possibly with safeguarding mechanisms where technologies deemed necessary to reach targets in any event are repeatedly unsuccessful, it being understood that one of the aims of this mechanism is to support market parity. The tenders will be for the purpose of entering into contracts for difference based on the overall value of the recognised tariff once the procedure has been carried out, according to the 'two way' criteria
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete support mechanism for large-scale renewables. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument and a core mitigation policy.

parent_statement: Electricity sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Implement Ministerial Decree of 4 July 2019 (RES1) to incentivise almost 8 GW of renewable plants through six rounds up to 2021.
source_quote: In  line  with  those  intentions,  in  2019  Ministerial  Decree  4/7/2019  (RES1)  was  published, providing an incentive for almost 8GW (of which 7.4GW new) for renewable energy plants with a high level of technological maturity. The quotas are allocated by means of competitive procedures (tenders and registers, depending on the size) in six rounds up until 2021.
extraction_rationale: This is a highly concrete support measure with quantified capacity and implementation rounds. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

parent_statement: Electricity sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Create a market platform for long-term power purchase agreements under the Ministerial Decree of 4 July 2019.
source_quote: The Ministerial Decree of 4 July 2019 provides that a regulatory framework for the creation of a market platform for long-term trading be set up within 180 days of its entry into force. For this purpose, a study has already been launched with the aim of investigating the legal, regulatory and technical framework surrounding widespread use of PPAs.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete regulatory and market-design commitment with a deadline. It qualifies because it establishes a specific platform and implementation timeframe.

parent_statement: Electricity sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Share renewable objectives with Regions and identify suitable and unsuitable areas for renewable plants.
source_quote:
The renewables targets, especially in the electricity sector, will be met chiefly through wind and  photovoltaic  energy.  Adequate  land  surface  will  therefore  be  needed.  While  in  the photovoltaic sector existing buildings and compromised areas not suitable for other uses will

be exploited, national objectives will be shared and agreed with the Regions under a national regulatory framework.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete planning and governance measure for siting renewable plants. It qualifies because it commits to a national-regional framework and area identification.

parent_statement: Electricity sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Support innovative renewable technologies through RES2 and other tailored support instruments.
source_quote: In this context a provision to support these technologies (RES2) is being drafted. This will complete the work of the support measures already activated before the new Renewable Energy Directive was implemented, and will incentivise, by means of the usual auction (plants with power above 1 MW) and register mechanisms (plants with power below 1 MW), sources and  technologies  not  covered  by  Ministerial  Decree  RES1.
extraction_rationale: This is a named support measure under preparation for innovative technologies. It qualifies because it specifies the support mechanisms and scope.

parent_statement: Electricity sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Promote energy reconversion of decommissioned hydrocarbon platforms for marine renewable energy projects.
source_quote: In addition, in the context of the decommissioning of platforms and connected infrastructures already used for production from hydrocarbon reserves that are depleted, almost depleted or in any case unusable, innovative energy reconversion projects will be promoted. These  include  energy  production  plants  fuelled  by  available  marine  resources (Ministerial  Decree  of  15 February 2019  -  national  guidelines on the decommissioning  of platforms for producing hydrocarbons at sea and connected infrastructure).
extraction_rationale: This is a specific project-based intervention for reusing hydrocarbon infrastructure. It qualifies because it names the intervention and legal basis.

parent_statement: Electricity sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Implement the Ministerial Decree of 14 July 2017 for small islands with renewable targets and specific incentives.
source_quote: Italy has already started a process for the gradual coverage of the requirements of smaller islands not interlinked with energy from renewable sources. In this context, the Ministerial Decree of 14 July 2017 sets out specific targets for covering consumption with renewable energy sources, available locally for each island. It establishes specific incentives, the scope of which is defined by ARERA Decision No 558 of 6 November 2018 and is proportionate to the avoided fuel cost.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete island-specific renewable policy with targets and incentives. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

parent_statement: Electricity sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Simplify procedures and environmental assessments for revamping and repowering existing renewable installations.
source_quote:
Notwithstanding the contents of the previous section in relation to hydroelectric concessions, the specific measures of a non-economic nature for revamping and repowering existing installations include the following.

- -SAPs, setting criteria that enable actions to be taken to extend them and exclude or simplify  EIA/environmental  screening.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete procedural reform for existing renewable assets. It qualifies because it specifies the intervention and administrative mechanism.

parent_statement: Electricity sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Promote reconversion of certain renewable plants, including biogas plants to biomethane.
source_quote: - -Promoting the reconversion of some types of plant which, at the end of the incentives period, should in theory no longer be competitive on the market, into plants that better meet the  needs  of  the  system  in  its  energy  transition  journey.  This  includes,  for  example,  the reconversion  of  biogas  plants  to  biomethane,  already  provided  for  in  the  existing  legal framework.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific intervention for plant reconversion. It qualifies because it names the technology and transition purpose.

parent_statement: Electricity sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Support small agricultural biogas plants after incentives end, including through the 2020 Budget Law.
source_quote: For these, especially those in the agricultural sector, forms of support will be promoted that are  efficient  and  compatible  with  EU  rules  on  State  aid,  with  a  view  to  safeguarding production. The biogas plants in question must also be able to make efficient use of livestock manure, for the purposes of a well-functioning circular economy To that end, the Budget Law for  2020  envisages  the  right  to  use  an  incentive  on  electricity  produced.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific support commitment for a defined plant category and legal basis. It qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Transport sector renewable energy measures.
source_quote:
## Transport sector

For  the  purposes  of  reaching  the  targets  in  relation  to  penetration  of  renewables  in  the transport sector, the following measures have been identified.
extraction_rationale: This is a parent because the transport subsection introduces a list of specific measures. It qualifies as an umbrella policy package.

parent_statement: Transport sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Maintain mandatory biofuel release for consumption up to 2022 using a quota system with bonuses for advanced biofuels and waste-based fuels.
source_quote:
##  Mandatory biofuel mixing rate, up to 2022

Mandatory release of biofuels for consumption, based on a share system in which, inter alia , a bonus is recognised for advanced biofuels and biofuels from waste oils and animal fats.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear regulatory obligation with a defined period and mechanism. It qualifies as a policy.

parent_statement: Transport sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Require fuel suppliers to achieve a 6% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions from fuels by 2020.
source_quote:
##  Reduction of GHG emissions from fuels by 6% by 2020

In 2020, fuel suppliers will have to meet a savings target, in terms of GHG emissions in the total fuels released for consumption in that year, in relation to a reference value.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified regulatory target imposed on suppliers. It clearly qualifies as a policy.

parent_statement: Transport sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Incentivise biomethane and advanced biofuels through certificates of release for consumption over ten years.
source_quote:
##  Incentives to meet the biofuel emissions quota using biomethane and other advanced biofuels: 2018-2022

Incentives to use biomethane and advanced biofuels for the purposes of meeting the existing obligation to mix fossil fuels with biofuels, through a system of collecting the biomethane produced, with issuing of certificates of release for consumption for a duration of ten years.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific incentive mechanism with a defined duration and instrument. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

parent_statement: Transport sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Transpose RED II and update mandatory quotas for normal and advanced biofuels up to 2030.
source_quote:
##  Obligation to use biofuels and other renewables in transposing RED II: 2022-2030

The drafting and issuing of an Italian Legislative Decree transposing RED II and subsequent interministerial decrees updating the decrees currently in force in the sector are planned. The  main  objectives  are:  updating  the  mandatory  quotas  for  release  for  consumption  of normal and advanced biofuels up to 2030;
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete legislative transposition commitment with a defined period and objective. It qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Heating sector renewable energy measures.
source_quote:
## Heating sector
