In  order  to  meet  the  mandatory  national  target  in  relation  to  renewable  energy,  the contribution of the heating sector is fundamental.
extraction_rationale: This is a parent because the heating subsection introduces multiple specific measures and instruments. It qualifies as an umbrella policy package.

parent_statement: Heating sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Continue tax deductions for energy-efficient retrofitting and restoration of buildings to support thermal renewables.
source_quote:
##  Tax deductions for energy-efficient retrofitting and restoration of existing buildings

Tax deductions for energy-efficient retrofitting of buildings are currently in place and have played a vital role in the development of energy efficiency and of thermal renewable energy sources in the housing sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a named fiscal support mechanism already in place and explicitly linked to thermal renewables. It qualifies as a financial instrument.

parent_statement: Heating sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Use the Conto Termico to incentivise renewable heat technologies such as heat pumps, biomass boilers, solar thermal and hybrid systems.
source_quote:
In relation to production of heat from renewable sources, one or more interventions, listed below, carried out by public authorities and by private individuals, are incentivised:

- -replacement  of  existing  winter  heating  systems  with  winter  heating  systems, including combined systems for producing domestic hot water, equipped with electric or gas heat  pumps,  using  aerothermal,  geothermal  or  hydrothermal  energy,  along  with  the installation of heat metering systems in the case of installations with useful thermal output greater than 200kW;
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete incentive programme with named eligible technologies. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

parent_statement: Heating sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Use White Certificates to support renewable heat and high-efficiency cogeneration.
source_quote:
White certificates  are  tradeable  assets  which  certify  that  a  reduction  of  end  -use  energy consumption has been attained as a result of interventions and projects to increase energy efficiency.

As part of this scheme, the development of projects that provide for use of renewable sources for  non-electric  uses  is  also  encouraged,  in  relation  to  their  capacity  to  increase  energy efficiency and to permit savings of non-renewable energy.
extraction_rationale: This is a named market-based support mechanism with explicit application to renewable heat. It qualifies as a financial instrument.

parent_statement: Heating sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Maintain and update mandatory renewable energy integration requirements for new and majorly renovated buildings.
source_quote:
The  requirements  are  currently  fixed  in  terms  of  percentages  (increasing  per  year)  of coverage with renewable energy sources of the building's energy requirement for providing heating, cooling and domestic hot water services.

In particular, it is envisaged that in the case of new buildings or buildings subject to major renovation,  installations  for  the  production  of  thermal  energy  have  to  be  designed  and created  so  as  to  guarantee  compliance  with  coverage,  with  energy  produced  from installations powered by renewable sources, of 50% of expected consumers of domestic hot water
extraction_rationale: This is a binding regulatory obligation with explicit percentages and building scope. It clearly qualifies as a policy.

parent_statement: Heating sector renewable energy measures.
policy_statement: Provide municipal contributions for energy efficiency, renewable installations and sustainable local development.
source_quote: Decree-Law No 34 of 30 April 2019 (the Growth Decree-Law) established a contribution for municipalities, up to a maximum of €500 million for 2019, drawn from the Development and Cohesion Fund (FSC), to be channelled into investment in energy efficiency and sustainable local  development. The contribution is allocated to each  municipality on the basis of the resident population as at 1 January 2018, as follows:
extraction_rationale: This is a clear budgetary support measure with a total amount and allocation basis. It qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Continue and reform the White Certificates scheme to simplify it and improve recognition of energy savings.
source_quote: The process for updating and reinforcing the White Certificates will be continued with a view to simplifying the scheme and optimising the methodologies for quantifying and recognising energy  savings,  and  reducing  the  time  frames  for  approval,  issuance  and  supply  of certificates on the market. These aspects, which also came up in the public consultation, are fundamental for the effective continuation of the measure in 2020-2030.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete continuation and reform commitment for a named instrument. It qualifies as a policy and financial instrument.

policy_statement: Maintain and integrate tax deductions for building energy retrofits, seismic upgrades and renovations into a single mechanism.
source_quote:
A  tax  deduction  scheme  for  the  energy-efficient  retrofitting  and  restoration  of  existing buildings, to run for three years, is currently being assessed.

In order to strengthen the measure, maximise results and optimise resources, the plan is to integrate the Ecobonus, Sismabonus and Bonus Casa schemes into a single mechanism.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete fiscal reform and continuation of an existing support mechanism. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Create a dedicated section of the National Energy Efficiency Fund to guarantee loans for private building retrofits.
source_quote: Lastly, pursuant to Article 1(3)(a) of the Budget Law for 2018, an implementing provision is being drafted for the creation of a specific segment in the National Energy Efficiency Fund for providing guarantees to credit institutions that issue loans to private persons or jointowners of housing blocks for the purpose of improving the energy efficiency of their part of, or the whole, building, in synergy with the tax schemes described.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific financial support mechanism involving guarantees for retrofit loans. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Refocus the Conto Termico on non-residential public and private tertiary buildings and simplify access for public bodies.
source_quote: As the results of the public consultation showed, to avoid fragmentation and overlapping of instruments for promoting energy efficiency, the plan is to focus the Conto Termico scheme on energy-efficient retrofitting and restoration of non-residential buildings, in the public and private  tertiary  sector.  The  intention  is  to  continue  the  task  of  simplifying  access  to  the scheme for public bodies, also through promotion of the ESCo model and the use of energy performance contracts (EPCs).
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete reform of a named incentive scheme with a defined sectoral focus. It qualifies as a policy and financial instrument.

policy_statement: Increase the National Fund for Energy Efficiency and direct it more toward buildings and transport.
source_quote: In  order  to  increase  the  capacity  of  the  Fund  to  promote  energy-efficient  measures, the financial allocation currently available will be increased, favouring the payment of resources dedicated to energy efficiency managed by central and local public bodies (structural funds, European investment funds) and directing the scheme towards the promotion of measures in the civil sector (both the housing and tertiary sectors) and the transport sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear funding and targeting commitment for a named fund. It qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Continue PREPAC funding and simplify procedures for central government building efficiency upgrades.
source_quote: Funding for the measure will cover 2021-2030 and updating and strengthening measures will be implemented in order to simplify administrative procedures. The aim is to draw on the synergies between the public bodies involved in managing the scheme and enable adequate management IT support to be developed.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete continuation and administrative strengthening of a named programme. It qualifies as a policy and financial instrument.

policy_statement: Continue information and training programmes on energy efficiency through 2030 and assess a new programme.
source_quote: From 2021 to 2030 more importance will be placed on information-sharing and training activities, and the launch of a potential new programme based on experience gained as a result of the one coming to a close will be assessed. The theme of monitoring the savings generated  by  awareness-raising  programmes  will  be  explored,  with  a  view  to  offering evermore robust support to decision-making in that area, as well as to meeting the energy efficiency targets.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete continuation commitment for a named policy tool. It qualifies because it specifies the activity and period.

policy_statement: Accelerate mandatory procurement of alternative-fuel public vehicles to 30% by 2022, 50% by 2025 and 85% by 2030.
source_quote: It  is proposed to accelerate the provisions set out in paragraph 10 of  Article 18 of Italian Legislative Decree 257/2016 (transposition of the DAFI directive) stipulating that the public administration, the Regions, local bodies and providers of public utilities for activities carried out  in  the  provinces  with  high  levels  of  PM10  particle  pollution,  when  replacing  their respective fleets of cars, buses and public utility vehicles, including those for collecting urban waste, must ensure that 30% by 2022, at least 50% by 2025 and 85% by 2030 of new vehicles purchased are electric vehicles and hybrid vehicles with off-vehicle charging, powered by methane and hydrogen, and electricity and methane in the case of buses.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified procurement mandate with deadlines and vehicle categories. It clearly qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Relaunch and strengthen Marebonus and Ferrobonus for 2021-2030 to support modal shift in freight transport.
source_quote: Marebonus and Ferrobonus are fundamental measures for improving energy efficiency in the transport sector, because the modal shift is a highly effective measure in terms of the cost  to  benefit  ratio.  It  will  therefore  be  important  to  relaunch  them  for  2021-2030,  to update and reinforce them on the basis of experience gained, and to monitor the resulting energy savings more effectively.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear continuation and strengthening commitment for named incentive schemes. It qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Continue and update the National Plan for Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure (PNIRE).
source_quote:
The PNIRE is currently being updated using an integrated approach that takes into account other measures for sustaining demand for electric vehicles and increasing the usability of the infrastructure.

The possibility of coordinating the development of recharging infrastructure with plans to rationalise fuel networks is also being explored.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete planning update for a named national plan. It qualifies because it commits to updating the plan and coordinating infrastructure development.

policy_statement: Provide subsidies for low-emission passenger vehicles and impose a tax on high-emission vehicles from March 2019 to December 2021.
source_quote: The first measures in this regard have already been introduced, having effect from March 2019 to December 2021, and consist of the granting of subsidy to those who purchase a vehicle with CO2 emissions lower than 70 g/km and an official  price  lower  than  €50,000.  The  subsidy is  differentiated  depending  upon  emission class (0-20 g/km and 21-70 g/km) and depending on whether the purchaser is at the same time scrapping a vehicle type approved in the Euro 1 to Euro 4 classes or not, and is between €1,500 and €6,000.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete fiscal incentive with quantified thresholds and subsidy amounts. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Make SUMPs mandatory by 2021 for metropolitan cities, large municipalities and polluted cities, and by 2025 for municipalities over 50,000 inhabitants.
source_quote: For all metropolitan cities, bodies covering extensive areas, municipalities with more than 100,000 inhabitants and for cities with high levels of PM10 and/or nitrogen dioxide pollution (also with a population of fewer than 100,000 inhabitants), it will be mandatory to prepare a  SUMP  (no  longer  linked  to  mere  provision  of  funding)  by  2021,  providing  also  that municipalities with a population of more than 50,000 inhabitants, using simplified guidelines, will have to prepare a SUMP as a mandatory requirement for access to funding by 2025.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear planning mandate with thresholds and deadlines. It qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Update the Emergency Plan for the Italian natural gas system and coordinate it with other countries' emergency plans.
source_quote:
##  Update of the Emergency Plan for the Italian natural gas system, in coordination with the  Emergency  Plans  of  the  other  Countries  connected  to  the  same  supply  corridors covered by Regulation (EU) 1938/2017

Update of Annex II to the Ministerial Decree of 18 October 2017.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete regulatory update with a named legal instrument and coordination requirement. It qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Update the Preventive Action Plan for the Italian natural gas system under Regulation (EU) 2017/1938.
source_quote:
##  Revision of the Preventive Action Plan for the Italian natural gas system, in accordance with the new Security Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2017/1938)

Update of Annex I to the Ministerial Decree of 18 October 2017.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete planning update under a named EU regulation. It qualifies as a policy commitment.

policy_statement: Increase LNG use and diversify gas supplies to support security and maritime fuel transition.
source_quote: Given the increased uncertainty and the possible critical issues - which have all occurred in the past but never all at the same time - arising from disruptions to gas pipeline supplies, Italy  is  actively  pursuing  a  strategy  for  diversifying  and  increasing  LNG  supplies  (which currently cover around 9% of national gas requirements), with the aim of also supporting the measure of gradually introducing a limit of 0.1% of sulphur content in fuels used by ships at berth in ports and passenger vessels (Sulphur Emission Control Areas) and guaranteeing the presence of more spot supply sources able to compete for the position of marginal source, keeping in line with European prices.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete supply diversification strategy with a named fuel and linked maritime objective. It qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Implement the capacity market through annual auctions to secure adequate low-emission capacity.
source_quote: The measure, (Ministerial Decree of 28 June 2019) initially approved by the EC in 2018 and then in 2019 in its revised version with new emissions limits for participating plants, provides for  annual  auctions  to  be  introduced  by  Terna,  open  to  all  technologies  capable  of contributing to the adaptation objective, in order to supply resources, including those from outside Italy, to cover the requirement expressed by Terna, which is based on a long-term assessment that is updated every year.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete market mechanism established by decree and implemented through annual auctions. It qualifies as a financial instrument because it remunerates capacity.

policy_statement: Update permits for thermoelectric plants and streamline procedures for minor modifications and temporary maintenance.
source_quote:
##  Adapting the rules governing the permits granted to thermoelectric power plants

Updating  the  rules governing  the permits granted  to  thermoelectric power  plants, streamlining the procedure in the event of minor modifications being made to existing plants in order to make the system more flexible, as well as governing any possible stages (maximum time frames and methods) of temporary maintenance, incorporating the current stages of permanently shutting down and decommissioning the plant.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete regulatory reform for plant permitting. It qualifies because it specifies the intervention and intended flexibility outcome.

policy_statement: Develop the intraday market with continuous trading close to real time.
source_quote:
##  Developing continuous trading in the intraday market

As part of the changes to the operational structure of the intraday market (IM), and also to enforce the provisions set out under EU law, a procedure for allowing market operators to submit  offers  up  to  one  hour  before  the  market  closes,  through  continuous  trading procedures, will be implemented.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete market reform with a named procedural change. It qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Introduce negative prices in Italian electricity markets and suspend incentives during negative-price hours.
source_quote:
Italy plans to remove the floor, thus allowing negative price bids on the day-ahead and intraday markets.

Nevertheless, account must be taken of the supply of subsidised generation and the potential market  power  this  implies,  given  that  these  aspects  could  attenuate  or  even  nullify  the beneficial effects of introducing negative prices.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete market design reform. It qualifies because it commits to removing the price floor and changing incentive treatment.

policy_statement: Complete liberalisation of the retail electricity market by ending regulated price plans and strengthening consumer protections.
source_quote: The  process  for  liberalising  the  retail  market  by  1 January 2020  will  be  completed  by identifying the measures instrumental in scrapping the regulated price plans for household customers and small businesses,  in  accordance with  criteria  for  promoting  a  competitive retail market structure. The initiatives will be put in place in coordination with the natural gas sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete market reform commitment with a date and implementation objective. Climate relevance is peripheral, but it qualifies as an energy policy.

policy_statement: Require all electricity suppliers to be registered and meet technical, financial and reputational requirements.
source_quote: - register  of  suppliers:  in  order  to  do  business  all  vendors  of  electricity  will  have  to  be registered on the list of electricity vendors. This will be established by Decree of the Ministry of Economic Development, as provided for in Law No 124/2017 (Article 1(80)-(81)). To be added to and to stay on the register, suppliers will have to comply with specific criteria and procedures  and  meet  technical,  financial  and  reputational  requirements,  which  will  be published and updated on the Ministry of Economic Development's website.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear regulatory requirement for market participation. It qualifies as a policy due to its binding mechanism.

policy_statement: Deploy second-generation smart electricity meters nationwide, with large-scale replacement completed by 2026.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete rollout commitment with deadlines and coverage targets. It qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Complete the transition to smart gas metering according to staged deadlines by distributor size.
source_quote:
In the gas sector the transition to  smart  metering  (Resolution  No 669/2018/R/GAS),  which  makes  solutions  with  better functionalities where the cost differential is kept to a minimum or in any case lower than the expected benefits possible as of now, is expected to be completed according to the following time scale:

-  for  distribution  companies  with  more  than  200,000  end-customers,  85%  in  service  by 31 December 2020;
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete rollout schedule with quantified thresholds and deadlines. It qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Set up a National Observatory of Energy Poverty in 2020.
source_quote: As regards the first measure, in order to better coordinate existing efforts, and given also the fragmented nature of skills and resources, an Observatory of Energy Poverty is scheduled to be set up by the Ministry of Economic Development at the beginning of 2020. Although the Observatory will be coordinated by GSE at operational level, various entities and institutions will be called upon to take part.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete institutional commitment with a start date and named body. It qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Replace electricity and gas social bonuses with a new energy social bonus adjusted by ISEE and household size.
source_quote: This will involve replacing the current electricity and gas social bonuses with a new 'energy social  bonus',  and  adjusting  the  benefit  on  the  basis  of  the  Equivalent  Economic  Status Indicator and the number of household members; the benefit will be, at most, equivalent to three months' energy costs (these consisting of both electricity and heating costs) - ideal for covering heating costs (during the winter) or air-conditioning costs (during the summer).
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete redesign of an existing subsidy instrument with a defined benefit basis. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Create an 'energy income' revolving fund to cover 100% of investment costs for domestic photovoltaic installations up to 20 kW.
source_quote: As for subsidies for households on low incomes (point 3), a provision entitled 'energy income' is being created. This involves setting up a rotation fund for granting capital contributions covering 100% of the cost of investment in photovoltaic installations for domestic use (up to 20 KW).
extraction_rationale: This is a clear revolving fund and capital contribution mechanism with explicit coverage and size limit. It strongly qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Launch a large-scale programme to improve the energy efficiency of social housing.
source_quote: The measure referred to in point 4 involves exploring the option of launching a large-scale programme for making social housing more energy efficient. Such an initiative would pursue a variety of objectives at the same time: making the use of energy resources taken up by the residential sector more efficient (thus having positive effects on both comfort and emission levels), bringing down energy bills for the most vulnerable families who will be using this service,  and  increasing  the  value  of  the  public  housing  assets.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete programme proposal with a defined target stock and intervention type. It qualifies despite some exploratory wording because the intervention is specific and central to the section.

policy_statement: Allow public housing managers and Regions to use net metering across public housing to cover their own and residents' consumption.
source_quote: To incentivise the use of electricity produced using renewable sources and provide support to disadvantaged sections of the population, the Budget Law for 2020 allows instrumental or non-instrumental  public  bodies  and  Regions  that  manage  subsidised,  residential  public housing to use, under given conditions, the mechanism of net metering of the electricity produced  by  the  plants  they  own,  with  no  power  limit  applied,  to  cover  their  own consumption and that of the residents of the public housing.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete regulatory support measure for public housing renewable electricity use. It qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Grant automatic access from 1 January 2021 to social bonuses for electricity, gas and water for eligible low-ISEE households.
source_quote: Decree-Law No 124 of 2019, converted into Law No 157 of 19 December 2019 (Tax Law for 2020) provides that from 1 January 2021, persons whose ISEE score is  within predefined limits will have automatic access to the social bonus for electricity, natural gas and integrated water supply.
extraction_rationale: This is a dated and concrete entitlement reform for social bonuses. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Research and innovation objectives for the energy transition.
extraction_rationale: This is a parent because it introduces two numbered objective areas followed by detailed sub-items. It qualifies as an umbrella research policy framework.

parent_statement: Research and innovation objectives for the energy transition.
policy_statement: Develop highly efficient photovoltaic components and systems.
source_quote:
## Goal  1)  monitor  and  develop  product  and  process  technologies  vital  to  the  energy transition:

- -development of components and systems for highly efficient photovoltaics, which allows  better  exploitation  of  occupied  areas  and  provides  opportunities  for  new entrepreneurship;
extraction_rationale: This is a specific R&D action under the numbered objective list. It qualifies because it names a concrete technology development area.

parent_statement: Research and innovation objectives for the energy transition.
policy_statement: Develop storage systems including thermal, electrochemical and power-to-gas.
source_quote: - -development of storage systems, including thermal, electrochemical and power-togas, and related interfaces with the networks, in order to guarantee high levels of penetration for non-programmable renewables;
extraction_rationale: This is a specific R&D commitment with named technologies and purpose. It qualifies as a policy action.

parent_statement: Research and innovation objectives for the energy transition.
policy_statement: Develop power-to-gas and hydrogen storage systems for excess renewable electricity.
source_quote: - -development of power-to-gas storage systems, particularly for the purpose of storage of  excess  production  of  non-programmable  renewables  by  means  of  secure  and reliable storage of hydrogen in liquid and gaseous energy carriers;
extraction_rationale: This is a specific technology development commitment. It qualifies because it names the intervention and climate function.

parent_statement: Research and innovation objectives for the energy transition.
policy_statement: Develop technologies, components and materials to improve building energy and environmental performance.
source_quote: - -development of technologies, components and materials to increase energy and environmental performance of buildings;
extraction_rationale: This is a specific R&D action focused on buildings. It qualifies because it names the intervention area.

parent_statement: Research and innovation objectives for the energy transition.
policy_statement: Improve energy efficiency of industrial products and processes, including high- and low-temperature processes.
source_quote: - -improvements  to  the  energy  efficiency  of  industrial  products  and  processes,  in particular  with  the  development  of  techniques  and  plant  solutions  for  boosting efficiency of industrial processes at high and low temperature;
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete R&D objective for industrial efficiency. It qualifies because it specifies the intervention and sector.

parent_statement: Research and innovation objectives for the energy transition.
policy_statement: Research and implement methodologies for energy communities and enabling technologies for consumer awareness.
source_quote: - -study and implementation of methodologies for development of energy communities and  definition  of  enabling  technologies  for  the  promotion  of  energy  efficiency through consumer awareness;
extraction_rationale: This is a specific research and implementation action. It qualifies because it names the intervention and intended outcome.

parent_statement: Research and innovation objectives for the energy transition.
policy_statement: Develop and test storage systems, battery controls and vehicle-to-home devices for electric mobility.
source_quote:
- -in terms of mobility, the trialling and testing of various storage systems, as well as the development  of  innovative  thermal  electronic  and  battery  controls  for  electric vehicles;
- -monitoring for purposes of safety and second-life use, devices for V2H (Vehicle To Home);
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete R&D and testing commitment for electric mobility technologies. It qualifies because it names specific technologies and applications.

parent_statement: Research and innovation objectives for the energy transition.
policy_statement: Study and trial high-power electric recharging infrastructure for local public transport.
source_quote: - -study and trialling of infrastructures for high-power electric recharging for local public transport, including through use of charging solutions incorporated along the route;
extraction_rationale: This is a specific R&D and demonstration action for charging infrastructure. It qualifies as a policy action.

parent_statement: Research and innovation objectives for the energy transition.
policy_statement: Develop technologies to increase electrification of end uses, including heat pumps and non-conventional storage.
source_quote: - -development of technologies for effective penetration of electricity carriers into enduse:  in  particular,  research  activities  will  be concentrated  on  complex  heat  pump systems or linked to non-conventional storage systems; study will also be made of the use of heat pumps at high temperatures in industrial processes in order to recover residual heat;
extraction_rationale: This is a specific technology development commitment. It qualifies because it names the intervention and applications.

parent_statement: Research and innovation objectives for the energy transition.
policy_statement: Develop floating platforms and innovative materials for marine renewable energy.
source_quote: - -as regards renewable energy from the sea, the development of diverse solutions is planned for floating platforms capable of supporting complex sea conditions and the study  of  innovative  materials  for  new  kinds  of  high  resistance  anchoring  and  for coupling these to the floating platforms.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete R&D commitment for marine renewables. It qualifies because it names the technologies and purpose.

parent_statement: Research and innovation objectives for the energy transition.
policy_statement: Develop smart-grid and system models to integrate renewables, self-production, storage, energy communities and aggregators.
source_quote:
## Goal 2) promote the introduction of technologies, organisational and operational models and systems used for the energy transition and for safety:

- -development  of  architectural  and  operational  models  for  the  system  and  for electricity networks which promote the integration of renewable, non-programmable energy production, self-production, storage, energy communities and aggregators, and which take into account electrical penetration;
extraction_rationale: This is a specific systems innovation commitment under Goal 2. It qualifies because it names the models and integration functions.

parent_statement: Research and innovation objectives for the energy transition.
policy_statement: Apply advanced information technologies, IoT and peer-to-peer electricity trading to improve network safety and resilience.
source_quote: - -application of advanced information technologies, the internet of things, peer to peer electricity trading, to improve the safety and resilience of networks;
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete innovation action with explicit resilience objective. It qualifies as a policy action.

parent_statement: Research and innovation objectives for the energy transition.
policy_statement: Create local demonstrators for distributed management and control of electricity networks.
source_quote: - -creation of demonstrators on a local-community level in order to establish innovative methods  of  management  and  control  of  the  electricity  network  by  means  of  a distributed  approach,  with  the aim  of  increasing  energy  efficiency  in  the  cycle  of production, transport and distribution of electricity;
extraction_rationale: This is a specific demonstration commitment with a named objective. It qualifies because it identifies a concrete intervention type.

parent_statement: Research and innovation objectives for the energy transition.
policy_statement: Continue modernising electricity networks toward smart grids.
source_quote: - -continue with the task of modernising electricity networks, including in the shortterm, with a view to smart grids. The increase in distributed generation in fact requires real  transformation  of  the  distribution  networks  and  of  the  related  operational modes,  with  modernisation  both  of  the  hardware  component  (e.g.  to  also  make distribution  networks  also  bi-directional)  and  of  the  software  component  (e.g.  to enable demand response management initiatives).
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete network modernisation commitment with named hardware and software changes. It qualifies as a policy action.

policy_statement: Use the Electric System Research Fund to support research of general interest and industrial research in the energy sector.
source_quote: Financed through a levy placed on electricity tariffs (available resources for the 2015-2017 three-year period equal to €210 million), and having the principal objective of supporting both  research  of  general  interest  (currently  carried  out  by  the  National  Agency  for  New Technologies, Energy and Sustainable Economic Development (ENEA), the National Research Council (CNR) and the energy system research company RSE as part of specific programme agreements),  and  industrial  research.
extraction_rationale: This is a named fund with a stated financing source and objective. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Use the Fund for actions and measures for technological and industrial development to support renewable energy and efficiency technologies.
source_quote: A fund held at the Fund for Energy and Environmental Services (CSEA), set up by Legislative Decree No 28/2011 and financed through a levy placed on electricity and natural gas tariffs sufficient to ensure resources of around €100 million/year. It aims to support actions and measures for technological and industrial development in the field of renewable sources and energy efficiency.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear financial instrument with annual resources and a defined purpose. It qualifies strongly.

policy_statement: Use the Fund for the development of intangible capital to finance technological research, including Mission Innovation activities.
source_quote: A fund set up by Article 1(c-1091) of the 2018 Budget Law, for the development of intangible capital, competitiveness and productivity, managed by the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Finance,  in  concert  with  the  Ministry  of  Economic  Development  and  the  Ministry  of Education, Universities and Research, which may also be used to finance technological research carried out by companies, in partnership with research bodies, with an allocation increasing up to €250 million for the 2018-2020 three-year period.
extraction_rationale: This is a named fund with a quantified allocation and eligible uses. It qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Provide guarantees to improve access to loans for companies and professionals through the Guarantee Fund.
source_quote:
##  Guarantee fund

Increasing the possibility of being granted a loan: supporting companies and professionals unable to readily be granted a bank loan as they lack the sufficient guarantees.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear guarantee instrument. Climate relevance is indirect because the quote itself is generic, but it appears in the climate-related innovation financing section.

policy_statement: Support investment in new capital goods and digital transformation through hyper-amortisation and super-amortisation.
source_quote:
##  Hyper-amortisation and super-amortisation

Supporting and incentivising companies that invest in new capital goods and tangible and intangible  assets  (software  and  IT  systems)  instrumental  in  the  technological  and  digital transformation of production processes.
extraction_rationale: This is a fiscal incentive instrument with a clear investment purpose. Climate relevance is indirect, but it qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Continue the New Sabatini subsidised loan and State contribution scheme for machinery and Industry 4.0 investments.
source_quote: The Budget Law for 2020 provides funds of €105 million for 2020, €97 million for each of the years  from  2021  to  2024  and  €47 million for  2025 for the New Sabatini  law,  intended to provide subsidised loans for investment in new machinery, plants and equipment, including those  that  fall  within  the  scope  of  Industry  4.0,  and  a  corresponding  State  contribution towards the construction of production facilities, based on the interest calculated on the above-mentioned  loans.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear financial instrument with explicit annual allocations and support form. It qualifies strongly.

policy_statement: Provide a tax credit for incremental R&D costs to stimulate private investment in innovation.
source_quote: This instrument, which forms part of National Industrial Plan 4.0, is for the more immediate use  by  companies,  and  is  aimed  at  stimulating  private  investments  in  R&D  in  order  to innovate processes and products and guarantee the future competitiveness of the companies (not only in the energy sector). It consists of a 50% tax credit for incremental Research and Development costs, which may be granted up to a maximum annual amount of €20 million per recipient
extraction_rationale: This is a clear tax credit instrument with a percentage and annual cap. It qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Use proceeds from CO2 auctions to support experimental development and demonstration projects.
source_quote:
##  Proceeds from CO2 auctions

The funds available from CO2 auctions (Legislative Decree No 30/2013) will cover experimental  development,  in  particular  in  order  to  ensure  that  demonstration  projects (first-of-a-kind) are supported, with the results being passed on to the production system.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear funding commitment using auction revenues for demonstration projects. It qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Use the National Innovation Fund to invest in innovative companies in strategic sectors including sustainable industry and mobility.
source_quote: The tool with which the National Fund operates is venture capital, that is, direct and indirect investments in qualified minority shareholdings in innovative companies by means of general funds, vertical funds or funds of funds, to support start-ups, scale-ups or innovative SMEs. The measures aim to cover the whole country, using an investment approach that progresses from seed capital to growth capital.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear public investment instrument using venture capital. Climate relevance is indirect because the quote is broad, but it is still a concrete policy instrument in the climate innovation section.

policy_statement: Japan will reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 46 percent from fiscal year 2013 levels by fiscal year 2030, while pursuing a 50 percent reduction challenge and aligning with net-zero by 2050.
source_quote: Japan aims to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions by 46 percent in fiscal year 2030 from its fiscal year 2013 levels, setting an ambitious target which is aligned with the longterm  goal  of  achieving  net-zero  by  2050.  Furthermore,  Japan  will  continue  strenuous efforts in its challenge to meet the lofty goal of cutting its emission by 50 percent.
section_header: Japan's Greenhouse Gas Emission Reduction Target
extraction_rationale: This is a core national mitigation policy because it sets a quantified emissions reduction target with a deadline. The 50 percent element is framed as a challenge rather than a firm target, but the 46 percent by 2030 target is concrete and clearly qualifies.

policy_statement: Japan will use the Joint Crediting Mechanism through public-private collaboration to secure about 100 million t-CO2 of international emission reductions and removals by fiscal year 2030 and count acquired credits toward its NDC.
source_quote: Japan aims to contribute to international emission reductions and removals at the level of a cumulative total of approximately 100 million t- CO 2 by fiscal year 2030 through public-private collaborations. Japan will appropriately count the acquired credits to achieve its NDC.
section_header: Japan's Greenhouse Gas Emission Reduction Target
extraction_rationale: This qualifies as a policy because it specifies a named intervention (JCM), a quantified target, and intended use of credits for NDC achievement. It is not merely descriptive because it commits to implementation and accounting.

policy_statement: Japan will maintain the implementation period of its NDC from April 1, 2021 to March 31, 2031 as a single-year fiscal year 2030 target.
source_quote:
FromApril 1, 2021 to March 31, 2031
Single year target (fiscal year 2030)
section_header: 2. Time frames and/or periods for implementation:
extraction_rationale: This is a formal implementation parameter of the NDC rather than a substantive policy measure. It is included as an edge case because it defines the operative period of the commitment, but it is less policy-like than action commitments.

policy_statement: Japan will cover all sectors and categories and all major greenhouse gases under its NDC, with 100 percent coverage.
source_quote: <Sectors of coverage> All sectors and categories encompassing the following: (a) Energy - Fuel Combustion (Energy industries, Manufacturing industries and Construction, Transport, Commercial/Institutional, Residential, Agriculture/Forestry/Fishing, and Other) - Fugitive emissions from fuels - CO 2 transport and storage (b) Industrial processes and product use (c) Agriculture (d) Land Use, Land-Use Change and Forestry (LULUCF) (e) Waste <Targeted gases> Carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), methane (CH 4 ), nitrous oxide (N 2 O), hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), perfluorocarbons (PFCs), sulfur hexafluoride (SF 6 ) and nitrogen trifluoride (NF 3 ). <Percentage of coverage> 100 percent
extraction_rationale: This is a formal scope commitment of the NDC with complete sector and gas coverage. It qualifies because it defines the binding breadth of the mitigation commitment, though it is more of a coverage specification than an intervention.

policy_statement: Japan has made net-zero by 2050 a Basic Principle of the Act on Promotion of Global Warming Countermeasures through legislative amendment.
source_quote: By the Act Partially Amending the Act on Promotion of Global Warming Countermeasures (Act No. 54 of 2021) which was enacted in 204th session of the Diet, net-zero by 2050 became a Basic Principle of the Act. The legislative amendment will enhance the continuity and predictability of policies and accelerate efforts and investments as well as innovation for decarbonization towards not only the achievement of the mid-term target, but also the realization of a decarbonized society.
extraction_rationale: This clearly qualifies as policy because it is a legislative change establishing a binding principle for decarbonization. It is stronger than an aspiration because it references a specific enacted law.

policy_statement: Japan will put forward all possible efforts across key decarbonization areas to support its 2030 target and robust growth.
source_quote: In order to create a virtuous cycle of the economy and the environment and to realize robust growth toward its ambitious goal for fiscal year 2030, Japan will put forward all possible efforts in all areas including by thorough energy efficiency measures, maximum introduction of renewable energy, as well as decarbonization of public sectors and local communities.
extraction_rationale: This functions as an umbrella initiative because it introduces multiple specific action areas in a list-like structure. The phrase 'including by' clearly signals sub-actions beneath a broader decarbonization effort.

parent_statement: Japan will put forward all possible efforts across key decarbonization areas to support its 2030 target and robust growth.
policy_statement: Japan will pursue thorough energy efficiency measures.
source_quote: In order to create a virtuous cycle of the economy and the environment and to realize robust growth toward its ambitious goal for fiscal year 2030, Japan will put forward all possible efforts in all areas including by thorough energy efficiency measures, maximum introduction of renewable energy, as well as decarbonization of public sectors and local communities.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific named intervention under the broader decarbonization effort. Although no numeric target is given here, energy efficiency measures are concrete policy actions.

parent_statement: Japan will put forward all possible efforts across key decarbonization areas to support its 2030 target and robust growth.
policy_statement: Japan will maximize the introduction of renewable energy.
source_quote: In order to create a virtuous cycle of the economy and the environment and to realize robust growth toward its ambitious goal for fiscal year 2030, Japan will put forward all possible efforts in all areas including by thorough energy efficiency measures, maximum introduction of renewable energy, as well as decarbonization of public sectors and local communities.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific intervention named within the broader package. It qualifies as policy because renewable energy deployment is a concrete mitigation action, even though no quantitative deployment target is stated here.

parent_statement: Japan will put forward all possible efforts across key decarbonization areas to support its 2030 target and robust growth.
policy_statement: Japan will decarbonize public sectors and local communities.
source_quote: In order to create a virtuous cycle of the economy and the environment and to realize robust growth toward its ambitious goal for fiscal year 2030, Japan will put forward all possible efforts in all areas including by thorough energy efficiency measures, maximum introduction of renewable energy, as well as decarbonization of public sectors and local communities.
extraction_rationale: This is a distinct action area under the umbrella decarbonization effort. It is somewhat broad, but still qualifies because it names a specific intervention domain rather than a general aspiration.

policy_statement: Japan will implement the Strategy for Sustainable Food Systems, MeaDRI, to enhance productivity potential and ensure sustainability through innovation in food, agriculture, forestry, and fisheries.
source_quote: In food, agriculture, forestry, and fisheries industries, based on the 'Strategy for Sustainable Food Systems, MeaDRI (Measures for achievement of Decarbonization and Resilience with Innovation) (decided by Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries on May 12 th , 2021),' Japan aims to enhance productivity potentials and ensure sustainability in a compatible manner through innovation.
extraction_rationale: This qualifies because it references a named government strategy and specifies sectors and intended intervention through innovation. The climate content is explicit in the strategy title, though the quoted sentence itself mixes sustainability and productivity goals.

policy_statement: Japan will implement MLIT's Green Challenge to advance cross-sectoral decarbonization in national land, urban, and regional spheres.
source_quote: Based on the 'MLIT's Green Challenge (decided by Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism on July 6 th , 2021),' Japan will steadily carry out efforts in cross-sectoral decarbonization in national land, urban and regional spheres.
extraction_rationale: This is a named government initiative with a specific intervention focus on cross-sectoral decarbonization. It qualifies despite lacking quantified targets because it is a concrete programmatic commitment.

policy_statement: Japan will pursue strategic transitions to a circular economy and nature-based solutions to create new industries and jobs necessary for decarbonization.
source_quote: Japan will create new industries and jobs by proceeding efforts in strategic transitions to a circular economy, which is necessary for decarbonization, as well as through nature-based solutions (NbS). Japan will continue its strenuous efforts towards 2030, and further towards 2050.
extraction_rationale: This qualifies as policy because it commits to strategic transitions in named areas tied explicitly to decarbonization. It is somewhat broad and combines two mechanisms, but both are concrete policy directions rather than background context.

policy_statement: Japan will promote growth-oriented policies with decarbonization as a central pillar across socio-economic activities.
source_quote: For those targets to be achieved, Japan will promote policies contributing to growth by holding decarbonization as its pillar.
extraction_rationale: This is a policy commitment but relatively high-level and vague. It is included because it commits the government to a policy orientation centered on decarbonization, though it lacks specific instruments.

policy_statement: Japan will continue annual progress management and review of measures under the Plan for Global Warming Countermeasures, including strengthening existing measures and introducing new ones where progress is delayed.
source_quote: Every year since the formulation of the plan, the Global Warming Prevention Headquarters, led by the Prime Minister with all Cabinet Ministers as its members, has made rigorous reviews and examinations on, among others, the state of progress in each countermeasure taken by the Government, by using the outcome in emission reductions including figures by greenhouse gases and other classifications, and indicators to evaluate the progress in implementing countermeasures. Specifically, by administering evaluations on each section of measures and policies and identifying sections whose progress is delayed, the Government conducted examinations on, among others, how to improve progress in the identified sections. In so doing, the Government considered not only the enhancement of measures and policies that are already included in the Plan for Global Warming Countermeasures but also the introduction of new measures and policies. Also, with regard to the new target for fiscal year 2030, the Government will continue progress management in a similar manner as mentioned in the above.
extraction_rationale: This qualifies as policy because it commits to an ongoing governance mechanism for implementation, review, and policy adjustment. It is procedural, but it contains a concrete institutional commitment tied to climate target delivery.

policy_statement: Japan will establish and implement the Joint Crediting Mechanism to quantify overseas emission reductions and removals from diffusion of decarbonizing technologies and measures, and use them toward its NDC.
source_quote: Japan will establish and implement the Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM) in order to quantitatively evaluate contributions of Japan to greenhouse gas emission reductions and removals which are achieved through the diffusion of, among others, leading decarbonizing technologies, products, systems, services, and infrastructures as well as through the implementation of measures in developing countries and others, and in order to use such contributions to achieve Japan's NDC. By doing so, through public-private collaborations, Japan aims to secure accumulated emission reductions and removals at the level of approximately 100 million t-CO 2 by fiscal year 2030. Japan will appropriately count the acquired credits to achieve its NDC.
section_header: 5. Assumptions and methodological approaches, including those for estimating and accounting for anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions and, as appropriate, removals:
extraction_rationale: This is a clear policy commitment with a named mechanism, implementation intent, and quantified outcome. It overlaps with the earlier JCM statement, but this version adds implementation detail and is retained as the fuller formulation.

policy_statement: Japan will ensure environmental integrity and avoid double-counting in the Joint Crediting Mechanism in line with international rules including the Paris Agreement.
source_quote: With regards to the JCM which Japan has initiated to establish, Japan secures environmental integrity and the avoidance of double-counting in line with the international rules including the Paris Agreement. Also, based on its experience in the JCM, Japan intends to lead international discussions, thereby contributing to the development of appropriate international rules for the use of market mechanisms.
section_header: 5. Assumptions and methodological approaches, including those for estimating and accounting for anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions and, as appropriate, removals:
extraction_rationale: This qualifies as a policy because it commits to a specific governance rule for a market mechanism. It is narrower than the broader JCM policy but still a distinct implementation commitment.

policy_statement: Japan will proactively support international cooperation to promote decarbonization and improve resilience in developing countries through policy development, institutional platforms, sector- and city-level efforts, and technology diffusion.
source_quote: Furthermore, Japan will also make proactive efforts in the area of international cooperation to promote decarbonization and to improve resilience in developing countries and others, including from developing policies and institutional platforms to promoting sector- and city-level efforts as well as facilitating technology diffusion.
section_header: 5. Assumptions and methodological approaches, including those for estimating and accounting for anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions and, as appropriate, removals:
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete international cooperation commitment with named intervention types. It explicitly combines decarbonization and resilience, so both mitigation and adaptation mechanisms are stated.

policy_statement: Japan will accelerate transitions toward a decarbonized society, a circular economy, and a decentralized society as part of redesigning its economy and society to be sustainable and resilient.
source_quote: Based on the declaration for net-zero by 2050, Japan will strongly promote the 're-design' of its economy and society to make it sustainable and resilient, through accelerating the three types of transitions, namely towards 'a decarbonized society,' 'a circular economy' and 'a decentralized society.'
section_header: 6. How the Party considers that its nationally determined contribution is fair and ambitious in the light of its national circumstances:
extraction_rationale: This qualifies because it commits to specific strategic transitions as instruments of climate action. It is broad and strategic rather than operational, but still names concrete policy directions.

policy_statement: Ensure implementation of Kuwait's National Adaptation Plan through a national coordination mechanism and partnerships with governmental and non-governmental institutions.
source_quote: The Government of Kuwait, represented by the Environment Public Authority (EPA), has committed itself to ensure the implementation of its National Adaptation Plan (NAP), in partnership with other governmental and non-governmental institutions, furthermore A national coordination mechanism has been identified to implement a range of national initiatives to protect the various vital sectors from the Negative impacts of climate change. Therefore, future programs have been developed to deal with the various risks face the sectors and across time periods.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear governmental commitment to implement the NAP through an identified coordination mechanism and future programs. It qualifies as a policy because it establishes an implementation arrangement for adaptation action, even though it does not specify funding or numeric targets.

policy_statement: Implement a sustainable program to increase resilience and national capacities across vital sectors through management, technical practices, land-use planning, water management, and health protection initiatives.
source_quote: Despite the difficulty of dealing with the risks of climate change due to its complexity and impacts on more than one sector, A sustainable program have been proposed to increase resilience and build national capacities to address the risks and negative impacts of climate change. The proposed programs are related to the four vital sectors focus on management practices, functional practices, technical practices, land use planning, water management, human health protection and identification of short, medium- and long-term initiatives to adapt to climate change.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation commitment because it proposes a sustainable program with named intervention types and sectoral scope. It is somewhat umbrella-like, but no explicit sub-list follows immediately in this section, so it is treated as an individual policy.

policy_statement: Establish a comprehensive ongoing monitoring program using environmental data and information to monitor climate change and assess its impacts in Kuwait.
source_quote: One of the expected results is a comprehensive ongoing monitoring program through the necessary environmental data and information to monitor climate change and assess its impact on the State of Kuwait on an ongoing basis, In partnership with all stakeholders such as the academia, private sector and nongovernmental actors in the areas of adaptation to climate change.
extraction_rationale: This qualifies as a policy because it commits to a specific intervention: an ongoing monitoring program for climate change impacts. It is direct adaptation governance infrastructure, though operational details are limited.

policy_statement: Seek technical assistance from international organizations, industry, and stakeholders to implement adaptation programs and reduce associated socio-economic impacts.
source_quote: Therefore, EPA will seek technical assistance from international organizations, industrial community and other stakeholders to implement the proposed programs to adapt to climate change and reduce the side effects associated with socio-economic problems. This will be achieved in the manner of implementing the national plan which is based on participation, while maintaining the coordination and oversight role of the EPA in the various activities and initiatives that aim to reach the desired goal to reduce the Negative impacts of climate change and adopt with it.
extraction_rationale: This is a policy commitment to mobilize technical assistance for implementation of adaptation programs. It is not merely descriptive because it states what EPA will do institutionally.

policy_statement: Launch a national initiative to design a National Adaptation Plan aimed at enhancing adaptive capacity and resilience and reducing vulnerability to climate impacts.
source_quote: The Kuwait Environment Public Authority together with the UN Environment and United Nations Development programme launched a national initiative in 2017 aimed at designing a National Adaptation Plan (NAP) to enhance national adaptive capacity and resilience to reduce vulnerability to the impacts of climate change. In Kuwait, coastal zones and marine life and fisheries are the most sensitive sectors to climate change and its induced disasters.
extraction_rationale: This is a named national initiative with a clear adaptation objective and date anchor. It qualifies as a policy because it is a deliberate government-led intervention to create the NAP.

policy_statement: Propose 56 adaptation initiatives across four sectors, divided into short-, medium-, and long-term implementation periods.
source_quote: A set of adaptation measures are proposed in the NAP. These were divided into three categories; shortterm initiatives to be implemented in less than a year; medium term-initiatives to be implemented in three years, and long-term initiatives those need three to five years to be accomplished. In total, 56 initiatives were proposed as follows; 21 short-term initiatives, 18 medium-term initiatives, and 17 long-term initiatives.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete policy package because it specifies the number of initiatives and implementation timeframes. While it summarizes later detailed actions, it is itself a defined commitment framework.

policy_statement: Urgently mobilize financial resources for technology transfer and implementation of proposed adaptation measures.
source_quote: In summary, the Action Plan recommends the preparation of sectoral action plan for adaptation with emphasis on the four main sectors. Mobilization of financial resources, therefore, is urgently needed for technology transfer and for implementing the proposed adaptation measures.
extraction_rationale: This is a climate-relevant finance commitment, though somewhat broad. It qualifies because it explicitly calls for mobilization of financial resources for adaptation implementation and technology transfer.

policy_statement: Reduce vulnerability to climate change impacts by building adaptive capacity and resilience.
source_quote:
According to the UNFCCC, COP 17 th , the main objectives of these action plan are 2 :

- a)  To  reduce  vulnerability  to  the  impacts  of  climate  change,  by  building  adaptive capacity and resilience;
section_header: 1.3. The need for National Adaptation Plan (NAP)
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit objective of the NAP process and functions as a policy commitment. It is broad, but still qualifies because it defines the intended adaptation outcome of the national plan.

policy_statement: Integrate climate change adaptation coherently into relevant policies, programmes, activities, and development planning across sectors and levels.
source_quote:
- b) To facilitate the integration of climate change adaptation, in a coherent manner, into relevant new and existing policies, programmes and activities, in particular, development planning processes and strategies, within all relevant sectors and at different levels, as appropriate.

Accordingly, the NAP shall incorporate long-term strategies, within the national policies for sustainable development, to adapt to climate change.
section_header: 1.3. The need for National Adaptation Plan (NAP)
extraction_rationale: This is a clear mainstreaming commitment and qualifies as policy because it directs integration of adaptation into planning and policy systems. It is broad but operationally meaningful.

policy_statement: Enhance national climatological, meteorological, and hydrological capabilities and early warning contributions for climate-induced disasters.
source_quote: It is also expected that NAP should enhance national climatological, meteorological and hydrological capabilities and the  means  to  contribute  to  climate  change-induced  disasters  early  warning.  It  should promote policies and strengthen institutional frameworks which develop cooperation and coordination, in a spirit of partnership between the government, local populations, and community groups and facilitate access by local populations to appropriate information and  technology.
section_header: 1.3. The need for National Adaptation Plan (NAP)
extraction_rationale: This qualifies because it commits to strengthening capabilities and early warning systems, which are specific adaptation interventions. It also explicitly promotes institutional frameworks and information access.

policy_statement: Build the NAP process in Kuwait around two main objectives: reducing vulnerability through resilience-building and integrating adaptation into policies, programs, and activities.
source_quote:
The UNFCCC technical guidelines for the national adaptation plan process is proposed to be followed in the preparation of the NAP process framework and roadmap. The main objectives of establishing the NAP process in Kuwait are to:

- a) build  an  adaptive  plan  with  capacity  and  resilience  that  can  reduce vulnerability to the climate change impacts; and
- b) facilitate  and  integrate  the  adaptation  of  climate  change  into  policies, programs,  and  activities,  in  specific  development  planning  strategies and processes, within all national relevant sector.
section_header: 1.6. Process and methodology of establishing the NAP
extraction_rationale: This is a parent policy because it introduces a named objective set followed by lettered sub-items. The umbrella commitment is to establish the NAP process around these objectives.

parent_statement: Main objectives of establishing the NAP process in Kuwait
policy_statement: Build an adaptive plan with capacity and resilience that can reduce vulnerability to climate change impacts.
source_quote:
The main objectives of establishing the NAP process in Kuwait are to:

- a) build  an  adaptive  plan  with  capacity  and  resilience  that  can  reduce vulnerability to the climate change impacts;
section_header: 1.6. Process and methodology of establishing the NAP
extraction_rationale: This is a sub-policy under the stated NAP objectives. It is a direct adaptation commitment with a specific resilience-building mechanism.

parent_statement: Main objectives of establishing the NAP process in Kuwait
policy_statement: Facilitate and integrate climate change adaptation into policies, programs, activities, and development planning processes across relevant sectors.
source_quote:
The main objectives of establishing the NAP process in Kuwait are to:

- b) facilitate  and  integrate  the  adaptation  of  climate  change  into  policies, programs,  and  activities,  in  specific  development  planning  strategies and processes, within all national relevant sector.
section_header: 1.6. Process and methodology of establishing the NAP
extraction_rationale: This is a sub-policy because it is one of the lettered objectives under the NAP process. It clearly commits to mainstreaming adaptation into sectoral planning.

policy_statement: Implement the NAP process through four main elements covering groundwork, preparatory work, implementation strategies, and reporting/monitoring/review.
section_header: 1.6. Process and methodology of establishing the NAP
extraction_rationale: This is a parent policy because it establishes the umbrella implementation structure for the NAP and is followed by enumerated sub-elements. It is a planning commitment rather than background text.

parent_statement: The NAP process defined by the UNFCCC comprises four main elements
policy_statement: Lay the groundwork and identify gaps as a core element of the NAP process.
source_quote:
The NAP process defined by the UNFCCC comprises four main elements that can be summarized as follows:

- (A) laying the groundwork and identifying gaps;
section_header: 1.6. Process and methodology of establishing the NAP
extraction_rationale: This is a sub-policy because it is one of the enumerated NAP process elements. It qualifies as a planning commitment within the adaptation framework.

parent_statement: The NAP process defined by the UNFCCC comprises four main elements
policy_statement: Undertake preparatory elements as a core element of the NAP process.
source_quote:
The NAP process defined by the UNFCCC comprises four main elements that can be summarized as follows:

- (B) making preparatory elements;
section_header: 1.6. Process and methodology of establishing the NAP
extraction_rationale: This is a sub-policy under the four-element NAP structure. It is a formal planning component of the adaptation process.

parent_statement: The NAP process defined by the UNFCCC comprises four main elements
policy_statement: Develop implementation strategies as a core element of the NAP process.
source_quote:
The NAP process defined by the UNFCCC comprises four main elements that can be summarized as follows:

- (C) implementation strategies and;
section_header: 1.6. Process and methodology of establishing the NAP
extraction_rationale: This is a sub-policy because it is one of the listed NAP process elements. It is a concrete implementation commitment within the adaptation framework.

parent_statement: The NAP process defined by the UNFCCC comprises four main elements
policy_statement: Establish reporting, monitoring, and reviewing as a core element of the NAP process.
source_quote:
The NAP process defined by the UNFCCC comprises four main elements that can be summarized as follows:

- (D) reporting, monitoring and reviewing.
section_header: 1.6. Process and methodology of establishing the NAP
extraction_rationale: This is a sub-policy because it is one of the enumerated NAP elements. It qualifies as a specific governance and accountability commitment for adaptation.

policy_statement: Recommend tree planting, citizen education, and public awareness to minimize the effects of projected temperature increases and precipitation declines.
source_quote: In conclusion, severe temperature  increases  and  decreases  in  precipitation  values  would  fundamentally change the02 ecosystem functions and socioeconomic aspects. Some recommended efforts to minimize the effect of these changes are tree plantings to decrease the albedo, educating citizens and raising public awareness about climate changes consequences.
extraction_rationale: This qualifies because it names specific adaptation interventions: tree planting, education, and awareness. The wording is somewhat recommendatory rather than binding, but it is still a concrete policy-relevant measure in the plan.

policy_statement: Construct desalination plants, apply water conservation technologies, and use treated sewage effluent for irrigation as adaptation measures in the water sector.
source_quote: Kuwait  has  implemented  several  projects  to  adapt  to  climate  change  in  the  water resources  sector.  These  projects  include  the  construction  of  desalination  plants,  the application of water conservation technologies and utilizing the Treated Sewage Effluent (TSE) water for irrigation purposes.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete set of implemented adaptation measures with named interventions. It qualifies as policy because it reflects deliberate government action in the water sector.

policy_statement: Construct tidal barriers and establish coastal information systems as climate change adaptation measures for coastal zones.
source_quote: On the coastal zone sector, Kuwait has implemented projects such as constructing tidal barriers and establishing Coastal Information systems as  a  climate  change  adaptation  measure.  Meanwhile,  awareness  campaigns  were conducted to the public and projects development among the coastal lines to take their precautions.
extraction_rationale: This qualifies as policy because it identifies specific adaptation infrastructure and information-system interventions for coastal protection. The awareness campaigns are also named, but the main extract focuses on the clearer interventions.

policy_statement: Implement green belts and increase protected areas to adapt to dust storms, with projects started in 2015 for a five-year duration.
source_quote: In  response,  Kuwait  has  undertaken  some  adaptation  projects  such  as implementing green belts project and increasing the protected areas to adapt to a dust storm. The green belt projects consist of planted areas with trees and shrubs of 50-180 Km in  length  and  5-20  Km  in  width.  These  projects  have  started  in  2015  for  5-year duration time.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation policy with named interventions, dimensions, and timing. It also uses ecosystem-based measures, making it clearly policy-relevant.

policy_statement: Introduce more than 50 tree types for greenery and landscape under the Agriculture Master Plan to reduce climate change effects.
source_quote: Many projects investing in the agriculture sector are taking place in Kuwait (Al Dosery et al., 2012). More than 50 types of trees for greenery and landscape that can reduce climate change effect, were introduced under the Agriculture Master Plan by Kuwait Institute for Scientific  Research  (KISR)  and  the  Public  Authority  for  Agricultural  Affairs  and  Fish Resources  (PAAFR).
extraction_rationale: This qualifies because it is a named intervention under a master plan with a specific scale ('more than 50 types of trees'). It is climate-directed and ecosystem-based.

policy_statement: Develop new crop varieties that can adapt to high temperatures and resist salinity and drought.
source_quote: Development  of  new  varieties  of  crops  that  can  adapt  to  high temperatures  and  have  high  resistance  to  salinity  and  drought  such  as  Conocarpus, Ficus,  Prosopis,  and  date  palm  trees,  were  implemented  in  Kuwait  (Al  Dosery  et  al., 2012). These types of plants are mainly planted in Wafraa and Abdali, Kuwait.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation intervention in agriculture with named crop/tree varieties and explicit climate hazards. It qualifies as policy due to the concrete implementation described.

policy_statement: Establish eMISK to build and maintain a comprehensive geo-environmental database and GIS system for updating and analyzing environmental data.
source_quote: Kuwait Environmental Public Authority (EPA) has established an electronic environmental Monitoring  Information  System  of  Kuwait  (eMISK)  and  beatona.  The  eMISK  aims  at building and maintaining a comprehensive geo-environmental database of Kuwait and a GIS  system  to  facilitate  updating  and  analyzing  environmental  data.
extraction_rationale: This is a named government system with a specific operational purpose. It qualifies as a policy because it creates adaptation-supporting monitoring and information infrastructure.

policy_statement: Implement the green belts project and Kuwait Green Wall Project to increase protected areas and plant 315,000 trees along a 420 km wall to hold back moving sand.
source_quote: Implementing green belts project and increasing the protected areas to adapt to dust storms. Kuwait has undertaken some adaptation projects such as implementing green belts project and increasing the protected areas to adapt to a dust storm. The green belt projects consist of planted areas with trees and shrubs of 50-180 Km in length areas with trees and shrubs of 50-180 Km in length and 5-20 Km in width. These projects are the 5-year duration and started in 2015 (KUNA, 2015). Meanwhile, Kuwait has implemented a project called 'Kuwait Green Wall Project. This project aims to increase the protected areas by planting 315,000 trees for 420 Km wall along the borderline to hold back the moving sand.
extraction_rationale: This is a strong policy extraction because it includes a named project, quantified tree planting, physical dimensions, and a climate hazard response. It is clearly adaptation via ecosystem measures.

policy_statement: Undertake agricultural projects to develop crops adapted to high temperatures and resistant to salinity and drought.
source_quote: Many  agricultural projects have been undertaken by Kuwait Institute for Scientific Research (KISR) in order to develop crops that can adapt to high temperatures and different spans of seasons and crops resistant to salinity and drought (Al Dosery et al., 2012). More than 50 types of trees for greenery and landscape that can reduce climate change effect, were introduced under the Agriculture Master Plan by (KISR) and the Public Authority for Agricultural Affairs and Fish Resources (PAAFR).
extraction_rationale: Although related to the Agriculture Master Plan, this item is separately framed as a project initiative in the numbered list and includes specific adaptation mechanisms. It qualifies as a policy action.

policy_statement: Establish the 2016 Food Security project comprising twelve projects across fisheries, water, natural resources, animal production, animal health, and technical capacity development.
extraction_rationale: This is a parent policy because it is a named project umbrella followed by listed fields and references to subprojects. It includes a time frame and budget, making it clearly policy-relevant.

parent_statement: Food security project established in 2016
policy_statement: Undertake fisheries management projects under the Food Security project.
extraction_rationale: This is a sub-policy because fisheries management is explicitly listed under the named Food Security project. The commitment is specific enough as a project field under a funded program.

parent_statement: Food security project established in 2016
policy_statement: Undertake water resource management projects under the Food Security project.
extraction_rationale: This is a sub-policy because water resource management is one of the listed project fields under the Food Security umbrella initiative.

parent_statement: Food security project established in 2016
policy_statement: Undertake natural resource management projects under the Food Security project.
extraction_rationale: This is a sub-policy because natural resource management is explicitly listed under the Food Security project.

parent_statement: Food security project established in 2016
policy_statement: Undertake animal production projects under the Food Security project.
extraction_rationale: This is a sub-policy because animal production is one of the listed fields under the parent Food Security project.

parent_statement: Food security project established in 2016
policy_statement: Undertake animal health projects under the Food Security project.
extraction_rationale: This is a sub-policy because animal health is explicitly listed under the Food Security project.
