parent_statement: Food security project established in 2016
policy_statement: Undertake technical capacity development projects under the Food Security project.
source_quote:
FAO  in  cooperation  with  the State of Kuwait planned to undertake twelve projects in the following fields:
- Animal health;
- Technical capacity development.

These projects have a time frame between 1-5 years under the Food Security Sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a sub-policy because technical capacity development is one of the listed fields under the parent Food Security project and has an associated time frame.

policy_statement: Establish a regional database and information center to support fisheries management and aquaculture development, with a budget of $250,000 per year.
source_quote:
The project aims at establishing a regional database and information center to support the fisheries management and aquaculture development

in the region. Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the Public Authority of Agriculture Affairs and Fish Resources (PAAFR) were the responsible authorities with a budget of $250,000/year.
extraction_rationale: This is a named project with a clear intervention and annual budget, so it qualifies as a policy. It supports adaptation in fisheries and aquaculture management.

policy_statement: Establish fisheries farms using Nile tilapia culture in agricultural farms in Al-Wafra, Abdali, and Al-Sulybia using brackish groundwater.
source_quote: Fisheries  are  considered  a  vital  source  of  food  in  Kuwait.  The establishment of fisheries farms is an important step to adapt to climate change under the food security sector. Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) culture is implemented in agriculture  farms  where  crops  such  as  alfa  alfa,  tomatoes,  potatoes,  onions  are cultivated. These farms are in the Al-Wafra, Abdali and Al-Sulybia areas.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation intervention with named species, locations, and implementation context. It qualifies as policy because it is an established project under food security adaptation.

policy_statement: Assess historic climate records for the past 70 years and develop future climate projection scenarios through 2100.
source_quote: Assessment of historic climate records and future projection .  The project aimed at assessing the historic climate records for the past 70 years and make future projection climatic  scenarios  until  the  year  2100.  The  project  started  in  2012  by  the  Kuwait University and UN Environment.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific project with a defined analytical scope and start year. It qualifies as a policy-relevant adaptation planning measure because it supports climate risk assessment.

policy_statement: Establish eMISK as an electronic system to build and maintain a comprehensive geo-environmental database and GIS system.
source_quote: Environmental  Monitoring  Information  System  of  Kuwait  (eMISK) .  eMISK  is  an electronic system established by the Environment Public Authority (EPA) of Kuwait and aims at building and maintaining a comprehensive geo-environmental database of Kuwait and a GIS system to facilitate updating and analyzing environmental data. The project starts in 2015 by EPA and is still ongoing.
extraction_rationale: This duplicates the earlier eMISK description but adds start year and ongoing status; retained here as the clearer project statement. It is a concrete adaptation-supporting information system.

policy_statement: Establish a national program through eMISK Industry to collect an environmental inventory of industrial facilities in Kuwait.
source_quote: eMISK Industry ; this project aims at establishing a national program for collecting an environmental inventory of industrial facilities in Kuwait. The Adaptation Sector for this project is Public Health.
extraction_rationale: This is a named project with a specific intervention. It qualifies as policy because it creates a national inventory program relevant to environmental health and adaptation planning.

policy_statement: Implement eMISK Waste to manage industrial liquid waste vehicle fleets and organize logistics.
source_quote: eMISK Waste ; this project aims at finding and implementing a solution to be able to manage  the  fleet  of  industrial  liquid  waste  vehicles  and  organizing  the  logistics process. The Adaptation Sector for this project is the Waste Sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific operational intervention with a named project and implementation purpose. Climate relevance is indirect because waste logistics are not primarily climate-focused in the quoted text.

policy_statement: Implement eMISK Marine to support policies and programs that enhance integrated coastal and ocean management in Kuwait.
source_quote: eMISK Marine ; The project aims at promoting and facilitating information management system in support of policies and programs that enhance integrated coastal and ocean management  in  Kuwait.  The  Adaptation  Sector  for  this  project  is  the  Coastal Zones/SLR.
extraction_rationale: This is a named project with a clear adaptation-supporting function for coastal and ocean management. It qualifies as policy because it establishes an information management system tied to SLR adaptation.

policy_statement: Build additional desalination plants and expand desalinated water capacity, including Al-Zour North, Al-Zour South, Al Khiran, and Doha projects.
source_quote: In 2016, Kuwait produced around 3.85 MCM/d of desalinated water. Eight additional plants were being commissioned by the government. Al-Zour North IWPP (capacity: 250  Million  of  Gallons  per  Day  (MGD)  for  EUR  320  million),  Al-Zour  South  Plant (capacity: 145 MGD), Al Khiran IWPP (capacity: 125 MGD), and Doha desalination plant (60 MGD) are examples of these projects.
extraction_rationale: This is a strong policy extraction because it includes specific infrastructure projects, capacities, and one explicit investment amount. It is adaptation-focused due to freshwater security.

policy_statement: Invest USD 5.5 million jointly with MIT in research on upgrading current desalination plants and developing next-generation desalination plants.
source_quote: Kuwait is investing USD 5.5 million jointly with MIT to conduct researches on updating the current desalination plants and next-generation desalination plants . The adaptation Sector for this project is the Water Resources Sector, and the Government is responsible for the implementation of this project since 2016 and it is still ongoing.
extraction_rationale: This clearly qualifies as a financial instrument because it is a public investment line with a stated amount. It is climate-relevant through water-resource adaptation.

policy_statement: Teach rural households in-house water desalination techniques to provide freshwater at low cost and in short time.
source_quote: Education on household desalination .  Kuwait jointly with United Nations taught the Kuwaiti  people  in  rural  areas  the  'in-house  water  desalination  techniques',  where households can have freshwater at low cost and short time. The Adaptation Sector for this project is the Water Resources and the Awareness sectors.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation intervention focused on household water access and awareness. It qualifies as policy because it describes an implemented educational program with a named technique.

policy_statement: Implement KIEIN-IV as an integrated GIS-based environmental indicator and spatial decision support system with a $1.2 million budget.
source_quote: Kuwait Integrated Environmental Information Network Phase-IV . The KIEIN-IV is an integrated GIS-based system that compiles the environmental indicator data and acts as a spatial decision support system tools (SDSS). This project was running from 2012-2014 by the UNDP and EPA with a budget of $1,200,000.
extraction_rationale: This is a named project with a defined function and budget, so it qualifies as policy. It supports climate adaptation planning through environmental data and decision support.

policy_statement: Implement the Kuwait Environmental Governance Initiative to support design of the National Adaptation Plan and related initiatives linked to water, city planning, and other sectors.
source_quote: Kuwait Environmental Governance Initiative (KEGI) . The Project supports the design of the National Adaptation Plan (NAP) of Kuwait and the relevant initiatives linked to water, city planning, and other sectors. This project was running from 2017-2018 by the UNDP and EPA with a budget of $2,000,000.
extraction_rationale: This is a named project with a clear adaptation-planning purpose and budget. It qualifies as a policy and as a financial instrument because it is a funded initiative.

policy_statement: Establish land and marine nature reserves in Kuwait, including Sabah Al-Ahmed and Jahra Pool reserve areas.
source_quote: Establishment of land and marine nature reserves .  The project aims to establish a series of land and marine nature reserves in the State of Kuwait. National reserves were  implemented  to  safeguard  the  Kuwait  marine  and  land  ecosystems.  These natural reserves are in Sabah Al-Ahmed natural reserve area and Jahra pool natural reserve area.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete ecosystem protection intervention with named reserve areas. It qualifies as policy because it establishes protected areas as a deliberate adaptation-related measure.

policy_statement: Apply water conservation technologies to reduce water consumption by 20 percent.
source_quote: Water Conservation (Partially implemented) Kuwait's Initial National Communications ; the application of  water conservation technologies was also one of the adaptation options  to  reduce  water  consumption by  20  %.  The Water  Resources  Sector  was responsible, and the project started in 2012 and is still ongoing.
extraction_rationale: This clearly qualifies because it includes a quantified target (20% reduction) and a named intervention. It is adaptation-oriented water demand management.

policy_statement: Establish a Coastal Information System to provide coastal information to planners and decision makers for protection of coastal zones and marine environments.
source_quote: Establishing a Coastal information system (CIS) ;  Coastal Information System (CIS) was established to help in the protection of coastal zones and marine environments in  Kuwait.  CIS  provides  information  about  Kuwait's  coastal  area  to  planners  and decision makers.
extraction_rationale: This is a named system with a specific adaptation purpose and user group. It qualifies as policy because it institutionalizes coastal information for climate-related planning.

policy_statement: Construct tidal gate systems and offshore breakwaters in new coastal developments to protect against erosion and rising sea levels.
source_quote: Constructing tidal barriers in new developments ; Sabah Al Ahmad Sea City, which is located near the Saudi Arabia border, is a new development which constructed a tidal gate system and offshore breakwater was built to protect the artificial promenade from erosion  of  waves  and  to  cope  with  the  rising  sea  levels  as  the  adverse  impact  of climate change.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation infrastructure measure with a named site and explicit hazard response. It clearly qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Conduct awareness campaigns and symposiums on sea level rise to increase stakeholder and public awareness of adaptation needs.
source_quote: Conducting awareness campaigns and symposiums regarding Sea level rise ; the 'Our Seas: Theories, Data, and Policies' Symposium highlighted the importance of human intervention regarding rising sea levels. International specialists, local researchers, and  non-governmental  organizations  attended  this  symposium.  This  symposium aimed  at  increasing  the  awareness  of  the  concerned  stakeholders  and  the  public about the adaptation to sea level rise as an impact of climate change.
extraction_rationale: This qualifies because it is a named awareness intervention focused on a specific climate hazard and adaptation response. It is softer than regulation but still a concrete policy action.

policy_statement: Implement the Coastal Management Program to produce Integrated Coastal Zone Management guidance and best-practice guidelines for coastal development.
source_quote: Coastal  Management  Program ;  the  CMP  produces  physical  modeling,  numerical modeling  and  field  survey  measurements.  The  CMP  was  responsible  to  produce Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM) for Kuwait. The project aims at identifying the best practice guidelines for the development of the coastal zone of Kuwait.
extraction_rationale: This is a named program with a clear planning output (ICZM and best-practice guidelines). It qualifies as policy because it guides coastal adaptation and development decisions.

policy_statement: Initiate the Water Resources Development and Management Program to optimize water use and management and develop integrated water policies, management options, and action plans.
source_quote: Establishment of the Water Resources Program ; A water resources development and management program (WRDM) was initiated by the Kuwait Institute for Science and Research (KISR). This program helps to identify ways to optimize the water resources use and management through applied research. WRDM program was designed to develop integrated  water  policies,  management options,  and action  plans  to  solve water  scarcity  problems  and  increase  Kuwait's  water  security  and  resilience.
extraction_rationale: This is a named program with explicit objectives and adaptation rationale. It qualifies as policy because it commits to integrated water policy and action-plan development.

policy_statement: Operate 40 Multi-Stage Flash desalination units with a total production capacity of 234 MGD.
source_quote: Constructing Desalination using Multi-Stage Flash technology ; Kuwait has a total of 40  operating  Multi-Stage  Flash  desalination  units  (MSF),  with  a  total  production capacity of 234 MGD. The project was completed by the Government and the MEW under the Technology Needs Assessment / Water Resources Sectors.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete infrastructure commitment with quantified capacity. It qualifies as policy because it reflects completed government action to secure water resources.

policy_statement: Implement a wastewater treatment and reclamation technologies program to reclaim and reuse wastewater for irrigation, with about 65 percent of treated wastewater already reused.

Increase access to housing.

policy_statement: London commits to becoming a zero carbon city by 2050.
source_quote: The Mayor's London Environment Strategy (May 2018) was one of the first plans of any world city to be compatible with the highest ambition of the Paris Agreement. It commits London to being a zero carbon city by 2050. It sets out the actions the Mayor will take, within his powers, to get there as soon as possible.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear, quantified long-term target with a deadline (2050), making it a qualifying climate policy commitment.

policy_statement: London will reduce emissions by 60 per cent below 1990 levels by 2030 and nearly 80 per cent by 2040.
source_quote: Understanding these different pathways has enabled us to set an ambitious emissions pathway in line with the IPCC recommendations. It will see London reduce its emissions by 60 per cent on 1990 levels by 2030 and by nearly 80 per cent by 2040.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified emissions-reduction pathway with explicit milestones, which qualifies as a mitigation policy target.

policy_statement: London will use carbon budgets over five-year periods to manage the transition to zero carbon by 2050.
source_quote:
Carbon budgets place a recommended limit on London's carbon emissions over the next 15 years. London's carbon budgets are more ambitious than the national government's and set us on our way to be a zero carbon city by 2050.

Carbon budgets help London's businesses, communities, boroughs, the Mayor and national government manage the transition to zero carbon, so that we don't leave everything until the last minute, incurring greater cost.
extraction_rationale: The document establishes carbon budgets as a formal emissions-limiting mechanism, which is a concrete policy instrument rather than background context.

policy_statement: At least 70 per cent of London's buildings need to reach EPC C by 2030.
source_quote: All our pathways to zero carbon in 2050 rely on a high level of energy efficiency building retrofits by 2030. Only 35 per cent of homes currently achieve adequate energy efficiency performance (EPC C or above) and many will still be in use by 2050. At least 70 per cent of London's buildings need to reach EPC C by 2030.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified building-efficiency target with a deadline. It is framed as necessary action, not merely descriptive analysis.

policy_statement: Building retrofit rates need to rise to nearly 160,000 houses per year by the mid-2020s.
source_quote: However, achieving this would require building retrofit rates per year to reach more than four times their historical peak. In 2012, around 40,000 houses in London were reached with energy efficiency programmes. By the mid 2020s we would need to reach nearly 160,000.
extraction_rationale: This specifies a concrete scale of intervention for retrofit deployment. Although framed as a requirement, it is sufficiently specific to count as a policy-relevant action benchmark.

policy_statement: Minimum Energy Efficiency Standards should be set at EPC C across all building types with effective enforcement.

extraction_rationale: This is a specific regulatory intervention with a named standard and enforcement mechanism, clearly qualifying as a policy.

extraction_rationale: This is a resource-mobilization commitment tied to a quantified investment need. It is somewhat broad on mechanism, but still qualifies because it calls for new policies to unlock a defined capital requirement.

policy_statement: Residual emissions of about 10 per cent will need to be offset through negative emissions technologies such as carbon capture and storage or tree planting.

extraction_rationale: This is a concrete mitigation approach for residual emissions, with a quantified residual share and named interventions. Tree planting is explicitly stated as an offset mechanism.

policy_statement: Strategy 1: Decarbonize the Energy Supply.
source_quote:
The Draft 2045 CAP is organized around 10 primary strategies that would be implemented by 25 measures and additional implementing actions that include new ordinances, policies, resolutions, programs, incentives, and outreach and education activities, which together would achieve the estimated reduction in GHG emissions presented above.

## 2.6.2.1 Strategy 1: Decarbonize the Energy Supply
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella strategy with multiple measures listed beneath it, so it qualifies as a parent policy under the hierarchy rules. It is a formal climate action strategy aimed at reducing emissions.

parent_statement: Strategy 1: Decarbonize the Energy Supply
policy_statement: Develop a sunset strategy for all oil and gas operations, with performance objectives to reduce oil and gas operations 40 percent below 2015 levels by 2030, 60 percent by 2035, and 80 percent by 2045.
source_quote:
## Measure ES1: Develop a Sunset Strategy for All Oil and Gas Operations.

The performance objectives for Measure ES1 are to reduce oil and gas operations 40 percent below 2015 levels by 2030, 60 percent by 2035, and 80 percent by 2045.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific named measure with quantified reduction targets and deadlines, clearly qualifying as a policy. It is nested under Strategy 1, so it is a sub-policy.

parent_statement: Strategy 1: Decarbonize the Energy Supply
policy_statement: Procure zero-carbon electricity by achieving 100 percent municipal participation by 2025 and 96 percent community participation by 2030 in 100 percent renewable electricity service.
source_quote:
## Measure ES2: Procure Zero-Carbon Electricity.

The performance objectives for Measure ES2 are to achieve 100 percent participation in the CPA's Green Power option, Southern California Edison's (SCE's) Green Rate option, or other available 100 percent zero-carbon electricity service by 2030 for municipal accounts, and for community accounts to achieve 96 percent participation in the CPA's Green Power option, SCE's Green Rate option, or other available 100 percent zero-carbon electricity service by 2030 (accounting for an approximately 4 percent opt-out rate).
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete measure with explicit participation targets and a timeline. It is directly aimed at decarbonizing electricity supply and is listed under Strategy 1.

parent_statement: Strategy 1: Decarbonize the Energy Supply
policy_statement: Increase renewable energy production through rooftop solar on existing and new buildings, County facilities, and affordable housing developments, with quantified deployment targets through 2045.
source_quote:
## Measure ES3: Increase Renewable Energy Production.

The performance objectives for Measure ES3 are to: (1) install rooftop solar PV on 20 percent of existing residential buildings (multifamily and single-family), 25 percent by 2035, and 35 percent by 2045; (2) install rooftop solar PV on 15 percent of existing commercial buildings by 2030, 22 percent by 2035, and 32 percent by 2045; (3) install rooftop solar PV on 80 percent of new multi-family residential buildings by 2030, 85 percent by 2035, and 95 percent by 2045; (4) install rooftop solar PV installations on 40 percent of new commercial buildings by 2030, 50 percent by 2035, and 70 percent by 2045; (5) install 20,000 kilowatts of solar PV at County facilities by 2030; and (6) install rooftop solar PV at all affordable housing developments.
extraction_rationale: This is a detailed measure with multiple quantified targets and specific interventions. It is clearly a climate mitigation policy nested under Strategy 1.

parent_statement: Strategy 1: Decarbonize the Energy Supply
policy_statement: Increase energy resilience through community electricity storage and generation, resilience hubs, microgrids, and energy efficiency and resilience programs at critical facilities.
source_quote:
## Measure ES4: Increase Energy Resilience.

The performance objectives for Measure E4 are to: (1) achieve community electricity storage and generation capacity equal to the community-wide 24-hour average usage by 2035/2045; (2) establish a community resilience hub program to equip community-serving County facilities (e.g., libraries, recreation centers, senior centers); (3) provide solar and battery systems sufficient to support emergency cooling and other emergency functions; (4) locate at least one hub in each County district, with a focus on vulnerable populations; (5) install microgrids based on a feasibility study; and (6) obtain a grant and establish a program to support an energy efficiency and assurance program for facilities that are large energy users and support critical community functions.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific measure with named interventions and timelines. Its primary mechanism is resilience to grid disruptions, though it sits within an energy decarbonization strategy.

parent_statement: Strategy 1: Decarbonize the Energy Supply
policy_statement: Establish greenhouse gas requirements for new development and require new development to be consistent with the 2045 CAP through codes, ordinances, conditions of approval, and a consistency checklist.
source_quote:
## Measure ES5: Establish GHG Requirements for New Development.

The performance objective for Measure ES5 is to require that new development is consistent with the Draft 2045 CAP's goals and GHG emissions reduction targets and to develop reach codes, ordinances, and conditions of approval as needed to achieve this objective. All new development not requiring General Plan amendments shall be consistent with the Draft 2045 CAP.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory measure with explicit mechanisms including reach codes, ordinances, and conditions of approval. It clearly qualifies as a policy and is nested under Strategy 1.

policy_statement: Strategy 2: Increase Densities and Diversity of Land Uses Near Transit.
source_quote:
## 2.6.2.2 Strategy 2: Increase Densities and Diversity of Land Uses near Transit

Strategy 2 focuses on coordinating land use development that leads to outcomes associated with reduced vehicle miles traveled, such as increased densities near transit, jobs-housing balance, and strategically located land uses that can reduce travel distances for many trip purposes.
section_header: 2.6.2.2 Strategy 2: Increase Densities and Diversity of Land Uses near Transit
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella strategy with subordinate measures. It is a policy parent because it organizes multiple specific land use measures.

parent_statement: Strategy 2: Increase Densities and Diversity of Land Uses near Transit
policy_statement: Increase density near high-quality transit areas by achieving minimum dwelling unit densities, locating most residential and employment centers within one mile of transit, and increasing dwelling units within HQTAs.
source_quote:
## Measure T1: Increase Density near High-Quality Transit Areas.

The performance objectives for Measure T1 are to: (1) achieve a minimum of 20 dwelling units (DUs) per acre (maximum of 30-150 DUs per acre) for HQTAs; (2) locate a majority of residential and employment centers in the unincorporated Los Angeles County within 1 mile of an HQTA; and (3) achieve a 27 percent increase in dwelling units within HQTAs. These densities would be achieved through implementation of the Housing Element Update rezoning programs.
section_header: 2.6.2.2 Strategy 2: Increase Densities and Diversity of Land Uses near Transit
extraction_rationale: This is a specific measure with quantified density and siting targets. It is a sub-policy under Strategy 2 and directly addresses transportation-related efficiency through land use.

policy_statement: Develop land use plans to improve jobs-housing balance and mixed use by achieving a job density target and reducing community jobs-housing imbalance below 20 percent.
source_quote:
## Measure T2: Develop Land Use Plans Addressing Jobs-Housing Balance and Increase Mixed Use.

The performance objective for Measure T2 is to achieve a job density of 300 jobs per acre for all new projects with nonresidential development by 2030. For communities with an imbalance of jobs/housing (±20 percent), community plans will identify and quantify strategies for bringing that imbalance below 20 percent. This density would be achieved through implementation of the Housing Element Update rezoning programs.

source_quote:
## 2.6.2.3 Strategy 3: Reduce Single-Occupancy Vehicle Trips

Strategy 3 focuses on development of transportation networks that increase the accessibility, comfort, and convenience of active travel modes to help reduce trips made in single-occupancy vehicles.

source_quote:
## Measure T3: Expand Bicycle and Pedestrian Network to Serve Residential, Employment, and Recreational Trips.

The performance objective for Measure T3 is to increase bikeway miles by 300 percent by 2035. This measure also requires implementing the County Bicycle Master Plan and completing updates to County's Pedestrian Action Plan, Bicycle Master Plan, and Active Transportation Plans every five years.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific transportation infrastructure measure with a quantified target and named plans. It is a sub-policy under Strategy 3.

parent_statement: Strategy 3: Reduce Single-Occupancy Vehicle Trips

source_quote:
## Measure T4: Broaden Options for Transit, Active Transportation, and Alternative Modes of Transportation.

The performance objectives for Measure T4 are by 2030 to: (1) double transit service hours from 560,000 to 1.12 million; (2) install bus-only lanes and signal prioritization on all major transit thoroughfares; and (3) have a minimum of 75 percent of unincorporated Los Angeles County residents live within one-half mile of a bus or active transportation option;
extraction_rationale: This is a specific measure with quantified service and access targets. It is a sub-policy under Strategy 3 and directly addresses transportation efficiency.

policy_statement: Limit and remove parking minimums through parking supply reduction, unbundled parking costs, and parking pricing to encourage park-once behavior.
source_quote:
## Measure T5: Limit and Remove Parking Minimums.

The performance objectives for Measure T5 are to: (1) reduce parking stipulations to reduce parking supply and encourage transit use; (2) unbundle parking costs to reflect the cost of parking; and (3) implement parking pricing to encourage 'park-once' behavior.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific parking reform measure with named interventions. It is a sub-policy under Strategy 3 and qualifies as a policy because it specifies concrete planning tools.

policy_statement: Strategy 4: Institutionalize Low-Carbon Transportation.
source_quote:
## 2.6.2.4 Strategy 4: Institutionalize Low-Carbon Transportation

Motorized vehicles needed for travel must transition to zero-carbon and near-zero-carbon technologies, such as EVs and zero-emission vehicles (ZEVs).
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella strategy with multiple transportation decarbonization measures beneath it. It qualifies as a parent policy.

parent_statement: Strategy 4: Institutionalize Low-Carbon Transportation
policy_statement: Increase zero-emission vehicle market share and reduce gasoline and diesel fuel sales through fleet targets and EV charging station deployment targets through 2045.
source_quote:
## Measure T6: Increase ZEV Market Share and Reduce Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Sales.

The performance objectives for Measure T6 are to: (1) increase the fleetwide percentage of light-duty vehicles in the unincorporated Los Angeles County that are ZEVs to 30 percent by 2030, 50 percent by 2035, and 90 percent by 2045; (2) increase the sales of new light-duty vehicles in the unincorporated Los Angeles County that are ZEVs to 68 percent by 2030 and 100 percent by 2035; (3) install 37,000 total new public and private shared EVCSs (including EVCSs at County facilities and properties) by 2030, 74,000 by 2035, and 140,000 by 2045; and (4) install 5,000 total new EVCSs at County facilities and properties by 2030, 10,000 by 2035, and 25,000 by 2045.
extraction_rationale: This is a detailed measure with multiple quantified targets for vehicle electrification and charging infrastructure. It is a sub-policy under Strategy 4.

parent_statement: Strategy 4: Institutionalize Low-Carbon Transportation
policy_statement: Electrify County fleet vehicles, including bus and shuttle fleets by 2035 and light-duty fleet vehicles through 2045.
source_quote:
## Measure T7: Electrify County Fleet Vehicles.

The performance objectives for Measure T7 are to: (1) electrify the County bus and shuttle fleets by 2035; (2) increase the fleetwide percentage of light-duty vehicles in the Countyowned fleet that are ZEVs to 35 percent by 2030, 60 percent by 2035, and 100 percent by 2045; and (3) support the state's goal that all new light-duty vehicle fleet purchases, with certain exceptions, will be ZEVs.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific fleet electrification measure with quantified targets and deadlines. It is a sub-policy under Strategy 4.

parent_statement: Strategy 4: Institutionalize Low-Carbon Transportation
policy_statement: Accelerate freight decarbonization through medium- and heavy-duty ZEV targets, drayage truck electrification, and charging infrastructure requirements for warehouse loading docks.
source_quote:
## Measure T8: Accelerate Freight Decarbonization.

The performance objectives for Measure T8 are to: (1) increase the fleetwide percentage of medium-duty and heavy-duty vehicles in the unincorporated Los Angeles County that are ZEVs to 40 percent by 2030, 60 percent by 2035, and 90 percent by 2045; (2) increase the fleetwide percentage of medium-duty and heavy-duty trucks in the County-owned fleet that are ZEVs to 50 percent by 2030, 70 percent by 2035, and 95 percent by 2045; (3) ensure that 100 percent of the drayage truck fleet is ZEV by 2035; (4) ensure that 100 percent of sales of medium- and heavy-duty trucks are ZEVs by 2045; (5) require that all new warehouse loading docks have EVCSs by 2030; and (6) require that all existing warehouse loading docks have EVCSs by 2030.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific freight decarbonization measure with multiple quantified targets and infrastructure requirements. It is a sub-policy under Strategy 4.

parent_statement: Strategy 4: Institutionalize Low-Carbon Transportation
policy_statement: Expand use of zero-emission technologies for off-road vehicles and equipment through fleet targets for off-road and construction, agriculture, and manufacturing equipment.
source_quote:

The performance objectives for Measure T9 are to: (1) increase the fleetwide percentage of off-road fleet and equipment in the unincorporated Los Angeles County that are ZEVs to 20 percent by 2030, 50 percent by 2035, and 95 percent by 2045; and (2) increase the fleetwide percentage of construction, agriculture, and manufacturing equipment in the unincorporated Los Angeles County that are ZEVs to 50 percent by 2030, 75 percent by 2035, and 100 percent by 2045.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific measure with quantified targets for off-road equipment electrification. It is a sub-policy under Strategy 4.

policy_statement: Strategy 5: Decarbonize Buildings.
source_quote:
## 2.6.2.5 Strategy 5: Decarbonize Buildings

Building decarbonization requires two complementary components: procuring clean, renewable sources of energy and shifting building energy loads for heating and cooking to electricity or renewable fuels rather than fossil fuels.
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella strategy with multiple building measures beneath it. It qualifies as a parent policy.

parent_statement: Strategy 5: Decarbonize Buildings

source_quote:
## Measure E1: Transition Existing Buildings to All-Electric.

The primary performance objectives for Measure E1 are to: (1) electrify 25 percent of the existing residential buildings by 2030, 40 percent by 2035, and 80 percent by 2045; (2) electrify 15 percent of the existing nonresidential buildings by 2030, 25 percent by 2035, and 60 percent by 2045; and (3) require zero net energy (ZNE) for 50 percent of all major renovations by 2030, 75 percent by 2035, and 100 percent by 2045.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific measure with quantified electrification and ZNE targets. It is a sub-policy under Strategy 5.

parent_statement: Strategy 5: Decarbonize Buildings
policy_statement: Standardize all-electric new development by requiring all applicable new buildings to be all-electric and most new buildings to be zero net energy by 2030 and beyond.
source_quote:

The performance objectives for Measure E2 are to: (1) require that all applicable new buildings are all-electric (taking into consideration the varying climate, geography, infrastructure, and sole-source dependency challenges that rural communities and unique industries may face), such that 90 percent of new residential and nonresidential buildings are all-electric by 2030, 95 percent by 2035, and 100 percent by 2045; and (2) require that all applicable new residential and nonresidential buildings are ZNE, such that 90 percent of new residential and nonresidential are ZNE by in 2030.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory measure with quantified targets for all-electric and ZNE buildings. It is a sub-policy under Strategy 5.

parent_statement: Strategy 5: Decarbonize Buildings
policy_statement: Implement other building decarbonization actions by increasing biomethane in the gas mix, using low-carbon concrete, and replacing high-global-warming-potential refrigerants.

The performance objectives of Measure E3 are to: (1) increase the proportion of biomethane in the utility natural gas mix to 20 percent by 2030, 30 percent by 2035, and 80 percent by 2045; (2) use low-carbon, carbon-neutral, or negative-carbon concrete for all new construction; and (3) replace high-global-warming-potential refrigerants with lowglobal-warming-potential refrigerants 15 percent by 2030, 25 percent by 2035, and 50 percent by 2045.

The performance objective of Measure E4 is to reduce building Energy Use Intensity (thousand British thermal units per square foot) below 2015 levels by 20 percent for residential, 15 percent for industrial, and 25 percent for commercial by 2030; 25 percent for residential and industrial and 35 percent for commercial by 2035; and 50 percent for residential, industrial, and commercial by 2045.

policy_statement: Strategy 7: Conserve Water.
source_quote:
## 2.6.2.7 Strategy 7: Conserve Water

The GHG emissions associated with water consumption are the result of the electricity and natural gas used to pump, treat, and convey water. Strategy 7 aims to reduce GHG emissions by decreasing the total amount of water consumed, as well as the energy intensity of the water consumed.
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella strategy with subordinate water measures. It qualifies as a parent policy.

parent_statement: Strategy 7: Conserve Water
policy_statement: Increase use of recycled water and gray water systems to meet Countywide, agricultural, and industrial water demand targets and implement direct potable reuse by 2025.
source_quote:
## Measure E5: Increase Use of Recycled Water and Gray Water Systems.

The performance objectives of Measure E5 are to: (1) meet 25 percent of total unincorporated Los Angeles County water demand with recycled water, gray water, or potable reuse by 2025, 50 percent by 2030, and 90 percent by 2045; (2) meet 30 percent of water demand for agricultural and industrial uses with recycled water or gray water by 2025, 50 percent by 2030, and 80 percent by 2045; and (3) implement a successful direct potable reuse project by 2025.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific water reuse measure with quantified targets and a deadline for direct potable reuse. It is a sub-policy under Strategy 7.

parent_statement: Strategy 7: Conserve Water
policy_statement: Reduce indoor and outdoor water consumption through total water use, landscaping water use, and municipal water consumption targets through 2045.
source_quote:
## Measure E6: Reduce Indoor and Outdoor Water Consumption.

The performance objectives of Measure E6 are to: (1) reduce total water use to less than 110 gallons per capita per day (GPCD) by 2030, 100 GPCD by 2035, and 85 GPCD by 2045; (2) reduce outdoor landscaping water use to 10 percent by 2030, 20 percent by 2035, and 50 percent by 2045; and (3) reduce municipal water consumption 10 percent by 2030, 20 percent by 2035, and 50 percent by 2045.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific water conservation measure with quantified targets and deadlines. It is a sub-policy under Strategy 7.

## Short-term objectives 2020:

The Municipality is willing to develop initiatives to reduce energy consumption, but a consistent plan needs to be implemented. More efforts should be done in raising staff awareness on simple change of behaviour to save energy without significant investment:

- -Open curtains and window shutters during daytime to avoid artificial lighting when outside air temperature is between 22°C and 27°C,
- -Keep the inside air temperature between 24°C - 25°C even in hot period to ensure good comfort all year long and make strong cut in energy consumption,
- -Avoid elevator and choosing staircase when going up or down one or two floors, only allow employee with health problems to use elevators,
- -Turn off electric equipment at end of working time or when not actually used, and
- -Unplug all electricity cables from wall's sockets as this could save about 5% of the energy use.

extraction_rationale: This is a clear quantified emissions-reduction target with baseline and deadlines, making it a policy commitment. It is communitywide and standalone rather than a sub-action.

policy_statement: City and County government operations will reduce building emissions 20% by 2020, 55% by 2035, and 80% by 2050, and fleet vehicle emissions 15% by 2020, 45% by 2035, and 80% by 2050.
source_quote:
Memphis and Shelby County should set GHG reduction targets that exceed the community-wide targets (see Chapter 1). Proposed reduction targets for both City and County government operations are as follows:

| Year   | Reduction Targets   | Reduction Targets   |
|--------|---------------------|---------------------|
|        | Buildings           | Fleet Vehicles      |
| 2020   | 20%                 | 15%                 |
| 2035   | 55%                 | 45%                 |
| 2050   | 80%                 | 80%                 |
section_header: LEADING BY EXAMPLE: LOCAL GOVERNMENT INVENTORY, REDUCTION TARGETS AND RECOMMENDATIONS
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified target for government operations with explicit percentages and years. Although phrased as 'should set,' it functions as the plan's formal recommended target.

policy_statement: Improve energy efficiency of buildings and key infrastructure through a package of building, housing, outreach, lighting, and retrofit financing actions.
source_quote: Emissions from energy use in buildings and stationary infrastructure make up the largest source of greenhouse gas emissions in the Memphis area. Commercial/institutional and residential buildings alone make up 41% of total community-wide emissions. While transitioning to cleaner, renewable sources of energy is an important part of reducing emissions, improving energy efficiency in new and existing buildings and infrastructure is also essential to achieving a more sustainable, prosperous, and equitable region.
section_header: IMPROVE ENERGY EFFICIENCY OF BUILDINGS AND KEY INFRASTRUCTURE
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella action area with multiple listed priority actions beneath it, so it qualifies as a parent policy rather than a standalone individual action.

parent_statement: Improve energy efficiency of buildings and key infrastructure
policy_statement: Codify and implement green building standards by 2022 with 100% compliance by 2025, including LEED Silver or Net Zero standards for new municipal buildings and major renovations.
source_quote:
Objective: Codify and implement green building standards by 2022, with 100% compliance by 2025

Require that all new municipal buildings and major renovations for the City and County meet LEED Silver or Net Zero Energy standards. Adopt green building and energy codes that improve upon the requirements of model codes; consider standards such as the International Green Construction Code, ASHRAE Standard 189.1, and stretch codes implemented in other jurisdictions.
section_header: Priority Action E.1: Implement Green Building Standards and Incentivize Innovative Green Building Design
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete regulatory commitment with deadlines and named standards. It clearly qualifies as a policy due to code adoption and compliance targets.

parent_statement: Improve energy efficiency of buildings and key infrastructure
policy_statement: Increase the number of low-income households served by weatherization and retrofit programs by 500% over 10 years and target a 30% reduction in household energy use.
source_quote:
Objective: Increase the number of low-income households served by weatherization and retrofit programs annually by 500% over 10 years, with a 30% target reduction in energy usage per household.

Aggressively pursue additional funding sources - both public and private - to expand existing weatherization programs for low-income residents. Leverage existing efforts such as the Healthy Homes Partnership (HHP), the Green & Healthy Homes Initiative (GHHI), and other public and private energy efficiency investments to improve coordination and maximize the benefit of existing programs.
section_header: Priority Action E.2: Improve Low-Income Housing Energy Efficiency
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified programmatic commitment with a clear target population, scale-up target, and intervention type. It is a sub-action under the broader energy efficiency action area.

parent_statement: Improve energy efficiency of buildings and key infrastructure
policy_statement: Reduce average electricity consumption in residential and commercial sectors by at least 10% through expanded outreach, education, and energy challenge programs.
source_quote:
Objective: Attain a 10% or greater reduction in average electricity consumption for residential and commercial sectors

This priority action aims to reduce energy use in existing residential and commercial buildings through outreach and education campaigns and an energy saving challenge. Depending on resources and capacity, the two sectors can be targeted at the same time or separately.
section_header: Priority Action E.3: Enhance and Expand Energy Outreach and Education Programs
extraction_rationale: This contains a quantified reduction objective and specific intervention mechanism. While softer than a regulation, it is still a defined programmatic commitment.

parent_statement: Improve energy efficiency of buildings and key infrastructure
policy_statement: Replace all existing non-LED streetlights and leased outdoor lighting with LED bulbs by 2030 or sooner, beginning in 2025.
source_quote:
Objective: Replace all existing non-LED streetlights and leased outdoor lighting with LED bulbs by 2030 or sooner, starting in 2025

This action aims to replace all non-LED streetlights and leased outdoor lights in Memphis and Shelby County with LED bulbs. Implementation of this action will involve developing a full life cycle cost/benefit analysis of making the switch to LED bulbs, identifying the best financing model for the upfront replacement costs, and determining an efficient and feasible schedule for bidding, contracting and installation.
section_header: Priority Action E.4: Retrofit Outdoor Streetlights to LED
extraction_rationale: This is a specific infrastructure intervention with a deadline and implementation pathway. It clearly qualifies as a policy.

parent_statement: Improve energy efficiency of buildings and key infrastructure
policy_statement: By 2025, equip 15% of residences with energy-efficient space heating, cooling equipment, and major appliances through financing and rebate mechanisms.
source_quote:
Objective: By 2025, 15% of all residences will have energy-efficient space heating and cooling equipment and major appliances.

This priority action seeks to achieve installation of energy-efficient heating and cooling equipment and major appliances in 15% of existing residences by 2025. Implementation of this action will involve advocating for and providing additional financial tools and incentives for residential enegy efficiency retrofits.
section_header: Priority Action E.5: Expand Financing Options for Residential Energy Efficiency Retrofits
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified retrofit target tied to named financial mechanisms. It is policy-relevant both as a deployment target and as a financing initiative.

policy_statement: Transform the energy supply by increasing carbon-free and renewable electricity in the Memphis area.
source_quote: Turning from a focus on cutting the amount of energy that we consume, this section directly addresses how we can increase the amount of clean, renewable sources in our energy supply. Greening our electric grid has the highest potential for achieving deep greenhouse gas emissions reductions, and the costs for renewable energy sources such as wind, solar, and biomass have decreased dramatically over the last several decades along with substantial improvements to the technology involved in these power sources.
extraction_rationale: This is a named action area with a distinct umbrella objective and one listed priority action beneath it, so it should be treated as a parent.

parent_statement: Transform our energy supply
policy_statement: Increase carbon-free electricity supply to 80% by 2035 and 100% by 2050, focusing on renewable sources such as solar and wind.
source_quote:
Objective: Increase the percentage of carbon-free energy in our electricity supply to 80% by 2035 and 100% by 2050, focusing on renewable sources such as solar and wind

This action aims to increase the share of carbon-free energy in our electricity supply by focusing on renewable sources such as wind and solar. With ambitious goals of 80% carbon-free energy by 2035 and 100% carbon-free energy by 2050 (from a 2020 baseline of 56%), implementation of this priority action will need to take a comprehensive approach.
section_header: Priority Action E.6: Decarbonize the Electric Grid with Renewable Energy
extraction_rationale: This is a clear quantified energy-supply target with dates and technologies. It is a direct mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Increase green infrastructure and community resilience through urban tree canopy expansion and alignment of mitigation and adaptation efforts.
source_quote: Reducing our community's contributions to climate change will take many different forms. While the previous sections looked at improving energy efficiency and increasing clean, renewable energy sources, this section explores strategies that can help us both mitigate our impact on climate change and adapt to climate risks that affect the Memphis area.
section_header: INCREASE GREEN INFRASTRUCTURE AND COMMUNITY RESILIENCE
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella action area with multiple subordinate priority actions. It is therefore a parent policy.

parent_statement: Increase green infrastructure and community resilience
policy_statement: Increase urban tree canopy coverage countywide to 60% by 2050 through planting, code updates, staffing, and partnerships.
source_quote:
Objective: Plant or replant trees with the intention of increasing urban tree canopy to 60% coverage countywide by 2050

This action aims to increase tree canopy coverage in the county from 37% to 60% by 2050. Based on the 2015 Memphis Regional Canopy Action Plan, implementation of this action will involve strengthening and enforcing standards that protect existing trees and encourage planting of native and other appropriate species to expand canopy cover, as well as planning, coordination, and outreach programs that focus on providing the resources and support to achieve this target.
section_header: Priority Action E.7: Nurture and Expand the Urban Tree Canopy
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified land-cover target with specific implementation mechanisms. It is a classic nature-based climate policy.

parent_statement: Increase green infrastructure and community resilience
policy_statement: Identify and prioritize cross-cutting strategies that jointly advance climate mitigation and adaptation, including resilience investments and demonstration projects.
source_quote:
Objective: Identify and prioritize cross-cutting strategies for climate change mitigation and adaptation

This action aims to identify and prioritize cross-cutting strategies that address climate change mitigation and adaptation. Many of the strategies and recommendations in this plan have both mitigation and adaptation benefits.
section_header: Priority Action E.8: Align Climate Mitigation and Climate Adaptation Efforts
extraction_rationale: Although not quantified, this is still a named intervention with specific implementation steps and institutional commitments. It is somewhat broader and more process-oriented than other actions, but still qualifies as a policy because it directs investments and implementation.

policy_statement: Shift to low-carbon transportation modes and reduce reliance on motor vehicles through land use, complete streets, transit, and demand management.
source_quote: Reducing emissions from the transportation sector starts with creating conditions where more trips can be completed by low-carbon and zero-carbon modes such as walking, biking, and transit. Transportation, in particular, is closely tied to land use and urban form.
section_header: SHIFT TO LOW-CARBON TRANSPORTATION MODES AND REDUCE RELIANCE ON MOTOR VEHICLES
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella transportation action area with several listed sub-actions, so it is a parent policy.

parent_statement: Shift to low-carbon transportation modes and reduce reliance on motor vehicles
policy_statement: Encourage denser, mixed-use development to reduce vehicle trips and support walking, biking, and transit through Memphis 3.0 implementation and code updates.
source_quote:
Objective: Encourage denser, mixed-use development to reduce vehicle trips and support walking, biking, and transit

This action sets out the broad goal of fostering land use patterns and urban development that better support walking, biking, and transit. Implementation of this action will largely involve following the vision and growth strategy laid out in the Memphis 3.0 Comprehensive Plan.
section_header: Priority Action T.1: Implement Land Use Patterns that Support Active Transportation and Transit
extraction_rationale: This is a specific planning and regulatory commitment tied to land use and zoning changes. While not numerically quantified, it names concrete interventions and therefore qualifies.

parent_statement: Shift to low-carbon transportation modes and reduce reliance on motor vehicles
policy_statement: Convert 10% of vehicle trips to walking and bicycling by 2030 and 40% by 2050, supported by complete streets investments and $20 million in annual bike/ped funding.
source_quote:
Objective: Starting in 2020, convert 10% of vehicle trips to pedestrian and bicycling modes by 2030, and increase this percentage linearly to 40% of vehicle trips by 2050

Establish a dedicated annual funding source of $20 million for pedestrian and bicycle safety improvements, and implement priority projects identified in the Memphis Pedestrian and School Safety Action Plan and the Memphis MPO's Regional Bicycle & Pedestrian Plan.
section_header: Priority Action T.2: Create Complete Streets that Prioritize Walking and Bicycling
extraction_rationale: This is a strong policy commitment because it includes quantified mode-shift targets and a specified annual funding level.

parent_statement: Shift to low-carbon transportation modes and reduce reliance on motor vehicles
policy_statement: Fully implement the Memphis 3.0 Transit Vision by 2022, increase ridership and frequency, and convert MATA's entire fleet to electric by 2050.
source_quote:
Objective: Fully implement the Memphis 3.0 Transit Vision by 2022. Increase ridership and improve frequency to meet long-range (2040/2050) ridership objectives. Convert MATA's entire fleet to electric by 2050.

Provide dedicated annual funding to MATA and increase immediate annual funding by $30 million to implement the Memphis 3.0 Transit Vision.
section_header: Priority Action T.3: Enhance Public Transit
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified transit and fleet-electrification commitment with a specific funding commitment. It clearly qualifies as a policy.

parent_statement: Shift to low-carbon transportation modes and reduce reliance on motor vehicles
policy_statement: Reduce drive-alone commute trips by 10% by 2022 and 40% by 2050 through employer transportation demand management programs and parking reforms.
source_quote:
Objective: Reduce drive-alone commute trips 10% by 2022 and 40% by 2050.

Implement Transportation Demand Management programs at all major employers (500+ employees) in the Memphis area and encourage the inclusion of specific TDM strategies such as: Create incentives for multi-modal trips and travel; Increase parking management and fees; Increase promotions and incentives for carpooling/vanpooling.
section_header: Priority Action T.4: Reduce Commute Trips through Transportation Demand Management
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified travel-demand target with named implementation mechanisms. It is a clear policy action.

policy_statement: Set the stage for vehicle electrification through EV adoption targets, charging infrastructure, and supportive codes and planning.
source_quote: While reducing passenger vehicle trips and increasing transit, walking, and bicycling trips are the focus of this plan, electric vehicles also present opportunities for lowering carbon emissions from the transportation sector. The goals and strategies in this section seek to support increased adoption of electric vehicles through planning efforts, removing barriers to the development of charging infrastructure, and ensuring that local government leads by example in transitioning its fleets to electric.
section_header: SET THE STAGE FOR VEHICLE ELECTRIFICATION
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella action area with one detailed priority action beneath it, so it is a parent.

parent_statement: Set the stage for vehicle electrification
policy_statement: Increase passenger EV travel to 5% by 2025, 30% by 2035, and 50% by 2050, and freight EV travel to 3%, 20%, and 50% on the same timeline, while building charging infrastructure and transitioning government fleets.
source_quote:
Objective: Increase passenger vehicle travel using electric vehicles to 5% by 2025; 30% by 2035; and 50% by 2050. Increase freight vehicle travel using electric vehicles to 3% by 2025; 20% by 2035; and 50% by 2050.

To lead by example, Memphis and Shelby County government should commit to transitioning their fleets to electric and begin building necessary charging infrastructure.
section_header: Priority Action T.5: Encourage Electric Vehicle Adoption and the Development of Charging Infrastructure
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified technology-adoption target with explicit infrastructure and fleet commitments. It is a direct mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Reduce waste and move toward a zero-waste future through organic diversion, waste reduction, and inorganic diversion actions.
source_quote: This Action Area focuses on three main priority actions including diverting greater amounts of organic and inorganic waste sent to landfills as well as reducing the overall amount of waste generated in Shelby County. Incentivizing practices to use waste products in the local economy and generate revenue from these waste streams is central to these efforts.
section_header: REDUCE WASTE AND MOVE TOWARD A ZERO-WASTE FUTURE
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella waste action area with multiple subordinate actions, so it is a parent policy.

parent_statement: Reduce waste and move toward a zero-waste future
policy_statement: Cut the portion of yard and wood waste sent to landfills in half by 2035 through curbside composting, facility expansion, and state landfill regulation advocacy.
source_quote:
Objective: By 2035, cut the portion of yard and wood waste in municipal solid waste destined for landfills in half relative to 2016.

Implement a municipal curbside composting program for yard waste that includes fee changes to incentivize composting. Expand municipal composting facility capacity or consider contracting with a private composting facility for this service.
section_header: Priority Action W.1 Divert Greater Amounts of Organic Waste from Landfills
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified waste-diversion target with specific municipal program actions. It clearly qualifies as a policy.

parent_statement: Reduce waste and move toward a zero-waste future
policy_statement: By 2030, reduce paper and cardboard in landfill-bound municipal solid waste from commercial, institutional, and industrial sectors by 20% and food waste by 10%.
source_quote:
Objective: By 2030, achieve a 20% reduction in the share of paper and cardboard in the municipal solid waste stream from commercial, institutional, and industrial (cii) sectors sent to landfills. By 2030, achieve a 10% reduction in the share of food waste in the municipal solid waste stream sent to landfills from cii sectors.

Consider new regulations that require private waste hauling companies to offer recycling and food waste composting services.
section_header: Priority Action W.2 Reduce the Overall Amount of Waste Generated
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified waste-reduction target with a possible regulatory mechanism. It is a clear policy commitment.

parent_statement: Reduce waste and move toward a zero-waste future
policy_statement: Increase diversion of inorganic materials, especially construction and demolition waste and plastics, from municipal solid waste landfills through code revisions, campaigns, and state advocacy.
source_quote:
Objective: Increase the diversion rate of inorganic materials, namely construction and demolition waste as well as plastics, from disposal in municipal solid waste landfills.

Reduce commercial and demolition waste by revising the building code so permitting would require the reduction, reuse, and recycling of materials. Improve and develop public awareness and behavior change campaigns in the short-term to minimize single-use plastics.
section_header: Priority Action W.3 Divert Greater Amounts of Inorganic Materials from Landfills
extraction_rationale: This is a named intervention with specific regulatory and programmatic mechanisms. It lacks a numeric target but still qualifies because it includes code revision and concrete actions.

policy_statement: Promote a cultural shift in the community's approach to waste through tire management and education/outreach actions.
source_quote: In order to improve waste practices in the Memphis region, this action area seeks to promote cultural changes and better decision making in regards to waste production and disposal choices. Tire management and collection practices were identified as a priority action through stakeholder technical advisory group meetings, and as such was developed more fully with that stakeholder input.
section_header: PROMOTE A CULTURAL SHIFT IN OUR APPROACH TO WASTE
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella action area with two listed sub-actions. It should be extracted as a parent.

parent_statement: Promote a cultural shift in our approach to waste
policy_statement: Increase use of recycled tire materials in building projects and reduce improper tire disposal through targeted pickup, recycling, and tracking programs.
source_quote:
Objective: Increase the use of recycled tire materials in building projects and reduce improper tire disposal through targeted programs

Reuse tires to offset carbon emissions from the production of other materials, for example using tires as a roofing material rather than asphalt, which is emissions intensive to produce. Reduce improper tire disposal through reworking current pickup practices and incentivizing recycling programs.
section_header: Priority Action W.4 Improve Tire Management and Collection Practices
extraction_rationale: This is a specific intervention with named programmatic actions. It is somewhat less climate-direct than other policies, but still qualifies because it specifies targeted programs and material substitution.

parent_statement: Promote a cultural shift in our approach to waste
policy_statement: Launch waste outreach and education campaigns to inform residents about waste management programs and proper disposal, with needs assessments, targets, and monitoring.
source_quote:
Objective: Launch outreach and education campaigns to inform and support residents about waste management in their community, including programs they can take part in and information regarding how to properly dispose of waste.

Conduct informal needs assessments with area stakeholders to determine marketing or social behavior change campaigns most needed in the region in 2020. Create specific and targeted goals and outputs to assess impact.
section_header: Priority Action W.5 Expand Education and Outreach Efforts to Encourage Behavior Change
extraction_rationale: This is a named program with explicit implementation steps and monitoring commitments. It is less direct on emissions but still a concrete policy action.

policy_statement: Improve practices and technology at wastewater treatment facilities and landfills to reduce methane and biogas emissions.
source_quote: In addition to actions that focus on waste reduction and changing community approaches to waste, it is important to consider actions that reduce emissions from existing landfills and wastewater treatment plants (WWTP). Given that both landfills and wastewater treatment plant activities release biogas, these practices provide potential for emissions reduction.
section_header: IMPROVE PRACTICES AND TECHNOLOGY AT WASTEWATER TREATMENT FACILITIES AND LANDFILLS
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella action area with one detailed sub-action beneath it, so it is a parent.

parent_statement: Improve practices and technology at wastewater treatment facilities and landfills
policy_statement: Extend biogas controls to Class III and IV landfills, raise Class I landfill biogas capture from 75% to 85% by 2020, and install methane recovery systems in all Shelby County wastewater treatment plants by 2035.
source_quote:
Objective: Extend the use of biogas controls to Class III and Class IV landfills. Improve the biogas capture rate at Class I landfills from 75% to 85% by 2020, and promote greater methane recovery over biogas flaring.

Wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) operators can plan to install methane recovery systems in all facilities within Shelby County by the end of 2035 with support from DPD and City government personnel.
section_header: Priority Action W.6 Enhance Methane Recovery and Landfill Gas Destruction
extraction_rationale: This is a highly specific and quantified emissions-control policy with deadlines and technical measures. It clearly qualifies.

policy_statement: The Office of Sustainability and Resilience will complete annual implementation progress reports, update greenhouse gas inventories at least every other year, and comprehensively update the plan every five years.
source_quote: The Office of Sustainability and Resilience will complete annual progress reports on plan implementation along with updated greenhouse gas inventories at least every other year. Since this is a long-range document, staff will need to lead a more comprehensive update of the plan every 5 years.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete governance and monitoring commitment with explicit reporting and update intervals. It is climate-relevant as an implementation policy, though not itself an emissions-reduction measure.

policy_statement: City and County government should align capital improvement program processes and purchasing policies with climate action goals, including life-cycle cost assessments for projects.
source_quote: City and County government should first look at existing Capital Improvement Program (CIP) processes to see how these large capital investments can better align with climate action and GHG reduction goals. In addition, City and County government should work toward incorporating life-cycle cost assessments into the evaluation of CIP projects and the development of purchasing policies.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete planning and procurement commitment tied to climate goals. It is somewhat procedural, but it specifies institutional changes and therefore qualifies.

policy_statement: City and County government should pursue innovative financing tools such as Pay for Success and Environmental Impact Bonds for climate mitigation and adaptation projects.
source_quote: The scale of the issue and our corresponding climate action goals will also require the pursuit of new, innovative financing tools. For example, Pay for Success (PFS) - or Social Impact Bonds - offer one potential mechanism for implementing actions that have both social and GHG reduction impacts. In addition, Environmental Impact Bonds represent another private sector tool that can be leveraged to finance municipal projects that advance climate mitigation and adaptation.
extraction_rationale: This is a financing-policy commitment naming specific instruments to fund climate action. It qualifies as a policy because it identifies deliberate financing mechanisms, though it is broader than a budget appropriation.

policy_statement: Miami-Dade County commits to reduce communitywide greenhouse gas emissions 50% by 2030 from 2019 levels and achieve net zero by 2050.
source_quote: Officially launched on Oct. 27, 2021, this plan describes work taking place on multiple fronts to cut MiamiDade's greenhouse gas emissions 50 percent by 2030 from 2019 levels, with the goal of achieving net zero by 2050. This Strategy reflects an unprecedented level of teamwork both within County government and throughout our entire community.
section_header: LETTER FROM MAYOR DANIELLA LEVINE CAVA
extraction_rationale: This is a clear quantified emissions target with deadlines, making it a core climate policy commitment.

policy_statement: Miami-Dade County commits under Race to Zero to reduce GHG emissions 50% by 2030 compared to 2019 levels and achieve net zero by 2050.
source_quote: On April 22, 2021, in commemoration of the 51st anniversary of Earth Day, Mayor Daniella Levine Cava announced Miami-Dade County's commitment to the international Race to Zero, along with over 4,500 other governments, businesses, investors, and academic institutions. This pledge is mobilizing communities to swiftly enact measures to reduce GHG emissions 50% by 2030 compared to 2019 levels and then progress forward to achieve net zero by 2050.
section_header: I N T R O D U C T I O N
extraction_rationale: This repeats and formalizes the countywide target through an international pledge; retained because it is a distinct formal commitment framework supporting the CAS targets.

policy_statement: The Climate Action Strategy will be updated every five years and progress will be reported annually to reflect advances and policy changes.
source_quote: Combined, the approaches will reduce GHG emissions from 36.4 million metric tons in 2019 to 24.5 million metric tons in 2030, a reduction of 11.9 MMT or 33%. While a gap remains to reach the goal of a 50% cut by 2030, progress will be reported on an annual basis and the Strategy will be updated every five-years to reflect technological advances and new state and federal energy and transportation policies.
section_header: SEVEN APPROACHES TO CUT EMISSIONS 50% BY 2030
extraction_rationale: This is a procedural implementation commitment with a defined reporting and update cycle. It is climate-relevant but not itself an emissions-reduction measure, so relevance is indirect.

policy_statement: Approach 1 commits Miami-Dade to benchmark, retune, and retrofit existing buildings to reduce building energy use and costs.
source_quote:
## 1. BENCHMARK, RETUNE AND RETROFIT EXISTING BUILDINGS

- BENCHMARK 1.3 BILLION SQUARE FEET COMMUNITYWIDE BY 2026
- RETUNE 1.1 BILLION SQUARE FOOTAGE OF COMMUNITY WIDE BUILDINGS BY 2030
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella initiative with multiple listed sub-targets, so it qualifies as a parent policy.

parent_statement: Benchmark, retune and retrofit existing buildings
policy_statement: Benchmark 1.3 billion square feet of communitywide buildings by 2026.
source_quote:
## 1. BENCHMARK, RETUNE AND RETROFIT EXISTING BUILDINGS

- BENCHMARK 1.3 BILLION SQUARE FEET COMMUNITYWIDE BY 2026
- RETUNE 1.1 BILLION SQUARE FOOTAGE OF COMMUNITY WIDE BUILDINGS BY 2030
extraction_rationale: Quantified target for a named intervention in existing buildings.

parent_statement: Benchmark, retune and retrofit existing buildings
policy_statement: Retune 1.1 billion square feet of communitywide buildings by 2030.
source_quote:
## 1. BENCHMARK, RETUNE AND RETROFIT EXISTING BUILDINGS

- BENCHMARK 1.3 BILLION SQUARE FEET COMMUNITYWIDE BY 2026
- RETUNE 1.1 BILLION SQUARE FOOTAGE OF COMMUNITY WIDE BUILDINGS BY 2030
extraction_rationale: Quantified target for retro-commissioning/retuning buildings.

parent_statement: Benchmark, retune and retrofit existing buildings
policy_statement: Retrofit 167,500 homes by 2030 to reduce energy costs 28%, prioritizing low- to moderate-income homes.
source_quote:
- RETUNE 1.1 BILLION SQUARE FOOTAGE OF COMMUNITY WIDE BUILDINGS BY 2030
-   RETROFIT 167,500 HOMES TO REDUCE ENERGY COSTS 28% PRIORITIZING LOW TO MODERATE INCOME (LMI) HOMES BY 2030
extraction_rationale: Specific quantified retrofit target with equity prioritization. Climate benefit is substantial though framed partly around energy costs.

policy_statement: Approach 2 commits Miami-Dade to expand renewable energy generation through on-site and off-site solar and utility-scale renewable participation.
source_quote:
## 2. EXPAND RENEWABLE ENERGY GENERATION

-   INSTALL 61,725 KW OF SOLAR ENERGY BY 2030 ON COUNTY BUILDINGS, LAND, AND WATER EQUIVALENT TO 7,498 HOMES' ELECTRICITY USE FOR ONE YEAR
-   INSTALL 794,000 KW OF SOLAR ENERGY BY 2030 ON COMMERCIAL AND RESIDENTIAL BUILDINGS EQUIVALENT TO 104,014 HOMES' ELECTRICITY USE FOR ONE YEAR
extraction_rationale: Named umbrella initiative with multiple sub-actions and targets.

parent_statement: Expand renewable energy generation
policy_statement: Install 61,725 kW of solar energy on County buildings, land, and water by 2030.
source_quote:
## 2. EXPAND RENEWABLE ENERGY GENERATION

-   INSTALL 61,725 KW OF SOLAR ENERGY BY 2030 ON COUNTY BUILDINGS, LAND, AND WATER EQUIVALENT TO 7,498 HOMES' ELECTRICITY USE FOR ONE YEAR
-   INSTALL 794,000 KW OF SOLAR ENERGY BY 2030 ON COMMERCIAL AND RESIDENTIAL BUILDINGS EQUIVALENT TO 104,014 HOMES' ELECTRICITY USE FOR ONE YEAR
extraction_rationale: Quantified renewable energy deployment target.

parent_statement: Expand renewable energy generation
policy_statement: Install 794,000 kW of solar energy on commercial and residential buildings by 2030.
source_quote:
-   INSTALL 61,725 KW OF SOLAR ENERGY BY 2030 ON COUNTY BUILDINGS, LAND, AND WATER EQUIVALENT TO 7,498 HOMES' ELECTRICITY USE FOR ONE YEAR
-   INSTALL 794,000 KW OF SOLAR ENERGY BY 2030 ON COMMERCIAL AND RESIDENTIAL BUILDINGS EQUIVALENT TO 104,014 HOMES' ELECTRICITY USE FOR ONE YEAR
-   MAXIMIZE PARTICIPATION IN UTILITY-SCALE RENEWABLE ENERGY PROGRAMS
extraction_rationale: Quantified communitywide solar deployment target.

parent_statement: Expand renewable energy generation
policy_statement: Maximize participation in utility-scale renewable energy programs.
source_quote:
-   INSTALL 794,000 KW OF SOLAR ENERGY BY 2030 ON COMMERCIAL AND RESIDENTIAL BUILDINGS EQUIVALENT TO 104,014 HOMES' ELECTRICITY USE FOR ONE YEAR
-   MAXIMIZE PARTICIPATION IN UTILITY-SCALE RENEWABLE ENERGY PROGRAMS
extraction_rationale: Specific named intervention, though less quantified than the solar targets.

policy_statement: Approach 3 commits Miami-Dade to build ultra-low energy buildings and reduce energy use intensity of new buildings.
source_quote:
## 3. BUILD ULTRA-LOW ENERGY BUILDINGS

- REDUCE THE ENERGY USE INTENSITY OF NEW BUILDINGS 20% BY 2030 BELOW 2020 LEVELS
extraction_rationale: Named umbrella initiative with a specific target and additional actions later in the section.

parent_statement: Build ultra-low energy buildings
policy_statement: Reduce the energy use intensity of new buildings 20% by 2030 below 2020 levels.
source_quote:
## 3. BUILD ULTRA-LOW ENERGY BUILDINGS

- REDUCE THE ENERGY USE INTENSITY OF NEW BUILDINGS 20% BY 2030 BELOW 2020 LEVELS
extraction_rationale: Quantified efficiency target for new buildings.

policy_statement: Approach 4 commits Miami-Dade to reduce transportation-related fuel consumption through mode shift, electrification, and emissions cuts at major transport hubs.
source_quote:
## 4. REDUCE TRANSPORTATION-RELATED FUEL CONSUMPTION

- SHIFT 10% OF TRANSPORTATION MODE AWAY FROM SINGLE OCCUPANT VEHICLES BY 2030
- ELECTRIFY THE COUNTY FLEET: 80% OF LIGHT VEHICLES AND 50% OF PUBLIC TRANSIT BUSES BY 2030
extraction_rationale: Named umbrella initiative with multiple sub-targets.

parent_statement: Reduce transportation-related fuel consumption
