Finance  the  Transition:  Create  a  regional  'green  lending' network  in  collaboration  with  CDFIs  and  private  banks to leverage federal and state grants and loans to make it easy for low to moderate income (LMI) homeowners and businesses to finance energy efficiency upgrades including weatherization,  solar,  and  electric  vehicle  infrastructure. These same tools can be used to finance other resilience projects  like  septic  to  sewer,  green  infrastructure,  and floodproofing.
extraction_rationale: This is explicitly a financing mechanism and therefore a financial instrument. It also explicitly includes resilience projects, supporting a secondary adaptation category.

policy_statement: Miami-Dade's Water and Sewer Department will build a HyBrTec biosolids-to-hydrogen pilot plant supported by a $1.15 million Florida Department of Environmental Protection grant.
source_quote: Miami-Dade County's Water and Sewer Department is building a HyBrTec biosolids-hydrogen pilot plant, supported by a $1.15 million Florida Department of Environmental Protection grant. The plant will test a new technology that convert biosolids from wastewater treatment to green hydrogen, carbon dioxide, and heat.
extraction_rationale: Specific pilot project with identified funding and technology. The grant supports the project, but the policy itself is the pilot plant build commitment rather than the grant instrument.

policy_statement: Namibia commits to reduce GHG emissions by 91% below the BAU scenario by 2030, equivalent to 21.996 MtCO2e.
source_quote:
Namibia commits to reduce its GHG emissions conditionally by 14% (under limited domestic and international support) and towards 77% (with substantial international support) in 2030 compared to the Business As Usual levels,  corresponding  to  a  total  reduction  by  21.996  MtCO2e.  Namibia  is  committed  to  combating  climate change and accelerating the transition to a climate-resilient, low-carbon sustainable mode of development.

Namibia continues to play a part in an effective global response to climate change. Namibia is to implement an economy-wide target to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from 91 per cent below 2015 levels by 2030.
extraction_rationale: This is a core national climate commitment with quantified targets and a deadline. Although the wording mixes unconditional and conditional shares and contains an apparent inconsistency on baseline phrasing, it clearly states a binding national mitigation target.

policy_statement: Namibia will replace the NCCSAP with an NDC Implementation Strategy and Action Plan for 2021-2030 to guide implementation, reporting, and monitoring of priority NDC activities.
source_quote: The NCCSAP will be replaced by the NDC Implementation Strategy and Action Plan for 2021-2030. This document  will  clarify  national  goals  and  objectives  regarding  climate  change  and  lay  out  a  plan  for implementing, reporting and monitoring a series of priority activities to implement the updated NDC.
section_header: 1.3.1 Building Namibia's Adaptive and Mitigative Capacities
extraction_rationale: This qualifies as a policy because it commits to a specific named planning instrument with a defined time period and implementation function. It is a governance/planning policy rather than a direct emissions or resilience measure.

policy_statement: Namibia's NDC Partnership Plan identifies government priority areas for implementing the NDC under the Paris Agreement.
source_quote:
Building off progress already made through Namibia's existing climate plans and policies, the Namibia NDC Partnership Plan identifies priority areas set by the government for implementation of its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) under the Paris Agreement. The Plan takes ongoing action into account but, more importantly, looks to the future for development partners to deliver on their responsibility in supporting the global south to fight climate change.

extraction_rationale: This is a listed sub-action under the NDC Partnership Plan. It is a climate governance commitment rather than a sectoral technical measure, but still qualifies as a policy due to its explicit implementation function.

policy_statement: Namibia targets a primarily renewable energy mix during the Harambee period and calls for international financing support for renewable energy.
source_quote: The Harambee Prosperity Plan (HPP) acknowledges climate change is a reality of our time. Although the degree of contribution to global warming varies, Namibia has committed to reducing carbon dioxide emissions into the atmosphere because our planet is at stake 8 . Namibia fully supports the goals of COP21. That is why, during the Harambee period, Namibia is targeting a primarily renewable energy mix. The International Community is called upon to support Namibia in financing renewable energy 9 .
extraction_rationale: This is a policy because it sets a directional energy target and explicitly links it to emissions reduction and renewable energy financing. The target is qualitative rather than numeric, but still concrete enough to qualify.

policy_statement: NDP5 includes an intermediate target to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 30% against BAU by 2022, supported by domestic monitoring and annual reporting.
source_quote:
For the first time in a National Development Plan (NDP5), Namibia included an intermediate emissions reduction target (Greenhouse gas emissions 30% reduction against Business As Usual projection, by 2022). This target is a carbon budget which the country can 'spend' in diverse ways by allocating emission rights and commitments among those sectors most responsible for greenhouse gas emissions.

NDP5 targets 10 are subject to domestic monitoring and annual reporting: The Government of Namibia will necessarily follow an emission monitoring and reporting system based on the rules of the Paris Agreement (which were agreed at COP24).
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified emissions target with a deadline and monitoring provisions, clearly meeting the extraction criteria. It is a distinct policy from the 2030 NDC target because it is an intermediate NDP5 target.

policy_statement: Namibia will aggressively mobilize funding for innovation addressing energy and water insecurity through multilateral mechanisms, bilateral relationships, and private-sector partnerships.
source_quote: The  transition  to  low  carbon  and  climate-resilient  economy  offers  considerable  opportunities  to  address challenges  such  as  energy  and  water  insecurity.  Namibia  will  seek  to  aggressively  mobilize  funding  for innovation in these areas through multilateral financing mechanisms such as the Green Climate Fund and Global Environment Facility, and through bilateral relationships and partnerships with the private sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete implementation commitment to mobilize funding through named channels. It is not itself a fund or subsidy, so it is not a financial instrument, but it is a policy commitment on climate finance mobilization.

policy_statement: Namibia aims to reduce electricity imports by 30% through 0.8 TWh of new renewable generation and 330 MW of solar PV per annum until 2030.
source_quote: In the energy sector, Namibia's National Renewable Energy Policy aims to drive emerging technologies that reduce  emissions  and  support  cleaner  practices.  The  goal  is  the  substitution  of  existing  higher  emission technologies  with  cleaner,  more  efficient,  and  lower-cost  technologies. Namibia's efforts in renewables will contribute to a 30% reduction equivalent in the quantity (2.668 TWh) of electricity imported in 2018 which would result in 0.8 TWh (800 GWh) in new RE generation of 330 MW of Solar PV per annum until 2030.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified renewable energy deployment and import-substitution commitment with a deadline. It is directly tied to emissions reduction and therefore qualifies as a mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Namibia will use fuel switching and equipment upgrades to replace inefficient fuels with cleaner alternatives such as hydrogen or electric energy.
source_quote: Further measures that will build on Namibia's existing efforts include f uel switching to replace inefficient fuels with cleaner and economical alternatives, such as substituting hydrocarbons for hydrogen or electric energy. Complimented by modern equipment upgrades, fuel switching is a simple approach that Namibia will use in reducing energy consumption and costs for end-users, while also curbing carbon emissions.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific named intervention with explicit technological mechanisms. It qualifies despite lacking a standalone numeric target in this paragraph because it commits to a defined mitigation action.

policy_statement: Namibia will use fuel economy and GHG emission standards for light-duty vehicles to improve fuel consumption and reduce transport emissions.
source_quote: Fuel economy (FE) and greenhouse gas (GHG) emission standards regulations will be used as one of the main instruments available to Namibia to achieve significant improvements in fuel consumption and GHG emissions from light-duty vehicles (LDVs).  These  standards  through  continued  development  and  application  of  fuel-efficient  technologies  will reduce carbon emissions by 3% of total GHG emissions.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory policy with an explicit mechanism and quantified emissions effect. It clearly qualifies as a climate policy and includes both standards and expected emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Namibia will implement early action to reduce HFCs and introduce climate-friendly alternatives before the Kigali Amendment phase-down step in 2029.
source_quote:
To prevent lock-in of highly climate-damaging HFC refrigerants in the time between now and the first Kigali Amendment phase-down step in 2029, the Republic of Namibia aims to implement early action on the reduction of HFCs and the introduction of climate-friendly alternatives. Low GWP

technology options, particularly natural refrigerant technology options, exist as an alternative to HFCs for almost any  RAC  appliance.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear mitigation commitment tied to a named international framework and a specific intervention in refrigerants. It is direct climate policy because it targets high-GWP gases explicitly.

policy_statement: Namibia will introduce climate-friendly and energy-efficient RAC appliances through a ban on high-GWP equipment and minimum energy performance standards, targeting 60% penetration by 2030.
source_quote: Namibia  aims  at  the  introduction  of  climate-friendly  and  energy-efficient  appliances through the inclusion of a ban on high GWP equipment and the introduction of minimum energy performance standards (MEPS) that generate emission reductions, both from the use of refrigerants (direct emissions) and from low energy consumption (indirect emissions). The measures aim to achieve a penetration of 60% climatefriendly and energy-efficient residential air conditioners, as well as domestic and commercial refrigeration units by 2030.
extraction_rationale: This is a strong policy with binding regulatory mechanisms and a quantified target. It explicitly combines refrigerant transition and energy efficiency, justifying a secondary Resource Efficiency classification.

policy_statement: Namibia will train technicians in proper servicing, handling of low-GWP refrigerants, and safe disposal of old refrigeration and car air-conditioning equipment.
source_quote: These measures are complemented by training technicians on the proper servicing and handling of low GWP refrigerants. They are to be also trained in the safe and proper disposal of old refrigerators as well as car air conditioning equipment.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific implementation and capacity-building measure supporting RAC mitigation. It qualifies because it names concrete interventions rather than vague awareness-raising.

policy_statement: Namibia expects green hydrogen to contribute significant GHG reductions through decarbonization of the electric matrix by 2030 and is undertaking a feasibility study to become a global contributor.
source_quote: Currently, a feasibility study to explore whether Namibia can become a leading global contributor to green hydrogen is underway  18 . extraction_rationale: This is a specific planning and analytical commitment supporting climate implementation. It is concrete enough to qualify due to the named strategy and model.

policy_statement: Namibia will develop a national Green Jobs Assessment Model to measure the impacts of climate measures on GDP, jobs, skills, revenue distribution, inequalities, and gender inequality.

The assessment's findings and process of multi-stakeholder dialogues will help Namibia foster evidence-based NDC policymaking and a just transition.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete commitment to develop a named analytical tool for climate policy implementation. It is climate-relevant but more indirect than sectoral mitigation/adaptation measures.

policy_statement: Namibia seeks to integrate blue carbon ecosystems into future NDC revisions to capture services including coastal protection, wildlife habitat, and water filtration.

extraction_rationale: This is a forward-looking but still concrete planning commitment to include blue carbon ecosystems in future NDCs. It qualifies because it names a specific intervention area and intended policy integration.

policy_statement: Namibia estimates total NDC financing needs of USD 5.33 billion by 2030, including USD 3.61 billion for mitigation and USD 1.72 billion for adaptation.
source_quote:
Financial needs remain high amid ongoing efforts. Most actions that need financing and mobilisation of future resources will be a fair blend of national and foreign funds. The estimated net cost for the established NDC mitigation measures is expected to be about 3.61 USD billion and more than USD 1.72 billion for adaptation goals, reflecting a combined requirement of about USD 5.33 billion in financing.

TABLE 4.1 summarises the approximate worth of the finance needed over the next ten years.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified public investment requirement for implementing the NDC. It qualifies as a financial instrument because it establishes a broad financing envelope for climate action.

policy_statement: Namibia prioritizes improving access to public and private financing sources and conditions full NDC implementation on enhanced international support including finance, technology transfer, technical assistance, and capacity-building.
source_quote: Similarly,  this  NDC  update includes conditions for their full implementation, such as additional or enhanced international support in the form of finance, technology transfer, technical assistance and capacity-building. Improving access to public and private financing sources is, therefore, a high priority for Namibia.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete financing strategy commitment tied to NDC implementation. It is not a discrete fund, tax, or subsidy, so it is not coded as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Namibia will explore de-risking instruments including insurance, guarantees, and derivative-based products to improve the risk-return profile of low-carbon technologies.
source_quote: Investment in climate mitigation activities will be associated with high perceived and actual risks related to environmental, technological, financial, and regulatory uncertainties. Namibia will explore various de-risking instruments that include insurance, guarantees and derivative-based products, as tools that can directly improve the risk-return profile in favour of low carbon technologies.
section_header: 4.5 Barriers and Opportunities towards the NDCs implementation
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete commitment to use financial-risk instruments in support of low-carbon investment. It qualifies as a financial instrument because the policy itself is about deploying broad financial de-risking tools.

policy_statement: Namibia is strengthening institutional arrangements to build a national MRV system covering mitigation, adaptation, GHG inventory, support received, and support needed.
source_quote: Namibia's efforts will undo ubtedly contribute to the global efforts to mitigate the adverse impacts of climate change. In this context, the country is strengthening the existing institutional arrangements, to ensure a robust and transparent climate action that would enable to build a vibrant national Measurement, Reporting and Verification system (MRV). The system is expected to harmonize and track all data needs of the relevant local and international stakeholders. It  is  to  comprise  of  the  following  components:  mitigation,  adaptation,  GHG inventory, support received, and support needed.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete institutional commitment to establish and strengthen a national MRV system with specified components. It qualifies as a climate governance policy.

policy_statement: Achieve statewide GHG emissions reductions of 40% by 2030 and 85% by 2050 from 1990 levels, with net zero emissions statewide by 2050.
source_quote: It identifies actions needed for New York to achieve 70% renewable electricity by 2030, 100% zero-emission electricity by 2040, a 40% reduction in statewide GHG emissions from 1990 levels by 2030, an 85% reduction in statewide GHG emissions from 1990 levels by 2050, and net zero emissions statewide by 2050. It outlines a variety of regulatory and legal changes, market mechanisms, and technologies essential to achieving the goals and requirements of the Climate Act.
extraction_rationale: This is a core quantified statewide climate target with deadlines and explicit implementation mechanisms, so it clearly qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Electrify approximately 1 to 2 million efficient homes with heat pumps by 2030.
source_quote: Energy efficiency and end-use electrification are essential parts of any pathway that achieves New York State emission limits: Approximately 1 to 2 million efficient homes must be electrified with heat pumps by 2030. Approximately 3 million zero-emission vehicles (predominantly battery electric) will be needed by 2030.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified deployment target tied directly to achieving emission limits. It is specific enough to count as a policy commitment.

policy_statement: Deploy approximately 3 million zero-emission vehicles by 2030.
source_quote: Energy efficiency and end-use electrification are essential parts of any pathway that achieves New York State emission limits: Approximately 1 to 2 million efficient homes must be electrified with heat pumps by 2030. Approximately 3 million zero-emission vehicles (predominantly battery electric) will be needed by 2030.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified transportation decarbonization target with a deadline, making it a clear mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Improve electric grid resilience through storm hardening, elevating equipment and substations, undergrounding lines, and deploying storage or onsite renewables.
source_quote: Recommended investments in building and electric grid infrastructure, such as storm hardening, elevating equipment and substations, moving lines underground, and deploying energy storage or onsite renewables will improve the reliability and resilience of the electric grid in the face of worsening storms and other impacts of climate change. The transition will also spur investments in New York's homes and commercial buildings.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific package of resilience interventions for climate hazards. It is operationally concrete and directly tied to worsening storms and climate impacts.

policy_statement: Develop and finalize criteria to identify Disadvantaged Communities and review them annually.
source_quote: As required by the Climate Act, the CJWG identified Disadvantaged Communities based on geographic, public health, environmental hazard, and socioeconomic criteria. The CJWG released the draft criteria for public comment in March 2022 and received more than 3,000 comments. The CJWG is considering those comments as it works to finalize the criteria by early 2023. After final criteria are established, the CJWG will review them annually to ensure that they remain appropriate and effective.
extraction_rationale: This is a statutory implementation commitment with a defined mechanism and ongoing review requirement. It is climate-relevant because it structures equity delivery under climate policy, though not itself an emissions or resilience measure.

policy_statement: Ensure Disadvantaged Communities receive at least 35% of benefits from clean energy and energy efficiency spending, with a goal of 40%.
source_quote: The Climate Act requires that Disadvantaged Communities receive a minimum of 35%, with a goal of 40%, of the benefits of spending on clean energy and energy efficiency programs, projects, or investments in the areas of housing, workforce development, pollution reduction, low-income energy assistance, energy, transportation, and economic development. State agencies, in consultation with the CJWG and other relevant stakeholders, are developing a methodology for defining the benefits of State investments in Disadvantaged Communities.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified statutory allocation requirement governing climate-related spending. It is a policy because it sets a binding distribution rule for climate investments.

policy_statement: Implement actionable just transition recommendations to prepare and support New York's workforce for the clean energy transition.
source_quote: This Scoping Plan presents and strengthens the work coordinated by the JTWG including the following actionable recommendations to ensure that New York's workforce is prepared for and stands to benefit from the State's transition to a low-carbon economy: - Provide direct displaced worker support to mitigate any economic impact and ensure that current and former fossil fuel workers benefit from the transition to clean energy. - Ensure application of labor standards across all sectors and projects, helping create good union jobs and helping the State take advantage of new federal tax credit requirements and attract greater financial benefits to New York.
section_header: 1.3 Economic Opportunities and a Just Transition
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella initiative followed by a list of specific sub-actions, so it should be extracted as a parent policy.

extraction_rationale: This is a specific workforce development intervention under the parent initiative. It is concrete and implementation-oriented.

section_header: 1.3 Economic Opportunities and a Just Transition
extraction_rationale: This is a specific implementation action under the parent initiative. It is somewhat process-oriented, but still qualifies because it commits to a defined intervention supporting climate workforce transition.

policy_statement: Create a new Office of Just Transition and a Worker Support and Community Assurance Fund.
source_quote: - Create a new Office of Just Transition and a Worker Support and Community Assurance Fund to guide ongoing program and policy support for the near- to medium-term: host community support, existing worker support, and new worker support. New York will re-tool existing businesses; attract new businesses; and seek opportunities to manufacture, assemble, and distribute the equipment and components that are needed to realize sector-specific outcomes and provide jobs for New Yorkers.
section_header: 1.3 Economic Opportunities and a Just Transition
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete institutional and funding commitment under the parent initiative. It clearly qualifies as policy and includes a financial mechanism.

policy_statement: Implement an economywide cap-and-invest program to ensure Climate Act emission limits are met and support clean technology market development.
source_quote: The Scoping Plan recommends implementation of an economywide cap-and-invest program that would ensure the Climate Act's emission limits are met while providing support for clean technology market development. By establishing a consistent market signal across all economic sectors, an economywide program will help individuals and businesses make decisions that reduce their emissions and yield the emissions reductions specified by the program.
extraction_rationale: This is a named, economywide policy instrument with a clear mechanism and climate objective. It is one of the document's central policies.

policy_statement: Direct at least 35% of cap-and-invest proceeds to benefit Disadvantaged Communities, with a goal of 40%.
source_quote: In addition, as required by the Climate Act, at least 35% of the investments made with program proceeds will benefit Disadvantaged Communities, with a goal of 40%. Offsets would have little, if any, role in a cap-and-invest program designed to comply with the Climate Act.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified spending allocation rule within the cap-and-invest design. It is a clear financial policy commitment.

policy_statement: Provide rebates or other mechanisms to mitigate cap-and-invest financial impacts on low- and moderate-income households.
source_quote: In addition, the strategy recommends rebates or other mechanisms to mitigate the program's financial impacts on LMI households so these households will benefit from program investments without bearing any additional energy costs as a result of the program's implementation.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific compensatory financial mechanism tied to the cap-and-invest program. It qualifies as a policy despite some flexibility in exact design.

policy_statement: Draft and promulgate enforceable regulations by January 1, 2024 to ensure the State meets the Climate Act's statewide GHG emission limits.
source_quote: - DEC will have until January 1, 2024, to draft and promulgate enforceable regulations to ensure that the State meets the Climate Act's statewide GHG emission limits (i.e., 40% reduction in Statewide GHG emissions by 2030 and 85% reduction by 2050, both from 1990 levels) as outlined in the Scoping Plan. - The State Energy Plan will be updated to incorporate the recommendations of the Scoping Plan.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding regulatory deadline with explicit emissions targets. It clearly qualifies as a policy commitment.

policy_statement: Issue biennial PSC reviews of the renewable energy program beginning July 1, 2024, including progress toward renewable electricity, zero-emission electricity, offshore wind, solar PV, and storage targets.
source_quote: - By July 1, 2024, and every two years thereafter, the PSC will issue a comprehensive review of the renewable energy program, including progress in meeting the overall targets for 70% renewable electricity by 2030 and 100% zero-emission electricity by 2040. This review will also include a progress update on the programs the PSC has established to require procurement of 9 GW of offshore wind by 2035, 6 GW of solar PV by 2025, and 3 GW of energy storage by 2030.
extraction_rationale: This is a recurring statutory review requirement tied to specific climate targets. It is process-oriented but still a concrete policy obligation.

policy_statement: Continue PSC programs designed to provide substantial benefits to Disadvantaged Communities through renewable energy, energy efficiency, and energy storage implementation.
source_quote: - The PSC will continue to advance programs that are designed to provide substantial benefits to Disadvantaged Communities in the implementation of the renewable energy, energy efficiency, and energy storage programs.
extraction_rationale: This is a continuing implementation commitment tied to named climate programs. It is somewhat broad but anchored to specific program areas.

policy_statement: Invest in resiliency measures while aggressively reducing GHG emissions.
source_quote: Although no single entity can solve this global problem on its own, the Climate Act established New York as a leader in the critical effort to maintain a livable planet. IPCC's AR6 makes the critical nature of this work more clear. The report notes that, while many of the changes observed in the climate are unprecedented, strong and sustained reductions in GHG emissions would limit climate change. It is imperative that New York take immediate action to aggressively reduce GHG emissions as well as invest in resiliency measures.
extraction_rationale: This is a direct commitment to invest in resilience, but it is somewhat broad and lacks a named program or quantified target. It is included as an edge case because it contains a clear action commitment and resource allocation language.

policy_statement: Promote integration of climate change adaptation and resilience planning into all relevant policies and programs using the best available science.
source_quote: The benefits of adaptation and resilience actions include improved economic opportunities, infrastructure, and equity in our rural and urban communities. New York will promote the integration of climate change adaptation and resilience planning into all relevant policies and programs using the best available science.
extraction_rationale: This is a statewide planning commitment with a clear implementation direction, though it is broad and not quantified. It qualifies because it commits the State to integrate adaptation into policy and program design.

policy_statement: Follow technological and research developments on green hydrogen for reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
source_quote: The Scoping Plan recommends following technological and research developments on the use of hydrogen as a tool to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The Scoping Plan recommends the use of green hydrogen but acknowledges that in Sector Strategies, references to green hydrogen can also include pink hydrogen.
extraction_rationale: This is a technology-monitoring and directional policy commitment. It is weaker than a deployment mandate, but still a specific policy stance on hydrogen development.

policy_statement: Consider future versions of the Scoping Plan using technology and market advancements in evaluating hydrogen production and use toward Climate Act emissions limits.
source_quote: Future versions of this Scoping Plan will consider technology and market advancements when evaluating the production and use of hydrogen towards the achievement of the Climate Act emissions limits.
extraction_rationale: This is a forward-looking planning commitment tied to a specific technology and emissions objective. It is somewhat procedural but sufficiently concrete to extract.

policy_statement: Establish statewide GHG emission limits of 40% below 1990 levels by 2030 and 85% below 1990 levels by 2050, with a net zero goal by 2050.
source_quote: The heart of the Climate Act is the addition of Article 75 to the Environmental Conservation Law (ECL), which, among other things, directs DEC to establish statewide greenhouse gas (GHG) emission limits, requiring a 40% reduction in statewide GHG emissions from 1990 levels by 2030 and an 85% reduction by 2050. The Climate Act also establishes a goal of net zero emissions across all sectors of the economy by 2050.
section_header: 3.1 Landmark Accomplishment of the Climate Act and Key Components of the Legislation
extraction_rationale: This is a statutory climate target and one of the strongest policy commitments in the document. It is extracted separately from the executive summary because this section states the legal basis.

policy_statement: Promulgate regulations within four years of the Climate Act's effective date to ensure compliance with statewide GHG emission limits.
source_quote: Within four years of the effective date, the Climate Act requires DEC to promulgate regulations to ensure compliance with such statewide GHG emission limits.
section_header: 3.1 Landmark Accomplishment of the Climate Act and Key Components of the Legislation
extraction_rationale: This is a binding statutory regulatory requirement with a deadline. It clearly qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Require PSC to establish a program for 70% renewable electricity by 2030 and 100% zero-emission electricity by 2040.
source_quote: Specifically, the program must have two targets: 70% of the State's electricity deriving from renewable energy by 2030 (70x30) and 100% zero-emission energy by 2040 (100x40). The Public Service Law provisions also codify previously existing ambitious clean energy goals, including a requirement for the procurement of at least 9,000 megawatts (MW) of offshore wind by 2035, 6,000 MW of distributed solar generation by 2025, and 3,000 MW of energy storage by 2030.
section_header: 3.1 Landmark Accomplishment of the Climate Act and Key Components of the Legislation
extraction_rationale: This is a statutory electricity decarbonization program with quantified targets and deadlines. It is a core mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Require procurement of at least 9,000 MW of offshore wind by 2035, 6,000 MW of distributed solar by 2025, and 3,000 MW of energy storage by 2030.
source_quote: The Public Service Law provisions also codify previously existing ambitious clean energy goals, including a requirement for the procurement of at least 9,000 megawatts (MW) of offshore wind by 2035, 6,000 MW of distributed solar generation by 2025, and 3,000 MW of energy storage by 2030.
section_header: 3.1 Landmark Accomplishment of the Climate Act and Key Components of the Legislation
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified statutory procurement requirement with deadlines and technologies specified. It clearly qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Require Disadvantaged Communities to receive at least 35% of overall benefits of clean energy and energy efficiency spending, with a goal of 40%.
source_quote: This includes a requirement that Disadvantaged Communities receive at least 35% of the overall benefits of spending on clean energy and energy efficiency programs, with a goal of 40%.
section_header: 3.1 Landmark Accomplishment of the Climate Act and Key Components of the Legislation
extraction_rationale: This is a statutory equity allocation requirement for climate spending. It is a clear policy with quantified thresholds.

policy_statement: Establish a community air monitoring program to identify locations for monitoring, develop emissions reduction strategies, and implement emissions reduction programs in selected communities.
source_quote: The Climate Act establishes a community air monitoring program to identify locations to deploy community air monitoring systems, to develop a strategy to reduce toxic and criteria air pollutant emissions in Disadvantaged Communities, and to select communities around the State in which to implement emissions reduction programs.
section_header: 3.1 Landmark Accomplishment of the Climate Act and Key Components of the Legislation
extraction_rationale: This is a statutory program with specific functions and implementation steps. It is climate-relevant through co-pollutant reduction in climate justice implementation.

policy_statement: Require State agencies to ensure permitting and other decisions do not disproportionately burden Disadvantaged Communities and prioritize reductions of GHG emissions and co-pollutants in those communities.
source_quote: The Climate Act also requires State agencies to ensure that permitting, licensing, contracting, and other approvals and decisions will not disproportionately burden Disadvantaged Communities and to prioritize reductions of GHG emissions and co-pollutants in Disadvantaged Communities.
section_header: 3.1 Landmark Accomplishment of the Climate Act and Key Components of the Legislation
extraction_rationale: This is a binding statutory decision-making standard. It is a clear policy requirement, though broad in application.

policy_statement: Require State agencies to consider GHG emissions and limits in permitting, licensing, contracting, and other approvals and decisions, and justify inconsistent actions with alternatives or mitigation measures.
source_quote: The Climate Act also requires state agencies to consider GHG emissions and limits in permitting, licensing, contracting, and other approvals and decisions, and that wherever such decisions are deemed inconsistent or would interfere with the statewide GHG emission limits, State agencies must provide a detailed statement of justification for the action, notwithstanding the inconsistency, and identify alternatives or GHG mitigation measures.
section_header: 3.1 Landmark Accomplishment of the Climate Act and Key Components of the Legislation
extraction_rationale: This is a binding cross-government procedural requirement with a clear mechanism. It qualifies as policy because it changes regulatory decision standards.

policy_statement: Expand the Community Risk and Resiliency Act to additional DEC permitting programs and allow mitigation of climate risks, including adverse impacts on Disadvantaged Communities.
source_quote: The Climate Act also expands the scope of the existing Community Risk and Resiliency Act (CRRA), including by covering additional DEC permitting programs such as State Pollutant Discharge Elimination System permitting and Air Pollution Control permitting, and by allowing State agencies and other entities to require mitigation of climate risks, including adverse impacts on Disadvantaged Communities.
section_header: 3.1 Landmark Accomplishment of the Climate Act and Key Components of the Legislation
extraction_rationale: This is a statutory expansion of adaptation-related permitting authority. It is a clear resilience policy with explicit climate risk mitigation language.

policy_statement: Establish statewide GHG emission limits at 245.87 MMT CO2e for 2030 and 61.47 MMT CO2e for 2050 through 6 NYCRR Part 496.
source_quote: DEC promulgated 6 NYCRR Part 496 that established the two statewide GHG emission limits called for in the Climate Act: a limit for 2030 that is equal to 60% of 1990 GHG emission levels and a limit for 2050 that is equal to 15% of 1990 emission levels. Specifically, using a 20-year global warming potential (GWP) and including upstream emissions from fossil fuels imported into New York as required by the Climate Act, the statewide GHG emission limit for 2030 is 245.87 million metric tons (MMT) of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2e), and the statewide GHG emission limits for 2050 is 61.47 MMT CO2e.
section_header: 3.1 Landmark Accomplishment of the Climate Act and Key Components of the Legislation
extraction_rationale: This is a finalized regulation establishing quantified statewide emissions caps. It is a definitive mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Use Value of Carbon guidance in State agency decision-making, including benefit-cost analyses, rulemaking, environmental assessments, and demonstrations of climate policy benefits.
source_quote: Further, DEC, in consultation with NYSERDA, established the Value of Carbon guidance to help State agency decision-making by placing a monetary value for the avoided emissions of GHGs. The Value of Carbon guidance provides metrics that may be broadly applicable to actions by all State agencies and authorities-such as benefit-cost analyses, rulemaking processes, environmental assessments, and demonstrations of the benefits of climate change policies-to demonstrate the global societal value of actions to reduce GHG emissions.
section_header: 3.1 Landmark Accomplishment of the Climate Act and Key Components of the Legislation
extraction_rationale: This is a formal guidance instrument directing how agencies value avoided emissions in decisions. It is not a tax or fee, so not a financial instrument under the schema.

policy_statement: Use the $4.2 billion Environmental Bond Act to support Climate Act implementation through GHG mitigation, open space conservation, flood risk reduction, and resilient infrastructure, with at least 35% of benefits to Disadvantaged Communities and a goal of 40%.
source_quote: In 2022, New York voters approved a $4.2 billion Environmental Bond Act with 68% of the vote. The 'Clean Water, Clean Air, and Green Jobs' Environmental Bond Act will provide funds to support the implementation of the Climate Act through GHG mitigation projects and other initiatives such as open space conservation, flood risk reduction, and continued funding for resilient infrastructure. The Bond Act is also aligned with the environmental justice provisions of the Climate Act in that Disadvantaged Communities must receive at least 35% of the benefit of the funds, with a goal of 40%.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is a major public investment line with explicit climate purposes and equity allocation requirements. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Implement Executive Order 22 to accelerate sustainability and decarbonization of State operations through GreenNY purchasing specifications, operational directives, and annual reporting.
source_quote: Governor Kathy Hochul signed the nation-leading Executive Order 22, Leading by Example: Directing State Agencies to Adopt a Sustainability and Decarbonization Program, 2022, to accelerate efforts to make State operations more sustainable. Through the Executive Order, the GreenNY Council will ensure that State agencies follow best practices in green purchasing and in their operations by building upon current green purchasing specifications and operational directives as well as by strengthening and issuing new specifications. Required annual reporting from agencies and authorities will help ensure that the goals of the Executive Order are achieved.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is a formal executive order with implementation mechanisms and reporting requirements. It is a clear policy.

policy_statement: Develop an Extreme Heat Action Plan in response to more frequent and intense extreme heat events driven by climate change.
source_quote: The 2022 State of the State address directed DEC and NYSERDA to develop an Extreme Heat Action Plan in response to more frequent and intense extreme heat events driven by climate change.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is a specific planning directive tied to a named climate hazard. It qualifies as an adaptation policy.

policy_statement: Achieve net zero investment portfolios by 2040 across State agencies and authorities representing an estimated $50 billion in investments.
source_quote: Governor Hochul announced that State agencies and authorities, representing an estimated $50 billion in investments, have committed to achieving net zero in their investment portfolios by 2040. This ensures New York's financial resources are aligned with the Climate Act.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified portfolio decarbonization commitment with a deadline and a large investment base. It is climate-relevant and financial in nature.

policy_statement: Require all new passenger cars, pickup trucks, and SUVs sold in New York to be zero-emission by 2035 through regulations modeled on California's Advanced Clean Cars II.
source_quote: Governor Hochul directed DEC to adopt regulations that will require all new passenger cars, pickup trucks, and SUVs sold in New York State be zero-emission by 2035 and be modeled on California's Advanced Clean Cars II regulation finalized in 2022.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is a clear regulatory sales mandate with a deadline and covered vehicle classes. It is a direct mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Implement Advanced Clean Trucks standards and large-entity reporting requirements for medium- and heavy-duty trucks.
source_quote: Advanced Clean Trucks (DEC 6 NYCRR Part 218 Regulation), adopted in 2021, incorporated California's Advanced Clean Truck zero-emission vehicle standards for MHD trucks as well as large entity reporting requirements for owners and operators of MHD trucks as part of New York's existing low emission vehicle program.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is an adopted regulation with specific standards and reporting requirements. It clearly qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Lower methane and VOC emissions from New York's oil and natural gas sector through DEC Part 203 regulations.
source_quote: Oil and Natural Gas Sector regulations (DEC 6 NYCRR Part 203 Regulations), adopted and effective in 2022 to support the goals and requirements of the Climate Act, lowers methane and volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions for sources in New York's oil and natural gas sector.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is an adopted regulation targeting methane and VOC emissions. It is a direct mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Prohibit specified high-GWP HFC uses in certain refrigerants, aerosol propellants, and foam-blowing agent end uses where safer alternatives are available.
source_quote: Hydrofluorocarbon Standards and Reporting (DEC 6 NYCRR Part 494 Regulations) prohibits specific HFCs, potent GHGs in certain refrigerants, aerosol propellants, and foam-blowing agent end uses that represent avoidable HFC emissions where safer alternatives are available.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is an adopted regulation with a clear prohibition mechanism and targeted substances. It is a direct mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Require large generators of food scraps to donate excess edible food and recycle remaining food scraps if within 25 miles of an organics recycler.
source_quote: Food Donation and Food Scraps Recycling (DEC 6 NYCRR Part 350 Regulations), adopted in 2022 pursuant to ECL Article 27, Title 22, requires large generators of food scraps to donate excess edible food and to recycle all remaining food scraps if they are located within 25 miles of an organics recycler, which will reduce methane and VOC emissions in support of the goals and requirements of the Climate Act.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is an adopted regulatory requirement with a clear threshold and action. It directly reduces methane emissions from waste.

policy_statement: Update the Forest Tax Law program to lessen administrative burdens while strengthening sustainable forest management standards.
source_quote: Taxation of Forest Land (DEC Proposed 6 NYCRR Part 199 Regulations), proposed in 2022, seeks to improve the Forest Tax Law program by lessening administrative burdens while strengthening the sustainable forest management standards.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed regulation tied to a named tax law program and a specific intervention. It is climate-relevant through forest carbon management, though still proposed.

policy_statement: Establish statewide sea-level rise projections for use in permits and decision-making under CRRA and update them at least every five years.
source_quote: Projected Sea-Level Rise (DEC 6 NYCRR Part 490 Regulations), finalized in early 2017, establishes statewide sea-level rise projections for use in the consideration of permits and other decision-making processes specified under CRRA. Under CRRA, DEC is required to update these sea-level rise projection regulations at least every five years.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is a finalized adaptation regulation with a clear planning and permitting function and update cycle.

policy_statement: Implement RGGI as a declining cap-and-invest program for CO2 emissions from electric generation facilities.
source_quote: Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI; DEC 6 NYCRR Part 242 Regulations and NYSERDA 21 NYCRR Part 507) is the first mandatory market-based emissions trading program in the United States to reduce CO2 emissions and the first anywhere to use the cap-and-invest model for reducing pollution. New York and other RGGI-participating states set a cap for total emissions of CO2 from electric generation facilities in the region. The RGGI cap declines over time, gradually lowering CO2 emission limits.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is an existing mandatory market-based emissions program with a declining cap. It is a direct financial climate instrument.

policy_statement: Impose a two-year moratorium on certain cryptocurrency mining permits using behind-the-meter electricity and proof-of-work authentication, and prepare a generic environmental impact statement on such operations.
source_quote: Chapter 628 of the Laws of 2022 established a two-year moratorium on the issuance of certain permits by DEC for cryptocurrency mining operations that use behind-the-meter electricity and proof-of-work authentication methods to validate blockchain transactions. This law directs DEC, in consultation with the New York State Department of Public Service (DPS), to prepare a generic environmental impact statement on this type of cryptocurrency mining operation.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is a binding legislative moratorium with a defined scope and accompanying environmental review requirement. It is climate-relevant because it constrains energy-intensive emissions growth.

policy_statement: Study disproportionate heat conditions, or urban heat islands, in Disadvantaged Communities.
source_quote: Chapter 563 of the Laws of 2022 directs DEC to study the impacts of disproportionate heat conditions, otherwise known as urban heat islands, in Disadvantaged Communities.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is a legislative directive for a specific climate hazard study. It is more analytical than operational, but still a concrete adaptation policy action.

policy_statement: Develop a regulatory structure for utility thermal energy networks and direct utilities to launch pilot projects.
source_quote: Chapter 375 of the Laws of 2022 (Utility Thermal Energy Network and Jobs Act) requires the PSC to develop a regulatory structure for utility thermal energy networks, including district geothermal and other community-scale thermal infrastructure projects, for heating and cooling homes and to direct utilities to launch pilot projects in their service territories.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is a legislative requirement with a named intervention and pilot mandate. It is a clear policy.

policy_statement: Strengthen New York's regulatory and policy environment for building energy efficiency, GHG reduction strategies, expanded appliance standards, and use of certain HFC substitutes.
source_quote: Chapter 374 of the Laws of 2022 (Advanced Building Codes, Appliance and Equipment Efficiency Standards Act of 2022) bolsters New York's regulatory and policy environment to support energy efficiency and GHG reduction strategies in buildings, expanded appliance standards, and changed building code law to allow the utilization of certain HFC substitutes.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is enacted legislation with multiple concrete building-sector interventions. It is a direct climate policy.

policy_statement: Require prevailing wage for renewable energy projects of one megawatt and larger involving procurement of renewable energy credits from a public entity.
source_quote: Chapter 372 of the Laws of 2022 requires prevailing wage for renewable energy projects one megawatt and larger that involve the procurement of renewable energy credits from a public entity.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is a binding labor standard attached to renewable energy projects. It is climate-relevant through implementation of mitigation infrastructure.

policy_statement: Establish procurement guidelines for low-embodied carbon concrete.
source_quote: Chapter 724 of the Laws of 2021 established procurement guidelines for low-embodied carbon concrete.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is a specific procurement policy targeting embodied emissions in construction materials. It is a clear mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Target new non-road vehicles and equipment sold in New York to be zero-emission by 2035 and new medium- and heavy-duty vehicles sold in New York to be zero-emission by 2045.
source_quote: Chapter 423 of the Laws of 2021, as amended by Chapter 109 of the Laws of 2022, related to ZEV sales states that new non-road vehicles and equipment sold in New York are targeted to be zero-emissions by 2035 and that new MHD vehicles sold in New York are targeted to be zero-emissions by 2045.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is a legislative sales target with deadlines and covered equipment classes. It qualifies as a policy despite the word 'targeted' because it is statutory and specific.

policy_statement: Accelerate and streamline siting and construction of large-scale renewable energy projects through the Accelerated Renewable Energy Growth and Community Benefit Act and ORES.
source_quote: Chapter 58 of the Laws of 2020 established the Accelerated Renewable Energy Growth and Community Benefit Act as part the State Fiscal Year 2020-2021 budget to dramatically speed up the siting and construction of clean energy projects to combat climate change and help jumpstart the State's economic recovery from the COVID-19 health crisis. This law created a first-in-the-nation Office of Renewable Energy Siting (ORES) to improve and streamline the process for the environmentally responsible and cost-effective siting of large-scale renewable energy projects across New York, while also delivering significant benefits to local communities.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is enacted legislation creating a new office and streamlining mechanism for renewable deployment. It is a clear mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Implement congestion pricing in Manhattan's Central Business District to reduce congestion and enhance mobility, with air quality and equity benefits.
source_quote: Chapter 59 of the Laws of 2019 established the Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) Reform & Traffic Mobility Act (Congestion Pricing) that directs MTA to design, develop, build, and run a toll program that applies to vehicles that enter or remain in Manhattan's Central Business District. The purpose of the program is to reduce congestion and enhance mobility in Manhattan's Central Business District. By reducing traffic and helping improve mass transit, the program would improve air quality and enhance equity by expanding access.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is a legislated tolling program with a clear mechanism and transportation demand objective. Climate benefits are significant though framed partly through congestion and mobility.

policy_statement: Build resilience to rising sea levels and extreme flooding through CRRA and associated flood risk management guidance.
source_quote: Chapter 355 of the Laws of 2014 established New York CRRA to build New York's resilience to rising sea levels and extreme flooding. The Climate Act made modifications to CRRA, expanding the scope of climate hazards and projects for consideration, which became effective January 1, 2020.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is a legislative resilience framework with explicit climate hazards. It is a direct adaptation policy.

policy_statement: Limit CO2 emissions from major generating facilities and phase out coal-fired power plants through 6 NYCRR Part 251.
source_quote: Chapter 388 of the Laws of 2011 established the Power NY Act, which directed DEC to promulgate rules and regulations limiting emissions of CO2 by newly constructed major generating facilities. DEC adopted 6 NYCRR Part 251 in 2012, setting CO2 emission limits that effectively prohibited new coal-fired power plants. In 2018, DEC adopted further revisions to this regulation applicable to existing facilities, effectively phasing out all remaining coal-fired power plants in the State.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is a binding emissions standard with demonstrated effect on coal phaseout. It is a direct mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Prohibit State infrastructure agencies from approving, undertaking, supporting, or financing public infrastructure projects unless, to the extent practicable, they are consistent with 11 smart growth criteria.
source_quote: Chapter 433 of the Laws of 2010 established the State Smart Growth Public Infrastructure Policy Act, ECL Article 6, prohibiting a state infrastructure agency from approving, undertaking, supporting, or financing a 'public infrastructure project' unless, to the extent practicable, the project is consistent with 11 smart growth criteria.
section_header: 3.2 Overview of New York's Climate Policies
extraction_rationale: This is a binding statutory infrastructure decision rule. It is climate-relevant through land use and transportation efficiency, though climate is not the sole stated purpose.

policy_statement: Create a statewide dashboard of community GHG emission inventories to support local climate action planning, equity monitoring, progress measurement, and data consistency.
source_quote: This strategy calls for a dashboard that would promote local climate action planning, monitor equity considerations, measure progress, and ensure data consistency at the county and municipal levels. This dashboard would bring together data from several sources to describe the community GHG emissions picture.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific local government support strategy with a named intervention and clear functions. It qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Develop model above-minimum energy conservation codes and construction policies to encourage local energy policy decisions that accelerate energy efficiency with a focus on equity.
source_quote: This strategy recommends development of model above-minimum energy conservation codes and construction policies to encourage local energy policy decisions that accelerate energy efficiency with a focus on equity. Recognizing that many local governments struggle with tight budgets and limited staff capacity, which limits their ability to take local climate action, this strategy also includes leveraging and expanding existing State programs to help support communities with a focus on equity.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific policy development strategy for local governments. It is concrete enough to qualify and clearly tied to energy efficiency.

policy_statement: Support renewable energy growth through model local laws and streamlined permitting for renewable energy and storage technologies.
source_quote: This strategy looks to foster collaboration among State and local governments to support renewable energy growth, such as development and promotion of model local laws and streamlined permitting for renewable energy and storage technologies.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific local government support intervention for renewable deployment. It is a clear mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Promote municipal leadership through Community Choice Aggregation, microgrids, district systems, and community-scale campaigns to expand clean energy adoption and reduce GHG emissions.
source_quote: This strategy includes connecting homes, businesses, and community institutions with clean energy products and services through Community Choice Aggregation programs, microgrids, district systems, and community-scale campaigns to encourage adoption of innovative technologies that will generate savings and reduce GHG emissions for consumers in an equitable manner. The intent is to allow more consumers to participate in the energy markets in ways that advance Climate Act goals and requirements while improving project economics, saving money, and generating new sources of revenue and ownership for consumers.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific package of interventions to support local clean energy adoption. It is concrete and climate-focused.

policy_statement: Continue and expand program opportunities, incentives, technical assistance, financial support, and centralized procurement services for local governments to improve assets they control with high-impact actions.
source_quote: These strategies include continuing and expanding program opportunities, incentives, technical assistance, financial support, and centralized procurement services to motivate local governments, local government municipal bodies, and related public entities to improve assets they control with high-impact actions. This includes LED lighting installations, energy efficiency upgrades, heat pump projects, methane recovery for energy production from wastewater treatment and landfills, solar installations on municipal premises, and municipal and school district fleet electrification.
extraction_rationale: This is a broad but concrete support package with named interventions and funding/support mechanisms. It qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Implement adaptation and resilience strategies across three themes to build capacity, enhance community and infrastructure resilience, and enhance resilience of living systems.
source_quote: The Scoping Plan recommends strategies within three themes to take action to adapt to climate change and enhance resilience in communities, infrastructure, and living systems.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella initiative introducing multiple named strategy themes beneath it, so it is extracted as a parent.

parent_statement: Adaptation and resilience strategies across three themes
policy_statement: Build capacity through statewide planning, consideration of future conditions in State decision-making, enhancement of climate understanding, adaptive capacity, and financing options for adaptation.
source_quote: Build Capacity: The build capacity theme comprises strategies related to statewide planning, consideration of future conditions in State decision-making, enhancement of general understanding of climate change, improving the public's adaptive capacity, and identifying options for financing adaptation actions and reducing or shifting risk.
extraction_rationale: This is a named strategy theme under the adaptation parent and functions as a policy umbrella for subsequent actions.

parent_statement: Adaptation and resilience strategies across three themes
policy_statement: Enhance community and infrastructure resilience through planning support, incorporation of future conditions, addressing flooding and extreme heat, and ensuring energy system resilience.
source_quote: Enhancing resilience of communities and infrastructure includes strategies to help municipalities prepare for and react to increasingly severe climate hazards. Strategies include expanding State support for regional and local planning, assisting municipalities and local communities in their efforts to incorporate future conditions into local planning and regulatory decisions, addressing risks of flooding and extreme heat, and ensuring resilience of the energy system.
extraction_rationale: This is a named strategy theme under the adaptation parent with explicit hazard and resilience measures.

parent_statement: Adaptation and resilience strategies across three themes
policy_statement: Prioritize natural resources and nature-based features in implementing community and infrastructure resilience strategies.
source_quote: Implementation of all components of these strategies should prioritize the use of natural resources and nature-based features to enhance resilience.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific implementation directive within the resilience theme. It is explicit enough to extract and clearly invokes ecosystem-based resilience.

parent_statement: Adaptation and resilience strategies across three themes
policy_statement: Enhance resilience of living systems by addressing ecosystem and biodiversity risks, agricultural adaptation, and protecting forests as carbon sinks.
source_quote: Strategies recommended to enhance resilience of living systems include addressing risks to ecosystems and biodiversity, enhancing resilience and adaptation of the agricultural sector, and protecting the ability of forests to serve as carbon sinks.
extraction_rationale: This is a named strategy theme under the adaptation parent with explicit ecological and agricultural resilience actions.

policy_statement: Develop a coordinated gas system transition plan with a clear timeline and principles including emissions reductions, equity, workforce protections, affordability, safety, reliability, electric system coordination, and consumer engagement.
source_quote: Specifically, the Scoping Plan includes a detailed framework through which agencies can develop a coordinated gas system transition plan. The framework provides strategies and guidance to ensure the transition plan sets a clear timeline for the transition while satisfying key principles such as GHG and co-pollutant emission reductions, equity considerations, workforce protections, affordability, safety and reliability, decision-making informed by independent analysis, coordination with electric system expansion, and consumer engagement.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific planning framework with named principles and a clear transition objective. It qualifies as policy despite being a framework rather than a final regulation.

policy_statement: Establish the path to 70% renewable energy by 2030, 100% zero-emission electricity by 2040, 40% GHG reduction by 2030, 85% GHG reduction by 2050, and net zero emissions by 2050.
source_quote: New York will undertake a sweeping set of measures to reduce the State's GHG footprint, transform electricity generation in the State, and drive innovative solutions through technology advancement. This Scoping Plan establishes the path forward for New York to achieve 70% renewable energy by 2030 (70x30), 100% zero-emission electricity by 2040 (100x40), a 40% reduction in statewide GHG emissions from 1990 levels by 2030, an 85% reduction in statewide GHG emissions from 1990 levels by 2050, and net zero emissions statewide by 2050.
extraction_rationale: This restates the statewide climate target package as the formal climate vision. It is duplicative of earlier targets but still a core policy statement; retained here only once in substance would normally be preferable.

policy_statement: Implement fundamental strategies identified by the Scoping Plan to achieve GHG emission limits and net zero emissions.
source_quote: Through the process of the developing this Scoping Plan, the Council recognized several key strategies that are fundamental to achieving the GHG emission limits and net zero GHG emissions:
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella statement introducing a list of fundamental strategies, so it is extracted as a parent.

parent_statement: Key strategies that are fundamental to achieving the GHG emission limits and net zero GHG emissions
policy_statement: Achieve the Climate Act energy efficiency requirement through energy efficiency measures.
source_quote: - Energy efficiency measures that achieve the Climate Act energy efficiency requirement - Transition from fossil natural gas to electrification in buildings
extraction_rationale: This is a listed fundamental strategy under the parent summary. It is concise but clearly a policy direction.

parent_statement: Key strategies that are fundamental to achieving the GHG emission limits and net zero GHG emissions
policy_statement: Transition buildings from fossil natural gas to electrification.
source_quote: - Energy efficiency measures that achieve the Climate Act energy efficiency requirement - Transition from fossil natural gas to electrification in buildings
extraction_rationale: This is a listed fundamental strategy with a clear intervention and sector focus.

parent_statement: Key strategies that are fundamental to achieving the GHG emission limits and net zero GHG emissions
policy_statement: Achieve zero-emission electricity.
source_quote: - Zero-emission electricity - Transportation electrification
extraction_rationale: This is a listed fundamental strategy under the parent summary and directly climate-focused.

parent_statement: Key strategies that are fundamental to achieving the GHG emission limits and net zero GHG emissions
policy_statement: Electrify transportation.
source_quote: - Zero-emission electricity - Transportation electrification
extraction_rationale: This is a listed fundamental strategy with a clear mitigation mechanism.

parent_statement: Key strategies that are fundamental to achieving the GHG emission limits and net zero GHG emissions
policy_statement: Enhance transit, smart growth, and reduced vehicle miles traveled.
source_quote: - Enhancement of transit, smart growth, and reduced vehicle miles traveled (VMT) - Transition to low global warming potential (GWP) refrigerants and enhanced refrigerant management
extraction_rationale: This is a listed strategy with explicit transport demand and land use mechanisms. It is climate-relevant and concrete enough to extract.

parent_statement: Key strategies that are fundamental to achieving the GHG emission limits and net zero GHG emissions
policy_statement: Transition to low-GWP refrigerants and enhanced refrigerant management.
source_quote: - Enhancement of transit, smart growth, and reduced vehicle miles traveled (VMT) - Transition to low global warming potential (GWP) refrigerants and enhanced refrigerant management
extraction_rationale: This is a listed strategy with a clear mitigation mechanism targeting refrigerants.

parent_statement: Key strategies that are fundamental to achieving the GHG emission limits and net zero GHG emissions
policy_statement: Maximize carbon sequestration in New York's lands and forests.
source_quote: - Maximization of carbon sequestration in New York's lands and forests - Mitigation of fugitive methane emissions across the waste, agriculture, and energy sectors
extraction_rationale: This is a listed strategy focused on biological carbon removal. It is a clear climate policy direction.

parent_statement: Key strategies that are fundamental to achieving the GHG emission limits and net zero GHG emissions
policy_statement: Mitigate fugitive methane emissions across the waste, agriculture, and energy sectors.
source_quote: - Maximization of carbon sequestration in New York's lands and forests - Mitigation of fugitive methane emissions across the waste, agriculture, and energy sectors
extraction_rationale: This is a listed cross-sector methane reduction strategy. It is direct mitigation.

parent_statement: Key strategies that are fundamental to achieving the GHG emission limits and net zero GHG emissions
policy_statement: Pursue a diverse portfolio of industrial solutions including efficiency, electrification, and strategic use of alternative fuels and carbon capture technologies for certain applications.
source_quote: - Diverse portfolio of solutions in industry, including efficiency, electrification, and strategic use of alternative fuels and carbon capture technologies for certain industrial applications
extraction_rationale: This is a listed industrial decarbonization strategy with named mechanisms. It is sufficiently specific to extract.

policy_statement: Track and report investments and benefits in Disadvantaged Communities to evaluate compliance with the 35% minimum and 40% goal for clean energy and energy efficiency spending benefits.
source_quote: To evaluate compliance with the Climate Act's requirement for Disadvantaged Communities to receive at least 35% of the benefits of clean energy and energy efficiency spending, with a goal of 40%, the State's program administrators will track and report on the investments and benefits occurring in Disadvantaged Communities. It is expected that reporting will include an accounting of clean energy and energy efficiency funding invested in Disadvantaged Communities and a quantification of measurable co-benefits of these investments such as energy savings, bill savings, workforce development, and projected health impacts.
section_header: 6.1 Climate Justice and the Climate Act
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete reporting and accountability commitment tied to a statutory spending requirement. It qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Conduct statewide community air monitoring in 10 high-burden Disadvantaged Communities and use the results to design emissions reduction strategies and programs.
source_quote: Exceeding the four required by the Climate Act, 10 communities were identified as having a disproportionate air pollution burden. These communities are Buffalo/Niagara Falls/Tonawanda, Capital Region, Bronx, Manhattan, Rochester, Syracuse, Mount Vernon/Yonkers/New Rochelle, Brooklyn, Queens, and Hempstead/Uniondale/Westbury/New Cassel. Monitoring will include GHG emissions and other co-pollutants.
section_header: 6.2 Prioritizing Measures to Reduce Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Co-Pollutants in Disadvantaged Communities
extraction_rationale: This is a specific monitoring program with identified communities and pollutants. It is a concrete climate justice implementation policy.

policy_statement: Provide $2 million in grants for community-led complementary air monitoring and $1 million in Community Air Monitoring Capacity Building Grants.
source_quote: The air monitoring effort will be bolstered by an additional $2 million in grants that will support community-led, complementary air monitoring efforts, and $1 million in Community Air Monitoring Capacity Building Grants.
section_header: 6.2 Prioritizing Measures to Reduce Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Co-Pollutants in Disadvantaged Communities
extraction_rationale: This is a clear funding commitment with specified amounts and purposes. It qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Complete the statewide community air monitoring program by the third quarter of 2023 and prepare strategies by June 1, 2024 to reduce toxic and criteria air pollutants in Disadvantaged Communities.
source_quote: The statewide community air monitoring program is scheduled to be completed in the third quarter of 2023. DEC will provide quarterly project updates to the 10 communities and post these preliminary data summaries to the DEC website. By June 1, 2024, DEC will prepare, in consultation with the CJWG and community-based organizations, strategies to reduce emissions of toxic and criteria air pollutants in Disadvantaged Communities.
section_header: 6.2 Prioritizing Measures to Reduce Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Co-Pollutants in Disadvantaged Communities
extraction_rationale: This is a dated implementation commitment with reporting and strategy deadlines. It qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Require any worker displaced by climate mitigation efforts to be promptly reemployed with the same or better wages, benefits, and terms and conditions of employment while maintaining their choice of collective bargaining representative.
source_quote: A truly just transition means that the State must enact measures to ensure that any worker who loses their job as a result of climate change mitigation efforts be promptly reemployed with the same or better wages, benefits, and terms and conditions of employment, while maintaining their choice of collective bargaining representative. Further, jobs created as a result of the State's climate change mitigation efforts should be good, family-sustaining, union jobs, and accessible to all New Yorkers.
extraction_rationale: This is a strong normative commitment to enact worker protection measures. It is broad but clearly framed as a required policy response.

policy_statement: Implement recommendations to ensure New York's workforce is prepared for and benefits from the transition to a clean economy.
source_quote: This Scoping Plan identifies the following recommendations to help ensure that New York's workforce is prepared for and stands to benefit from the State's transition to a clean economy.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella statement introducing a set of workforce recommendations, so it is extracted as a parent.

parent_statement: Recommendations to help ensure that New York's workforce is prepared for and stands to benefit from the State's transition to a clean economy
policy_statement: Establish continuing education, apprenticeships, certifications, and licensing support for current workers and support companies in transitioning their workforce to clean energy jobs.
source_quote: To mitigate any economic impact and ensure that current and formerly employed fossil fuel workers benefit from the transition to clean energy, it is imperative to support displaced workers as much as possible and early on. This means establishing continuing education, Registered Apprenticeships, certifications, and licensing in trades and professions for current workers and supporting companies in transitioning their workforce to building operations and maintenance, design, construction, and other clean energy jobs.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific workforce support intervention under the parent recommendation set. It is concrete and actionable.

parent_statement: Recommendations to help ensure that New York's workforce is prepared for and stands to benefit from the State's transition to a clean economy
policy_statement: Create a bridge to retirement for displaced workers nearing retirement age at the time of plant or facility closure.
source_quote: This also means creating a bridge to retirement for displaced workers nearing retirement age at the time of a plant or facility closing. The State should also provide and coordinate other discrete benefits for displaced workers facing a gap in employment or wishing to pursue an alternative path, including transitional unemployment benefits (including, but not limited to, supplemental payments), federal and state Continuation of Health Coverage insurance, and grants/credits for post-secondary education at two- and four-year programs at public institutions.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific worker support measure with defined benefit types. It qualifies as a policy and financial support mechanism.

parent_statement: Recommendations to help ensure that New York's workforce is prepared for and stands to benefit from the State's transition to a clean economy
policy_statement: Apply robust labor standards across all sectors and projects, including prevailing wage, project labor agreements, labor peace agreements, licensing standards, and apprenticeship utilization.
