source_quote: As such, the State should apply robust labor standards across all sectors and projects. During implementation, the application of any such labor standards by relevant public entities should take into consideration unique sector- and project-specific characteristics, so as to tailor the standards accordingly.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear labor standards policy commitment under the workforce recommendations. It is implementation-specific.

parent_statement: Recommendations to help ensure that New York's workforce is prepared for and stands to benefit from the State's transition to a clean economy
policy_statement: Provide targeted financial support for businesses, including MWBEs, SDVOBs, cooperatives, unions, and community-based organizations, to support hiring, training, retention, and access to clean energy contracting opportunities.
source_quote: To build a diverse, equitable, and inclusive clean energy economy, businesses must be supported with targeted financial support to ensure access to contracting and procurement opportunities in the transition away from fossil fuels. Funding must provide for supported on-the-job, recruitment, training, hiring, and job retention for businesses in Disadvantaged Communities, minority- and women-owned businesses (MWBEs), service-disabled veteran-owned businesses (SDVOBs), employee-owned businesses, cooperatives, design and installation firms, community-based organizations, start-ups, and unions, as well as pre-apprenticeship and apprenticeship programs.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific financial support policy with named beneficiary groups and uses. It clearly qualifies.

parent_statement: Recommendations to help ensure that New York's workforce is prepared for and stands to benefit from the State's transition to a clean economy
policy_statement: Develop new training curricula and comprehensive training programs focused on Disadvantaged Communities and employer hiring needs.
source_quote: New training curricula, trained trainers, and comprehensive training programs will be critical to this economywide transition. These programs must be developed with a focus on Disadvantaged Communities and be designed to meet employer hiring needs.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific workforce development commitment with target populations and design criteria.

parent_statement: Recommendations to help ensure that New York's workforce is prepared for and stands to benefit from the State's transition to a clean economy
policy_statement: Develop comprehensive career pathway programs into clean energy for existing workers and new entrants, including technical upskilling and supportive services.
source_quote: The State must develop comprehensive programs to develop career pathways into clean energy for both existing and future workers. Existing workers include workers from transitioning fossil fuel, clean energy industries, manufacturers, community-based organizations, MWBEs, SDVOBs, as well as State/public workers.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific workforce pathway commitment under the parent recommendation set.

parent_statement: Recommendations to help ensure that New York's workforce is prepared for and stands to benefit from the State's transition to a clean economy
policy_statement: Continue stakeholder engagement and market assessments to identify skills gaps, labor demand, and training needs, with SMART targets.
source_quote: Finally, it is imperative to continue stakeholder engagement to identify and assess industry skills gaps, employee demand, as well as curriculum and training needs. Open dialogue among relevant stakeholders will be key to sharing needs and best practices, support industry opportunity awareness, and enhance recruitment efforts for new, transitioning, and existing workers.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific ongoing implementation commitment, though more process-oriented than others. It still qualifies because it commits to defined assessments and engagement.

policy_statement: Create an Office of Just Transition and an accompanying fund to coordinate workforce development, community support, existing worker support, and new worker support related to the Climate Act transition.
source_quote: That apparatus should take the form of a newly created, dedicated state office charged with realizing a just transition and resourced with an accompanying fund, which would be overseen and administered by the office in consultation with DOL and NYSERDA, to provide support for workers, communities, and other transitional priorities. The Office of Just Transition will help coordinate all funding and financial incentives for workforce development, community support, existing worker support, and new worker support related to the Climate Act transition.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete institutional and funding proposal with a defined mandate. It clearly qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Focus the Office of Just Transition and fund on host community support, existing worker support, and new worker support.
source_quote: As the mission and programmatic priorities of the office and fund are built out, there are three main areas to focus on in the near- to medium-term: host community support, existing worker support, and new worker support.
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella structure introducing three specific support areas, so it is extracted as a parent.

parent_statement: Three main areas to focus on in the near- to medium-term for the Office of Just Transition and fund
policy_statement: Expand and extend the Electric Generation Facility Cessation Mitigation Program and transfer its administration to the Office of Just Transition.
source_quote: New York should enact legislation to expand and extend the Electric Generation Facility Cessation Mitigation Program and transfer administration of the program to this proposed Office of Just Transition. The program was created to provide funding assistance to support counties, towns, cities, villages, school districts and special districts that experience a reduction in real property taxes and/or payments in lieu of taxes stemming from the closure of an electric generation facility.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific legislative and funding action under host community support. It clearly qualifies as policy.

parent_statement: Three main areas to focus on in the near- to medium-term for the Office of Just Transition and fund
policy_statement: Provide support to existing energy workers facing displacement, including wage and benefit bridge funding, retention incentives, skills assessments, training, and additional benefits.
source_quote: The Office of Just Transition should provide support to existing energy workers facing known or potential displacement from their current positions/occupations, through mechanisms described above. Significant new funding should supplement existing support programs already available through state agencies and authorities.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific worker support commitment under the Office of Just Transition structure. It includes funding and defined mechanisms.

parent_statement: Three main areas to focus on in the near- to medium-term for the Office of Just Transition and fund
policy_statement: Support new workers entering clean energy occupations through apprenticeships, pre-apprenticeships, and early-career training focused on underserved and historically marginalized communities.
source_quote: Another key portion of the office's work and funding should be set aside to support new workers seeking entry into emerging clean energy occupations. This support can take the form of a number of mechanisms as outlined above, including for apprenticeships, pre-apprenticeships, and other forms of early-career training, and it should be focused on expanding access to clean energy jobs in underserved and historically marginalized communities.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific new-worker support policy under the Office of Just Transition structure. It is concrete and funding-based.

policy_statement: Recognize early action, set industry-specific benchmarks, use market incentives, minimize burdens on EITE industries, and apply Buy American/Buy New York measures to reduce leakage risk.
source_quote: The following are potential measures to mitigate this risk. A more detailed analysis can be found in Appendix C. - Recognize early action: The State should credit emitters for early investments to reduce their GHG emissions.
section_header: 7.3 Measures to Minimize the Carbon Leakage Risk and Minimize AntiCompetitiveness Impacts
extraction_rationale: This section contains a list of leakage-mitigation measures, but the excerpted text in the document is fragmented. Included as a single summarized policy because the section clearly commits to a package of measures, though source support is less complete than ideal.

policy_statement: Adopt Zero-Emission Vehicle and fleet strategies so that nearly 100% of new light-duty vehicle sales and 40% or more of medium- and heavy-duty vehicle sales are zero-emission by 2030.
source_quote: By 2030 nearly 100% of LDV sales and 40% or more of medium- and heavy-duty vehicle sales must be zero-emission and a substantial portion of personal transportation in urbanized areas would be required to shift to public transportation and other low-carbon modes. New York can achieve these goals through ZEV sales requirements and accompanying incentives, investments to help achieve these mandates, historic investments in expanded public transportation and micro-mobility, enhanced bicycle and pedestrian infrastructure, smart growth development, market-based policies that support lower-carbon transportation choices, and potentially a clean transportation standard that reduces the average carbon intensity of fuels as the transition to ZEVs proceeds.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified transportation transition target with identified implementation mechanisms. It clearly qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Transition to zero-emission vehicles and equipment through regulations, incentives, infrastructure, and enabling strategies.
source_quote: Transition to Zero-Emission Vehicles and Equipment: Vehicles using zero-emission technologies, including vehicles that use either battery electric, hydrogen fuel cell, or future zero-emission propulsion technologies, must progressively replace existing vehicles that use gasoline or diesel fuel. The strategies to achieve these goals involve a combination of regulations requiring vehicle manufacturers to sell zero-emission vehicles, fleet requirements, incentives for purchasing zero-emission vehicles, expansion of easily accessible charging infrastructure, and other enabling strategies.
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella transportation initiative with multiple sub-strategies beneath it, so it is extracted as a parent.

parent_statement: Transition to Zero-Emission Vehicles and Equipment
policy_statement: Prioritize deployment of zero-emission vehicles in Disadvantaged Communities, especially replacing or converting trucks and buses and expanding light-duty adoption.
source_quote: Deployment of zero-emission vehicles, particularly replacing or converting trucks and buses to zero-emission vehicles and expanding light-duty zero-emission vehicle adoption, will be prioritized in Disadvantaged Communities that bear a disproportionate burden of transportation-related emissions.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific prioritization commitment under the zero-emission transportation initiative. It is concrete and equity-focused.

policy_statement: Enhance public transportation and mobility alternatives through service enhancements, mobility-oriented development, convenience and connectivity, and fleet modernization.
source_quote: Enhance Public Transportation and Mobility Alternatives: Enhancing the availability, accessibility, reliability, and affordability of public transportation services with an emphasis on unserved and underserved communities will be one of the more impactful supporting strategies for achieving the Climate Act's energy efficiency, housing, and land use GHG emission reduction requirements. The strategies to achieve these goals and requirements involve service enhancements, mobility-oriented development, convenience and connectivity, and fleet modernization.
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella initiative with multiple component strategies, so it is extracted as a parent.

parent_statement: Enhance Public Transportation and Mobility Alternatives
policy_statement: Reduce vehicle miles traveled by improving public transportation availability, accessibility, reliability, and affordability, especially in unserved and underserved communities.
source_quote: Enhancing the availability, accessibility, reliability, and affordability of public transportation services with an emphasis on unserved and underserved communities will be one of the more impactful supporting strategies for achieving the Climate Act's energy efficiency, housing, and land use GHG emission reduction requirements. These strategies will help reduce vehicle miles traveled (VMT) by providing alternatives to driving personal vehicles.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific transport demand reduction commitment under the parent initiative. It is explicit about mechanism and outcome.

policy_statement: Promote smart growth and mobility-oriented development to reduce transportation emissions and support clean energy investments.
source_quote: Promote Smart Growth and Mobility-Oriented Development: Smart growth land use patterns facilitate reductions in GHG emissions in the transportation sector by reducing VMT and increasing the use of mobility alternatives, including walking, biking, and public transportation. A concentration of compact, mixed-use development around transit and in municipal centers such as downtown areas also provides a critical mass of energy users to support clean energy investments, such as EV charging stations and solar carports.
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella initiative with multiple land use and mobility mechanisms, so it is extracted as a parent.

policy_statement: Facilitate market-based solutions and financing to generate resources and market signals for transportation decarbonization.
source_quote: Facilitate Market-Based Solutions and Financing: Public and private investments in transportation alternatives should be facilitated, in part, through market-based and other supportive policies to generate necessary resources. These policies can also provide a market signal, encouraging private action that reduces emissions from increased use of public transportation to the purchase of zero-emission vehicles.
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella initiative with financing and market-based sub-strategies, so it is extracted as a parent.

parent_statement: Facilitate Market-Based Solutions and Financing
policy_statement: Develop a clean transportation standard emphasizing electrification in Disadvantaged Communities and replacement of petroleum fuels with electricity and possibly other lower co-pollutant fuels.
source_quote: Potential strategies to achieve these goals include the development of a clean transportation standard that would support the replacement of petroleum fuels with electricity and possibly other fuels if they are shown to have lower co-pollutant emissions, with a primary emphasis on supporting electrification in Disadvantaged Communities.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific proposed market-based fuel policy under the parent initiative. It is concrete and climate-focused.

policy_statement: Adopt zero-emission codes and standards and require energy benchmarking for buildings.
source_quote: Adopt Zero-Emission Codes and Standards and Require Energy Benchmarking for Buildings: Policy action to decarbonize buildings must address both energy efficiency and electrification.
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella initiative with multiple specific building code and standards actions beneath it, so it is extracted as a parent.

parent_statement: Adopt Zero-Emission Codes and Standards and Require Energy Benchmarking for Buildings
policy_statement: Require residential and commercial buildings to be built to a zero-emission and highly efficient standard starting in 2025 for low-rise residential new construction and in 2028 for commercial new construction.
source_quote: Advanced State codes is a key strategy for requiring residential and commercial buildings to be built to a zero-emission and highly efficient standard (without equipment used for the combustion of fossil fuels) starting in 2025 for low-rise residential new construction and in 2028 for commercial new construction, and for incorporating strategies for building resilience.
extraction_rationale: This is a dated code requirement with explicit building classes and standards. It clearly qualifies as policy.

parent_statement: Adopt Zero-Emission Codes and Standards and Require Energy Benchmarking for Buildings
policy_statement: Adopt equipment standards requiring buildings to transition to modern technologies such as heat pumps when equipment is replaced.
source_quote: This Scoping Plan includes recommendations for the adoption of equipment standards that require buildings to transition to modern technologies such as heat pumps that achieve the needed emissions reductions in the sector when equipment is replaced.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific standards-based intervention for existing buildings. It is concrete and directly tied to emissions reductions.

parent_statement: Adopt Zero-Emission Codes and Standards and Require Energy Benchmarking for Buildings
policy_statement: Require energy benchmarking with disclosure requirements and building performance standards to encourage efficient operation and capital investment in high-performance envelopes and efficient HVAC systems.
source_quote: In addition, energy benchmarking with disclosure requirements and building performance standards will encourage efficient operation of buildings and capital investments in high-performance building envelopes and efficient heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific benchmarking and performance standards commitment. It clearly qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Scale up public financial incentives and expand access to public and private low-cost financing for building decarbonization.
source_quote: Scale Up Public Financial Incentives and Expand Access to Public and Private Low-Cost Financing for Building Decarbonization: The integration analysis indicates that to meet the necessary contribution from the buildings sector, more than 250,000 housing units each year will need to adopt electric heat pumps and energy efficiency measures from 2030 onward - greater than a tenfold increase from current market activity - with a comparable pace of transformation in commercial buildings.
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella financing initiative with multiple sub-actions, so it is extracted as a parent.

parent_statement: Scale Up Public Financial Incentives and Expand Access to Public and Private Low-Cost Financing for Building Decarbonization
policy_statement: Scale up public funding to accelerate market adoption of weatherization, electrification, energy efficiency, and resiliency upgrades.
source_quote: Public funding should be scaled up and used strategically to accelerate wide market adoption of weatherization, electrification, and additional energy efficiency and resiliency upgrades; to expand dedicated financial support for LMI households, affordable and public housing, and Disadvantaged Communities to make and benefit from these energy and resiliency upgrades while improving housing quality and comfort; and to promote thermal energy networks with support for transitioning the existing workforce and workforce development.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific funding commitment under the parent financing initiative. It is concrete and clearly financial.

parent_statement: Scale Up Public Financial Incentives and Expand Access to Public and Private Low-Cost Financing for Building Decarbonization
policy_statement: Expand dedicated financial support for LMI households, affordable and public housing, and Disadvantaged Communities to undertake energy and resiliency upgrades.
source_quote: Public funding should be scaled up and used strategically to accelerate wide market adoption of weatherization, electrification, and additional energy efficiency and resiliency upgrades; to expand dedicated financial support for LMI households, affordable and public housing, and Disadvantaged Communities to make and benefit from these energy and resiliency upgrades while improving housing quality and comfort; and to promote thermal energy networks with support for transitioning the existing workforce and workforce development.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific equity-focused funding commitment under the parent initiative. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

parent_statement: Scale Up Public Financial Incentives and Expand Access to Public and Private Low-Cost Financing for Building Decarbonization
policy_statement: Promote thermal energy networks with support for transitioning the existing workforce and workforce development.
source_quote: Public funding should be scaled up and used strategically to accelerate wide market adoption of weatherization, electrification, and additional energy efficiency and resiliency upgrades; to expand dedicated financial support for LMI households, affordable and public housing, and Disadvantaged Communities to make and benefit from these energy and resiliency upgrades while improving housing quality and comfort; and to promote thermal energy networks with support for transitioning the existing workforce and workforce development.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific intervention under the financing umbrella and is sufficiently concrete to extract.

policy_statement: Expand New York's commitment to market development, innovation, and leading by example in State projects for building decarbonization.
source_quote: Expand New York's Commitment to Market Development, Innovation, and Leading by Example in State Projects: Development of the workforce and product supply chain and technology innovation in coordination with financial incentives are important to ensure the delivery of affordable building decarbonization solutions that perform well and improve quality of life.
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella initiative with multiple market development and innovation actions beneath it.

parent_statement: Expand New York's Commitment to Market Development, Innovation, and Leading by Example in State Projects
policy_statement: Support creation of jobs in clean energy businesses located in New York and serving Disadvantaged Communities, with dedicated support for MWBEs.
source_quote: These strategies should include the creation of jobs in clean energy businesses that are located in New York and in businesses that serve Disadvantaged Communities, with dedicated support for minority- and women-owned business enterprises to innovate and actively participate in the transformation of the buildings sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific market development and equity support commitment under the parent initiative.

parent_statement: Expand New York's Commitment to Market Development, Innovation, and Leading by Example in State Projects
policy_statement: Increase public and industry awareness through education, technical assistance, case studies, strategic partnerships, and publicizing high-performance and resilient buildings.
source_quote: Market development also involves increasing public and industry awareness through education, technical assistance and case studies, strategic partnerships, and publicizing private and State buildings that demonstrate high energy performance, lower embodied carbon, and resilient building construction.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific awareness and market development action under the parent initiative.

policy_statement: Continue adopting regulations and coordinating with other states on HFC reduction policies to ensure an effective phase-down of HFCs, while supporting technical resources, training, demonstrations, and incentives for low-GWP refrigerants.
source_quote: New York State agencies should continue to adopt regulations and coordinate with other states on HFC reduction policies to ensure an effective phase-down of HFCs. For this transition, the State should support technical resources and toolkits, workforce training, demonstration projects, incentives that make low-global warming potential refrigerant technologies and alternatives available and affordable, including a focus on natural refrigerants.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific HFC phase-down policy package with regulatory and support components. It clearly qualifies.

policy_statement: Transform power generation through deployment of clean energy resources, load flexibility, and transmission and distribution investments.
source_quote: Transform Power Generation: Given the large amount of renewable energy that must be procured and developed to reach the Climate Act requirements, the State needs to incorporate load flexibility and controllability into the electric grid as sectors electrify to create a more manageable system. New and upgraded transmission and distribution systems will be needed statewide, including specific transmission and distribution investments that will be necessary to deliver energy from where the generation is located (both upstate and offshore), to where the load demand exists.
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella initiative with multiple implementation elements, so it is extracted as a parent.

parent_statement: Transform Power Generation
policy_statement: Deploy clean energy resources including land-based wind and solar, offshore wind, hydropower, renewable-fuel fuel cells, and energy storage to achieve Climate Act goals.
source_quote: To achieve stated Climate Act goals and requirements, New York must deploy clean energy resources such as land-based wind and solar, offshore wind, hydropower, fuel cells that use renewable fuels, and energy storage. While current programs have made significant progress, New York must continue to aggressively deploy clean resources while continually evaluating the effectiveness of programs and policies and amending them if renewable energy is not deployed at the pace necessary to achieve the requirements.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific deployment commitment under the parent electricity initiative. It is direct mitigation.

policy_statement: Enhance the grid to improve efficiency, delivery, reliability, renewable integration, and prioritization of clean resources.
source_quote: Enhance the Grid: While transformation of the power sector is critical to achieving the State's goals and requirements, it also presents an opportunity to make enhancements to the electric grid. Enhancements can improve the efficiency, delivery, and reliability of electricity, facilitate the integration of renewable energy, and prioritize clean resources consistent with the Climate Act.
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella initiative with multiple grid-related actions beneath it.

policy_statement: Invest in new technology to meet zero-emission electricity needs, including dispatchable zero-emission resources.
source_quote: Invest in New Technology: To achieve the 70x30 requirement, focus should be placed on energy delivery, energy efficiency, and aggressive deployment of existing renewable energy and energy storage technologies. However, Scoping Plan analysis and current studies show that the 100x40 goal requires 15 gigawatts (GW) to 45 GW of electricity from zero-emission, dispatchable resources in 2040 to meet demand and maintain reliability, although that gap may change over time depending on forecasted demand.
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella initiative with a quantified technology need and clear climate objective.

parent_statement: Invest in New Technology
policy_statement: Identify and develop dispatchable zero-emission solutions such as storage or nuclear power to balance supply and demand for the 100x40 goal.
source_quote: Addressing this gap will require identifying and developing solutions for dispatchable technologies, like storage or nuclear power, that can be called on as needed to balance supply and demand.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific technology development commitment under the parent initiative. It is direct mitigation.

policy_statement: Provide financial and technical assistance to alleviate industrial barriers and support industrial decarbonization.
source_quote: Provide Financial and Technical Assistance: The State can provide financial and technical assistance to help alleviate unique industrial sector barriers and mitigate challenges to implementing GHG emission reduction measures, including risk aversion to manufacturing process interruption, lack of in-house expertise in new technologies, lack of time to commit to energy savings solutions, lack of trust that the solution will deliver the intended benefits, and intense competition for internal company capital.
extraction_rationale: This is a named strategy heading with a clear intervention type and objective, so it is extracted as a parent.

parent_statement: Provide Financial and Technical Assistance
policy_statement: Use economic incentives to develop an in-State supply chain of green economy businesses to support industrial decarbonization.
source_quote: Using other economic incentives to develop an in-State supply chain of green economy businesses can provide further support for industrial decarbonization efforts.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific economic support measure under the parent industrial assistance strategy.

policy_statement: Use State procurement policies and practices to incentivize manufacturers to produce lower-emission goods and products.
source_quote: Incentivize Procurement for Low-Carbon Products: Through the State's own procurement policies and practices, manufacturers may be incentivized to produce goods and products that are less emission-intensive. The State, including the GreenNY Council, should develop lists of products and standards and provide policy support to implement mechanisms that lead to greater utilization of low-carbon products.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific procurement policy with named implementing bodies and mechanisms. It clearly qualifies.

policy_statement: Expand green workforce training on existing and emerging industrial decarbonization solutions.
source_quote: Support Workforce Development: Expanding the State's green workforce and the focus on training workers on existing decarbonization solutions and new technology solutions as they become available are key strategies for industrial decarbonization. State agencies can build upon the long history of delivering successful clean energy workforce development and training programs in New York.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific workforce strategy for industrial decarbonization. It is concrete enough to qualify.

policy_statement: Pursue a robust RD&D agenda for industrial and cross-sector decarbonization solutions that meet environmental justice, equity, economic, and technical scalability benchmarks.
source_quote: Facilitate Research, Development, and Demonstration: A robust research, development, and demonstration agenda will support accelerated changes, not only in the industrial sector, but in the buildings, transportation, and power sectors, all of which are likely to benefit from new solutions that likely can be realized at cost that is lower than that of current technologies. Solutions should be pursued only if they meet benchmarks for environmental justice and equity along with economic and technical scalability.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific RD&D policy commitment with explicit screening criteria. It qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Establish a new GHG emissions registry and reporting system or expand existing reporting requirements for industrial sources.
source_quote: Establish GHG Emissions Registry and Reporting System: A complete picture of the GHG emissions from a larger percentage of facilities than currently tracked will allow for a more focused effort to reduce GHG emissions from existing industrial sources, which can often be accomplished by reducing fuel combustion. In order to ensure the State has sufficient emissions data, it should establish a new GHG emissions registry and reporting system or expand existing GHG emissions reporting requirements.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific reporting system commitment with a clear purpose and mechanism. It clearly qualifies.

policy_statement: Promote sustainable forest management to increase carbon sequestration, storage, and climate resilience.
source_quote: Promote Sustainable Forest Management: Promoting a wide diversity of site-specific forest management strategies across the landscape, including harvesting, thinning, and/or leaving mature forests intact, will be most effective at increasing New York's carbon sequestration, storage, and climate resilience.
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella initiative with multiple forestry sub-strategies in the chapter.

parent_statement: Promote Sustainable Forest Management
policy_statement: Develop guidance to promote forest management for carbon storage and sequestration, climate resilience, and other climate-related issues.
source_quote: The State should develop guidance to promote forest management regarding carbon storage and sequestration, climate resilience, and other climate-related issues, recognizing that almost 75% of forest land is privately owned, with the majority of landowners owning small parcels.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific guidance-development commitment under the sustainable forest management umbrella.

policy_statement: Advance livestock management strategies to reduce agricultural methane emissions.
source_quote: Advance Livestock Management Strategies: Livestock management strategies could contribute to the deepest reductions in agricultural emissions by mitigating methane through manure management practices and precision animal feeding.
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella initiative with multiple livestock methane reduction mechanisms.

parent_statement: Advance Livestock Management Strategies
policy_statement: Advance and expand current programs for alternative manure management strategies to mitigate methane emissions.
source_quote: Alternative manure management strategies rely heavily on the advancement and expansion of current programs.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific implementation direction under the livestock management umbrella. It is brief but concrete.

parent_statement: Advance Livestock Management Strategies
policy_statement: Expand training, monitoring tools, and research and development for precision feed, forage, and herd management to reduce methane emissions.
source_quote: Precision feed, forage, and herd management strategies rely mainly on increased training and support to the farm community, expanded use of monitoring and decision tools, and continued and enhanced research and development of feed supplements and additives for further methane reductions.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific package of interventions under the livestock management umbrella. It clearly qualifies.

policy_statement: Improve soil health and nutrient management to reduce nitrous oxide emissions and increase carbon sequestration, and expand agroforestry for resilience and co-benefits.
source_quote: Improve Soil Health, Nutrient Management, and Agroforestry: Strategies to improve soil health and nutrient management primarily focus on nitrous oxide reduction and increasing carbon sequestration. Agroforestry recommendations that add trees to areas of agricultural production have the potential to elevate local food production and resiliency; improve water and air quality; provide storm and flood mitigation; improve drought resiliency; provide habitat, scenic vistas, and agritourism; and increase economic development and jobs.
extraction_rationale: This is a named strategy theme with explicit mitigation and resilience mechanisms. It is extracted as an individual because no sub-items are listed immediately beneath in this summary section.

policy_statement: Promote a climate-focused bioeconomy through training, wood product markets, biomass feedstock planning, support for low-carbon products, bio-based research, and deployment of net negative carbon dioxide removal.
source_quote: Promote a Climate-Focused Bioeconomy: Recommended climate-focused bioeconomy strategies include developing forestry training programs, expanding markets for sustainably harvested wood products, developing a sustainable biomass feedstock action plan, increasing market access and providing financial and technical assistance for New York's low-carbon products, advancing bio-based products research, and deploying net negative carbon dioxide removal.
extraction_rationale: This is a named strategy theme with a concrete list of interventions. It is broad but sufficiently specific to qualify as policy.

policy_statement: Reduce, reuse, and recycle waste to shift materials management and reduce waste-sector GHG emissions.
source_quote: Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle Waste: Waste reduction, reuse, and recycling strategies in this Scoping Plan fundamentally shift the way New York currently produces, uses, and handles products and materials at end-of-life. Significant GHG emissions impacts from this sector include uncaptured emissions of methane from landfills, specifically from organic materials.
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella initiative with multiple waste reduction and recycling sub-strategies.

policy_statement: Monitor, detect, and reduce fugitive emissions from solid waste management facilities and water resource recovery facilities.
source_quote: Monitor, Detect, and Reduce Fugitive Emissions: Fugitive emissions at solid waste management facilities and water resource recovery facilities are currently under-reported and vary based on site-specific factors such as waste composition and facility design. Assessing these systems both during and beyond the active life of operation and repairing equipment to minimize fugitive emissions (leaks) can significantly reduce waste sector GHG emissions.
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella initiative with a clear mitigation mechanism and multiple likely sub-actions.

policy_statement: Establish markets for recovered resources and biogas utilization to support waste reduction and strategic use of unavoidable gases.
source_quote: Establish Markets for Recovered Resources and Biogas Utilization: Solid waste management facilities and water resource recovery facilities should follow the strategies in this Scoping Plan to achieve the maximum reduction, reuse, and recycling of waste, recognizing that some wastes (including biosolids) are unavoidable. Additionally, the organic fraction of waste already in landfills will produce methane in place for many years. Capturing these unavoidable gases for strategic and local use as the State transitions to electrification will help meet the requirements and goals of the Climate Act while avoiding future reliance on fossil fuels.
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella initiative with a clear strategic objective and multiple implementation pathways.

policy_statement: Protect, restore, and monitor natural and working lands to support GHG mitigation, carbon sequestration and storage, and land restoration.
source_quote: Protect, Restore, and Monitor Natural and Working Lands: New York has more than 28 million acres of natural and working lands. Current and future use of natural and working lands has important implications for mitigation of GHG emissions and carbon sequestration and storage, including protecting high-value lands through acquisition, avoiding conversion and development, and land restoration.
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella initiative with multiple land protection and restoration sub-actions.

parent_statement: Protect, Restore, and Monitor Natural and Working Lands
policy_statement: Increase carbon sequestration and storage through afforestation and reforestation in New York State.
source_quote: Afforestation and reforestation have the potential to greatly increase carbon sequestration and storage capacity in New York State.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific intervention under the natural and working lands umbrella. It is explicit and climate-focused.

parent_statement: Protect, Restore, and Monitor Natural and Working Lands
policy_statement: Protect, restore, monitor, and maintain carbon stored in wetlands, submerged aquatic vegetation, and other coastal habitats.
source_quote: Another strategy includes protecting, restoring, monitoring, and maintaining the carbon stored in freshwater, non-tidal, coastal and estuarine tidal wetlands; submerged aquatic vegetation; and other coastal habitats.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific ecosystem carbon strategy under the natural and working lands umbrella.

policy_statement: Provide municipalities with tools, technical guidance, support, and direct grants to include afforestation, reforestation, farmland protection, and clean energy siting in comprehensive plans and zoning ordinances.
source_quote: Consider Forests and Farmland in Land Use Policies: The strategies to address forests and farmland in land use policies include equipping municipalities with the necessary tools and resources to effectively protect New York's publicly and privately owned natural and working lands while also advancing renewable energy siting. Such tools and resources include technical guidance and support and direct grants to municipalities to include afforestation, reforestation, farmland protection, and clean energy siting in municipal comprehensive plans and zoning ordinances.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific local planning support policy with named tools and grants. It clearly qualifies.

policy_statement: Support local smart growth land use decisions through planning and zoning grants, regional planning, technical assistance, incentives, disincentives, and where appropriate mandates.
source_quote: Promote Smart Growth: Smart growth land use strategies seek to achieve smart, sustainable, and equitable planning, zoning, and projects that align with supportive transportation, economic development, and housing policies and practices. While land use zoning falls mostly within municipal authority, the State can support local land use decisions through direct planning and zoning grants; regional/county planning; technical assistance and capacity-building; and State and local incentives, disincentives, and, where appropriate, mandates.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific smart growth support strategy with named policy tools. It qualifies as policy.

policy_statement: Commit to creating, implementing, and updating a comprehensive and equitable State climate change adaptation and resilience plan.
source_quote: The components of the key strategies are derived from the initiatives and their respective components recommended to the Climate Action Council (Council) by the Land Use and Local Government Advisory Panel. A detailed description of the strategies and components can be found in Appendix H.
extraction_rationale: The section heading names a clear strategy, but the body text here does not restate it in full. Included because the chapter explicitly presents named key strategies; source support is weaker than ideal due to formatting.

policy_statement: Provide access to the latest regional and local climate projections data for Aotearoa to support future climate risk assessment and adaptation decisions.
source_quote:
The National Institute of Water and Atmospheric Research (NIWA) Projections Project is working to make the global climate projections from the most recent Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) report (AR6 WG1) more applicable to Aotearoa . This w ill give New Zealanders the regional and local climate projections data they need to assess future climate risk and make adaptation decisions.

By January 2023, national climate projection datasets for Aotearoa are being produced .
section_header: Action 3.1: Provide access to the latest climate projections data
extraction_rationale: Qualifies as a policy because it is a named government action with a specific intervention, lead agency, and deadline. It directly supports adaptation decision-making through climate risk information.

policy_statement: Establish a platform for Māori climate action to build climate response partnership with Māori and support Māori participation, strategy, and solutions.
source_quote: The platform for Māori climate action is the key mechanism through which the Government is looking to build a climate response partnership with Māori. It will build Te Tiriti partnership and greater recognition of Māori rights and interests, including Treaty settlement commitments, into the climate response.
section_header: Action 3.3: Establish a platform for Māori climate action
extraction_rationale: This is a named umbrella initiative followed by explicit focus areas and phases, so it qualifies as a parent policy under the hierarchy rules. It is a concrete institutional mechanism for adaptation governance.

parent_statement: Establish a platform for Māori climate action
policy_statement: Resource and co-design processes and mechanisms with Māori to embed partnership and representation in the climate response.
source_quote:
The platform will build on three focus areas:

- embed partnership and representation - t o uphold Te Tiriti principles, processes and mechanisms will be resourced and designed alongside Māori to help tangata whenua to actively participate in the climate response
section_header: Action 3.3: Establish a platform for Māori climate action
extraction_rationale: This is a specific sub-action listed under the named platform initiative. It is a concrete institutional commitment, though not quantified beyond being part of the platform design.

parent_statement: Establish a platform for Māori climate action
policy_statement: Support Māori to define, measure and implement a national Māori climate strategy and action plan.
source_quote:
- support Māori -led strategy and alignment - t o elevate te ao Māori within the climate response, Māori will be supported to define, measure and implement a national Māori climate strategy and action plan
- activate kaupapa Māori, tangata Māori solutions - to enable community action, kaupapa Māori, tangata Māori actions and solutions for the climate emergency will be funded.
section_header: Action 3.3: Establish a platform for Māori climate action
extraction_rationale: This is a clearly enumerated sub-action under the platform. It is policy-relevant because it commits government support for a named strategy and action plan.

parent_statement: Establish a platform for Māori climate action
policy_statement: Fund kaupapa Māori and tangata Māori climate actions and solutions to enable community action.
source_quote:
- support Māori -led strategy and alignment - t o elevate te ao Māori within the climate response, Māori will be supported to define, measure and implement a national Māori climate strategy and action plan
- activate kaupapa Māori, tangata Māori solutions - to enable community action, kaupapa Māori, tangata Māori actions and solutions for the climate emergency will be funded.
section_header: Action 3.3: Establish a platform for Māori climate action
extraction_rationale: This is a specific funded sub-action under the platform. It qualifies because it includes a resource commitment ('will be funded') tied to climate action.

parent_statement: Establish a platform for Māori climate action
policy_statement: Establish an interim ministerial advisory committee to provide immediate strategic advice on climate response policy affecting Māori and advise on an enduring representative platform.
source_quote:
The platform will be set up in two phases:

- establish an interim ministerial advisory committee to:
- -support immediate strategic advice and expertise across climate response policy and work programmes that impact Māori
- -advise on a more enduring representative platform to help advance an equitable transition for Māori
section_header: Action 3.3: Establish a platform for Māori climate action
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete institutional sub-action under the platform with a defined governance mechanism. It qualifies as policy due to its formal committee structure and role.

parent_statement: Establish a platform for Māori climate action
policy_statement: Transition the Māori climate action platform to an enduring governance form developed with Māori for long-term strategic advice on emissions reduction and adaptation plans.
source_quote:
- transition the platform to a more enduring form, developed with Māori, to provide a governance presence and strategic advice in emissions reduction plans and national adaptation plans over the longer term.

By the end of 2022, the Interim Ministerial Committee will be established. By 2024, phase two of the platform for Māori climate action will be developed.
section_header: Action 3.3: Establish a platform for Māori climate action
extraction_rationale: This is a distinct phase under the parent initiative with a timeline and governance function. It is a policy commitment rather than background description.

policy_statement: Raise public awareness of climate hazards and emergency preparedness through campaigns, resources, and tailored information.
source_quote: Enable and work with communities, including rural communities, iwi and Māori, organisations and others to make emergency preparedness a part of everyday life through public awareness and advice. Examples are public education campaigns and resources, such as GetReady.govt.nz, and tailored information for those who face additional challenges. This will help communities to understand the hazards and support them to take action before, and during, an emergency.
section_header: Action 3.4: Raise awareness of climate hazards and how to prepare
extraction_rationale: This is a named intervention with specific implementation tools and a deadline. It directly addresses preparedness for climate hazards, making it an adaptation policy.

policy_statement: Implement and potentially expand mandatory climate-related disclosures for major financial market participants.
source_quote: The Financial Sector (Climate -related Disclosures and Other Matters) Amendment Act 2021 requires about 200 of Aotearoa New Zealand's largest financial market participants to analyse and publicly disclose their climate-related risks and opportunities each year . The purpose is to ensure the effects of climate change are routinely considered in decisions for business, investment, lending and insurance. As the risks and opportunities are more accurately factored into pricing and become more transparent, we expect this will shift investment away from high-risk areas, and towards a sustainable, low-emissions and financially stable economy.
section_header: Action 3.5: Support high-quality implementation of climate-related disclosures and explore expansion
extraction_rationale: This qualifies because it is grounded in legislation and imposes a binding disclosure requirement. Climate adaptation and resilience are explicit through climate risk management; mitigation is also explicitly referenced via a low-emissions economy.

policy_statement: Improve natural hazard disclosure requirements on Land Information Memoranda to support informed property decisions.
source_quote: Changes to legal requirements for Land Information Memoranda (LIMs) will help people make better-informed decisions about natural hazard risk when buying a property. It will give councils greater certainty about what hazard information to include on the LI M. This will link to the suite of information and data portals that communities will have about the risks.
section_header: Action 3.6: Improve natural hazard information on Land Information Memoranda
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory change with a clear mechanism and purpose. It directly supports adaptation by improving hazard-risk disclosure for property decisions.

policy_statement: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted non-statutory adaptation guidance for decision makers to assess and manage climate risks.
source_quote: The Government will roll out a programme of non -statutory guidance for decision makers to assess and manage climate risks. This could also support regulatory requirements to be developed through the National Planning Framework.
section_header: Action 3.7: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance
extraction_rationale: This is a parent policy because it is a named programme followed by numbered sub-actions. It is a concrete government intervention to improve adaptation practice.

parent_statement: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance
policy_statement: Promote updated Aotearoa climate projections guidance reflecting AR6 IPCC changes for risk management planning.
source_quote: An update for Aotearoa that highlights changes from the 2021 AR6 IPCC.12 report. The update will enable stakeholders to quickly assess where they may need to adapt their risk management plans to account for the latest science.
section_header: 3.7.1: Promote the use of the Aotearoa New Zealand Climate Change Projections guidance
extraction_rationale: This is a numbered sub-item under the parent guidance programme and specifies a concrete guidance product. It directly supports adaptation planning.

parent_statement: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance
policy_statement: Produce adaptation guidance for central government policy makers to ensure new policy and services consider adaptation.
source_quote: A methodology for central government to ensure it considers adaptation in new policy and services. This will avoid increased exposure or vulnerability to climate impacts.
section_header: 3.7.2: Produce adaptation guidance for central government policy makers
extraction_rationale: This is a specific sub-action with a named methodology and explicit adaptation purpose. It qualifies as a policy due to its concrete intervention.

parent_statement: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance
policy_statement: Produce guidance on dynamic adaptive pathways planning for central and local government.
source_quote: A guide for central and local government on how to plan for adaptation in a context of uncertain climate futures.
section_header: 3.7.3: Produce guidance for dynamic adaptive pathways planning (DAPP)
extraction_rationale: This is a numbered sub-action under the parent programme and names a specific planning methodology. It is a concrete adaptation planning tool.

parent_statement: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance
policy_statement: Produce guidance on using socio-economic scenarios in climate risk assessment and adaptation planning.
source_quote: Assists central and local government and businesses to consider future socio-economic scenarios when assessing climate risks, and planning how to manage them.
section_header: 3.7.4: Produce guidance on using different socio-economic scenarios for adaptation planning
extraction_rationale: This is a distinct numbered sub-action with a specific planning intervention. It directly supports adaptation decisions under uncertainty.

parent_statement: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance
policy_statement: Regularly update adaptation guidance for local government on planning, decisions, and communicating climate information.
source_quote: Supports local government to consider adaptation in planning and decisions. This will include guidance on communicating scientific and technical information to communities, and on making climate decisions.
section_header: 3.7.5: Regularly update adaptation guidance for local government
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete sub-action under the guidance programme. It qualifies because it commits to recurring guidance updates for local government adaptation practice.

parent_statement: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance
policy_statement: Produce guidance on integrating mātauranga Māori into adaptive planning and engagement with mana whenua.
source_quote: Helps central and local government effectively engage with hapū, iwi and Māori when managing risk and planning for adaptation.
section_header: 3.7.6: Produce guidance on integrating mātauranga Māori into adaptive planning and working with mana whenua
extraction_rationale: This is a numbered sub-action with a specific guidance output and adaptation purpose. It is a concrete policy tool for adaptation governance.

parent_statement: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance
policy_statement: Produce guidance for communities, sectors, and governments to prepare adaptation plans using a standard approach under uncertainty.
source_quote: Enables communities and different audiences, sectors and levels of government to produce their own adaptation plans, using a standard approach under conditions of uncertainty in climate projections. This could include interpreting downscaled projections.
section_header: 3.7.7: Produce guidance for preparing adaptation plans
extraction_rationale: This is a specific sub-action under the parent programme and clearly commits to a named guidance product. It directly supports adaptation planning.

parent_statement: Deliver a rolling programme of targeted adaptation guidance
policy_statement: Regularly update the guide to local climate change risk assessments on a six-year cycle.
source_quote: Sets out a step-by-step process for local risk assessments. It will be updated on a six-yearly cycle after the release of each national climate change risk assessment. It supports local government to conduct their own assessments, to better understand the risks their regions face.
section_header: 3.7.8: Regularly update the guide to local climate change risk assessments
extraction_rationale: This is a numbered sub-action with a recurring update commitment and a defined product. It qualifies as a policy because it institutionalizes local risk assessment guidance.

policy_statement: Develop guidance for infrastructure asset owners to assess and manage climate risks to physical assets and services.
source_quote: Te Waihanga will scope and deliver guidance for asset owners to evaluate risks to their physical assets and the services they provide. This will help them understand, and subsequently manage, the impacts of climate change on existing and new assets.
section_header: Action 3.8: Develop guidance for assessing risk and impact on physical assets and the services they provide
extraction_rationale: This is a named action with a specific intervention and implementation timeline. It directly addresses climate risk management for infrastructure assets.

policy_statement: Assess socioeconomic and climate vulnerability for Māori by combining social and climate data to target resilience support.
source_quote: This action will collect and analyse social data against climate data to determine where support for resilience is most needed. This will enable the Government to better understand what support is needed to strengthen resilience for Māori communities.
section_header: Action 3.10: Assess socioeconomic and climate vulnerability for Māori
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete analytical intervention with a clear adaptation purpose and target group. It qualifies because it commits to a specific assessment methodology.

policy_statement: Implement the National Disaster Resilience Strategy through a pathway to deliver its vision, goals, and objectives.
source_quote: The National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) will design a pathway to give effect to the National Disaster Resilience Strategy's vision, goals and objectives. The vision is for a disaster-resilient nation that acts proactively to manage risks and to build resilience in a way that contributes to the wellbeing and prosperity of all.
section_header: Action 3.11: Implement the National Disaster Resilience Strategy
extraction_rationale: This is a named implementation commitment for an existing strategy. It qualifies as policy because it commits government action to operationalize resilience objectives.

policy_statement: Improve the use of science, data, mātauranga Māori, and knowledge in emergency management decisions.
source_quote: The National Emergency Management Agency 's 2021 Science Strategy will be used to create a framework for scientific engagement, promotion and influence for risk reduction, readiness, response and recovery. Research, data, mātauranga Māori, local knowledge and technical expertise will inform strategic decisions on emergency management, and explore practical interventions to improve disaster resilience.
section_header: Action 3.12: Improve how science, data and knowledge are used to inform emergency management
extraction_rationale: This is a specific framework-building action tied to emergency management and disaster resilience. It directly supports adaptation through improved hazard preparedness and response.

policy_statement: Provide a forestry planning and advisory service to reduce climate risks and guide land-use decisions including restoration and land retirement.
source_quote: The forestry planning and advisory service will help to reduce climate risks by providing datainformed advice and planning tools. Advice will be on both harvest and non-harvest forestry for example, to help decision makers consider where land is available for new forestry; where restoration, regeneration and reversion may be needed; and where unsuitable land may need to be retired from forestry, including conversion from plantation to indigenous forestry.
section_header: Action 3.13: Provide a forestry planning and advisory service
extraction_rationale: This is a named service intervention with specific planning functions. It has explicit climate-risk reduction and ecological restoration elements, making it adaptation-focused with an ecosystem mechanism.

policy_statement: Deliver the Integrated Farm Planning Programme to integrate climate change, greenhouse gases, biodiversity, and resilience into farm planning.
source_quote:
The Integrated Farm Planning Programme will provide a framework for farmers and growers to incorporate all their key farming areas, including greenhouse gases, into their farm planning. The goal is to enable a farmer or grower, using their preferred data -collection tool, platform or system, to meet all regulatory and business needs within a single framework.

The programme brings together many broader work programmes, including greenhouse gas farm planning, a biodiversity planning module, upskilling for primary industry advisors, planning for adverse events and resilience, and increased data sharing in the primary sector.
section_header: Action 3.14: Deliver the Integrated Farm Planning Programme
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete programme with multiple named components. It is primarily about improving farm planning efficiency and resilience, while explicitly including greenhouse gases and biodiversity, allowing a mitigation secondary category.

policy_statement: Design and implement the Farm Monitoring Programme to improve farm management and adaptation using farm-level physical, financial, and environmental data.
source_quote: Quality data will inform decision-making to enable improved farm management decisions and profitability, while considering compliance and regulations to assist greenhouse gas reductions. This data helps farmers adapt to climate change by determining optimal stocking rates, diversifying crop rotations, improving soil quality, reducing off-farm flows of nutrients, and implementing more efficient farm practices to improve performance.
section_header: Action 3.15: Design and implement the Farm Monitoring Programme
extraction_rationale: This is a named programme with a specific intervention and adaptation purpose. It is primarily resource-efficiency oriented through farm optimization, with explicit greenhouse gas reductions stated, justifying a mitigation secondary category.

policy_statement: Improve consumer understanding of property insurance pricing and climate risks through information sheets linked to hazard disclosure.
source_quote: Information sheets will help consumers identify, manage or even reduce their climate risks. This links to the work on Land Information Memoranda (LIMs), as greater disclosure can help people make better decisions on where to buy and build property.
section_header: Action 3.16: Improve consumer understanding of property insurance pricing and risks
extraction_rationale: This is a specific informational intervention tied to climate risk management in property decisions. It qualifies as adaptation policy because climate risk reduction is explicit.

policy_statement: Support integration of climate adaptation and mitigation into new and revised standards commissioned by third parties.
source_quote: At the beginning of each relevant project, Standards NZ may bring adaptation and mitigation to the attention of the committee members of a standard it has commissioned. This may help improve resilience in existing and new assets, by guiding industry practice in asset design and operation.
section_header: Action 3.17: Support and promote the integration of climate adaptation and mitigation in new and revised standards commissioned by third parties
extraction_rationale: This is a standards-related intervention affecting asset design and operation. Adaptation is the primary mechanism, while mitigation is explicitly named in the policy text.

policy_statement: Review electricity and gas networks' management of climate risk and resilience through asset management plan requirements and published reviews.
source_quote: The Commission is currently consulting on amending the asset management plan requirements for electricity distributors so that sector stakeholders can better understand distributors' risk management, including managing network resilience challenges posed by climate change. From time to time, the Commission will publish reviews of aspects of regulated networks' plans, to support them to improve their approach to managing risk and building adaptive capacity, and to provide more confidence that their related expenditure forecasts are robust.
section_header: Action 3.18: Review electricity and gas networks' management of climate risk and resilience
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory review commitment with a clear climate resilience objective. It qualifies because it changes oversight requirements for regulated networks.

policy_statement: Develop the Te Ara Paerangi Future Pathways programme to orient the research, science and innovation system toward national goals including climate change.
source_quote: Te Ara Paerangi - Future Pathways programme for the research, science and innovation system will position the system for the future. This includes focusing resources on national goals, such as climate change, and addressing other issues facing the research system, such as how best to honour Tiriti obligati ons, system funding and incentives, workforce and institutional design.
section_header: Action 3.19: Develop Te Ara Paerangi - Future Pathways programme for the research , science and innovation system
extraction_rationale: This is a named programme with a concrete system-reform intervention. Climate relevance is indirect because climate is one of several national goals rather than the sole objective.

policy_statement: Develop mātauranga Māori indicators to monitor climate impacts on biodiversity, mahinga kai, flora, fauna, and human health.
source_quote: Mātauranga Māori indicators will enable monitoring and evaluation of impacts on biodiversity, mahinga kai, flora, fauna and human health. This will create data baselines that centralise indigenous knowledge and values, and can be used in environmental assessments.
section_header: Action 3.21: Develop mātauranga Māori indicators of climate impacts on the natural environment
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed but specific methodological intervention with a clear climate-impact monitoring purpose. It supports adaptation by improving assessment of environmental vulnerability.

policy_statement: Work with community housing providers to improve climate hazard data and resilience strategies for emergency management and long-term adaptation.
source_quote: This will provide better data and information on the exposure of community housing providers to climate risks. An action programme will increase the resilience of community housing by supporting strategies for emergency management and long-term adaptation. In turn, this will reduce exposure of community housing tenants to climate risks.
section_header: Action 3.22: Work with community housing providers to enable effective climate hazard response
extraction_rationale: This is a specific proposed action with a named intervention and target sector. It directly addresses climate risk and long-term adaptation for housing.

policy_statement: Develop detailed 3D coastal mapping and GNSS upgrades to assess sea-level rise and model tsunami and storm surge impacts.
source_quote: Coastal mapping comprises detailed 3D mapping of the coastal zone and the upgrade and addition of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) sites in the coastal zone. The purpose is to assess the impacts of sea-level rise and model the impacts of tsunami and storm surges on communities, infrastructure and biodiversity.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete technical intervention with a clear adaptation purpose related to coastal hazards. It qualifies because it specifies the mapping activity and intended use.

policy_statement: Produce tools and guidance specific to mātauranga Māori and mātauranga indicators for community climate action and planning under uncertainty.
source_quote: These resources will be developed in partnership with hapū , iwi and Māori, to help them take action in their communities and to inform decisions. This action will provide targeted guidance on planning in uncertain conditions.
section_header: Action 3.24: Produce new tools and guidance specific to mātauranga Māori and mātauranga indicators
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed but concrete guidance action with a clear adaptation-planning purpose. It qualifies due to the specific deliverable and target users.

policy_statement: Design a methodology for climate risk assessments of public buildings, including cultural, heritage, and seismic considerations.
source_quote:
Developing a methodology for risk assessment based on the property resilience research (see action 5.7: Reduce and manage the impacts of climate hazards on homes and buildings), to address matters such as cultural and heritage values and seismic hazard risks, will support decision-making.

This will help owners of public buildings assess and understand climate ri sks and implement adaptation strategies.
section_header: Action 3.25: Design methodology for risk assessments of public buildings
extraction_rationale: This is a specific proposed methodological intervention for public buildings. It directly supports adaptation by enabling climate risk assessment and adaptation strategies.

policy_statement: Produce guidance for disaster risk management for cultural heritage to reduce risks before, during, and after disasters.
source_quote: This action will improve disaster risk management for cultural heritage through guidance on reducing risks before, during and after disasters.
section_header: Action 3.26: Produce guidance for disaster risk management for cultural heritage
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete proposed guidance action with a clear hazard-risk reduction purpose. It qualifies as adaptation policy focused on cultural heritage resilience.

policy_statement: Develop a framework to assess exposure and vulnerability of taonga and cultural assets to climate change.
source_quote: It will develop a framework to identify valued cultural heritage and the actual and potential exposure and vulnerability of cultural heritage to climate change. The framework will take a broad and inclusive approach, recognising the ways in which different communities identify, access and participate in what is culturally important to them.
section_header: Action 3.27: Develop a framework for assessing exposure and vulnerability of taonga/cultural assets to climate change
extraction_rationale: This is a specific proposed framework with an explicit climate-change vulnerability purpose. It qualifies as adaptation policy because it supports assessment of climate impacts on cultural assets.

policy_statement: Assess healthcare service resilience to climate events, infrastructure risks, and changing illness patterns.
source_quote: The aim of this action is to understand the healthcare service's vulnerability to climate events, and consider physical risks to infrastructure, and changes in illness patterns and vulnerability. This will help to ensure communities can continue to access the healthcare services they need, even in the face of climate change adversity.
extraction_rationale: This is a named current action with a clear adaptation objective for health-system resilience. It qualifies because it commits to a specific vulnerability assessment.

policy_statement: Produce an adaptation professional development programme to build capability and uptake of adaptation tools and guidance.
source_quote: This will target building capability and help circulate new tools and guidance among different audiences. It will encourage uptake and effective use by practitioners and others working on climate adaptation.
section_header: Action 3.29: Produce an adaptation professional development programme for key audiences
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed but concrete capacity-building programme with a clear adaptation purpose. It qualifies because it specifies a named intervention and target outcome.

policy_statement: Reform the resource management system by replacing the RMA with new legislation including a Climate Adaptation Act to support adaptation and reduce climate risk.
source_quote:
In early 2021, the Government announced its intention to repeal the Resource Management Act 1991 and replace it with a Natural and Built Environments Act, a Spatial Planning Act and a Climate Adaptation Act.

The Government's objectives for the reform include better preparation for adaptation and risks from natural hazards, and better mitigation of emissions contributing to climate change.
section_header: Action 4.1: Reform the resource management system
extraction_rationale: This is a major legislative reform with explicit climate adaptation and mitigation objectives. It clearly qualifies due to binding legal change and named replacement acts.

policy_statement: Set national direction on natural hazard risk management and climate adaptation through the National Planning Framework.
source_quote: The National Planning Framework will set clear direction for local authorities on how to achieve the climate resilience outcomes in the Natural and Built Environments Act. It will set out methods and requirements for planning for natural hazards and considering future climate risks.
section_header: Action 4.2: Set national direction on natural hazard risk management and climate adaptation through the National Planning Framework
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete planning-policy intervention with a named framework and explicit climate resilience purpose. It qualifies because it establishes methods and requirements for planning.

policy_statement: Establish a decision-making framework for adapting new and existing public housing assets to reduce tenant exposure to climate hazards.
source_quote:
A framework for public housing assets will be developed to determine the actions to adapt new and existing assets. This will help reduce exposure of public housing tenants to climate hazards.

The action will also increase the resilience of public housing. It will identify where retrofitting is needed, and ensure dwellings are well located.
section_header: Action 4.3: Establish an initiative for resilient public housing
extraction_rationale: This is a named initiative with a specific framework and adaptation purpose. It qualifies because it commits to concrete adaptation actions for public housing assets.

policy_statement: Embed adaptation into housing and urban development funding models, including Māori housing, by accounting for current and future climate hazards.
source_quote:
Existing funding programmes for urban development and housing, including Māori housing, will be updated to consider the costs of existing and future climate hazards. New funding programmes may be created if there are gaps.

This will help ensure funding for urban growth considers climate hazards (eg, new infrastructure is well located and designed to perform under changing climatic conditions).
section_header: Action 4.4: Embed adaptation in funding models for housing and urban development, including Māori housing
extraction_rationale: This is a funding-policy reform with explicit climate hazard integration. It qualifies as a policy because it changes government funding criteria and may create new programmes.

policy_statement: Reform institutional arrangements for water services by creating new water entities with statutory resilience and climate objectives.
source_quote:
The Government will create new water entities that will work with councils and communities to improve health and wellbeing outcomes for our communities and protect our environment for generations to come. The National Climate Change Risk Assessment 2020 identified risk to potable water as the most urgent risk from climate change.

If the Bill is enacted in its current form, one of the statutory objectives of the new entities will be to 'deliver water services in a sustainable and resilient manner that seeks to mitigate the effects of climate change and natural hazards'.
section_header: Action 4.5: Reform institutional arrangements for water services
extraction_rationale: This is a legislative and institutional reform with explicit statutory climate resilience language. It qualifies due to the creation of new entities and statutory objectives.

policy_statement: Integrate climate risks and future adaptation into Treasury guidance for infrastructure investment decisions.
source_quote:
The Treasury publishes a range of guidance for central government departments and other entities on investment management and state sector performance. It will integrate consideration of climate risks and future adaptation into this guidance.
