This will help ensure that planning for new assets, renewals and major upgrades will: - include climate risks in the strategic case, and early assessment of the options - include options to build adaptive capacity (eg, nature-based solutions) - incorporate the full cost of adaptation over the life of an asset into decision-making
section_header: Action 4.6: Integrate adaptation into Treasury decisions on infrastructure
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete change to government investment guidance with explicit adaptation requirements. It qualifies because it alters decision-making criteria for infrastructure investments.

policy_statement: Integrate adaptation into Waka Kotahi investment decision-making, including business cases, risk assessment, and intervention hierarchy.
source_quote: Waka Kotahi will incorporate adaptation in the Investment Decision Making Framework, its structured approach to decisions on investment in land transport. This will include business case development and risk assessment. Also embedded will be an intervention hierarchy, which considers integrated planning, demand management, and the best use of existing networks before developing new infrastructure.
section_header: Action 4.7: Integrate adaptation into Waka Kotahi decision-making
extraction_rationale: This is a named institutional decision-making reform with explicit adaptation integration. It qualifies because it changes the framework governing transport investment decisions.

policy_statement: Amend the Environmental Reporting Act 2015 to improve measurement and reporting of environmental change.
source_quote: This work seeks to improve how the Ministry for the Environment (MfE) monitors, manages, accesses and reports on the environment. The amendments will extend the Environmental Reporting Act's functionality and breadth so that environmental reports have more impact.
section_header: Action 4.8: Amend the Environmental Reporting Act 2015 to allow better measurement of environmental change
extraction_rationale: This is a legislative amendment with a concrete mechanism. Climate relevance is indirect because it improves environmental reporting broadly rather than targeting climate adaptation alone.

policy_statement: Pass legislation through the Climate Adaptation Act to support managed retreat and address associated technical, legal, and financial issues.
source_quote:
The Government will develop legislation to address the complex technical, legal and financial issues associated with managed retreat as described by the Resource Management Review Panel. This legislation is being progressed through the development of the Climate Adaptation Act.

By the end of 2023, the Government is expecting to introduce the Climate Adaptation Bill, setting out the managed retreat framework.
section_header: Action 5.1: Pass legislation to support managed retreat
extraction_rationale: This is a clear legislative commitment with a named bill and framework. It directly addresses climate-related relocation from intolerable risk, making it a core adaptation policy.

policy_statement: Conduct the Future for Local Government review to recommend changes enabling agile, sustainable, and proactive adaptation governance and funding.
source_quote: Adaptation will bring new challenges and opportunities to local governance. The system must be equipped for agile, sustainable and proactive decision-makin g and implementation. The review is likely to include recommendations on what local government does, how it does it and how it pays for it.
section_header: Action 5.2: The Future for Local Government review
extraction_rationale: This is a formal review with a defined scope around adaptation governance and financing. It qualifies because it is a named government process intended to shape institutional arrangements.

policy_statement: Complete a Westport case study to explore co-investment options for flood resilience with councils and local iwi.
source_quote: The Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) is working with the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), the West Coast Regional Council, the Buller District Council and local iwi to explore options to increase flood resilience in Westport. This case stud y will focus on the challenges facing small local authorities and vulnerable communities in funding flood risk management.
section_header: Action 5.3: Complete case study to explore co-investment for flood resilience
extraction_rationale: This is a specific government-led case study with a named place, partners, and resilience objective. It qualifies because it is a concrete intervention to inform adaptation financing and flood risk management.

policy_statement: Develop options to maintain access and affordability of home flood insurance to support resilience and recovery.
source_quote: Work is underway to increase understanding of the scale and timing of changes to the insurance market arising from greater use of risk-based pricing by insurers and flooding exacerbated by climate change . This work includes exploring options to support access and affordability of flood insurance. The Government intends to develop options that ensure home flood insurance continues to play an appropriate role in supporting community resilience.
section_header: Action 5.4: Develop options for home flood insurance
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete policy development process focused on climate-related insurance resilience. It qualifies because it commits to developing options for a specific financial risk-management mechanism.

policy_statement: Publish and maintain a government-wide programme of work on how Aotearoa meets climate change costs and invests in resilience.
source_quote: The Government is also considering adaptation criteria for the Climate Emergency Response Fund (CERF) and is launching its Sovereign Green Bond programme (see action 5.15: Public investment in climate change initiatives). In addition, it continues to explore other options to encourage climatepositive, resilient investment. It will communicate how this range of work is progressing across government in one place. A dedicated webpage will be kept up to date as work evolves and new actions are developed.
section_header: Action 5.5: Publish the programme of work on how Aotearoa meets the costs of climate change and invests in resilience
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete transparency and coordination commitment with a specific output (dedicated webpage). It qualifies because it formalizes communication of resilience investment work across government.

policy_statement: Scope a resilience standard or code for infrastructure to encourage risk reduction and resilience planning in existing and new assets.
source_quote:
Te Waihanga will scope the impact (including of costs, benefits and regulations) of a standard or code for resilient infrastructure.

This action will focus on: - how a standard or code would encourage risk reduction and resilience planning in existing and new assets - how to integrate resilience planning into the asset-management cycle, to maximise uptake and impact
section_header: Action 5.6: Scope a resilience standard or code for infrastructure
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete standards-development action with a clear resilience objective. It qualifies because it may lead to a formal standard or code affecting infrastructure planning.

policy_statement: Reduce and manage the impacts of climate hazards on homes and buildings through research, guidance, assessment frameworks, and incentives.
source_quote:
This action includes five components that build off one another and are necessary to inform regulatory change and other actions in this chapter . These five components are :

- collate existing information to help people adapt their homes and buildings
- carry out research to understand the impacts of climate hazards on various housing typologies, and the costs and benefits of adaptation at the property level
section_header: Action 5.7: Reduce and manage the impacts of climate hazards on homes and buildings
extraction_rationale: This is a parent policy because it is a named action explicitly broken into five components. It is a concrete adaptation programme for the built environment.

parent_statement: Reduce and manage the impacts of climate hazards on homes and buildings
policy_statement: Collate existing information to help people adapt their homes and buildings.
source_quote:
- collate existing information to help people adapt their homes and buildings
- carry out research to understand the impacts of climate hazards on various housing typologies, and the costs and benefits of adaptation at the property level
section_header: Action 5.7: Reduce and manage the impacts of climate hazards on homes and buildings
extraction_rationale: This is a listed component under the parent action. It qualifies as a sub-policy because it is a specific intervention supporting household adaptation.

parent_statement: Reduce and manage the impacts of climate hazards on homes and buildings
policy_statement: Research climate hazard impacts on housing typologies and the costs and benefits of property-level adaptation.
source_quote:
- carry out research to understand the impacts of climate hazards on various housing typologies, and the costs and benefits of adaptation at the property level
- develop property-level guidance based on updated climate data to inform homeowners and renters about climate impacts and their options to respond to risks
section_header: Action 5.7: Reduce and manage the impacts of climate hazards on homes and buildings
extraction_rationale: This is a specific listed component under the parent action. It qualifies because it commits to targeted research to inform adaptation decisions.

parent_statement: Reduce and manage the impacts of climate hazards on homes and buildings
policy_statement: Develop property-level guidance using updated climate data to inform homeowners and renters about risks and response options.
source_quote:
- develop property-level guidance based on updated climate data to inform homeowners and renters about climate impacts and their options to respond to risks
- develop an assessment framework to help building owners, developers and new home builders identify relevant climate hazards and understand their building's adaptation requirements
section_header: Action 5.7: Reduce and manage the impacts of climate hazards on homes and buildings
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete sub-action under the parent programme. It qualifies because it specifies a guidance product for climate adaptation at property level.

parent_statement: Reduce and manage the impacts of climate hazards on homes and buildings
policy_statement: Develop an assessment framework for building owners, developers, and new home builders to identify hazards and adaptation requirements.
source_quote:
- develop an assessment framework to help building owners, developers and new home builders identify relevant climate hazards and understand their building's adaptation requirements
- investigate incentives that could help building owners to increase their building's resilience.
section_header: Action 5.7: Reduce and manage the impacts of climate hazards on homes and buildings
extraction_rationale: This is a specific component under the parent action with a clear deliverable. It qualifies because it creates a structured tool for adaptation requirements.

parent_statement: Reduce and manage the impacts of climate hazards on homes and buildings
policy_statement: Investigate incentives to help building owners increase building resilience.
source_quote:
- develop an assessment framework to help building owners, developers and new home builders identify relevant climate hazards and understand their building's adaptation requirements
- investigate incentives that could help building owners to increase their building's resilience.
section_header: Action 5.7: Reduce and manage the impacts of climate hazards on homes and buildings
extraction_rationale: This is a listed sub-component under the parent action. It qualifies because it explicitly explores incentive mechanisms to support resilience investment, though details remain undeveloped.

policy_statement: Support kaitiaki communities with information, advice, expert assistance, and funding advice to adapt and conserve taonga and cultural assets.
source_quote: Work across government to ensure hapū, iwi and Māori and communities have access to information so they can plan for a changing climate and adapt their cultural assets. Support includes advice, wānanga (conferences, forums, seminars), expert assistance, information sharing and funding advice for kaitiaki to self -determine adaptation pathways.
section_header: Action 5.8: Support kaitiaki communities to adapt and conserve taonga/cultural assets
extraction_rationale: This is a named cross-government support action with specific intervention types. It directly addresses adaptation of cultural assets to climate change.

policy_statement: Prioritise nature-based solutions in planning and regulations for both carbon removals and climate change adaptation.
source_quote: To address the climate and biodiversity crises together, the Government will prioritise nature -based solutions in planning and regulations, where possible, for both carbon removals and climate change adaptation. It will also investigate how to best ensure that climate change policy and planning use a biodiversity lens to prioritise nature-based solutions.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear policy commitment to prioritize a named intervention type in planning and regulation. It explicitly references both adaptation and carbon removals, supporting a mitigation secondary category.

policy_statement: Develop and implement the Transpower Adaptation Plan for climate-resilient national grid design, operation, maintenance, and investment.
source_quote: The Transpower Adaptation Plan will outline how Transpower will adapt to climate change through the design, delivery and operation of the national grid. It will address exposed assets and new investment in infrastructure, and consider adaptation in maintenance and development programmes.
section_header: Action 5.10: Develop and implement the Transpower Adaptation Plan
extraction_rationale: This is a named adaptation plan with a clear scope over grid assets and operations. It qualifies as a concrete adaptation policy for infrastructure resilience.

policy_statement: Encourage and support evaluation of climate risks to landfills and contaminated sites using a council tool.
source_quote:
Coastal inundation and flooding could be a significant risk to existing and closed landfills and contaminated sites across the country. At least 110 closed landfills are vulnerable to sea-level rise.

The Ministry for the Environment (MfE) has helped councils develop a tool to evaluate climate risks for landfills and contaminated sites . This may make it easier for local government to evaluate these risks and support planning to address them.
section_header: Action 5.11: Encourage and support the evaluation of climate risks to landfills and contaminated sites
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete support action centered on a specific evaluation tool. It directly addresses climate hazard risk management for waste infrastructure.

policy_statement: Explore funding options for investigation and remediation of contaminated sites and landfills vulnerable to climate change.
source_quote:
The liability of legacy landfill remediation generally sits with territorial authorities, which have variable ability to pay, particularly in smaller local government areas. Considering this, the Government has agreed to consider how best to support the funding of remediation.

Access to funding will help to turn risk assessment into risk reduction, and ensure remediation occurs before inundation risks become a reality.
section_header: Action 5.12: Explore funding options to support the investigation and remediation of contaminated sites and landfills vulnerable to the effects of climate change
extraction_rationale: This is a funding-related policy development action with a clear adaptation purpose. It qualifies because it explicitly concerns financing remediation for climate-vulnerable sites.

policy_statement: Connect communities to locally led, regionally coordinated, and nationally supported disaster response and recovery networks.
source_quote: This action will continue work with central and local government, communities (including rural communities), iwi, organisations and others to support effective, integrated disaster response and recovery. Communities affected by disasters will be assisted by networks that are locally led, regionally coordinated and nationally supported.
section_header: Action 5.13: Connect communities to wider response and recovery support
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete support action for disaster response and recovery. It qualifies as adaptation because it addresses climate-related disruption and community resilience.

policy_statement: Support development of a green taxonomy to define climate- and nature-positive investments and encourage resilient investment.
source_quote: This will support the development of a 'green' taxonomy to identify a common definition of climate and naturepositive investments. This could help guide businesses that are investing in both adaptation and mitigation to protect against greenwashing. If aligned with best practice, it could support greater international investment in Aotearoa New Zealand's climate-resilient projects, including nature-based solutions.
section_header: Action 5.14: Support the development of definitional tools to encourage greater investment in 'green' projects
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete definitional and market-guidance intervention. Climate relevance is indirect because it shapes investment classification rather than directly implementing adaptation measures.

policy_statement: Use the Climate Emergency Response Fund and Sovereign Green Bonds to finance climate change initiatives, with possible future adaptation funding.
source_quote:
The Government is supporting climate change objectives through its approach to the public finance system. This includes the establishment of the Climate Emergency Response F und (CERF) and the Sovereign Green Bond (Green Bond) programme.

In Budget 2022, the CERF was focused on the emissions reduction plan. However, for future Budgets the Government will consider extending the scope of the CERF to fund measures to support climate change adaptation.
section_header: Action 5.15: Public investment in climate change initiatives
extraction_rationale: This is a broad public finance instrument with explicit climate funding mechanisms. It qualifies because it commits budgetary and bond-financing tools to climate initiatives, though adaptation funding is partly future-oriented.

policy_statement: Identify options to integrate nature-based solutions into urban form to reduce flooding and heatwaves and improve biodiversity.
source_quote:
This work will build on indigenous knowledge and new research to produce new data and insights on nature-based solutions such as vegetation (eg, street trees and green roofs) and water elements (eg, open canals and waterways). This includes understanding barriers and identifying ways to accelerate nature-based solutions through changes to urban form and development.

This action will help reduce the impact of climate events, such as flooding and heatwaves, in our urban areas to improve outcomes for people, communities and biodiversity.
section_header: Action 5.16: Identify options to increase the integration of nature-based solutions into urban form
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed but specific action focused on urban nature-based adaptation. It explicitly names hazards (flooding and heatwaves), so adaptation is a valid secondary category.

policy_statement: Implement the Department of Conservation Climate Change Adaptation Action Plan to assess ecosystem vulnerability and enhance resilience.
source_quote:
The Department of Conservation (DOC) Climate Change Adaptation Action Plan (CCAAP) is a medium-term plan, which applies to public conservation land and waters managed by DOC, as well as threatened native species and systems.

The plan aims to assess ecosystem and species vulnerability to climate impacts, and the adaptation actions to enhance their resilience.
section_header: Action 6.1: Implement the Department of Conservation Climate Change Adaptation Action Plan
extraction_rationale: This is a named adaptation plan with a clear implementation commitment and ecological focus. It qualifies as a direct adaptation policy for the natural environment.

policy_statement: Engage with councils to implement the New Zealand Coastal Policy Statement to protect coastal biodiversity and manage coastal ecosystem risks.
source_quote:
The NZCPS provides the policy mechanism for protecting indi genous biodiversity in the coastal environment, and for managing risks to coastal ecosystems (policies 11, and 24-27 NZCPS). The NZCPS's coastal hazard management mechanisms include managed retreat and nature - based solutions.

By 2024, DOC will review progress on NZCPS implementation by councils.
section_header: Action 6.2: Engage with councils to implement the New Zealand Coastal Policy Statement
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete implementation action tied to an existing policy statement. It explicitly includes coastal hazard management and nature-based solutions, making it a climate adaptation policy.

policy_statement: Implement Te Mana o te Taiao Biodiversity Strategy 2020 to protect, restore, and sustainably use biodiversity while addressing climate resilience.
source_quote:
Te Mana o te Taiao - Aotearoa New Zealand Biodiversity Strategy 2020 (ANZBS) is a strategic document for the protection, restoration and sustainable use of biodiversity in Aotearoa from 2020 to 2050.

A priority of ANZBS is to ensure efforts to tackle biodiversity loss and climate change are reciprocal. Climate-specific goals come under objective 13: Biodiversity provides nature-based solutions to climate change and is resilient to its effects.
section_header: Action 6.3: Implement Te Mana o te Taiao - Aotearoa New Zealand Biodiversity Strategy 2020
extraction_rationale: This is a named strategy implementation commitment with explicit climate-specific goals. It qualifies as a climate policy because biodiversity resilience and nature-based climate solutions are directly stated.

policy_statement: Implement the National Policy Statement on Indigenous Biodiversity to protect, maintain, restore biodiversity, and create ecological corridors.
source_quote:
The objective of the NPS -IB is to protect, maintain and restore indigenous biodiversity.

The NPS -IB plays a part in building the resilience of biodiversity to climate change through its role in protecting, maintaining and restoring biodiversity, including requiring councils and landowners to consider creating ecological corridors.
section_header: Action 6.4: Implement the proposed National Policy Statement on Indigenous Biodiversity
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory policy statement with explicit biodiversity resilience and corridor requirements. It qualifies as a climate-relevant policy through ecosystem-based adaptation.

policy_statement: Implement the Water Availability and Security programme to help food and fibre businesses and rural communities adapt to variable water availability.
source_quote: The Water A vailability and Security programme will help food and fibre businesses and rural communities adapt to increasingly variable natural water availability through a range of complementary activities to both reduce demand and make best use of available water. It will help restore and maintain the health of waterways, taking its lead from the National Policy Statement on Freshwater Management.
section_header: Action 6.6: Implement the Water Availability and Security programme
extraction_rationale: This is a named programme with explicit adaptation and water-demand management functions. It is primarily adaptation, with an explicit efficiency mechanism of reducing demand and making best use of water.

policy_statement: Implement the National Policy Statement on Freshwater Management 2020 to protect freshwater ecosystem health and manage land-use impacts.
source_quote: The National Policy Statement on Freshwater Management 2020 (NPS-FM 2020) applies to all freshwater, including groundwater, and will require management of freshwater in both rural and urban areas. It requires councils to give effect to Te Mana o te Wai, which prioriti ses the health and wellbeing of water bodies and freshwater ecosystems. Water users will adapt landuse practices in response to these and as the climate impacts become apparent.
section_header: Action 6.7: Implement the National Policy Statement on Freshwater Management 2020
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory policy statement with explicit adaptation implications for freshwater management. It qualifies because it requires councils and water users to change practices in response to climate impacts.

policy_statement: Deliver a collection of Biosecurity New Zealand actions to reduce invasive species risks and build ecosystem climate resilience.
source_quote: The following actions address risks to indigenous ecosystems and species that result from the greater spread, survival and establishment of invasive species. They also help build climate resilience of ecosystems generally.
section_header: Action 6.8: Deliver a collection of actions run by Biosecurity New Zealand
extraction_rationale: This is a parent policy because it introduces a grouped set of numbered sub-actions. It is a concrete adaptation programme focused on climate-amplified biosecurity risks.

parent_statement: Deliver a collection of actions run by Biosecurity New Zealand
policy_statement: Implement an on-farm biosecurity programme to improve voluntary biosecurity practices on dairy and sheep and beef farms.
source_quote: This programme aims to improve biosecurity on dairy and sheep and beef farms and create a more resilient biosecurity system. It is responsible for developing and implementing an action plan to overcome barriers and increase voluntary on-farm biosecurity practices.
section_header: Action 6.8.1: Implement an on-farm biosecurity programme
extraction_rationale: This is a numbered sub-action under the biosecurity parent. It qualifies because it commits to a specific programme and action plan to address climate-sensitive pest risks.

parent_statement: Deliver a collection of actions run by Biosecurity New Zealand
policy_statement: Invest in strengthening border biosecurity for mail and sea cargo pathways to protect biodiversity from pest arrivals.
source_quote: Two significant projects (Sea Cargo Programme and Mail Pathways Project) delivered by Biosecurity New Zealand will improve how we address the biosecurity risk from mail and sea cargo pathways. They will also protect biodiversity by identifying pest species that arrive through our international borders.
section_header: Action 6.8.2: Invest in strengthening border biosecurity
extraction_rationale: This is a specific sub-action under the biosecurity parent and includes an investment commitment. It qualifies because it names concrete projects to address climate-sensitive invasive species risks.

parent_statement: Deliver a collection of actions run by Biosecurity New Zealand
policy_statement: Continue the Freshwater Biosecurity Partnership Programme to protect waterways from freshwater pests and improve detection and control tools.
source_quote:
The programme's vision is to take collaborative action to protect Aotearoa New Zealand's freshwater from the impacts of freshwater pests. A changing climate could make more waterways vulnerable to freshwater p est establishment.

The programme will include a focus on supporting the development of effective early -detection and control tools.
section_header: Action 6.8.3: Continue the Freshwater Biosecurity Partnership Programme
extraction_rationale: This is a numbered sub-action with explicit climate vulnerability language and concrete programme activities. It qualifies as adaptation policy for freshwater ecosystem resilience.

parent_statement: Deliver a collection of actions run by Biosecurity New Zealand
policy_statement: Reduce marine pest spread through the Clean Hull behaviour change programme for domestic vessel movements.
source_quote: This involves implementing a behaviour change programme to address the risks of marine pest spread via domestic vessel movements. This will build on existing marine biosecurity partnerships in the upper North Island, upper South Island and Fiordland.
section_header: Action 6.8.4: Reduce the spread and impacts of marine pest species through the Clean Hull programme
extraction_rationale: This is a specific sub-action under the biosecurity parent with a named programme and intervention. It qualifies because it addresses climate-sensitive marine pest risks.

parent_statement: Deliver a collection of actions run by Biosecurity New Zealand
policy_statement: Prevent spread of wilding conifers and contain or eradicate established areas by 2030.
source_quote:
Established in 2016, this programme ensures a collaborative, coordinated and effective national approach to wilding conifer control. This reduces fire risk, improves water availability (including for hydropower generation), prevents the loss of productive land and preserves the biodiversity of indigenous ecosystems.

By 2024, the programme will protect 4 million hectares of land that is significantly vulnerable to invasion by controlling wilding conifer infestations.
section_header: Action 6.8.5: Prevent the spread of wilding conifers, and contain or eradicate established areas of wilding conifers by 2030
extraction_rationale: This is a numbered sub-action with a quantified target year and explicit resilience benefits. It is primarily adaptation, with explicit fire-risk and water-availability benefits.

parent_statement: Deliver a collection of actions run by Biosecurity New Zealand
policy_statement: Continue the National Interest Pest Responses programme to eradicate or reduce infestations of harmful weeds.
source_quote: Nine harmful weeds are managed under the National Interest Pest Responses (NIPR) programme, with the aim of eradicating them or significantly reducing infestations. These weeds could cause serious harm to Aotearoa's environment and economy if allowed to spread.
section_header: Action 6.8.6: Continue the National Interest Pest Responses programme
extraction_rationale: This is a specific sub-action under the biosecurity parent with a clear intervention and objective. Climate relevance is indirect because climate is not explicit in the quoted lines, though the parent context is climate-related.

parent_statement: Deliver a collection of actions run by Biosecurity New Zealand
policy_statement: Invest in plant health and environmental capability facilities to improve resilience to pests and diseases and support new plant varieties.
source_quote: Significant investment in Ministry for Primary Industry (MPI) plant health and environment work (currently in Tāmaki, Auckland) will support growth and development in the arable, forestry and horticulture sectors. It will speed up access to high-value plant varieties and cultivars, to support commercialisation of new products. Faster access to genetic material can support innovation and bring benefits such as higher yields and resilience to pests and diseases.
section_header: Action 6.8.7: Invest in plant health and environmental capability facility
extraction_rationale: This is a numbered sub-action with an explicit investment commitment. Climate relevance is indirect because climate is not explicit in the quote, though resilience to pests and diseases is central.

parent_statement: Deliver a collection of actions run by Biosecurity New Zealand
policy_statement: Use national animal and plant health laboratories to improve diagnosis and understanding of pests and diseases likely to establish in a changing climate.
source_quote: The Animal Health Laboratory (AHL) and Plant Health Environment Laboratory (PHEL) are national reference laboratories that identify and validate suspected exotic and endemic pests and diseases affecting farm and aquatic animals. They bring a better understanding of new and emerging pests and diseases that are likely to establish in a changing climate.
section_header: Action 6.8.8: Use the Animal Health Laboratory and Plant Health and Environment Laboratory
extraction_rationale: This is a specific sub-action under the biosecurity parent with explicit climate linkage. It qualifies because it commits institutional capability to climate-sensitive pest and disease risks.

policy_statement: Deliver Jobs for Nature projects to restore ecosystems, control pests, and mobilise community action.
source_quote: This action support s more than 200 projects to restore ecosystems, control pests and mobilise community action across the country. Biodiversity can be strengthened by restoring ecosystems and reducing pests.
section_header: Action 6.9: Deliver Jobs for Nature to restore indigenous ecosystems
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete programme with a quantified scale ('more than 200 projects'). Climate relevance is indirect in the quote, but ecosystem restoration supports resilience and biodiversity.

policy_statement: Implement Revitalising the Gulf actions including marine protection, fisheries planning, habitat restoration, and marine biosecurity.
source_quote:
This initiative includes establishing 19 new areas of marine protection and an area-based fisheries plan in the Hauraki Gulf Marine Park. Other elements include restricting trawling to specified trawl corridors, protected species initiatives, active habitat restoration, marine biosecurity, aquaculture and Ahu Moana (local marine management by mana whenua and communities).

Together , these actions will enhance the health of the marine ecosystem in the Hauraki Gulf / Tīkapa Moana (and therefore its resilience).
section_header: Action 6.10: Implement Revitalising the Gulf: Government action on the Sea Change Plan
extraction_rationale: This is a named initiative with multiple concrete interventions and a quantified protection element. It qualifies as a nature-based resilience policy for marine ecosystems.

policy_statement: Implement the South-east Marine Protection Initiative to create new marine protected areas and improve ecosystem resilience.
source_quote: This initiative may result in 12 new areas of marine protection in the southeast waters of the South Island, comanaged by the Crown and Ngāi Tahu . It will improve the health of the marine ecosystem (and therefore its resilience) by managing impacts, and will inform future management through science, mātauranga Māori and monitoring.
section_header: Action 6.11: Implement the South-east Marine Protection Initiative
extraction_rationale: This is a named initiative with a quantified intervention (12 new areas). It qualifies as a nature-based policy because it uses ecosystem protection to build resilience.

policy_statement: Implement the Sustainable Land Management Hill Country Erosion Programme to treat erosion-prone land and support afforestation.
source_quote:
Th e Sustainable Land Management Hill Country Erosion Programme will support regional planning for, and treatment of, erosion-prone land and, in turn, contribute to afforestation.

Afforestation can reduce soil loss and other effects from the increasing scale and magnitude of storms. It also mitigates downstream damage to infrastructure.
section_header: Action 6.12: Implement the Sustainable Land Management Hill Country Erosion Programme
extraction_rationale: This is a named programme with explicit ecological and hazard-reduction mechanisms. It is primarily nature-based, with explicit storm-related resilience benefits supporting adaptation.

policy_statement: Research how cultural heritage contributes to community wellbeing and climate change adaptation.
source_quote: This research will look at the value of cultural heritage in building and sustaining communities, and how this links to community resilience and wellbeing.
section_header: Action 7.1: Research how cultural heritage contributes to community wellbeing and climate change adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed research action with an explicit adaptation link. It qualifies because it commits to a defined research agenda on climate adaptation and wellbeing.

policy_statement: Partner with Māori landowners to produce tools and resources that increase resilience of Māori-owned land, homes, and cultural sites.
source_quote: This work will be progressed in partnership with Māori landowners to produce resources and tools to improve understanding of climate-related risks and increase the resilience of housing on Māori land. It will promote mātauranga Māori and increase the resilience of Māori -owned land, homes and cultural sites.
section_header: Action 7.2: Partner with Māori landowners to increase the resilience of Māori -owned land, homes and cul tural sites
extraction_rationale: This is a specific proposed partnership action with concrete outputs and explicit climate-risk purpose. It qualifies as an adaptation policy for Māori-owned assets.

policy_statement: Partner with Māori to support Māori-led adaptation planning and use of mātauranga Māori and Māori urban design principles.
source_quote: This work will be progressed in partnership with Māori to support Māori -led adaptation planning for example, in the new resource management system. This will support Māori -led adaptation solutions and the use of mātauranga Māori and Māori urban design principles in response to climate hazards.
section_header: Action 7.3: Partner with Māori to support Māori - led approaches to adaptation planning
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete proposed planning support action with explicit adaptation language. It qualifies because it commits to Māori-led adaptation planning mechanisms.

policy_statement: Update building regulatory requirements using forward-looking climate data so buildings withstand more extreme climate hazards.
source_quote:
Updated forward-looking climate data and modelling (action 3.2: Design and develop risk and resilience and climate adaptation information portals) will be used to:

- update Building Code performance requirements
- identify and add climate hazards not currently in the Building Code
- produce guidance and tools to help people meet new performance requirements.
section_header: Action 7.4: Update regulatory requirements to ensure buildings are designed and constructed to withstand more extreme climate hazards
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed regulatory update with explicit Building Code changes. It qualifies because it is a binding standards-oriented intervention for climate resilience.

policy_statement: Review housing and urban strategies, programmes, and regulations to ensure they are fit for a changing climate.
source_quote:
Current strategies, programmes and regulations will be reviewed to ensure housing and urban environments are fit for the changing climate. For example, this could lead to updated requirements for homeowners and landlords, or for public and community housing.

This action will help ensure the built environment is designed and planned to cope with extreme events and the changing climate.
section_header: Action 7.5: Update housing and urban settings
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed review with explicit potential regulatory consequences and climate-resilience purpose. It qualifies because it commits to updating housing and urban settings for climate adaptation.

policy_statement: Manage adverse impacts of adaptation-related regulatory change on vulnerable communities through monitoring and possible support measures.
source_quote:
The Government will monitor the effects of action 5.7: Reduce and manage the impacts of climate hazards on homes and buildings and action 7.4: Update regulatory requirements to ensure buildings are designed and

constructed to withstand more extreme climate hazards to identify who these regulatory changes may adversely affect.

Future actions could include advice or guidance to support local initiatives, and offering incentives.
section_header: Action 7.6: Manage potential impacts of adaptation related to regulatory change
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed policy to monitor and address distributional impacts of adaptation regulation. It qualifies because it commits to a defined government response pathway and possible incentives.

policy_statement: Develop and implement the Waka Kotahi Climate Adaptation Plan for climate-resilient land transport design, operation, maintenance, and investment.
source_quote:
In 2022, Waka Kotahi will publish and begin applyin g an adaptation plan. This will outline how Waka Kotahi will adapt to climate change through the design, delivery, operation and use of the land transport system.

The plan will address exposed existing assets and new investment in infrastructure. It will also explore adaptation in maintenance programmes of the roading network, including renewals.
section_header: Action 8.1: Develop and implement the Waka Kotahi Climate Adaptation Plan
extraction_rationale: This is a named adaptation plan with a clear implementation commitment and scope. It qualifies as a direct adaptation policy for transport infrastructure.

policy_statement: Develop the National Energy Strategy to guide a net-zero, secure, reliable, accessible, and affordable energy system.
source_quote: The Government has committed to developing an energy strategy by the end of 2024, fully collaborating and engaging with Māori and working with energy system stakeholders. The vision is for a net-zero economy in 2050, where energy is accessible and affordable, secure and reliable, and supports New Zealanders' wellbeing. The strategy addresses challenges in the energy sector and signals pathways away from fossil fuels.
section_header: Action 8.2: Develop the National Energy Strategy
extraction_rationale: This is a named strategy with a clear deadline and explicit net-zero and fossil-fuel transition goals. It is primarily mitigation, though energy security and reliability imply adaptation co-benefits.

policy_statement: Manage dry-year electricity risk through the New Zealand Battery Project, including assessing pumped hydro feasibility at Lake Onslow.
source_quote: The New Zealand Battery Project will assess the options for managing dry-year risk in a highly renewable electricity system. The current focus is on the feasibility of pumped hydroelectricity at Lake Onslow. The feasibility study will be completed by the end of 2022. The aim is to increase the resilience of the electricity system when hydro lakes have low inflows for long periods.
section_header: Action 8.3: Manage dry-year risk through the New Zealand Battery Project
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete project with a named technology option and explicit dry-year resilience objective. It is primarily adaptation, while the highly renewable electricity system provides an explicit mitigation mechanism.

policy_statement: Allow regulated electricity and gas network revenues to reflect prudent and efficient resilience costs, including climate resilience expenditures.
source_quote: In the Commerce Commission's next reviews of regulated price-quality paths - from 2025 for electricity networks and from 2026 for gas networks - it will consider the extent to which revenue limits should provide for differe nt expenditure levels from the current period. This will include if expenditure levels need to change due to any increased costs of resilience to climate change, where these are based on robust forecasts.
section_header: Action 8.4: Provide for regulated network revenues to reflect the prudent and efficient costs of resilience
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory pricing policy affecting network revenues and resilience spending. It qualifies because it changes allowable expenditure treatment for climate resilience.

policy_statement: Progress the Rail Network Investment Programme to restore the rail network to a resilient and reliable state with climate resilience considerations.
source_quote: KiwiRail's Rail Network Investment Programme (RNIP) is a 10-year programme of investment in Aotearoa New Zealand's rail network, to restore it to a resilient and reliable state. Mitigating climate change is a key focus within the RNIP when considering resilience projects for investment. Restoration of the national rail network to a reliable and resilient state will also reduce its vulnerability to climate hazards and provide a platform for future investment to support growth.
section_header: Action 8.5: Progress the Rail Network Investment Programme
extraction_rationale: This is a named long-term investment programme with explicit resilience and mitigation language. It qualifies due to its concrete investment scope and climate objectives.

policy_statement: Invest in public transport and active transport to improve transport system resilience, equity, and emissions outcomes.
source_quote: Investment in multi-modal infrastructure can increase the resilience of the transport system and help manage the vulnerability of existing assets. More use of public transport and active modes will help reduce reliance on private vehicles. It will increase system redundancy, improve equity and support sustainable growth. Safe and attractive alternatives to driving create a more resilient transport system, support sustainable growth and reduce emissions.
section_header: Action 8.6: Invest in public transport and active transport
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete investment commitment with explicit resilience and emissions outcomes. It is primarily resource efficiency through transport mode shift, with explicit emissions reduction supporting mitigation as secondary.

policy_statement: Embed nature-based solutions in transport policy and investment to reduce transport emissions and improve adaptation and biodiversity outcomes.
source_quote:
Nature-based solutions involve sustainable management and natural features and processes to tackle socio-environmental challenges such as climate change. At a local, regional and national scale these measures can reduce transport emissions and improve climate adaptation as well as biodiversity. Key initiatives include:

- considering the role of nature-based solutions in reducing transport emissions and contributing to other benefits
- ensuring transport policy and investment encourage nature-based solutions, including protecting existing carbon sinks and supporting new long-term carbon sequestration opportunities.
section_header: Action 8.7: Embed nature-based solutions as part of the response to reducing transport emissions and improving climate adaptation and biodiversity outcomes
extraction_rationale: This is a named policy action with explicit nature-based, emissions-reduction, and adaptation mechanisms. It qualifies clearly and supports both mitigation and adaptation.

policy_statement: Support knowledge sharing and implementation of adaptation actions across infrastructure asset owners through regular convening.
source_quote: Te Waihanga will convene a regular event for local government, central government and private sector asset owners to share information on the implementation of actions in the national adaptation plan and to support alignment across the sector.
section_header: Action 8.8: Support knowledge sharing and the implementation of adaptation actions across the sector
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete coordination mechanism with a defined recurring activity. It qualifies as adaptation policy because it supports implementation across infrastructure sectors.

policy_statement: Modernise the emergency management system through legislative reform, clearer roles, community engagement, and stronger Māori partnership.
source_quote: The National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) plans to modernise emergency management, including through legislative reforms, working with communities and organisations, clearer roles and responsibilities, and a strengthened partnership with Māori. This work in Aotearoa. It will also sharpen the focus on disproportionately affected groups by seeks to improve the regulatory framework that underpins emergency management strengthening community resilience.
section_header: Action 9.1: Modernise the emergency management system
extraction_rationale: This is a named modernization programme with legislative reform and institutional changes. It qualifies as a direct adaptation policy for disaster preparedness and resilience.

policy_statement: Develop the Health National Adaptation Plan and regional climate health action plans to prepare the health sector for climate impacts.
source_quote: The Health National Adaptation Plan (HNAP) will complement the national adaptation plan and be supported by regional climate health action plans developed by the health sector. The aim of the HNAP is to prepare the health sector to meet the needs of communities in terms of the effects of climate change, including physical, mental and cultural health and wellbeing.
section_header: Action 9.2: Develop the Health National Adaptation Plan
extraction_rationale: This is a named adaptation plan with explicit climate-health objectives and follow-on regional plans. It clearly qualifies as a direct adaptation policy.

policy_statement: Develop the emergency management workforce to improve national, regional, and local capacity for more frequent and severe natural hazards.
source_quote: Work is ongoing to expand the operational capacity and capability of the emergency management workforce at the national, regional and local levels. This will position Aotearoa better to address the increased frequency and severity of natural hazards and support all people in response and recovery.
section_header: Action 9.3: Develop the emergency management workforce
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete workforce-capacity action with explicit hazard-response purpose. It qualifies as adaptation because it strengthens response and recovery capacity for climate-related hazards.

policy_statement: Implement the Climate Migration Action Plan to support Pacific communities facing climate-related displacement and migration.
source_quote: Key values of the Climate Migration Action Plan include retaining social and cultural identity for Pacific communities, and supporting Pacific peoples to live in their own countries where possible. This work aims to support these communities to grow and th rive despite the challenges of climate-related displacement and migration .
section_header: Action: 9.4: Implement the Climate Migration Action Plan
extraction_rationale: This is a named action plan with explicit climate-displacement objectives. It qualifies as a direct adaptation policy addressing migration and community resilience.

policy_statement: Continue reform of the health and disability system to improve coordination, equity, and public health capacity relevant to climate impacts.
source_quote:
The structure of the health and disability system and the delivery of health services are undergoing a period of reform. The new system will be simpler and more coordinated, allowing for better and more consistent care, shaped by the voices of consumers, communities and whānau.

The Public Health Agency within the Manatū Hauora Ministry of Health (MOH) will lead and strengthen population and public health, with greater emphasis on equity and the wider determinants of health such as income, education and housing.
section_header: Action 9.5: Continue with the reform of the health and disability system
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete system reform with relevance to climate-vulnerable communities, though climate is not the sole objective in the quoted text. Climate relevance is therefore indirect.

policy_statement: Build community resilience through social cohesion by improving inclusion, participation, and belonging.
source_quote: This work will improve inclusion and participation in society and build community resilience to lessen instability and isolation caused by climate change. The aim is to support the understanding of diversity within and across communities to allow everyone to feel safe and belong, and to access opportunities.
section_header: Action 9.6: Build community resilience through social cohesion
extraction_rationale: This is a named action with explicit climate-change rationale and community resilience objective. It qualifies as adaptation policy focused on social resilience.

policy_statement: Strengthen teaching and learning on climate change in local curricula and marau ā-kura to support community resilience and social cohesion.
source_quote: This work will improve community resilience by addressing inequities in learning outcomes that impact on lifelong wellbeing. It will support early learning services, schools and kura to include understanding of, and responses to, climate change in their local curricula and marau ā -kura (living, breathing curriculum), as well as learning that is important for social cohesion .
section_header: Action 9.7: Strengthen teaching and learning related to climate change
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete education-system action with explicit climate-change content. It qualifies as adaptation policy because it builds adaptive capacity through education.

policy_statement: Continue overhauling the welfare system to improve income and support for vulnerable people and communities.
source_quote: This action will make ongoing improvements in support - such as for employment, health and communities - and in incomes for those interacting with the welfare system. This aims to achieve the Government's vision of a welfare system that ensures people have an adequate income and standard of living; are treated with, and can live in, dignity; and can participate meaningfully in their communities.
section_header: Action 9.8: Continue to overhaul the welfare system
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete reform action, but climate relevance is indirect because the quoted text does not explicitly mention climate. It is included because the plan frames it as supporting vulnerable communities' adaptive capacity.

policy_statement: Expand proactive community resilience funding, including through Whānau Ora, to help communities future-proof and adapt.
source_quote:
This will seek to expand funding for Māori to build their community resilience through the COVID-19 pandemic, and plug funding gaps for communities to carry out their long-term resilience plans.

Funding would be decentralised by expanding the scope of funds provided through Whānau Ora .
section_header: Action 9.9: Expand current funding for proactive community resilience
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed funding expansion with a clear resilience objective. It qualifies because it commits to expanding and decentralizing funding for long-term resilience plans.

policy_statement: Develop an income insurance scheme to cushion workers and communities from climate-related economic disruption and support transitions.
source_quote: Workers would have the financial security to find a job that matches their skills, needs and aspirations. Bus inesses would be able to better match workers to jobs. This policy would reduce the economic impacts of a changing climate on workers and communities by, for example, cushioning the impact of a large employer closing or resizing in a small town or region, and enabling workers to transition to new job opportunities afforded by changes in the economy.
section_header: Action 9.10: Implement an income insurance scheme to support adaptive capacity of communities and the economy
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed insurance scheme with a defined benefit structure and explicit climate-related purpose. It qualifies as a financial instrument supporting adaptive capacity.

policy_statement: Develop and deliver Defence initiatives from Responding to the Climate Crisis to adapt infrastructure, capability, and response operations.
source_quote: The plan identifies actions Defence will take as part of a broader government programme on climate change and sustainability. It sets out initiatives for mitigation and adaptation of Defence Force infrastructure, capability and response operations that protect the security of New Zealanders and the region.
section_header: Action 9.11: Develop and deliver initiatives in Responding to the Climate Crisis: An Implementation Plan (2019)
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed implementation plan with explicit mitigation and adaptation initiatives. It qualifies because it commits Defence to concrete climate-related actions.

policy_statement: Produce guidance and tools for monitoring and evaluating adaptation initiatives, including real options analysis and calculators.
source_quote: This will help ensure adaptation actions effectively increase our resilience and manage the risks we face. Monitoring is essential for an effective plan, and this guidance will help users identify signals that an action is no longer meeting its objectives. Tool s such as real options analysis (ROA), online calculators and other assessment tools will help with adaptation decisions.
section_header: Action 9.12: Produce guidance and tools for monitoring and evaluating the impact of adaptation initiatives
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed but concrete guidance action with named tools and explicit adaptation purpose. It qualifies as a policy because it creates operational tools for adaptation management.

policy_statement: Review active labour market programmes and expand them to support workers and communities affected by economic changes including climate impacts.
source_quote: The Government has been reviewing the ALMPs it provides and funds. It has committed to expanding existing, and introducing new, ALMPs to support people into work, or back to work, and to take up new job opportunities arising from changes in the economy. ALMPs will reduce the impact of a changing climate on workers and communities.
section_header: Action 9.13: Review of active labour market programmes
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed review and expansion commitment with explicit climate-impact rationale. It qualifies because it commits to programme changes to support adaptation in labour markets.

policy_statement: Deliver the New Zealand Freight and Supply Chain strategy to ensure freight and supply chains are resilient, reliable, and prepared for disruption.
source_quote: This strategy will present a long -term and system-wide view of the freight system. Climate adaptation is being considered through the resilience outcome, to ensure Aotearoa New Zealand's freight and supply chain system is resilient, reliable and prepared for disruption. This will inform investment by the Government, councils and private sector players.
section_header: Action 10.1: Deliver the New Zealand Freight and Supply Chain strategy
extraction_rationale: This is a named strategy with explicit climate adaptation and resilience objectives. It qualifies as a direct adaptation policy for economic infrastructure and supply chains.

policy_statement: Strengthen fisheries rules through legislative changes that enable more responsive catch limits and sustainability measures under climate change.
source_quote:
The Bill also allows for more agile and streamlined decisions in response to changes in fish stock abundance, by enabling development of the pre-set decision rules.

These rules will allow adjustment of the catch limits, and other sustainability measures within pre-agreed limits, in response to change in abundance. This will allow for the system to be more responsive to the effects of climate change.
extraction_rationale: This is a legislative reform with explicit climate responsiveness in fisheries management. It qualifies as adaptation policy because it adjusts management rules to climate-driven stock changes.

policy_statement: Deliver the Aquaculture Strategy to support sustainable industry growth and adaptation to climate change.
source_quote:
The Government's Aquaculture Strategy sets objectives and actions to support Aotearoa in becoming a world leader in sustainable and innovative aquaculture. One of the strategy's objectives is to support the industry to adapt to climate change.

Actions include: forecasting the effects of climate change on the aquatic environment and supporting actions for resilience; helping industry to transition to hatchery spat production; spatial planning approaches informed by climate change considerations to enable industry growth and adaptation; and the development of a comprehensive biosecurity approach.
extraction_rationale: This is a named strategy with explicit climate adaptation objectives and concrete actions. It qualifies as a direct adaptation policy for the aquaculture sector.

policy_statement: Integrate climate change into Reserve Bank supervisory, stress-testing, and policy work to improve financial entities' climate risk management.
source_quote:
The Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) is taking action to help regulated financial entities identify and manage climate risks better . This includes:

- introducing climate-related stress tests that model the effect of severe but plausible scenarios on the balance sheets of regulated financial institutions
- incorporating climate change in scheduled supervisor engagements with the management and boards of regulated entities
- developing guidance on managing risk for the entities the RBNZ regulates.
section_header: Action 10.4: Reserve Bank of New Zealand supports the stability of the financial system
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete regulatory and supervisory package with explicit climate-risk tools. It qualifies as a direct adaptation policy for financial system resilience.

policy_statement: Deliver the Māori agribusiness extension programme to support Māori landowners' productive, sustainable, and climate-adaptive land use.
source_quote: This action will deliver a tailored extension programme for whenua Māori . This will support collectives of Māori landowners and agribusiness to take a te ao Māori approach to meeting their aspirations for their whenua in a productive and sustainable way. As part of the programme, landowners will consider how best to plan intergenerationally for the impacts of climate change on their whenua.
section_header: Action 10.5: Deliver the Māori agribusiness extension programme
extraction_rationale: This is a named extension programme with explicit climate-change planning for Māori landowners. It qualifies as adaptation policy for agribusiness resilience.

policy_statement: Continue research programmes to help agriculture adapt to climate change, measure emissions, and mitigate freshwater impacts.
source_quote: This work will fund research and develop tools to support the agriculture sector to adapt to climate change better, measure emissions and mitigate land-use impacts on freshwater. It includes science extension and policy research and the ability to respond to the social impacts of climate change.
section_header: Action 10.6: Continue delivering the Sustainable Land Management and Climate Change and Greenhouse Gas Inventory research programmes
extraction_rationale: This is a named research funding programme with explicit adaptation and emissions functions. It qualifies as a climate policy with adaptation primary and mitigation secondary due to explicit emissions measurement.

policy_statement: Continue delivering the Sustainable Food and Fibre Futures Fund to co-invest in innovative primary-sector solutions to climate risks.
source_quote: The Sustainable Food and Fibre (SFF) Futures Fund supports innovative projects that design and test new approaches and solutions to risks such as climate change in the primary sector. The fund supports innovation in Aotearoa New Zealand's food and fibre sector by co-investing in initiatives that bring economic, environmental and social benefits for all New Zealanders.
section_header: Action 10.7: Continue delivering the Sustainable Food and Fibre Futures Fund
extraction_rationale: This is a clear financial instrument because it is a fund that co-invests in climate-related innovation. It qualifies due to explicit climate-risk focus and funding mechanism.

policy_statement: Establish innovation grants to share risk and accelerate climate-focused private-sector research and development.
source_quote: These grants will boost investment in private sector research and development and support innovation. They will share the risk with Aotearoa companies. This means more climatefocused innovation should happen faster, to better enable adaptation action and the transition to a low-emissions economy.
extraction_rationale: This is a financial instrument with explicit grant funding and climate-focused innovation goals. It supports adaptation directly and explicitly references transition to a low-emissions economy.

policy_statement: Model climate change impacts on regional economies and provide guidance for local economic climate-risk decisions.
source_quote: This work will involve modelling the economic impacts of a changing climate on regional economies and providing guidance for assessing climate impacts in local economic decisions. This will help to identify likely impacts and determine where our vulnerable communities are by exploring the distribution of economic impacts across different parts of Aotearoa.
section_header: Action 10.9: Identify the impacts of climate change on regional economies
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete analytical and guidance action with explicit climate-impact assessment purpose. It qualifies as adaptation policy for regional economic resilience.

policy_statement: Monitor residential insurance premiums and uptake to understand shifts in insurance availability and affordability.
source_quote: Monitoring residential premiums and uptake of insurance gives a better understanding of the scale of shifts in insurance availability and affordability.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific monitoring commitment tied to climate-related insurance resilience in the chapter context. It qualifies as a policy because it establishes an ongoing monitoring function.

policy_statement: Consider climate risk in Treasury economic and fiscal monitoring and forecasting.
source_quote: Treasury's six -monthly economic updates are a core way to monitor and forecast the economic and fiscal environment. This includes the impact of shocks (eg , COVID-19 or natural disasters) on the Crown's financial position and tracking longrun changes. The updates highlight known quantifiable and unquantifiable climate adaptation risks as a tool in fiscal and economic management.
section_header: Action 10.11: Consider climate risk in economic and fiscal monitoring and forecasting
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete integration of climate adaptation risks into fiscal monitoring. It qualifies because it changes the content of official economic and fiscal updates.

policy_statement: Implement the government response to the Chief Science Advisor's commercial fishing report to support innovation, ecosystem management, and habitat protection.
source_quote: This report makes several recommendations for the fisheries management system and for commercial fishers. The Government's response is underway and includes actions that support innovation across the system, progress an ecosystem approach to fisheries management and protect habitats of significance to fisheries management.
section_header: Action 10.12: Implement the Government response to the Prime Minister's Chief Science Advisor's report on commercial fishing
extraction_rationale: This is a named implementation commitment with concrete fisheries-management directions. Climate relevance is indirect in the quote, but the chapter frames it as part of climate adaptation for fisheries.

policy_statement: Deliver the Tourism Industry Transformation Plan using the Tourism Adaptation Roadmap to assess sector-wide climate risks and actions.
source_quote: The goal of this work is regenerative tourism. The first phase focuses on 'better work' and the second phase on the environment. The Tourism Adaptation Roadmap developed by the Aotearoa Circle will be an input for the environmental phase of the Tourism Industry Transformation Plan. This allows for a sector-wide assessment of risks and actions.
section_header: Action 10.14: Deliver the Tourism Industry Transformation Plan
extraction_rationale: This is a named transformation plan with explicit use of an adaptation roadmap. It qualifies as adaptation policy for a climate-exposed economic sector.

policy_statement: Review the International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy settings to support resilient, adaptable infrastructure and natural environments used by visitors.
source_quote: This includes ensuring international visitors contribute to resilient, adaptable infrastructure and the natural environment they use during their visit. Resilient infrastructure, including a healthy environment, will reduce the risks from extreme weather. This action will support a focus on the spending priorities of the IVL, as well as any further work across the life of the national adaptation plan (eg, other tools) to support adaptation and climate resilience in tourism.
section_header: Action 10.15: Review the settings for the International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy
extraction_rationale: This is a levy-setting review with explicit adaptation and resilience spending priorities. It qualifies as a financial instrument because it concerns a levy and its use for resilient infrastructure and environment.

policy_statement: Leverage government procurement policy to enable mitigation and adaptation in public investments, especially construction.
source_quote: This action w ill check the current government's procurement policy framework enables mitigation and adaptation in government investments. The greatest opportunity will likely be in construction contracts, making buildings and infrastructure resilient to a changing climate, and reducing carbon emissions and waste.
section_header: Action 10.16: Leverage government procurement for climate outcomes
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete procurement-policy review with explicit adaptation and mitigation objectives. It qualifies because it aims to change procurement rules for climate outcomes.

policy_statement: Support Māori small and medium enterprises to develop low-emissions growth strategies and improve resilience to climate risks.
source_quote: The aim of this work is to support Māori small and medium enterprises to develop low -emissions growth strategies, respond to climate-related risks and opportunities, and adopt resilient ways of working. Businesses would commit to reducing their emissions or improving their resilience to physical climate events.
section_header: Action 10.17: Support Māori small business resilience and transitions
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed support programme with explicit low-emissions and resilience commitments. It qualifies as a climate policy with adaptation primary and mitigation secondary.

policy_statement: Research small business adaptation preparedness and provide targeted guidance to reduce climate risks.
source_quote: This will help small businesses reduce their climate risks through targeted guidance and information. The guidance will be based on research that will increase understanding of what businesses are doing to adapt, and the pain points for business owners.
section_header: Action 10.18: Research business adaptation preparedness and provide guidance for small businesses to adapt
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed but concrete research-and-guidance action with explicit adaptation purpose. It qualifies because it commits to both baseline research and targeted guidance.

policy_statement: Enhance industry partnership networks to pool knowledge and resources for complex challenges including climate adaptation.
source_quote: This action will pool knowledge and resources to solve sector problems. The partnerships will recognise the complexity and interrelatedness of issues, such as climate adaptation, and the need for sophisticated networks to test, scale up and spread innovation to help address challenges facing Aotearoa.
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed network-building action with explicit climate adaptation relevance. It qualifies because it commits to a structured partnership mechanism for adaptation innovation.

policy_statement: Establish central government oversight and coordination for implementing the national adaptation plan, including annual agency reporting.
source_quote:
This will provide transparency of implementation of the plan across government, improve coordination within central government and enable accountability.

Annual reporting requirements by agencies will be completed each year, commencing in 2023.
section_header: Action 11.1: Establish central government oversight and coordination for implementing the national adaptation plan
extraction_rationale: This is a named governance action with a concrete coordination and reporting mechanism. It qualifies as adaptation policy because it institutionalizes implementation oversight for the plan.

policy_statement: Reduce Italy's greenhouse gas emissions by 6.5% below 1990 levels under the Kyoto Protocol burden-sharing commitment.
source_quote: Italy's greenhouse gas emissions should be reduced by 6.5%, compared to 1990 levels, as agreed under the European 'burden sharing' adopted by the European Union on 4 th March 2002; the emission reduction policies and measures shall be finalised: - to improve the efficiency of the Italian economy; - to  promote  energy  sources  differentiation  and energy security;
extraction_rationale: This is a clear quantified national emissions target tied to an international legal commitment, so it qualifies as a policy. It is standalone in the ratification law summary.

policy_statement: Finalize emission reduction policies to improve the efficiency of the Italian economy.
source_quote: the emission reduction policies and measures shall be finalised: - to improve the efficiency of the Italian economy; - to  promote  energy  sources  differentiation  and energy security; - to increase the share of renewables in the energy portfolio;
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit policy direction in the ratification law tied to emission reduction measures. It is somewhat broad, but it names a specific intervention mechanism: improving efficiency.

policy_statement: Finalize emission reduction policies to promote energy source diversification and energy security.
source_quote: the emission reduction policies and measures shall be finalised: - to improve the efficiency of the Italian economy; - to  promote  energy  sources  differentiation  and energy security; - to increase the share of renewables in the energy portfolio;
extraction_rationale: This is part of the ratification law's mandated policy package. It is climate-relevant because it is explicitly framed as part of emission reduction policies, though the mechanism is broader than climate alone.

policy_statement: Finalize emission reduction policies to increase the share of renewables in the energy portfolio.
source_quote: the emission reduction policies and measures shall be finalised: - to improve the efficiency of the Italian economy; - to  promote  energy  sources  differentiation  and energy security; - to increase the share of renewables in the energy portfolio;
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit mitigation commitment centered on renewable energy expansion. It is clearly part of the ratification law's policy package.

policy_statement: Finalize emission reduction policies to promote technology innovation in the energy and transportation sectors.
source_quote: the emission reduction policies and measures shall be finalised: - to  promote  technology innovation in the energy and transportation sectors; - to  promote  sustainable  agricultural  and  forestry activities, and the related carbon sinks; - to  add  value,  and  to  improve  the  international technology cooperation supporting the participation  of  the  Italian  companies  in  the  'Clean Development Mechanism' and 'Joint Implementation';
extraction_rationale: This is a named policy direction under the ratification law. It is broad but still qualifies because it specifies innovation in sectors central to emissions reduction.

policy_statement: Finalize emission reduction policies to promote sustainable agricultural and forestry activities and related carbon sinks.
source_quote: the emission reduction policies and measures shall be finalised: - to  promote  technology innovation in the energy and transportation sectors; - to  promote  sustainable  agricultural  and  forestry activities, and the related carbon sinks; - to  add  value,  and  to  improve  the  international technology cooperation supporting the participation  of  the  Italian  companies  in  the  'Clean Development Mechanism' and 'Joint Implementation';
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit policy commitment to land-sector mitigation through sustainable agriculture, forestry, and sinks. Because carbon sinks are named, it directly qualifies.

policy_statement: Improve international technology cooperation to support Italian company participation in the Clean Development Mechanism and Joint Implementation.
source_quote: the emission reduction policies and measures shall be finalised: - to  promote  sustainable  agricultural  and  forestry activities, and the related carbon sinks; - to  add  value,  and  to  improve  the  international technology cooperation supporting the participation  of  the  Italian  companies  in  the  'Clean Development Mechanism' and 'Joint Implementation';
extraction_rationale: This is a specific policy direction tied to Kyoto mechanisms and international cooperation. It is climate policy because it explicitly supports emissions-reduction mechanisms.

policy_statement: Allocate 25 million Euro per year for 2002-2004 to support pilot projects on energy efficiency, clean fuels and engines, and carbon sinks.
source_quote: 25  millions  Euro/year  have  been  allocated,for the period 2002-2004, to support pilot projects to enhance energy efficiency, to promote clean fuels and engines, to increase carbon sinks; 4. 68  millions  Euro/year  have  been  allocated,  by 2003,  to  support  projects  in  the  developing countries aimed to reduce greenhouse gas emissions reduce, and to promote the adaptation to the adverse effects of climate change.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete budget allocation with amount, duration, and eligible activities. It clearly qualifies as a policy and as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Allocate 68 million Euro per year by 2003 to support projects in developing countries that reduce greenhouse gas emissions and promote adaptation to climate change impacts.
