source_quote: 68  millions  Euro/year  have  been  allocated,  by 2003,  to  support  projects  in  the  developing countries aimed to reduce greenhouse gas emissions reduce, and to promote the adaptation to the adverse effects of climate change.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific international climate finance commitment with a quantified annual allocation and explicit mitigation and adaptation purposes.

policy_statement: The trend scenario for 2010 under current legislation includes already adopted measures across electricity, efficiency, buildings, and biofuels.
source_quote: The 'trend' emission scenario for 2010, 'under current legislation', includes measures already adopted: - minimum  share  (2%)  of  electricity  production from  new  plants  using  renewable  sources  (law decree 79/1999); - Prime  Minister  Decree  of  4  August  1999  providing for selling by ENEL of approximately 15,000 MW, and compulsory  conversion  of  existing  oil fired thermo-electric plants into natural gas combined cycle plants for about 10,000 MW;
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella package introducing a list of adopted measures. Because clear sub-items follow, it should be extracted as a parent policy.

parent_statement: The 'trend' emission scenario for 2010, 'under current legislation', includes measures already adopted
policy_statement: Require a minimum 2% share of electricity production from new plants using renewable sources.
source_quote: The 'trend' emission scenario for 2010, 'under current legislation', includes measures already adopted: - minimum  share  (2%)  of  electricity  production from  new  plants  using  renewable  sources  (law decree 79/1999); - Prime  Minister  Decree  of  4  August  1999  providing for selling by ENEL of approximately 15,000 MW, and compulsory  conversion  of  existing  oil fired thermo-electric plants into natural gas combined cycle plants for about 10,000 MW;
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified regulatory requirement with a clear percentage target and legal basis. It is a classic mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Use voluntary agreements, a mandatory renewable share, and dispatching priority for cogeneration to promote electric-sector mitigation objectives.
source_quote: Some major tools have been used to promote the aforementioned  objectives:  voluntary  agreements with industries, mandatory renewable sources share (renewable obligation) in total electricity production and dispatching priority for energy produced in cogeneration plants.
section_header: 4.2.1 Measures implemented in the electric sector, including renewable sources
extraction_rationale: This sentence identifies concrete policy instruments used in the electric sector. It qualifies because it names binding and operational mechanisms.

policy_statement: Implement the voluntary agreement with Enel to reduce emissions by 22 MtCO2 by 2006 compared to 1990 through efficiency, renewables, reduced network leaks, and demand-side management.
source_quote: The voluntary agreement with Enel has the objective  of  reducing  emissions  of  22  MtCO 2 by  2006, compared to the emissions of 1990, by: - increasing the efficiency of existing plants and converting 15.000 MW to combined-cycle plants; of the reduced 12 MtCO2, only 10 MtCO2 are to be attributed to the measures implemented after the Kyoto Protocol;
section_header: 4.2.1 Measures implemented in the electric sector, including renewable sources
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified voluntary agreement with a target year and explicit implementation mechanisms. It clearly qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Implement the 2% renewable production obligation to promote an additional 9,000 GWh and reduce emissions by about 6 MtCO2.
source_quote: The resolution establishing the 2% production obligation from renewable source , could promote an additional production capacity of 9.000 GWh, with a reduction effect of about 6 MtCO 2 . Legislative  Decrees  of 24 April 2001 provide for the  reduction  of  electricity  and  gas  consumptions through the implementation of measures adopted by distribution companies;
section_header: 4.2.1 Measures implemented in the electric sector, including renewable sources
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified renewable obligation with expected output and emissions impact. It is a clear mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Implement Legislative Decrees of 24 April 2001 to reduce electricity and gas consumption through measures adopted by distribution companies, with expected reductions of 7-8 MtCO2.
source_quote: Legislative  Decrees  of 24 April 2001 provide for the  reduction  of  electricity  and  gas  consumptions through the implementation of measures adopted by distribution companies; these measures are expected to  be  fully  adopted  since  non-compliance    would incur  financial  penalties.  The  overall  effect  of  such Decrees is expected to entail a reduction from 7 to 8 MtCO2.
section_header: 4.2.1 Measures implemented in the electric sector, including renewable sources
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete regulatory measure with enforcement and quantified emissions impact. It clearly qualifies.

policy_statement: Partially implement the programme of 10,000 photovoltaic roofs, with estimated emission reductions of about 0.12 MtCO2 per year.
source_quote: The  programme  of 10,000  photovoltaic  roofs is expected to be partially implemented and, according to  rough  estimates,  emission  reduction  should  be around 0.12 MtCO2 year.
section_header: 4.2.1 Measures implemented in the electric sector, including renewable sources
extraction_rationale: This is a named program with a quantified scale and estimated emissions impact. It qualifies as a policy intervention.

policy_statement: Increase waste-based electricity generation by expanding incinerator burning capacity by 220,000 tonnes per year to achieve a 1.6 MtCO2 reduction by 2010.
source_quote: As  concerns  electricity  generated  from waste  by 2010 it is assumed that the burning capacity of the existing incinerators will increase by 220,000 tonnes every year, entailing a reduction of 1.6 MtCO 2 .
section_header: 4.2.1 Measures implemented in the electric sector, including renewable sources
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified waste-to-energy intervention with annual capacity growth and emissions impact. It qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Replace liquid and solid fossil fuels with natural gas to mitigate CO2 and overall greenhouse gas emissions.
source_quote: The replacement of liquid and solid fossil fuels with natural  gas    is  an  option  aimed  at  mitigating  CO 2 emissions  and  overall  greenhouse-gas  emissions, given that the increase in methane leaks from networks, especially the distribution networks, and from end  users  seems  to  be  negligible.
section_header: 4.2.1 Measures implemented in the electric sector, including renewable sources
extraction_rationale: This is a specific fuel-switching mitigation option explicitly justified by emissions reductions. It qualifies as a policy direction.

policy_statement: Construct an additional 3,200 MW of combined-cycle capacity beyond the trend scenario, yielding an estimated 8.9 Mt emission reduction.
source_quote: In the  reference  scenario,  a  higher capacity  of  new  combined  cycles  is  assumed  for additional 3,200 MW, implying an emission reduction equal to 8.9 Mt. The  hypotheses  of  an  increase  exceeding  3,200 MW, in addition to the 20,000 MW already anticipated  in  the  trend  scenario,  seem  to  be  hardly achievable and not compatible with the equilibrium required  by  the  future  electric  market
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified capacity expansion with explicit emissions impact. It is a clear policy measure in the reference scenario.

policy_statement: Expand electricity import capacity by an additional 2,300 MW to reduce domestic emissions by 10.6 Mt.
source_quote: Another measure included in the reference scenario is the additional expansion of 2.300 MW enabling: - a remarkable emission reduction of 10.6 Mt, considering  that  the  entire  import  capacity  from abroad,  supposedly  from  under-exploited  plants, would cause a reduction in domestic emissions.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified infrastructure measure with explicit emissions reduction. It qualifies as a policy commitment.

policy_statement: Increase renewable electricity by an additional 11 TWh by 2010 to reach about 75 TWh, mainly through biomass, waste, and wind.
source_quote: The  policy  aiming  at  spurring  the  expansion  of renewable sources still further indicates as feasible an additional expansion by 2010,  of 11 TWh, mainly  on  account  of    increased  biomass,  waste  and wind  contribution.  This    additional  expansion requires    an  increase  of  0.3%  each  year  of  the mandatory  2%  obligation,  from  2005  to  2012..
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified renewable expansion policy with a specified mechanism: increasing the mandatory obligation. It clearly qualifies.

policy_statement: Increase the mandatory 2% renewable obligation by 0.3% each year from 2005 to 2012.
source_quote: This    additional  expansion requires    an  increase  of  0.3%  each  year  of  the mandatory  2%  obligation,  from  2005  to  2012.. Moreover,  the  prospected  scenario  is  in  line  with the  terms  of  the  White  Paper  aimed  at  valorising renewable sources,  approved by  the  Interministerial Committee for Economic Planning of  6  August  1999.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified regulatory adjustment to the renewable obligation. It is a clear policy mechanism.

policy_statement: Promote simplified authorization procedures for renewable plants with capacity below 10 MW.
source_quote: An important measure to aim to achieve such an objective is the promotion of simplified authorization  procedures  for  plants  with  power  capacity inferior  to  10  MW,  already  proposed  by  some regional administrations.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific regulatory reform to facilitate renewable deployment. It qualifies as a policy despite lacking a quantified emissions effect.

policy_statement: Pursue an additional 500-1200 MW increase in renewable energy production beyond the reference scenario.
source_quote: This is an option which, in any case, must take into account the strong development already hypothesised in the reference scenario, where the achievement of 75 TWh of renewable energy by 2010 is taken for granted, as indicated in the White Paper of  1999.  Sectorial  studies  shows  further  projects with positive Net Present Value (NPV) of investment thanks to the inclusion in the valorisation of transferred electric energy of the green certificate, which is supposed to be at 5 cents of Euro/kWh.
section_header: Increase in the production of energy from renewable sources for 500-1.200 MW
extraction_rationale: The subsection heading itself provides the quantified intervention, and the text confirms it as an option supported by green certificates. It qualifies as a policy option though still not established.

policy_statement: Support research and development in the photovoltaic sector for niche uses, with an additional expansion of about 150 MW.
source_quote: The possibility of an additional expansion of about 150 MW with an investment of 1.125 million Euros and a  negative  NPV  of  220  million  Euros  is  identified. The  unit  cost  is  therefore  equal  to  a  110  Mill. Euros/Mt.
section_header: Research and development in the photovoltaic sector
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified technology-development option with investment and expansion figures. It qualifies as a policy option and financial instrument.

policy_statement: Measures implemented in the industry sector consist of voluntary agreements and direct or indirect financing in specific sectors.
source_quote: The  measures  implemented  in  the  industry  sector can  be  grouped  into  two  typologies:  voluntary agreements and direct or indirect financing in several  specific  sectors.  A  list  of  the  measures  and expected effects on emissions is shown in table 4.7.
section_header: 4.3.1 Measures implemented in the industry sector
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella characterization of industrial policy instruments. It introduces specific sub-policies and is best treated as a parent.

policy_statement: Implement the voluntary agreement with Montedison, originally targeting a 10 MtCO2 reduction.
source_quote: The two most important voluntary agreements are contracted with Montedison and Assovetro. The voluntary  agreement  with  Montedison, unfortunately,  will  not  produce  the  expected effects,    estimated  at  10  MtCO2;
section_header: 4.3.1 Measures implemented in the industry sector
extraction_rationale: This is a named voluntary agreement with a quantified expected reduction. Even though the text notes underperformance, it still qualifies as an implemented policy.

policy_statement: Increase the use of natural gas in the industrial sector.
source_quote: The  realisation  of  a  marine  stocking  terminal  will certainly support the growth of gas demand in Italy and will help its expansion; but the terminal alone will not be adequate to produce such an increase in the use of natural gas as to entail  3 MtCO2 reduction in emissions.
section_header: 4.3.1 Measures implemented in the industry sector
extraction_rationale: This passage identifies a mitigation measure in industry: increasing natural gas use, with an estimated emissions effect. It qualifies despite the caveat about adequacy.

policy_statement: Require compulsory appointment of energy managers in industrial plants consuming more than 10,000 tep/year and service companies consuming more than 1,000 tep/year.
source_quote: Law no. 10/91 Art. 19 assigned compulsory appointment of an energy manager in industrial plants consuming more than 10 000 tep year of primary energy and in the services companies consuming more than 1000 tep/ year.
section_header: Table 4.7 - List of measures implemented in the industry sector
extraction_rationale: This is a binding legal requirement with explicit thresholds. It clearly qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Co-finance research and reconversion activities and regulate the market to replace industrial motors with high-efficiency F1 engines by 2007, supported by tax credits and a voluntary agreement with ANIE.
source_quote: In order to the application of this policy the following measures are necessary: -  co-financing  for  research  and  re-conversation activities  for  the  production  of  last-generation engines  (F1,  high  efficiency, including  a  total amount  of  investment  of  about  300-350  million Euros),  to  be  determined  in  the  voluntary  agreement with ANIE; -  regulations  establishing  that  all  electric  engines introduced on the market are of the F1 (high efficiency) type as from 2007
section_header: 4.3.3.1 Increase in the efficiency of electric motors
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete package with funding, regulation, and a date. It clearly qualifies as a policy and includes both financial and regulatory mechanisms.

policy_statement: Raise the COS standard from 0.9 to 0.95 with higher tariff charges on reactive power.
source_quote: The raising of the COS standard is envisaged from 0.9  to  0.95  (the  same  as  the  European  average), with an aggravation of the tariff component connection to the reactive power.
section_header: 4.3.3.3 Raising of the COS j standard
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified technical standard change with a tariff mechanism. It qualifies as a policy intervention.

policy_statement: Expand medium-size industrial cogeneration by 10-20 TWh through tariff support, green certificates, or white certificates for plants below 50 MW.
source_quote: A  potential  additional  expansion  of  medium-size cogeneration plants in the industrial sector is estimated in the range of 10-20 TWh with a reduction in CO2 emissions between 0.8 and 1.5 Mt. Incentives to cogeneration shoud be  actuated  through  the  following  alternative options:
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified cogeneration expansion option with explicit incentive mechanisms. It qualifies as a policy option and financial instrument.

policy_statement: Increase energy recovery from waste in industry and electricity generation, including use of waste in cement works, with investments of 1.1-2.4 billion Euro and reductions of 1.8-3 Mt.
source_quote: Altogether, the investments on the use of heat from wastes both in the industry sector and for the production of electric energy are estimated in a range between 1.100 and 2.400 million Euros, with a NPV near to zero, proportionate to the tariffs of waste disposal  which  should  be  established  in  order  to enable  the  investment  return.  Potential  emission savings are estimated between 1.8 and 3 Mt.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified waste-to-energy policy option with investment and emissions figures. It qualifies clearly.

policy_statement: Measures implemented in the transport sector include low-carbon fuels, collective transport, freight efficiency, and infrastructure actions.
source_quote: The most significant measures  are  described  in  chapter  5  of  the  Second National  Communication and they are briefly  summarised hereafter. The voluntary  agreement  with  Fiat (integrated with agreement between the European Commis-sion and the car producers) foresee a reduction in specific car emissions from 164 gCO2/Km to 145 gCO2/km.
section_header: 4.4.1 Measures implemented in the transport sector
extraction_rationale: This section introduces multiple transport measures and is best represented by a parent entry, though the text is partly narrative.

policy_statement: Implement the voluntary agreement with Fiat to reduce specific car emissions from 164 gCO2/km to 145 gCO2/km.
source_quote: The voluntary  agreement  with  Fiat (integrated with agreement between the European Commis-sion and the car producers) foresee a reduction in specific car emissions from 164 gCO2/Km to 145 gCO2/km. This measure is estimated to enable a reduction of 6.8 MtCO2 by 2010.
section_header: 4.4.1 Measures implemented in the transport sector
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified vehicle efficiency agreement with explicit emissions intensity and reduction impact. It clearly qualifies.

policy_statement: Increase diffusion of methane, LPG, and biodiesel vehicles to reduce emissions by 1 MtCO2.
source_quote: The increasing diffusion of methane, LPG and biodiesel vehicles will  enable  an  additional  reduction of 1 MtCO2.
section_header: 4.4.1 Measures implemented in the transport sector
extraction_rationale: This is a specific low-carbon fuel vehicle policy with quantified emissions impact. It qualifies as a policy measure.

policy_statement: Promote collective transport measures with an estimated direct reduction of 0.5 MtCO2.
source_quote: The direct effects of the measures promoting the use of collective  transport  means is  limited  to  0.5 MtCO2.
section_header: 4.4.1 Measures implemented in the transport sector
extraction_rationale: This is a transport demand-management measure with quantified emissions impact. It qualifies, though the exact instruments are not detailed here.

policy_statement: Shift 12 Gt/km of freight from road to rail and sea to reduce emissions by about 1 MtCO2, with total freight measures yielding 2.6-3.2 MtCO2.
source_quote: A  series  of  measures  aim  at  increasing  the efficiency  of  goods  transport :    the  reduction achievable    through  the  shift  of  12  Gt/km  from road to rail/sea traffic, is of about 1 MtCO 2 ; assuming that all  other  anticipated  measures  are achieved,  the  emission  reduction  will  be  in  the range of 2.6 and 3.2 MtCO2.
section_header: 4.4.1 Measures implemented in the transport sector
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified modal-shift policy with explicit freight transfer and emissions effects. It clearly qualifies.

policy_statement: Established transport measures are grouped into low-carbon fuels, optimization of private transport systems, and infrastructure.
source_quote: The established measures incorporated in the reference scenario are described and classified into three categories as follows: - -measures aimed toward the shift to low-carbon fuels; - -optimisation  of private transport systems  and car pooling; - -infrastructures.
section_header: 4.4.3 New initiatives already established for the transport sector

extraction_rationale: This is a broad but explicit infrastructure category under established transport measures. It qualifies as a policy grouping sub-action.

policy_statement: Shift to low-carbon fuels such as LPG and methane to reduce emissions by 1.5 MtCO2 by 2010.
source_quote: These measures should enable a reduction of 1.5 Mt of  CO 2 by 2010 (standard value 2,0 Mt), and total investment  up  to  880  million  Euros,  530  of which charged to the public sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified transport fuel-switching policy with investment and emissions figures. It clearly qualifies.

policy_statement: Promote natural gas use in transport through the Ministry of Environment-Fiat-Oil Industries protocol.
source_quote: The Protocol potentialities are only partly exploited for the time being. The development of natural gas - which, in any case, gives positive results since it reduces  CO2 emissions  -  will  produce  the  best results when 'dedicated' engines will be available, that is to say, engines purposely devised and optimised  for  fuelling  vehicles  with  natural  gases.
section_header: Promotion of natural gas use. Protocol of the Ministry of Environment - Fiat - Oil Industries board
extraction_rationale: This is a named protocol promoting natural gas vehicles. It qualifies as a policy despite lacking a precise target in this paragraph.

policy_statement: Replace buses older than 10 years with gas-driven or hybrid buses through programme agreements and local regulations.
source_quote: Having  considered  the  reassuring  results  of  Law no.194/98 and following developments (MD 25 May 1999), a proposal is made to spur the local transport companies  to  replace,  by  means  of  Programme Agreements  and  local  regulations,  their  outdated buses  (registered  more  than  10  years  before)  with gas-driven buses or hybrids.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific fleet replacement proposal with a clear age threshold and implementation mechanism. It qualifies as a policy option.

policy_statement: Promote LPG use through the Ministry of Industry-Fiat-LPG Consortium protocol and financial incentives for LPG vehicles or conversions within 36 months of registration.
source_quote: The protocol  was  signed  recently  and  it  includes  a series  of  financial  incentives  for  the  acquisition  of LPG-fuelled vehicles or in favour of those subject who are willing to convert their vehicles into LPG-fuelled cars within 36 months from the registration date. A series  of  mutual  commitments are also foreseen to the aim of improving the diffusion of this fuel.
section_header: Promotion of LPG use Protocol of the Ministry of Industry- Fiat - LPG Consortium
extraction_rationale: This is a specific protocol with financial incentives and an eligibility window. It clearly qualifies as a policy and financial instrument.

policy_statement: Optimize private transport systems through car pooling, car sharing, collective taxis, telematics, and fuel tax reform.
source_quote: These measures should enable a reduction of 2.1 Mt of  CO2 by 2010 (4.6  Mt  when  completed),  energy saving equal to 0.8 Mtoe (2 at completion ) and total investments amounting up to 60 million Euros, 49 of which charged to the public sector. The unit cost for the  reduction  of  emissions  is  estimated  around  3 euro/t.
section_header: 4.4.3.2 Systems aimed toward the optimisation of the private transport sector
extraction_rationale: This subsection introduces a package of listed measures with quantified impacts and investments. It should be treated as a parent.

parent_statement: Systems aimed toward the optimisation of the private transport sector
policy_statement: Implement car pooling coordinated by local mobility managers and voluntary agreements with businesses.
source_quote: Established under Decrees of Environment M. of 17 February 2000 and of 20 December 2000, the sharing  of  private  means  of  transport  among  several users, co-ordinated by local mobility managers for the formation of car crews, could be implemented also  through  the  signing  of  voluntary  agreements with  businesses  with  a  number  of  employees exceeding a given threshold.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific transport demand-management measure with legal basis and implementation mechanism. It qualifies clearly.

parent_statement: Systems aimed toward the optimisation of the private transport sector
policy_statement: Implement car sharing through local public transport enterprises to reduce urban traffic impacts.
source_quote: Established under Decree of Environment M. of 20 December 2000, proposes the organisation of operating units within local public transportation enterprises  for  the  purpose  of  initiating  the  joint  management of a vehicle available to a wide range of users  while  encouraging  the  use  of  vehicles  that provide low environmental impact.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific operational measure with a named decree and implementation structure. It qualifies as a policy.

parent_statement: Systems aimed toward the optimisation of the private transport sector
policy_statement: Introduce collective taxis as an intermediate transport service between public buses and private taxis.
source_quote: Already contemplated Decree of Environment M. of 20 December 2000, proposes a transport offering that represents a middle road between public  buses and private taxis and contributes to lessening  the  congestion  of  routes  where  the  demand for  transport is  high;
extraction_rationale: This is a specific transport service innovation under an existing decree. It qualifies as a policy measure.

parent_statement: Systems aimed toward the optimisation of the private transport sector
policy_statement: Create one or more coordination centers for telematic freight transport to reduce empty trips.
source_quote: As has already been proposed in the PGT, given that considerable  portion  of  the  kilometres  travelled  by vehicles  of  heavy  transport  without  working  loads (10% -  25%),  it  is  recommended  that  a  voluntary agreement  be  reached  with  the  Federtrasporto (industry board), providing incentives for the creation of  one  or  more  centres  of  coordination  that  can establish synergy among the initiatives already undertaken while assisting an increasingly large number of transporters to cover their 'empty trips'.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific freight-efficiency proposal with a named mechanism and incentive structure. It qualifies as a policy option.

parent_statement: Systems aimed toward the optimisation of the private transport sector
policy_statement: Reform excise taxes on fuels by the end of 2004 to favor fuels with lower health, environmental, and CO2 impacts while keeping revenue constant.
source_quote: By the end of 2004 the Ministry of Finance should reformulate the excise taxes on fuels in such a way that,  with  the  revenue  flow  remaining  equal,  fuels that cause less damage to human health and to the environment, as well as lower emissions of CO2, are promoted.
extraction_rationale: This is a time-bound fiscal reform with explicit climate and environmental criteria. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Develop transport infrastructure measures to reduce emissions by 3.6 MtCO2 by 2010 and 17.6 Mt at full operation.
source_quote: The measures in question, already contemplated, and on a priority basis, under the 'objective law' of 21 December 2001, should permit by 2010, when considered  altogether,  reductions  of  3.6  Mt  of  CO2 (17.6 Mt at full operation), for energy savings of 1.1 Mtep (at full operation 2.0).
extraction_rationale: This subsection introduces a package of infrastructure measures with quantified reductions. It should be extracted as a parent.

parent_statement: Infrastructure measures under the objective law of 21 December 2001
policy_statement: Implement the Highway of the Sea project through restructuring and modernization of port structures to support coastal shipping.
source_quote: In light of Law no. 27/2000, as well as the voluntary agreement with the Confitarma, plus the impetus in this direction on the European-Community level, the investments made for the restructuring and modernisation of port structures will prepare Italy (which sits at the centre of the transport flows in the Mediterranean basin) to meet the growing demand for coastal shipping, making that mode of transport competitive even for voyages of less than 500 km .
section_header: Maritime transport. Implementation of the 'Highway of the Sea' project
extraction_rationale: This is a specific infrastructure investment policy with a named project and clear transport-shift purpose. It qualifies.

parent_statement: Infrastructure measures under the objective law of 21 December 2001
policy_statement: Reactivate and develop inland waterways for transport.
source_quote: The implementation of inland naval transport may be accomplished in a relatively brief period of time, and with  significant  levels  of  positive  fall-out,  with  the investment  priority  being  placed  on  the  areas  that lead to the market of Rome,   to the 'petrochemical rectangle'  of  Mantua  -  Marghera  -  Ferrara  Ravenna, as well as the Mestre - Treviso basin.
section_header: Maritime transport. Reactivation and development of inland waterways.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific transport infrastructure development measure. It qualifies because it names the intervention and priority areas.

parent_statement: Infrastructure measures under the objective law of 21 December 2001
policy_statement: Complete high-speed railway lines and extend local railway networks.
source_quote: Completion  of  high-speed  railway  lines.  Railway transportation  -  Extension  of  the  local  railway  network. Extension  of  the  network  is  a  measure  needed  to ensure balanced and sustained development.
section_header: Completion of high-speed railway lines. Railway transportation - Extension of the local railway network.
extraction_rationale: This is a named infrastructure measure in rail transport. It qualifies as a policy commitment.

parent_statement: Infrastructure measures under the objective law of 21 December 2001
policy_statement: Build new lines and extend existing subways and dedicated-lane bus systems in urban areas.
source_quote: Among the  European  countries,  ours  is  the  least equipped  with  public  transport  structures  using dedicated (single occupancy) lanes. The programs approved  and  currently  being  implemented  have made possible improvements in the structural facilities  of  a  number  of  cities,  but  the  overall  needs would appear to be significantly greater than the initiatives undertaken.
section_header: New lines and the extension of existing lines: subways and bus transport on dedicated lanes (urban )
extraction_rationale: The subsection heading and supporting text indicate a concrete urban transit expansion policy. It qualifies despite the text being partly descriptive.

parent_statement: Infrastructure measures under the objective law of 21 December 2001
policy_statement: Develop interconnectors and regional hubs to reduce traffic congestion and emissions.
source_quote: The projects to improve interconnectors and regional hubs  prove  to  be  a  strategic  tool  for  the  entire national  transportation  system  (freight  and  passenger);  thanks to the reduction in traffic congestion, there  will  also  be  positive  side-effects  in  terms  of emissions.
section_header: Development of interconnectors and regional hubs
extraction_rationale: This is a specific transport-system infrastructure measure with explicit congestion and emissions benefits. It qualifies.

parent_statement: Infrastructure measures under the objective law of 21 December 2001
policy_statement: Develop medium- and long-range roadway infrastructure to shorten routes and improve vehicle utilization.
source_quote: The  development of the infrastructures will make possible shorter routes and improved criteria for the utilisation of vehicles, with positive consequences for emissions as well.
section_header: Work on medium and long-range roadway infrastructures.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific infrastructure policy with an operational mechanism and emissions rationale. It qualifies, though climate is not the sole purpose.

policy_statement: Additional transport initiatives are grouped into technological/tax-related measures, infrastructure work, and research.
source_quote: The additional measures regarding the transport sector have been grouped into three main categories: - technological/tax-related - infrastructure work - research.
section_header: 4.4.4 Additional initiatives planned for the transport sector
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella grouping of additional transport measures with clear subcategories. It should be extracted as a parent.

parent_statement: Additional initiatives planned for the transport sector
policy_statement: Replace circulating vehicles with low-consumption, low-emission cars at 120 gCO2/km, saving 1.5-2.5 Mtoe and reducing 3.5-6 MtCO2.
source_quote: - -supplement  to  the  Fiat-Acea  agreement  for  the development of vehicles producing lower emissions of CO2 and incentives in the form of subsidies for the replacement of existing automobiles with new vehicles providing consumption rates lower than 5 lt/100 km (average CO2 emissions equal to or lower than 120 g/Km); it is expected that a directive on the subject  will  be  issued  before  the  end  of  this  year. Estimates  show  that  this  measure,    should  lead  to reductions in CO 2 from 3.5 to 6 Mt, with energy savings of between 1.5 and 2.5 Mtoe
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified vehicle replacement policy with explicit efficiency and emissions thresholds plus subsidies. It clearly qualifies.

parent_statement: Additional initiatives planned for the transport sector
policy_statement: Improve energy efficiency of heavy transport vehicles through stricter registration rules and a voluntary agreement with industry.
source_quote: - -Improvement  in  the  energy  efficiency  of  heavy transport vehicles . The measure would make registration of vehicles used for transport dependent on compliance with more restrictive rules in terms of both consumption and emissions. At the same time, a  voluntary  agreement  is  to  be  reached  with  the industry involved.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific regulatory and voluntary-agreement package for heavy vehicles. It qualifies as a policy.

parent_statement: Additional initiatives planned for the transport sector
policy_statement: Blend diesel fuel with biodiesel up to 5%, beginning around 2006 and reaching 4-5% by 2010.
source_quote: - -Bio-fuels. There  are  plans  for  the  blending  of diesel  fuel  used  in  engines  with  bio-diesel  (produced through the esterification of rape oil) up to a level of 5%. Within 4-6 years, the national industry  could  be  capable  of  turning  out  an  annual quantity of bio-diesel of between 1 and 1.3 Mt..
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified biofuel blending policy with a clear percentage target and implementation timeline. It qualifies.

parent_statement: Additional initiatives planned for the transport sector
policy_statement: Revise vehicle owner tax calculations to reflect vehicle weight and restore annual vehicle inspections.
source_quote: - -Revision of the method for calculating the owner's tax on vehicles so that it no longer reflects only the maximum horsepower of the vehicle,  but  also:  a) the weight of the vehicle, in this way pointing users towards  lower-weight  vehicles,  with  significant advantages in terms of CO2 emissions, lower consumption and less pervasive pollution; b) a return to annual vehicle inspections
extraction_rationale: This is a fiscal and regulatory reform with explicit climate and efficiency rationale. It clearly qualifies.

parent_statement: Additional initiatives planned for the transport sector
policy_statement: Improve fuel quality and standardization from 2004 by reducing sulphur in gasoline and standardizing LPG and natural gas for motor propulsion.
source_quote: - -Improvement of quality and standardisation of fuels beginning in 2004: - -Reduction  of  the  maximum  level  of  sulphur allowed  in  gasolines : this  measures  is  an  irreplaceable  precondition  to  the  development  of vehicles with low or extremely low levels of consumption.
extraction_rationale: This is a dated fuel-quality regulatory package with explicit technical standards. It qualifies as a policy.

parent_statement: Additional initiatives planned for the transport sector
policy_statement: Adjust excise taxes on fuels and finance national sinks through a 0.005 euro per unit increase or allocation.
source_quote: - -adjustment  of  excise  taxes  on  fuels  and financing of national sinks . Given the difficulty of reducing emissions in the transport sector, it is proposed that the industry be assigned the absorption potential of the sinks, both domestic and abroad; a reformulation  of  the  increases  in  excise  revenues resulting  from  the  carbon  tax  could  make  possible the  financing  of  internal  measures  of  forestation/reforestation and/or other measures relating to the sinks. The increases in the excise tax (or the allocation  of  a  portion  of  the  existing  tax)  for  the financing of these costs amounts to 0.005 euro/unit of sale to the public.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific fiscal proposal with a quantified tax amount and explicit sink-financing purpose. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

parent_statement: Additional initiatives planned for the transport sector
policy_statement: Promote campaigns to raise awareness about driving methods to reduce fuel waste and emissions.
source_quote: Given that no small percentage of wasted fuel and excess emissions is the result of the ways in which vehicles  of  individual  transport  are  driven  on  a daily  basis,  campaigns  designed  to  heighten awareness among roadway users would be able, even  in  relatively  brief  periods  of  time,  to  have extremely positive consequences on emission levels
extraction_rationale: This is a softer policy instrument focused on behavior change. It qualifies because it names a specific intervention and expected emissions effect, though it is less binding than others.

parent_statement: Additional initiatives planned for the transport sector
policy_statement: Promote automobile transport on trains through integration of parking exchanges with vehicle-loading zones and a program agreement with Trenitalia.
source_quote: - -promotion and development of automobile transport on trains . This service, which has been offered for many years now, offers interesting pos-sibilities  for  reducing  emissions  and  contributing  to limiting fuel consumption. A measure that will have positive consequences for medium to long-range trips is the functional integration of the parking exchanges with the zones where the vehicles are loaded onto the trains. There are plans for a program agreement with the Trenitalia company.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific intermodal transport policy with a named implementation partner. It qualifies clearly.

parent_statement: Additional initiatives planned for the transport sector
policy_statement: Reorganize urban traffic through car pricing, taxi-buses, computerized traffic-light systems, and access restrictions to historic centers.
source_quote: - -reorganisation of urban traffic by means of: - car pricing : setting of a fee for entry of vehicles into metropolitan areas; - introduction of taxi-buses into roads with the highest demand for traffic; - activation of computerised systems for traffic management and control of  traffic  lights
extraction_rationale: This is a package of concrete urban traffic management measures, including a fee. It clearly qualifies as policy.

parent_statement: Additional initiatives planned for the transport sector
policy_statement: Support research on optimized natural gas and LPG engines, fuel-cell propulsion, lighter materials, and hydrogen production/distribution.
source_quote: Support for research into vehicles that are intrinsically more efficient and operated with fuels that contain lower  levels  of  carbon  is  worthy  of  note  among measures  designed  to  reduce  emissions  of  greenhouse gases, in addition to which it could contribute significantly to the modernisation of Italy's transport system as a whole and to roadway safety. The following topics deserve mention:
extraction_rationale: This is a specific R&D policy package with named technology areas. It qualifies as a policy option.

policy_statement: Measures implemented in the residential and tertiary sector include lower-carbon fuels, better building insulation, and more efficient electric and thermal equipment.
source_quote: The measures implemented can be classified under three  categories:  use  of  fuels  with  a  lower  carbon content, increased building insulation and promotion of more efficient equipment, both electric and thermal.
section_header: 4.5.1 Measures implemented in the residential and tertiary sector
extraction_rationale: This is an umbrella grouping of civil-sector measures with clear subcategories. It should be extracted as a parent.

parent_statement: Measures implemented in the residential and tertiary sector
policy_statement: Increase the use of fuels with lower carbon content in residential and tertiary sectors.
source_quote: The measures implemented can be classified under three  categories:  use  of  fuels  with  a  lower  carbon content, increased building insulation and promotion of more efficient equipment, both electric and thermal.
section_header: 4.5.1 Measures implemented in the residential and tertiary sector
extraction_rationale: This is a specific fuel-switching category under the civil-sector measures. It qualifies as a policy sub-action.

parent_statement: Measures implemented in the residential and tertiary sector
policy_statement: Increase building insulation in residential and tertiary sectors.
source_quote: The measures implemented can be classified under three  categories:  use  of  fuels  with  a  lower  carbon content, increased building insulation and promotion of more efficient equipment, both electric and thermal.
section_header: 4.5.1 Measures implemented in the residential and tertiary sector
extraction_rationale: This is a specific efficiency category under the civil-sector measures. It qualifies as a policy sub-action.

parent_statement: Measures implemented in the residential and tertiary sector
policy_statement: Promote more efficient electric and thermal equipment in residential and tertiary sectors.
source_quote: The measures implemented can be classified under three  categories:  use  of  fuels  with  a  lower  carbon content, increased building insulation and promotion of more efficient equipment, both electric and thermal.
section_header: 4.5.1 Measures implemented in the residential and tertiary sector
extraction_rationale: This is a specific equipment-efficiency category under the civil-sector measures. It qualifies as a policy sub-action.

policy_statement: Increase natural gas use in residential units and more efficient heating equipment as the main measure for reducing emissions in buildings.
source_quote: The use of natural gas in residential units registered significant increases in the years following 1990 and is  expected  to  continue  growing  in  the  years  to come; this remains the most economical measure for reducing  emissions.  Tied  to  this  measure  is  the increased  use  of  more  efficient  equipment  (boilers and components) to heat buildings.
section_header: 4.5.1 Measures implemented in the residential and tertiary sector
extraction_rationale: This is an explicit building-sector mitigation measure with a named mechanism. It qualifies despite lacking a formal legal citation in this sentence.

policy_statement: Implement Law 10/91 thermal regulations to reduce energy consumption in new buildings by 10% compared to 1990 levels.
source_quote: The legislation  developed  for  the implementation of Law 10/91 , and in particular art. 4C, points 1 and 2, has reduced energy consumption in new buildings by 10% within the last two years, compared to the 1990 levels.
section_header: 4.5.1 Measures implemented in the residential and tertiary sector
extraction_rationale: This is a legal building-efficiency measure with a quantified effect. It clearly qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Extend the ministerial decrees of April 2001 on final-use efficiency beyond 2006, yielding an additional 3.8-6.5 MtCO2 reduction by 2010.
source_quote: There are plans for the ministerial decrees of April 2001 to remain in effect beyond 2006, with the same annual increases as those set for the period 2002-2006: the result would be a further reduction  -  in  addition  to  that  estimated  for  the  year 2006 - of from 3.8 to 6.5 Mt CO2 from an investment  that,  as  of  2010,  would  total  between  19 and 33 million euro.
section_header: 4.5.4.1 Extension of effect of decrees on the efficiency of final uses
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified extension of an existing efficiency policy with emissions and investment figures. It clearly qualifies.

policy_statement: Expand use of thermal solar energy for low-temperature heat uses, targeting 70,000 toe savings and about 0.2 MtCO2 reductions.
source_quote: It  is  predicted  that  investments  can  be  made  for potential  energy  savings  of  70,000  t.o.e.,  which would result in reductions of approximately 0.2 Mt in  CO 2 investments.  Overall  investments  are  estimated at 800 million euro, with a negative VAN of 160  million  euro  and  a  unit  cost,  assuming  the investment will last for 20 years, of 40 million euro.
section_header: 4.5.4.2 More extensive use of thermal solar energy
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified solar thermal deployment policy option with energy savings and investment figures. It qualifies clearly.

policy_statement: Use carbon tax revenues for compensation, emissions reduction subsidies, energy efficiency, and renewable energy development.
source_quote: Law  448/98 ,  which  introduced  the  carbon  tax, mentioned that the Government would be able to draw on a portion of the resulting revenues for use as compensation for the measures taken in the different sectors and as subsidies for the reduction of emissions, for the promotion of energy efficiency and for the development of renewable sources.
extraction_rationale: This is a fiscal policy with explicit use of revenues for climate-related purposes. It clearly qualifies as a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Use Law 388/00 to lower taxation on products that reduce emissions, such as biodiesel, and to promote energy efficiency and renewable sources.
source_quote: Law 388/00 proposes a number of different procedures for the reduction of emissions:  specifically, lower taxation on products that permit decreas-es in emissions, such as bio-diesel, together with the promotion of energy efficiency and renewable sources.
extraction_rationale: This is a tax-based climate policy with explicit emissions-reduction purpose and named eligible products. It qualifies clearly.

policy_statement: Adopt thermal or catalytic treatment devices for adipic acid production to reduce N2O emissions.
source_quote: In  the  case  of  adipic  acid,  the  planned  course  of action calls for the adoption in Italy of the devices (thermal  or  catalytic)  already  used  in  the  other European countries for the treatment of effluent gases. The measure referred to consists of a voluntary agreement with the only enterprise involved.
section_header: Reduction of N2O emissions from the production of adipic acid and nitric acid
extraction_rationale: This is a specific industrial process mitigation measure with a named technology and implementation mechanism. It qualifies clearly.

policy_statement: Install SCR systems for nitric acid production process gases through a voluntary agreement with the industrial sector.
source_quote: As for nitric acid, the most advanced technology calls  for  installation  of  SCR  (selective  catalytic reduction)  systems  for  the  treatment  of  process gases.  The  cost  of  reduction  is  relatively  limited, amounting to less than 0.5 Euro for CO2 equivalent ton. The proposed measure consists of a voluntary  agreement  with  the  respective  industrial sector.
section_header: Reduction of N2O emissions from the production of adipic acid and nitric acid
extraction_rationale: This is a specific industrial mitigation measure with named technology and cost information. It clearly qualifies.

policy_statement: Promote organic agriculture to reduce CO2 emissions from agricultural energy consumption by 0.28-0.337 MtCO2.
source_quote: Organic agriculture is experiencing rapid growth, primarily  as  a  result  of  the  incentives  provided under EU Regulations no. 2078/92; the agricultural surface area on which the methods of organic agriculture are practiced, equal to 91,500 hectares in 1993, had already reached 1,069,339 hectares in the year 2000. Assuming that the specific level of energy consumption of organic agriculture is 30% lower than that of traditional agriculture, a projection through 2010 of current growth trends in the sector shows that the emissions avoided could total 0.337 Mt CO2.
extraction_rationale: This is a policy-relevant intervention because it links incentives for organic agriculture to quantified emissions reductions. The commitment is somewhat indirect, but the intervention is specific.

policy_statement: Rationalize fertilizer use and adopt codes of good agricultural practice to reduce N2O emissions from agricultural soils by about 0.46 MtCO2eq.
source_quote: The emission reductions in question can result from a rationalisation of the use of fertilisers, with a subsequent limitation of the consumption and related emissions of nitrous oxide from agricultural soils. Of essential importance to achieving the above objective are: - ongoing efforts to increase awareness of the practice, plus -  the adoption of codes of good agricultural practice.
section_header: Emissions of nitrous oxide from agricultural soils
extraction_rationale: This is a specific agricultural mitigation measure with named practices and an implied quantified reduction later in the paragraph. It qualifies clearly.

policy_statement: Cover liquid animal waste holding tanks and convey biogas to combustion or cogeneration plants to reduce methane emissions from manure management.
source_quote: The proposed initiative involves covering the holding  tanks  used  to  store  liquid  animal  waste  and then conveying the resulting biogas to combustion or  cogeneration plants. The primary focus of the activities would be pigs (between 10% and 40% of the animals) and, to a relatively limited degree, cattle,  with  a  reduction  in  methane  emissions  of between 7 and 39 kt of methane per year
section_header: Emissions of methane from manure management
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete methane-reduction intervention with explicit technology and quantified reduction range. It qualifies clearly.

policy_statement: Apply Directive 96/61/EC IPPC licensing to large poultry and pig farms based on best available technology.
source_quote: Another  measure  oriented  towards  this  same objective is Directive 96/61/EC (Integrated Pollution Prevention and Control, or IPPC), which calls  for  the  introduction  of  licensing  processes based on the adoption of the best possible technology available for poultry farms with more than 40,000 birds and pig farms with more than 2,000 animals (heavier than 30 kg) or 750 sows.
section_header: Emissions of methane from manure management
extraction_rationale: This is a binding regulatory licensing mechanism with explicit thresholds. It clearly qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Reduce biodegradable municipal waste in landfills by 50% by 2010 compared to 1995, in line with Directive 99/31/EC.
source_quote: fulfilment of the deadlines set for the reduction of  the  biodegradable  fraction  of  the  municipal waste  in  landfills,  as  stipulated  under  Directive 99/31/EC, which calls for a reduction of 50% as early as 2010, compared to the 1995 level, in the quantity of biodegradable municipal waste to be placed in landfills, making for a forecast decrease of 0,64 Mt;
section_header: 4.7.3 Waste: Stabilisation of the organic fraction and energy recovery
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified waste policy target with a legal basis and expected emissions effect. It clearly qualifies.

policy_statement: Recover energy from waste so that 30% of municipal waste undergoes energy-recovery treatment by 2010, adding 500 MWe of capacity.
source_quote: substantial respect of the objectives of Legislative Decree 22/97, in particular as regards the recovery of energy from waste: it is assumed that, by 2010, the  portion  of  municipal  waste  sent  to  energyrecovery treatments shall be 30% (in line with the indications  of  the  'White  Book  on  the  Energy Optimisation  of  Renewable  Sources',  ENEA, 1999),  making  for  an  additional  increase  of  500 MWe  municipal  electrical  capacity  from  waste, compared to 2000
section_header: 4.7.3 Waste: Stabilisation of the organic fraction and energy recovery
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified waste-to-energy target with a capacity figure and legal reference. It clearly qualifies.

policy_statement: Increase recycled aluminium to about 80% of total consumption by 2010 to reduce PFC emissions.
source_quote: - Aluminium. The recycling of aluminium not only generates the economic benefits due to reduced imports of the raw material and lower energy consumption, but also makes it possible to avoid emissions of PFCs from the processing of the raw mineral.  We  have  assumed  that,  on  the  quantity  of recycled aluminium will grow, between now and the  year  2010,  up  to  approximately  80%  of  the total consumption of this metal.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified recycling target with explicit fluorinated-gas mitigation purpose. It qualifies as a policy option.

policy_statement: Install abatement devices and use lower-GWP fluids in semiconductor production, in line with the European industry's voluntary commitment to keep 2010 emissions 10% below 1995 levels.
source_quote: - Production of semi-conductors. A limited initiative  consisting  of  the  installation  of  abatement devices and the use in the etching process of fluids  with  a  lower  level  of  GWP  is  currently  being studied.  The  European  industry  has  voluntarily agreed  to  limit  its  emissions  in  2010  to  a  figure 10% lower than 1995 levels.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific industrial mitigation initiative with a quantified voluntary target. It qualifies clearly.

policy_statement: Reduce leakage rates from mobile air conditioners from 10% to 5% through design and maintenance improvements.
source_quote: - Mobile air conditioners. Reduction of from 10% to 5% in the rate of leaks from mobile air conditioners, to be obtained through adjustments made during the design phase of the systems and during the  maintenance phase.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified leakage-reduction measure with explicit implementation mechanisms. It clearly qualifies.

policy_statement: Reduce leakage rates of SF6 from installed electrical equipment to 0.45% and from end-of-life equipment to 1% by 2010.
source_quote: In the case of the sulphur hexafluoride contained in electrical equipment, consideration was given to the effects of a scenario in which the leakage rate of  installed  equipment  is  reduced,  by  the  year 2010, from 0.9 to 0.45%, while the leakage rate for equipment at the end of its life cycle falls from 3 to 1%.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified leakage-reduction target for SF6 equipment. It clearly qualifies as a policy option.

policy_statement: Create the National Forestry Inventory of Carbon by 2005 and update it every five years to support Kyoto forest management accounting.
source_quote: From a technical perspective, the National Forestry Inventory of Carbon (INFOCARB) should be created by 2005. This inventory must then be updated every  5  years,  corresponding  to  the  end  of  the period  of  commitment  under  the  Kyoto  Protocol
extraction_rationale: This is a time-bound institutional measure necessary for carbon accounting under Kyoto. It qualifies as a policy because it mandates a specific inventory system.

policy_statement: Carry out new afforestation and reforestation plantings during 2003-2008 over 40,000 hectares, averaging 1 MtCO2 removals during 2008-2012.
source_quote: c) the new plantings to be made during the period 2003-2008, forecast  at  40,000  hectares,  for  an average  removal  of  1  Mt  CO 2 during  the  period 2008-2012 and of 20 Mt CO2 at the maturity.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified land-based intervention with hectares and removal estimates. It clearly qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Carry out afforestation and reforestation in hydrogeologically unstable areas at about 6,000 hectares per year from 2003-2012.
source_quote: The operating capacity of the Basin Authorities is approximately 6,000 hectares of reforestation per year for the period of 2003-2012, making for a total of 60,000 hectares. Average removal for this type of planting  is  estimated  at  1  Mt  CO 2 for  the  period 2008-2012 and at 10 Mt CO2 at the maturity.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified afforestation program in hazard-prone areas with explicit removals. It clearly qualifies and explicitly addresses hydrogeological instability.

policy_statement: Create the National Register of Agro-Forestry Carbon Storage Pools to certify carbon removed by the Italian agricultural and forestry system.
source_quote: The  National  Register  of  Agro-Forestry  Carbon Storage Pools  is the tool for certifying the quantities  of  carbon  removed  by  Italian  agricultural  and forestry system. The registry provides an overview of the use made of Italian soil, placing within this picture the statistical data on the carbon contents of the different catgories of agricultural and forestry activities.
section_header: 4.8.4 National Register of Agro-Forestry Carbon Storage Pools
extraction_rationale: This is a specific institutional mechanism for carbon certification. It qualifies as a policy because it establishes a formal registry.

policy_statement: Adopt specific programs or an agency to assist CDM and JI projects by providing guidelines, partnerships, consulting, and rapid preferential procedures.
source_quote: It is extremely important that the public sector adopt specific programs to assist the CDM and JI projects, eventually  under  the  coordination  of  a  specific agency. These programs (or the agency) can  provide guidelines, serve as a partner or provide consulting to companies  in  order  to  spread  information  on  the projects  and  facilitate  their  performance
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete institutional support proposal for Kyoto mechanisms. It qualifies as a policy option, though implementation details remain open.

policy_statement: Require the Ministry of the Environment and Territory to present by 30 April 2003 a detailed plan for 2004-2006 national carbon-removal activities under Table 6.
source_quote: Before 30 April 2003, the Ministry of the Environment and Territory, in agreement with the Ministry of Agricultural and Forestry Policies  and with the Conference of State-Regions, presents to this Committee the detailed plan referring to the first three-year period 2004-2006, for the realization of the national activities specified in Table 6 in the frame of public resources purposely devoted.
section_header: Annex 1: Revised guidelines for national policies and measures regarding the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions (Law 120/2002)
extraction_rationale: This is a dated implementation requirement with a named responsible ministry and scope. It clearly qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Identify by 30 July 2003 all Italian provisions since 1990 that support forest protection in order to certify natural reforestation activities eligible under Kyoto.
source_quote: Before 30 July 2003, the Ministry of the Environment and Defence of the Territory, in agreement with the Ministry of Agricultural and Forestry Policies, takes measures to identify among the regional, national and international provisions in force in Italy from 1990 to date, all regulations contemplating the defence of the Italian forest stand, with the aim of certifying 'natural reforestation' activities carried out on the national territory in the period 1990-2012
section_header: Annex 1: Revised guidelines for national policies and measures regarding the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions (Law 120/2002)
extraction_rationale: This is a dated administrative requirement tied to Kyoto eligibility for natural reforestation. It clearly qualifies.

policy_statement: Prepare the National Forestry Inventory on Carbon by 31 May 2005 to revise Italy's forest management credit limit.
source_quote: Before 31 May 2005 the Ministry of Agricultural and Forestry Policies, in agreement with the Ministry of the Environment and Territory, prepares the National Forestry Inventory on Carbon and other Carbon Reservoirs in order to start the procedure to revise the limit of use of the credits deriving from the management of forest resources, assigned to Italy
section_header: Annex 1: Revised guidelines for national policies and measures regarding the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions (Law 120/2002)
extraction_rationale: This is a dated institutional requirement with a clear purpose under Kyoto accounting. It qualifies as a policy.

policy_statement: Prepare the National Register of agro-forestry carbon reservoirs by 31 December 2006 to certify carbon flows from afforestation, reforestation, forest management, farmland and grazing land management, and revegetation from 2008 to 2012.
source_quote: Before 31 December 2006, the Ministry of Environment and Territory, in agreement with the Ministry of Agricultural and Forestry Policies, prepares the National Register of agro-forestry carbon reservoirs, in order to certify the carbon flows deriving from the sectors of afforestation, reforestation, deforestation, forest management, management of farmlands and grazing lands and revegetation from 2008 to 2012.
section_header: Annex 1: Revised guidelines for national policies and measures regarding the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions (Law 120/2002)
extraction_rationale: This is a dated institutional certification requirement with explicit sectors and timeframe. It clearly qualifies.

policy_statement: Portugal approved the National Adaptation Strategy (ENAAC 2020) as its national adaptation strategy focused on knowledge, mainstreaming, and implementation of adaptation measures.
source_quote:
Portugal also has a revised NAS - National Adaptation Strategy (ENAAC 2020, approved by the Council of Ministers Resolution n.º 56/2015, of 30 th of July) (English version in Annex 1), focusing on improving the articulation between domains (particularly those of transversal nature), on the integration in sectoral policies, and the implementation of adaptation measures.

The Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme, approved by the Resolution of the Council of Ministers Nº. 130/2019, of 2 nd of August (English version in Annex 2), complements and systematises the work carried out in the context of ENAAC 2020, focusing on its second objective: to implement adaptation measures.
section_header: 1.2. Legal and policy frameworks and institutional arrangements
extraction_rationale: This is a formal, approved national strategy with a named instrument and legal approval. It clearly qualifies as a policy framework for adaptation.

policy_statement: Portugal approved the Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme (P-3AC) to implement adaptation measures under ENAAC 2020.
source_quote:
The Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme, approved by the Resolution of the Council of Ministers Nº. 130/2019, of 2 nd of August (English version in Annex 2), complements and systematises the work carried out in the context of ENAAC 2020, focusing on its second objective: to implement adaptation measures.

The Adaptation to Climate Change Action Programme - P-3AC (NAP) complements and systematises the work done in the context of the NAS, aiming at its second objective, the implementation of adaptation measures.
section_header: 1.2. Legal and policy frameworks and institutional arrangements
extraction_rationale: This is a named, approved action programme with a specific implementation purpose. It is a concrete adaptation policy instrument rather than background description.

policy_statement: Environmental assessment procedures must consider climate vulnerabilities, resilient alternatives, and adaptation measures.
source_quote: The Environmental Assessment procedures consider national and territorial adaptation planning instruments; current and future climatic vulnerabilities through historical data on the climate and the occurrences of extreme weather events; environmental, social and economic impacts and consequences, considering CC scenarios; key risks/impacts of CC in the project; assessment if pre-existing vulnerabilities to CC will be exacerbated; alternatives more resilient to climate pressures and/or allowing a more significant climate vulnerability reduction; critical thresholds that compromise the project or the environment, forcing the adoption of adaptation measures; minimisation measures based on NAP for the relevant vulnerabilities or impacts.
section_header: Integration of climate change impacts and resilience into environmental assessment procedures

policy_statement: ENAAC 2020 is guided by three main objectives: improving climate knowledge, implementing adaptation measures, and integrating adaptation into sectoral policies.
source_quote:
NAS is guided by three main objectives:

- Improving the level of knowledge on climate change - updating, developing, and promoting understanding on climate change and assessing its potential risks, impacts and consequences, including those related to extreme weather events.
- Implement adaptation measures - assess current adaptive capacity and prioritise the implementation of adaptation options and measures that moderate future negative impacts and/or help take advantage of opportunities arising from climate change.
- Promote the integration of adaptation into sectoral policies - promote the integration and monitoring of the climate change adaptation component (mainstreaming) in the most relevant public and sectoral policies, including spatial planning and sustainable urban development policies and their territorial planning and management instruments.

policy_statement: P-3AC establishes nine lines of action to implement adaptation measures addressing Portugal's major climate vulnerabilities.
source_quote:

NAP elects eight direct intervention lines in the territory and infrastructures, complemented by an additional line of action of transversal nature, seeking to respond to Portugal's significant impacts and vulnerabilities.

These comprehend actions for wildfire prevention, soil conservation and improvement, sustainable water use, ecosystems resilience, heat waves prevention, invasive species, diseases and pests, flooding protection, coastal protection and capacity building, awareness and tools for adaptation.

policy_statement: Portugal is developing the National Adaptation Roadmap 2100 to update climate projections, produce regional adaptation narratives, guide spatial planning, and identify investment needs and strategic adaptation measures.
source_quote: Following a similar approach, the National Adaptation Roadmap 2100 (RNA 2100) is being drawn up and is expected to be completed in 2023. The RNA 2100 will update the knowledge of climate projections for Portugal and respective impacts in key sectors, for different Greenhouse Gases (GHG) concentration scenarios. RNA 2100 will result in regional adaptation narratives, with a view to stablish climate change adaptation guidelines for spatial planning and programmes, including at sub-national level. The roadmap will also help to identify investment needs and costs, including costs of inaction. In this way, strategic adaptation projects and measures will be identified to further support the adaptation policies on the ground.

extraction_rationale: This is a named roadmap with a completion timeline and specific outputs. Although still under preparation, it contains concrete planned deliverables and therefore qualifies as a policy commitment.

The Portuguese Environmental Fund was established in 2017. The purpose of this instrument is to support national environmental policies for the pursuit of Sustainable Development Objectives, contributing to the achievement of national and international objectives and commitments, in particular those related to climate change, water resources, waste and nature conservation and biodiversity.

One of the domains that is clearly identified as action domain of this Fund is international cooperation in the field of climate change, in accordance with the compliance of international commitments.

policy_statement: Under the P-3AC resolution, Portugal approved the programme and assigned implementation, integration, monitoring, and reporting responsibilities.
source_quote:
Under the terms of paragraph g) of Article 199 of the Constitution, the Council of Ministers resolves:

1. To approve the Action Programme on Climate Change Adaptation (P-3AC), annexed to this resolution and which forms an integral part thereof.
2. To establish that the lines of action and measures to reduce vulnerabilities to climate change contained in the P-3AC constitute the benchmark for national action on climate change adaptation, without prejudice to the guidelines contained in the National Adaptation Strategy 2020 (ENAAC 2020), and should integrate, among others, the sectoral planning and preparation of funding instruments to be developed under the Multiannual Financial Framework 2021 -2027.

extraction_rationale: This is a binding regulatory mechanism with explicit compliance requirements, so it clearly qualifies as policy. It is a sub-policy under the broader schemes section.
