policy_statement: The Energy Efficiency National Partnership Programme is a voluntary partnership that promotes energy management systems, learning events, and recognition schemes for best practices.
source_quote:
## Energy Efficiency National Partnership (EENP) Programme

This is a voluntary partnership programme for companies that includes:

- Promoting adoption of an energy management system (For example, ISO 50001)
- Organising learning events such as the National Energy Efficiency Conference
- Providing recognition schemes to encourage best practices in energy management
section_header: SCHEMES TO HELP COMPANIES ACHIEVE GREATER ENERGY EFFICIENCY
extraction_rationale: This is a named programme with specific interventions, even though voluntary. It is a sub-policy because it is one component of the broader schemes package.

parent_statement: Schemes to help companies achieve greater energy efficiency
policy_statement: The EE Financing Pilot Programme provides financing for up to 100% of upfront capital investment in energy efficiency projects, with savings shared between financier and company.
source_quote:
## EE Financing Pilot Programme

Under this programme, companies receive financing for up to 100 per cent of the upfront capital investment of energy efficiency projects. Cost savings are shared between the financier and the company.
section_header: SCHEMES TO HELP COMPANIES ACHIEVE GREATER ENERGY EFFICIENCY
extraction_rationale: This is a clear financial instrument because it provides project financing with defined coverage. It is a sub-policy under the umbrella schemes section.

parent_statement: Schemes to help companies achieve greater energy efficiency
policy_statement: NEA co-funds up to 50% of design workshop costs for integrating energy and resource efficiency into new facilities, capped at $600,000 per project.
source_quote:
## Resource-Efficient Design

NEA co-funds up to 50 per cent of the cost of design workshops to integrate energy and resource efficiency in the design of new facilities, capped at $600,000 per project.
section_header: SCHEMES TO HELP COMPANIES ACHIEVE GREATER ENERGY EFFICIENCY
extraction_rationale: This is a specific subsidy with a quantified co-funding rate and cap. It is a sub-policy within the broader company energy-efficiency schemes.

parent_statement: Schemes to help companies achieve greater energy efficiency
policy_statement: NEA co-funds 50% of energy audit costs for existing facilities, capped at $200,000 per project.
source_quote:
## Energy Audits

NEA co-funds 50 per cent of the costs of an energy audit, which assesses energy consumption and helps to develop energy efficiency improvement plans for existing facilities, capped at $200,000 per project.
section_header: SCHEMES TO HELP COMPANIES ACHIEVE GREATER ENERGY EFFICIENCY
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete grant programme with a defined funding share and cap. It is a sub-policy under the umbrella schemes section.

parent_statement: Schemes to help companies achieve greater energy efficiency
policy_statement: EDB and NEA co-fund up to 20% of investment costs for energy-efficient equipment or technologies in retrofit projects.
source_quote:
## Retrofit Projects

EDB and NEA co-fund up to 20 per cent of the investment cost of energy efficient equipment or technologies.
section_header: SCHEMES TO HELP COMPANIES ACHIEVE GREATER ENERGY EFFICIENCY
extraction_rationale: This is a direct co-funding instrument for efficiency retrofits with a quantified support level. It is a sub-policy under the broader schemes package.

parent_statement: Schemes to help companies achieve greater energy efficiency
policy_statement: The Accelerated Depreciation Allowance Scheme allows one-year write-off or depreciation of capital expenditure on more energy-efficient or energy-saving replacement equipment.
source_quote: Besides grants, tax incentive schemes are also available. The Accelerated Depreciation Allowance Scheme (ADAS) allows the writeoff or depreciation, within one year, of capital expenditure on more energy efficient or energysaving equipment to replace existing ones.
section_header: SCHEMES TO HELP COMPANIES ACHIEVE GREATER ENERGY EFFICIENCY
extraction_rationale: This is a tax incentive and therefore a financial instrument. It is part of the broader package of company energy-efficiency schemes.

parent_statement: Schemes to help companies achieve greater energy efficiency
policy_statement: The Investment Allowance - Energy Efficiency Scheme provides an additional 30% investment allowance for energy efficiency investments against taxable income.
source_quote: The Investment Allowance - Energy Efficiency Scheme (IA) allows an additional 30 per cent investment allowance for energy efficiency investments against taxable income, on top of normal capital allowances.
section_header: SCHEMES TO HELP COMPANIES ACHIEVE GREATER ENERGY EFFICIENCY
extraction_rationale: This is a tax-based financial incentive with a quantified allowance. It is a sub-policy under the umbrella schemes section.

policy_statement: EDB and NEA will study policy options and technologies to reduce non-CO2 GHG emissions from the semiconductor sub-sector.
source_quote: Although most of Singapore's GHG emissions consist of CO 2 , non-CO 2 GHGs also contribute a small percentage (2.1 per cent in 2012). In Singapore, most of the non-CO 2 GHG emissions are from the semiconductor sub-sector. 18 EDB and NEA will study policy options to support the implementation of appropriate measures and technologies to reduce non-CO 2 GHG emissions from the sub-sector.
extraction_rationale: This is somewhat less concrete because it commits to studying policy options rather than implementing a final measure. It still qualifies because it names a specific intervention area and explicit emissions-reduction objective.

policy_statement: EDB and NEA will study policy options to facilitate switching industrial heating fuels from fuel oil to cleaner fuels such as natural gas.
source_quote: In the industry sector, fuels such as fuel oil are directly combusted to meet heating needs, for example in boilers. Switching to cleaner fuels such as natural gas can decrease carbon emissions from heating processes by about 25 per cent. EDB and NEA will study further policy options to facilitate this switch.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific fuel-switching commitment tied to quantified emissions benefits, though the mechanism remains under study. It qualifies as a policy because it identifies a named intervention and responsible agencies.

policy_statement: BCA's 3rd Green Building Masterplan will step up retrofitting of tenanted spaces and support zero-capital energy efficiency retrofits, contributing to the goal of greening 80% of buildings by 2030.
source_quote: Beyond the existing Green Lease Toolkit 20  and user-centric Green Mark schemes, BCA will step up efforts to encourage the retrofitting of tenanted spaces with energy-efficient fittings, such as light fittings. To enhance current efforts to green existing buildings, BCA and Singapore Green Building Council (SGBC) have collaborated to develop the Zero Capital Partnership 21  scheme, which provides a 'zero capital' solution for building owners to carry out energy efficiency retrofits for buildings. These efforts will contribute to Singapore's aim of making 80 per cent of all buildings green by 2030.
section_header: Building a Greener Tomorrow 3rd Green Building Masterplan
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete masterplan commitment with named interventions and a quantified 2030 target. It is treated as an individual policy because the text does not present formal sub-items beneath the masterplan.

policy_statement: IDA has implemented standards, incentives, and RD&D support to improve energy efficiency in data centre design, operation, and management.
source_quote: Recognising this, IDA has implemented initiatives to encourage energy efficiency in the design, operation, and management of data centres. This includes the Green Data Centre Standard (Singapore Standard 564), the BCAIDA Green Mark for Data Centres, the Investment Allowance scheme for energy efficiency projects and the Green Data Centre Programme (GDCP) that supports high-impact research, development, and demonstration projects on energy efficiency in data centres.
extraction_rationale: This is a package of implemented measures with named standards and support programmes. It qualifies as policy because it specifies concrete instruments, though it aggregates several tools into one statement.

policy_statement: Singapore will expand public transport and active mobility infrastructure to raise public transport's morning peak mode share from 66% in 2015 to 75% by 2030 and 85% by 2050.
source_quote: These measures collectively aim to increase the use of public transport as a share of overall transport during morning peak hours from 66 per cent in 2015 to 75 per cent by 2030. By 2050, the aim is to further increase this share to 85 per cent.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified transport mode-share target with supporting infrastructure measures described in the section. It qualifies as a policy commitment even though the quote summarizes the package rather than listing every component.

policy_statement: Singapore will double the rail network to 360 km by 2030 and add more than 120 trains to existing lines.
source_quote: An ambitious plan to double the rail network in 15 years. With the opening of Downtown Line 2 in December 2015, Singapore's rail network increased by 10 per cent from 183km in 2014 to some 200km in 2015. This year, the Tuas West Extension for the East-West Line will be completed, adding a further 7.5km. By 2030, the rail network will be 360km, and will be comparable in rail density with developed cities like London, New York and Tokyo. More than 120 trains will also be added to existing train lines, increasing the total fleet size by more than 40 per cent.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific infrastructure expansion commitment with quantified targets and timeline. It qualifies as policy due to the named intervention and measurable outputs.

policy_statement: The Bus Service Enhancement Programme aims to increase the public bus fleet by 1,000 buses, about 25%, by 2017.
source_quote: The Bus Service Enhancement Programme, launched in 2012, aims to grow the public bus fleet by 1,000 buses or about 25 per cent by 2017 .
extraction_rationale: This is a named programme with a quantified fleet expansion target and deadline. It is a standalone policy in the transport section.

policy_statement: Singapore will expand sheltered walkways to 200 km by 2018, cycling paths to over 700 km by 2030, pilot bicycle-sharing, and require private developers to account for pedestrian and cyclist needs from July 2016.
source_quote: To facilitate walking and cycling, our sheltered walkway network will be quadrupled from the existing 56km to 200km by 2018. Cycling paths will double from 355km in 2015 to more than 700km by 2030. Bicycle-sharing will be piloted in various districts, and Ang Mo Kio will be transformed into a model walking and cycling town. From July 2016, LTA and the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) will require private developers to consider the safety, convenience, and accessibility needs of pedestrians and cyclists in their development plans.
extraction_rationale: This combines several concrete active-mobility commitments, including quantified infrastructure targets and a regulatory requirement. It qualifies as policy because the measures are specific and time-bound.

policy_statement: Seven new integrated transport hubs will be built by 2023, with additional hubs planned in selected redevelopment areas.
source_quote: Seven new integrated transport hubs will be built by 2023 to make it convenient for people to access different transport modes and to enjoy shopping and lifestyle services at the same location. Additional integrated transport hubs will be built for selected areas undergoing development or redevelopment.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete infrastructure commitment with a number and deadline. It qualifies as policy because it specifies a defined intervention by government.

policy_statement: By 2030, every HDB town will have a dedicated cycling network.
source_quote: By 2030, every HDB town will have a dedicated cycling network.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear, time-bound infrastructure target. Although brief, it is sufficiently concrete to qualify as policy.

policy_statement: Singapore uses COE, ERP, high vehicle taxes, registration fees, and fuel duties to curb private vehicle growth and use.
source_quote: The Certificate of Entitlement (COE) and the Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) systems have been in place for many years to curb the growth of the vehicle population and the use of private transport. This is supplemented by high vehicle taxes, registration fees and fuel duties.
extraction_rationale: These are binding transport demand-management instruments that directly shape vehicle ownership and use. Although longstanding, they are explicit policy mechanisms and therefore qualify.

policy_statement: Phase 2 of the EV Pilot Programme will trial fleet-based EV operations and introduce up to 1,000 EVs with up to 2,000 charging kiosks.
source_quote: In the second phase, the use of EVs will be trialled for fleet-based operations. An EV car-sharing pilot programme for this phase will introduce as many as 1,000 EVs and an island-wide charging infrastructure comprising up to 2,000 charging kiosks to support the eventual proliferation of EVs.
extraction_rationale: This is a named pilot with quantified deployment and infrastructure commitments. It qualifies as policy because it specifies a concrete intervention and scale.

policy_statement: IDA and SPRING Singapore launched a $20 million pilot project to develop an integrated delivery system for malls to reduce truck trips and emissions.
source_quote: In 2015, IDA and SPRING Singapore announced a $20 million pilot project to develop an integrated delivery system for malls. If scaled to cover all of Singapore's malls, such consolidation and coordination could reduce the number of trucks on the road by 25 per cent, reduce waiting time for deliveries by 65 per cent, reduce the manpower required for deliveries by 40 per cent, and result in lower carbon emissions from trucks.
extraction_rationale: This is a funded pilot project with a specific intervention and quantified expected outcomes. It qualifies as policy and is also a financial/public investment instrument.

policy_statement: The Carbon Emissions-based Vehicle Scheme gives rebates to low-emission vehicles and imposes registration surcharges on high-emission vehicles, with review in 2017.
source_quote: Under the CEVS, these vehicles are divided into categories based on their CO 2 /km performance. Low-emission cars are given incentives, while high-emission cars incur a penalty in the form of a registration surcharge. The rebates and surcharges are applied upfront at the point of purchase, to have a more significant impact on consumers' purchase decisions, and encourage them to choose lower-emission car and taxi models. The CEVS will be reviewed in 2017.
section_header: ENCOURAGING THE SHIFT TO MORE EFFICIENT VEHICLES
extraction_rationale: This is a clear fiscal instrument tied directly to vehicle emissions performance. It qualifies as policy because it uses explicit rebates and surcharges to influence purchases.

policy_statement: The Fuel Economy Labeling Scheme provides fuel performance information for each car model to help consumers choose fuel-efficient cars.
source_quote: The Fuel Economy Labeling Scheme (FELS) introduced in 2012 complements the CEVS by providing information on the fuel performance of each car model. Together, the CEVS and FELS allow consumers to choose fuel-efficient cars, which in turn leads to savings on fuel cost and lower carbon emissions.
section_header: ENCOURAGING THE SHIFT TO MORE EFFICIENT VEHICLES
extraction_rationale: This is a named standards/information policy with a specific intervention. It qualifies because it is an implemented scheme designed to shift vehicle efficiency choices.

policy_statement: Singapore will progressively raise Minimum Energy Performance Standards for appliances, including raising air-conditioner standards again in September 2016.
source_quote:
MEPS for air-conditioners were raised in 2013, and will be raised again in September 2016. As for lamps, MEPS were introduced in 2015 to remove the least efficient models, such as tungsten filament incandescent bulbs.

The minimum standards for appliances will be progressively raised to increase the efficiency of the appliances on the market , while ensuring that product availability and consumer choice are not adversely affected.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding standards policy with explicit implementation history and future tightening. It clearly qualifies due to the regulatory mechanism and named appliance categories.

policy_statement: NEA's Mandatory Energy Labelling Scheme provides comparative energy-efficiency information for appliances and may be extended to additional appliances in future.
source_quote: To help households make more informed purchasing decisions, NEA introduced the Mandatory Energy Labelling Scheme (MELS) in 2008. It provides information that allows consumers to compare the energy efficiency of different appliances. MELS currently covers household refrigerators, air-conditioners, clothes dryers, televisions, and lamps. NEA will consider including other appliances in the future.
section_header: Promoting and Increasing Awareness about Energy Efficient Appliances
extraction_rationale: This is a named mandatory labeling scheme with defined coverage. It qualifies as policy because it is an implemented regulatory/information instrument.

policy_statement: NEA will promote more energy-efficient water heaters and is studying the feasibility of heat pump water heaters.
source_quote: For water heaters, NEA will raise public awareness of more energy-efficient models and encourage suppliers to bring more high-efficiency heaters into the market. For example, a heat pump water heater is highly efficient and consumes about one-third of the energy used by a gas or electric heater. NEA is currently studying the technical, economic, and operational feasibility of such water heaters.
section_header: Promoting and Increasing Awareness about Energy Efficient Appliances
extraction_rationale: This is somewhat softer than a mandate, but it still names a specific intervention and agency action to shift appliance markets. It qualifies as a policy commitment, though implementation details remain exploratory.

policy_statement: NEA will continue public messaging campaigns such as 'Save Energy Save Money' to promote energy-efficient appliances.
source_quote: In addition to schemes like MEPS and MELS, NEA will continue to promote energy-efficient appliances through public messaging campaigns - such as the 'Save Energy Save Money' initiative - at retail outlets, HDB void decks, and through social media.
section_header: Promoting and Increasing Awareness about Energy Efficient Appliances
extraction_rationale: This is a named outreach initiative with a clear government commitment to continue implementation. It is less stringent than regulation but still qualifies as a specific programme action.

policy_statement: HEMS are being piloted in selected Yuhua households to assess feasibility for larger-scale implementation.
source_quote: Home Energy Management Systems (HEMS) analyse real-time energy usage and costs, alert residents to high energy use, and offer energy-saving tips. Overseas studies have shown that HEMS can potentially reduce energy consumption by up to 10 per cent. HEMS are currently being piloted in selected households in the Yuhua estate to assess the feasibility of larger scale implementation.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific pilot intervention with a named technology and implementation site. It qualifies as policy because it is an active government-led trial aimed at future deployment.

policy_statement: PUB is pilot testing desalination and used-water technologies aimed at halving desalination energy use and reducing energy use in water reclamation.
source_quote: PUB is pilot testing new technologies such as electrochemical desalting, with the aim of halving the energy used in the seawater desalination process. Improved technologies for reclaiming used water could also reduce energy use. These reductions in energy use would decrease carbon emissions from the water sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete pilot-testing commitment with a quantified energy-use objective. It qualifies as policy because it specifies a named intervention and expected climate-related outcome.

policy_statement: NEA is piloting district-level food waste collection and anaerobic co-digestion with used water sludge at Ulu Pandan to increase on-site electricity generation.
source_quote: NEA is also conducting a pilot programme to evaluate the economic viability and feasibility of the district-level collection and processing of food waste for anaerobic co-digestion 25  with used water sludge at the Ulu Pandan Water Reclamation Plant. Anaerobic co-digestion could help meet up to 50 per cent of the treatment plant's electricity needs, up from 20 to 25 per cent from used water sludge digestion alone.
extraction_rationale: This is a named pilot programme with a specific technology and quantified electricity contribution. It qualifies as policy because it is a concrete implementation effort.

policy_statement: NEA aims to raise the overall recycling rate from 61% in 2015 to 70% in 2030 through awareness and policy initiatives.
source_quote: Waste reduction and recycling can reduce GHG emissions from waste incineration. NEA aims to increase the overall recycling rate from 61 per cent in 2015 to 70 per cent in 2030, by increasing awareness and implementing other policy initiatives (see feature story).
section_header: Increasing Energy and Carbon Efficiency in the Waste Management Process
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified target with a deadline and implementation direction. It qualifies as policy despite broad wording on the exact policy mix.

policy_statement: Singapore has a set of initiatives to reduce waste and increase efficiency in the waste sector.
source_quote:
## INITIATIVES TO REDUCE WASTE AND INCREASE EFFICIENCY IN THE WASTE SECTOR

The National Recycling Programme was launched by NEA in 2001 to make recycling more convenient for households.
section_header: INITIATIVES TO REDUCE WASTE AND INCREASE EFFICIENCY IN THE WASTE SECTOR
extraction_rationale: This section introduces multiple distinct waste-sector measures, so it functions as a parent umbrella. The heading and subsequent list-like prose justify parent extraction.

parent_statement: Initiatives to reduce waste and increase efficiency in the waste sector
policy_statement: The National Recycling Programme makes recycling more convenient for households.
source_quote: The National Recycling Programme was launched by NEA in 2001 to make recycling more convenient for households. All new HDB developments launched from 2014 will be fitted with Centralised Chutes for Recyclables.
section_header: INITIATIVES TO REDUCE WASTE AND INCREASE EFFICIENCY IN THE WASTE SECTOR
extraction_rationale: This is a named programme with a clear intervention in household recycling access. It is a sub-policy under the broader waste-sector initiatives section.

parent_statement: Initiatives to reduce waste and increase efficiency in the waste sector
policy_statement: All new HDB developments launched from 2014 will be fitted with Centralised Chutes for Recyclables.
source_quote: All new HDB developments launched from 2014 will be fitted with Centralised Chutes for Recyclables. NEA has also made it mandatory for large hotels and shopping malls to submit waste data and waste reduction plans.
section_header: INITIATIVES TO REDUCE WASTE AND INCREASE EFFICIENCY IN THE WASTE SECTOR
extraction_rationale: This is a clear design requirement with a defined applicability date. It is a sub-policy under the waste-sector initiatives umbrella.

parent_statement: Initiatives to reduce waste and increase efficiency in the waste sector
policy_statement: Large hotels and shopping malls are required to submit waste data and waste reduction plans.
source_quote: NEA has also made it mandatory for large hotels and shopping malls to submit waste data and waste reduction plans. In addition, NEA has worked with the industry and non-governmental organisations to get various parties to sign the voluntary Singapore Packaging Agreement that aims to reduce packaging waste, which constitutes about one-third of Singapore's domestic waste.
section_header: INITIATIVES TO REDUCE WASTE AND INCREASE EFFICIENCY IN THE WASTE SECTOR
extraction_rationale: This is a binding reporting and planning requirement, so it clearly qualifies as policy. It is a sub-policy under the broader waste initiatives section.

parent_statement: Initiatives to reduce waste and increase efficiency in the waste sector
policy_statement: The voluntary Singapore Packaging Agreement aims to reduce packaging waste.
source_quote: In addition, NEA has worked with the industry and non-governmental organisations to get various parties to sign the voluntary Singapore Packaging Agreement that aims to reduce packaging waste, which constitutes about one-third of Singapore's domestic waste. From 2007 to 2015, the signatories cumulatively reduced about 26,000 tonnes of packaging waste, and saved more than $58 million in material costs.
section_header: INITIATIVES TO REDUCE WASTE AND INCREASE EFFICIENCY IN THE WASTE SECTOR
extraction_rationale: This is a named voluntary agreement with a specific waste-reduction objective. It qualifies as policy because it is an organised government-supported intervention, though climate relevance is peripheral.

policy_statement: Singapore is studying the need for carbon pricing to strengthen economy-wide energy efficiency and low-carbon technology adoption.
source_quote: As part of this, we will be studying the need to price carbon to enhance efforts across all sectors. A carbon price would send appropriate price signals to encourage changes in energy consumption, provide market incentives for the adoption of energy-efficient technologies and low-carbon solutions, and stimulate growth in green industries. However, a carbon price will incur costs, including affecting our competitiveness, and its overall impact will have to be studied.
extraction_rationale: This is an exploratory commitment rather than an adopted carbon price, so it is borderline. It still qualifies because it explicitly commits to studying a specific economy-wide policy instrument.

policy_statement: EMA will work with power generation companies to adopt more efficient power generation technologies.
source_quote: Power generation systems, such as Combined Cycle Gas Turbines (CCGT), are expected to increase in efficiency over time due to advancements in technology. Higher efficiencies translate into lower costs of production of electricity. The Energy Market Authority (EMA) will work with power generation companies to encourage them to adopt more efficient technologies. This will lower their production costs, reduce carbon emissions and keep prices competitive for electricity consumers.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific government commitment to promote adoption of efficient generation technologies. It qualifies as policy because it names the responsible agency and intervention area, though the exact instrument is not specified.

policy_statement: Singapore plans to raise solar deployment to 350 MWp by 2020, about 5% of peak electricity demand.
source_quote: Singapore plans to raise the adoption of solar power in our system to 350MWp by 2020, representing about 5 per cent of peak electricity demand. A key initiative aimed at developing the solar industry in Singapore is the SolarNova programme.
section_header: INCREASING RENEWABLE ENERGY: SOLAR PHOTOVOLTAIC (PV) SYSTEMS
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified renewable energy deployment target with a deadline. It clearly qualifies as a mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Agencies will support solar deployment through building PV deployment, continued solar R&D investment, policy enhancements, and engagement efforts.
source_quote: Agencies like BCA, EMA, EDB, and NEA will study ways to support this development and sustain the momentum generated by the SolarNova programme, through encouraging the deployment of solar PV systems on buildings, continued investments in solar R&D, policy enhancements, and engagement efforts with various sectors to promote solar adoption.
section_header: INCREASING RENEWABLE ENERGY: SOLAR PHOTOVOLTAIC (PV) SYSTEMS
extraction_rationale: This is a multi-pronged implementation commitment tied to solar expansion. It is somewhat broad, but still qualifies because it names concrete intervention types and responsible agencies.

policy_statement: Singapore will invest in solar forecasting, energy storage, and smart grids to support higher shares of intermittent solar generation.
source_quote: Solar energy generation is intermittent as it is affected by variable factors such as cloud cover. To support an increasing share of intermittent electricity generation, Singapore will invest in research efforts in solar forecasting, energy storage, and smart grids.
section_header: INCREASING RENEWABLE ENERGY: SOLAR PHOTOVOLTAIC (PV) SYSTEMS
extraction_rationale: This is a clear public investment commitment in enabling technologies for renewable integration. It qualifies as policy because it specifies the intervention areas and purpose.

policy_statement: The SolarNova programme aggregates government solar demand to build the solar ecosystem and encourage greater solar adoption.
source_quote: The SolarNova programme led by EDB and HDB promotes and aggregates solar demand across government agencies. It aims to build up and support the solar ecosystem in Singapore, in fields such as manufacturing, project development, system integration, and financing so as to encourage greater adoption of solar energy.
extraction_rationale: This is a named programme with a clear implementation mechanism and objective. It qualifies as policy and includes a financing-support dimension.

policy_statement: HDB will call solar leasing tenders of around 30–50 MW every 9 to 12 months on behalf of government agencies.
source_quote: In December 2015, the first SolarNova tender was awarded, covering 76MWp of solar PV panels on 831 HDB blocks and eight government facilities. HDB will structure and call for solar leasing tenders of around 30 to 50MW approximately every nine to 12 months on behalf of various government agencies.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete procurement commitment with quantified tender size and frequency. It qualifies as policy because it specifies an ongoing deployment mechanism.

policy_statement: PUB and EDB are test-bedding a floating solar PV system on Tengeh Reservoir at a cost of $11 million.
source_quote: PUB and EDB are test-bedding a floating solar PV system on Tengeh Reservoir which can generate up to 3.3GWh of electricity per annum, equivalent to the average annual energy consumption of 750 HDB households. At a cost of $11 million, the project will also assess the impact of solar PV deployment on reservoir evaporation, biodiversity and water quality.
extraction_rationale: This is a funded demonstration project with a named technology, site, and expected output. It qualifies as policy because it is a concrete public-sector deployment initiative.

policy_statement: NEA will work with developers of new waste-to-energy plants to adopt technologies that optimise resource and energy recovery.
source_quote: NEA will work with companies developing new WTE plants to help them harness new technologies that optimise resource and energy recovery . For example, the new WTE plant under construction in Tuas will be Singapore's largest, with the ability to incinerate 3,600 tonnes of waste per day and generate 120MW of electricity.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific implementation commitment in the waste-energy sector. It qualifies as policy because it names the agency, intervention, and intended efficiency outcome.

policy_statement: NEA will maximise resource and energy recovery in the new Integrated Waste Management Facility, to be completed in 2024 and co-located with Tuas Water Reclamation Plant.
source_quote: NEA will also maximise resource and energy recovery in its new Integrated Waste Management Facility (IWMF), which will be completed in 2024. It will be co-located with PUB's Tuas Water Reclamation Plant to further optimise efficiency. The IWMF will generate electricity for the water reclamation plant, while the latter will provide the IWMF with treated used water for cooling and washing.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete infrastructure commitment with a completion date and operational integration details. It qualifies as policy because it specifies a defined facility and efficiency mechanism.

policy_statement: Under RIE2020, Singapore will invest $0.9 billion in Urban Solutions and Sustainability from 2016 to 2020.
source_quote: Under the National Research Foundation's (NRF) Research, Innovation, and Enterprise (RIE) 2020 Plan, $0.9 billion will be invested in the Urban Solutions and Sustainability domain from 2016 to 2020 to tackle Singapore's energy, water, land, and liveability challenges. The plan seeks to further improve our built and natural environment to offer an even higher quality of life for all Singaporeans, despite resource constraints and the challenges of climate change.
section_header: INVESTING IN RESEARCH, DEVELOPMENT AND DEMONSTRATION (RD&D)
extraction_rationale: This is a clear budget appropriation/public investment with amount, timeframe, and climate-related purpose. It qualifies as policy even though it spans multiple sustainability domains.

policy_statement: Singapore's RIE2020 builds on earlier public-sector RD&D investments in environment, water, and energy through several strategic research programmes.
source_quote:
## RESEARCH, INNOVATION, AND ENTERPRISE 2020

Investments under RIE2020 build on past public-sector investments in RD&D across the environment, water, and energy domains.

## Some examples are listed below:
extraction_rationale: This is a parent because the section explicitly introduces multiple example programmes beneath it. The umbrella is a public RD&D investment portfolio rather than a single standalone measure.

parent_statement: Research, Innovation, and Enterprise 2020 public-sector RD&D investments
policy_statement: The Environment and Water Technologies - Clean Water Strategic Research Programme invested $470 million to support smart and energy-efficient water technologies.
source_quote: The $470 million Environment and Water Technologies - Clean Water Strategic Research Programme (SRP) was established in 2006 to support innovation in smart and energy-efficient water technologies, to address Singapore's need for water security.
extraction_rationale: This is a named funded programme with a specific amount and intervention area. It is a sub-policy under the broader RD&D investment portfolio.

parent_statement: Research, Innovation, and Enterprise 2020 public-sector RD&D investments
policy_statement: The Energy Strategic Research Programme invested $365 million in solar energy and later expanded to smart grids, green buildings, and power utilities, establishing SERIS and ERI@N.
source_quote: The $365 million Clean Energy SRP was established in 2007 with an initial emphasis on solar energy. It was renamed in 2011 as the Energy SRP to cover additional domains such as smart grids, green buildings, and power utilities. The Energy SRP established two energy research centres to support the growth of the clean energy industry, namely the Solar Energy Research Institute of Singapore (SERIS) and the Energy Research Institute @ Nanyang Technological University (ERI@N).
extraction_rationale: This is a funded strategic programme with a defined amount and institutional outputs. It is a sub-policy under the broader RD&D investment umbrella.

parent_statement: Research, Innovation, and Enterprise 2020 public-sector RD&D investments
policy_statement: The Energy National Innovation Challenge set aside $300 million from 2011 to 2015 to develop and deploy cost-competitive energy solutions that improve efficiency, reduce emissions, and broaden energy options.
source_quote: The Energy National Innovation Challenge (ENIC) was established in 2011 to develop and deploy cost-competitive energy solutions within 20 years that would improve Singapore's energy efficiency, reduce carbon emissions, and broaden our energy options. Funding of $300 million was set aside between 201 1 and 2015 for such solutions, covering areas such as green buildings, green data centres, energy storage, and waste-to-energy.

policy_statement: Stockholm's remaining emissions within the geographical area shall not exceed 0.6 tonnes CO2e per resident by 2030, and negative emissions shall exceed remaining emissions.
source_quote:
## Milestone 2.1 A Stockholm that is climate-positive by 2030 and fossil-free by 2040

Emissions shall be max. 0.6 tonnes CO2e per resident by 2030. The goal is based on WWF's OPCC 1.5°C Alignment Method 19 , which is based on the ability of a country or city to reduce emissions. The milestone also includes the aim that negative emissions shall be greater than remaining emissions by 2030.
section_header: Milestone 2.1 A Stockholm that is climate-positive by 2030 and fossil-free by 2040
extraction_rationale: This is a core quantified climate target with a deadline and explicit negative-emissions requirement.

policy_statement: Stockholm's emissions budget for 2024-2040 caps cumulative emissions at 9 million tonnes CO2e.
source_quote:
## Emission budget sets the pace in reducing emissions

This action plan defines a local emissions budget for Stockholm as a complement to milestone 2.1 A Stockholm that is climate-positive by 2030 and fossil-free by 2040 . The budget complements the climate goal by describing the total volume of emissions in carbon dioxide equivalents (CO2e) that may be emitted on the way to achieving the goal. Stockholm's emissions budget 2024-2040 states that a maximum of 9 million tonnes CO2e may be emitted for the period 2024-2040.
section_header: Emission budget sets the pace in reducing emissions
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified cap on cumulative emissions over a defined period, clearly functioning as a policy target.

policy_statement: Transport-sector emissions in Stockholm shall decrease by 80% by 2030 compared with 2010.
source_quote:
## Milestone 2.2 Reduced climate impact from the transport sector

Emissions from the transport sector include emissions from road transport, working machinery, shipping (ports and shipping channels) and emissions from take-off and landing at Bromma Airport.

Emissions must be a maximum of approximately 165,000 tonnes from the transport sector in Stockholm by 2030.
section_header: Milestone 2.2 Reduced climate impact from the transport sector
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified sectoral emissions target with a baseline and 2030 endpoint.

policy_statement: Consumption-based greenhouse gas emissions in Stockholm shall be halved by 2030 compared with 2019, to a maximum of 5.4 tonnes CO2e per resident.
source_quote:
## Milestone 2.4 A halving of emissions from consumption

Consumption-based emissions were 10.7 tonnes CO2e per resident (in 2019), 22 which corresponds to total emissions of just over 10,000,000 tonnes CO2e for all residents of the City. A halving by 2030 means emissions of a maximum of 5.4 tonnes per resident by 2030.
section_header: Milestone 2.4 A halving of emissions from consumption
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified citywide consumption-emissions target with a baseline and endpoint.

policy_statement: Fossil fuels shall be phased out of the City's own and procured operations by 2030.
extraction_rationale: The table is OCR-damaged, but milestone 2.3 is clearly identified elsewhere as 'A fossil-free organisation in 2030' and described as phasing out fossil fuels in the City's own and procured operations. This is a valid policy target despite imperfect quote quality.

policy_statement: Implement climate change adaptation across all relevant Tokyo Metropolitan Government initiatives.
source_quote:
## (1) Implement climate change adaptation into all of TMG's initiatives.

The effects of climate change adaptation are appearing in a broad range of fields, including natural disasters, human health, and agriculture, forestry, and fisheries. TMG will address climate change impacts at present and in the future by incorporating climate change adaptation into all relevant initiatives.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear government-wide policy commitment with a named strategic intervention to mainstream adaptation. It is broad and not quantified, but it qualifies because it specifies an institutional action.

policy_statement: Promote adaptation measures based on the latest scientific knowledge and technologies.
source_quote:
## (2) Promote climate change adaptation based on scientific knowledge.

Scientific knowledge, such as future projections of climate change and its impacts, is constantly renewed in parallel with advancements in research and study. TMG will promote adaptation measures based on the latest scientific knowledge. In addition, we will actively utilize the latest technologies related to climate change adaptation.
extraction_rationale: This is a strategic policy commitment to guide adaptation implementation using science and technology. It is somewhat procedural, but it contains a concrete governing approach for adaptation policy.

policy_statement: Support municipalities' locally tailored adaptation efforts through active information provision.
source_quote:
## (3) Support local efforts in cooperation with municipalities.

It is essential to develop policies according to local circumstances as the impacts of climate change vary greatly, depending on regional characteristics. TMG will support local efforts by actively providing information so that municipalities can develop their community-based initiatives.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete intergovernmental support commitment for adaptation. While not quantified, it specifies a named intervention and institutional role.

policy_statement: Develop a system to collect, provide, and disseminate adaptation information and risks to residents.
source_quote:
## (4) Promote dissemination of information, including risks, to facilitate understanding of Tokyo residents.

The understanding of Tokyo residents is indispensable for promoting initiatives for climate change adaptation. This poses the necessity of aggressively raising awareness of climate change adaptation. TMG will develop a system to collect and provide information on climate change adaptation and actively disseminate the information.
extraction_rationale: This qualifies as a policy because it commits TMG to establish an information system and dissemination effort for adaptation risks. It is operational rather than regulatory.

policy_statement: Accelerate intercity collaboration on climate adaptation through C40 and similar organizations.
source_quote:
## (5) Promote international cooperation in C40 and other organizations to accelerate intercity collaboration.

The impacts of climate change and countermeasures for the impacts have become a global challenge. TMG will accelerate intercity collaboration by utilizing organizations in which TMG has membership, such as C40 1 , in order to share knowledge.
extraction_rationale: This is a named strategic commitment to pursue international cooperation for climate response. It is policy-relevant though broad and focused on collaboration rather than direct implementation.

TMG will minimize impacts on biodiversity, such as changes in the distribution of organisms, resulting from the impacts of climate change. In order to improve resilience, we will strive to enhance efforts to utilize and restore the functions of the natural environment.

policy_statement: Establish the Tokyo Climate Change Adaptation Center in FY 2021 and collaborate with it on climate-impact information functions.
source_quote:
## Establishment of Local Climate Change Adaptation Center

For the establishment of a Local Climate Change Adaptation Center based on Article 13 of the Climate Change Adaptation Act, TMG is preparing to set up in FY 2021 the Tokyo Climate Change Adaptation Center (tentative name) in the Tokyo Metropolitan Research Institute for Environmental Protection of the Tokyo Environmental Public Service Corporation, which has been engaged in research on countermeasures for the urban heat island effect.

TMG will collaborate with the center to collect, organize, analyze, and provide information on climate change impacts and adaptation to climate change.

policy_statement: Salt Lake City will ensure renewable energy provides 100% of community electricity needs by 2032.
source_quote: Salt Lake City is working to ensure that renewable energy provides 100% of community electricity needs by 2032. This goal is foundational to the success of Climate Positive given that more than 50% of community carbon pollution is associated with electricity generation.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear quantified target with a deadline and explicit climate purpose, so it qualifies as a policy commitment.

policy_statement: The City will work with Rocky Mountain Power under a Joint Clean Energy Cooperation Statement on energy efficiency, EV infrastructure, smart grid investments, and pathways to net-100% renewable energy.
source_quote: Salt Lake City Mayor Jackie Biskupski and Rocky Mountain Power CEO Cindy Crane signed a Joint Clean Energy Cooperation Statement in August 2016 that details a vision to work together in good faith on energy goals. Energy efficiency, electric vehicle infrastructure, smart grid investments and pathways to net-100% renewable energy are all part of the vision.
extraction_rationale: This is a named formal cooperation statement with specific intervention areas. Although framed as a vision, it contains concrete policy domains and an institutional mechanism.

policy_statement: Salt Lake City's sustainable food program pursues goals to improve low-carbon food production, increase access to ecologically responsible healthy foods, and reduce consumable food waste.
source_quote: A sustainable, low carbon, equitable system that provides healthy food for the entire community is key to creating a climate resilient and healthy community. In Utah, our food choices contribute to 25% of the household carbon footprint, with impacts occurring throughout the entire life-cycle of the food we eat. From production to plate to food waste, there are countless opportunities to reduce emissions. Key goals of the Climate Positive sustainable food program are listed below.

To create a more resilient food system, the community must shift from carbon intensive meat and dairy agricultural practices to more diverse produce production methods.

Increasing availability to affordable, fresh, whole foods is integral to creating a healthy community.
